title: Public Education Budget Amendments
description: This bill supplements or reduces appropriations otherwise provided for the support and operation of public education for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2024, and ending June 30, 2025, and appropriates funds for the support an operation of public education for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2025, and ending June 30, 2026.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>increases an educator salary adjustment;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a salary bonus for certain education support professionals;<hr><ltbullet>repeals provisions regarding programs for which funding is eliminated, including:<hr><ltbullet1>Technology-Life-Careers;<hr><ltbullet1>student leadership organizations;<hr><ltbullet1>professional staff weighted pupil units;<hr><ltbullet1>the Capital Outlay Enrollment Growth Program; and<hr><ltbullet1>a pilot grant for professional learning;<hr><ltbullet>repeals a statutory increase for the legacy iteration of the Carson Smith Scholarship Program;<hr><ltbullet>provides appropriations for the use and support of school districts, charter schools and state education agencies;<hr><ltbullet>adjusts the number of weighted pupil units for Career and Technical Education (CTE) -Add-on, Professional Staff, and Special Education-Impact Aid WPU programs to reflect increased student weightings approved by the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet>makes certain statutory changes to adjust programmatic formulas with funding changes;<hr><ltbullet>provides appropriations for other purposes as described;<hr><ltbullet>provides intent language;<hr><ltbullet>provides a coordination clause to adopt and supersede S.B. 321, Public Education Funding Amendments, regarding the state guarantee for local property tax levies; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Murdered and Missing Indigenous Relatives Task Force Amendments
description: This bill reestablishes the Missing and Murdered Indigenous Relatives Task Force.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>reestablishes the Murdered and Missing Indigenous Relatives Task Force, with the membership consisting of nine members from government and community organizations;<hr><ltbullet>requires that any vacancy in the task force be filled in the same manner as the original appointment;<hr><ltbullet>designates the appointees from the Senate and House of Representatives as the cochairs of the task force;<hr><ltbullet>establishes that a quorum of the task force consists of five members and that majority action of the quorum is required for task force decisions;<hr><ltbullet>establishes compensation requirements for both legislator members and non-legislator members of the task force;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel provide staff support to the task force;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the responsibilities of the task force;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the task force must report its findings to the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee; and<hr><ltbullet>provides for the repeal of the task force.

title: Property Tax Code Recodification
description: This bill recodifies provisions related to relief granted through property tax.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>recodifies:<hr><ltbullet1>Title 59, Chapter 2, Part 12, Property Tax Relief;<hr><ltbullet1>Title 59, Chapter 2, Part 18, Tax Deferral and Tax Abatement; and<hr><ltbullet1>Title 59, Chapter 2, Part 19, Armed Forces Exemptions;<hr><ltbullet>creates a General Provisions part that clarifies the procedures and rights available for each type of tax relief; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Criminal Code Recodification and Cross References
description: This bill modifies criminal provisions in Title 76, Utah Criminal Code, by redrafting offense statutes into a new structure, reorganizing criminal statutes into a new format, and clarifying existing law.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTLAW", "name": "Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>reorders language into a standardized format and clarifies existing law, including the offenses in Title 76, Chapter 9, Offenses Against Public Order and Decency, and Chapter 10, Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, Welfare, and Morals;<hr><ltbullet>reorganizes Title 76, Chapters 9 and 10 into a new organization to better align with the contents of the statutes;<hr><ltbullet>reorganizes offenses to enact an embedded offense as a stand-alone statute or statutes, including offenses concerning:<hr><ltbullet1>emergency reporting, interference, and false reports;<hr><ltbullet1>prohibited use of a party line or public pay telephone;<hr><ltbullet1>commercial obstruction;<hr><ltbullet1>electronic communication harassment and disclosure of personal information;<hr><ltbullet1>cruelty to animals, dog fighting, and police service canines, including aligning exemptions and defenses based on the elements of each offense;<hr><ltbullet1>voyeurism;<hr><ltbullet1>abuse or desecration of a dead human body;<hr><ltbullet1>criminal street gang activities;<hr><ltbullet1>tobacco sales and related offenses;<hr><ltbullet1>gambling and related offenses;<hr><ltbullet1>bus hijacking and related offenses;<hr><ltbullet1>money laundering and related offenses;<hr><ltbullet1>the use of a laser pointer;<hr><ltbullet1>unlawful littering and related offenses;<hr><ltbullet1>unlawful possession, use, or control of a vehicle with a contraband compartment;<hr><ltbullet1>unlawful tattooing or piercing of a minor;<hr><ltbullet1>labeling of explosives and related offenses;<hr><ltbullet1>weapons offenses and related statutes;<hr><ltbullet1>corporate fraud and related offenses, including unlawful acts by a director, officer, or agent;<hr><ltbullet1>nuisances;<hr><ltbullet1>pornography and related offenses, including placing the definition of pornography in the relevant definition section;<hr><ltbullet1>prostitution, sexual solicitation, and related offenses; and<hr><ltbullet1>kickbacks and related offenses;<hr><ltbullet>for clarity, places contents of Title 76, Chapter 9, Part 5, Libel, into Title 45, Chapter 2, Libel;<hr><ltbullet>for clarity, places certain contents of Title 76, Chapter 10, Part 5, Weapons, into Title 53, Public Safety Code;<hr><ltbullet>for clarity, places certain law enforcement requirements concerning gang loitering from Title 76, Chapter 10, Part 9, Prohibition of Gang Activity, into Title 53, Chapter 25, Law Enforcement Requirements;<hr><ltbullet>for clarity, defines a minor as an individual younger than 21 years old for the offense concerning public intoxication;<hr><ltbullet>for clarity, provides a more detailed description of an actor for purposes of offenses involving providing a weapon to a minor;<hr><ltbullet>for clarity, technically revises language concerning vicious animal offense;<hr><ltbullet>for clarity, removes definition of image in offense concerning failure to report child sexual abuse material by a computer technician;<hr><ltbullet>adds penalty provisions to offenses concerning high explosives that had been inadvertently omitted;<hr><ltbullet>repeals certain statutes concerning the Utah Trade Commission, which entity no longer exists;<hr><ltbullet>for clarity, provides which prostitution-related offenses do not apply to a minor;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical corrections to certain statutes resulting from inadvertent omissions in the 2024 criminal code recodification, including:<hr><ltbullet1>reinserting a provision guaranteeing Native American rights in the statute concerning establishment of a prohibited item policy in a correctional or mental health facility;<hr><ltbullet1>reinserting the penalty to the offense of alteration of proposed legislative bill or resolution; and<hr><ltbullet1>providing clarifying language regarding the identity of the actor in the offense concerning trafficking in warrants; <hr><ltbullet>adds a coordination clause to explain that amendments to certain sections in this bill will be superseded or amended by amendments to those sections in H.B. 133, Dangerous Weapons Amendments, if both bills pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Prostitution Offense Amendments
description: This bill reorganizes and amends provisions concerning prostitution and related offenses.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTLAW", "name": "Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>adds and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>reorganizes provisions concerning prostitution and related offenses;<hr><ltbullet>for clarity, revises names of certain prostitution-related offenses;<hr><ltbullet>for clarity, provides that a child may not be prosecuted for engaging in sexual solicitation or prostitution;<hr><ltbullet>separates existing prostitution-related offenses into separate offenses based on the ages of the individuals involved;<hr><ltbullet>provides new penalties for child offenders of certain prostitution-related offenses that are based on the age of the child offender; <hr><ltbullet>for clarity, revises the offense of engaging in prostitution or sexual solicitation as an HIV positive offender; <hr><ltbullet>adds several prostitution-related offenses to the list of offenses for which a minor may not receive a nonjudicial adjustment; <hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to explain that amendments to certain sections in this bill will supersede amendments to those sections in H.B. 21, Criminal Code Recodification and Cross References, if both bills pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Insurance Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions relating to insurance.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the circumstances under which a public agency insurance mutual or a reserve fund is exempt from the Insurance Code;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to dual licensing;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to money appropriated from the Captive Insurance Restricted Account;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that an insurer does not need to file a certification that a non-English policy is in compliance with relevant laws;<hr><ltbullet>aligns state law with federal rules relating to preexisting condition limitations;<hr><ltbullet>limits the scope by which the Insurance Department can issue a waiver for a license;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the commissioner may take an action against a licensee if the licensee fails to pay a final judgment within 60 days;<hr><ltbullet>adds additional reporting requirements for a licensee against whom a judgment has been entered;<hr><ltbullet>changes the reporting period for agency title insurance producers;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to captive insurance companies;<hr><ltbullet>reduces the minimum capital requirement for an association captive insurance company;<hr><ltbullet>allows a captive insurance company to be formed as a not-for-profit organization;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that officers of a captive insurance company must be separate individuals;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to insurance investments;<hr><ltbullet>amends requirements relating to a sponsored captive insurance company's business;<hr><ltbullet>amends the grounds under which the commissioner may revoke the certificate of authority of a captive insurance company; title: Voting Precinct Amendments
description: This bill addresses voting precincts.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a county legislative body to establish a voting precinct consisting of two or more noncontiguous geographic areas in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>requires the name of a voting precinct to be distinguishable from any other voting precinct;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the county clerk to adjust the boundaries of a voting precinct in order to:<hr><ltbullet1>match the current boundaries of a local political subdivision; or<hr><ltbullet1>match the resulting boundaries of a local subdivision that expands, divides, alters, or changes the local political subdivision's boundaries;<hr><ltbullet>requires a county clerk who adjusts the boundaries of a voting precinct to:<hr><ltbullet1>file a notice with the Utah Geospatial Resource Center at least 65 days before the date of an election; and<hr><ltbullet1>provide a copy of the notice to the county legislative body; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Child Visitation Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to custody and visitation for individuals other than a parent.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies a standard required to support an award of non-parental custody or visitation;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that a court that has received a petition seeking non-parent custody or visitation may, as part of the adjudication of the petition, make findings relating to a parent's ability to exercise primary physical custody, and make findings relating to a claim of parental abuse or neglect of a minor child; and<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the time period that is applicable to a court's findings.

title: Indian Family Preservation Act Amendments
description: This bill addresses the preservation of Indian families.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>enacts the Indian Family Preservation Act (state act), including:<hr><ltbullet1>defining terms;<hr><ltbullet1>addressing effective date and severability;<hr><ltbullet1>requiring inquiry into Indian status;<hr><ltbullet1>providing for what constitutes best interests of an Indian child;<hr><ltbullet1>addressing jurisdiction over child custody proceedings;<hr><ltbullet1>providing for actions related to pending court proceedings;<hr><ltbullet1>stating parental rights;<hr><ltbullet1>providing for voluntary termination of rights;<hr><ltbullet1>establishing how consent or other actions are invalidated;<hr><ltbullet1>addressing placement of Indian children;<hr><ltbullet1>creating a process to return custody of an Indian child;<hr><ltbullet1>addressing information related to tribal affiliation and protection of rights;<hr><ltbullet1>authorizing agreements between the state and Indian tribes under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet1>addressing improper removal of an Indian child;<hr><ltbullet1>explaining the application of state or federal standards;<hr><ltbullet1>providing for emergency removal or placement of an Indian child; and<hr><ltbullet1>addressing recordkeeping and information availability;<hr><ltbullet>replaces cites to the federal Indian Child Welfare Act with cites to the state act;<hr><ltbullet>addresses right to counsel;<hr><ltbullet>addresses sharing of information by agreement;<hr><ltbullet>exempts certain time frame preferences under the state act; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends the enhancement for offenses committed in concert with three or more persons or in relation to a criminal street gang;<hr><ltbullet>amends certain theft, retail theft, and prostitution sentencing enhancements to include prior convictions in other state, federal, or military courts;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that in sentencing for an offense related to retail theft, the value of the stolen item is determined by the item's retail value;<hr><ltbullet>amends the offense of sexual extortion;<hr><ltbullet>amends the definition of "financial transaction card" in Section 76-6-506;<hr><ltbullet>adds offenses that may be charged as part of a pattern of unlawful activity;  <hr><ltbullet>increases the fine for an individual who is convicted of the offense of patronizing a prostitute;<hr><ltbullet>increases penalties for an individual who:<hr><ltbullet1>acts to bring a minor into a criminal street gang in certain circumstances; and<hr><ltbullet1>acts to intimidate a minor into remaining in a criminal street gang in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>includes coordination clauses to coordinate changes between this bill, H.B. 21, Criminal Code Recodification and Cross References, and H.B. 22, Prostitution Offense Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Correctional Health Amendments
description: This bill addresses health care for individuals who are involved with the criminal justice system.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Health and Human Services (department) to contract with a telehealth psychiatric consultation provider to provide consultation services to staff responsible for inmates' psychiatric care;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department to convene a working group to study the department's needs regarding an electronic health record system for inmate health care and provide recommendations to the Health and Human Services Interim Committee;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department to contract with psychiatrists to meet staffing needs for correctional health services, except under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department to provide an annual report to the Health and Human Services Interim Committee concerning the provision of comprehensive health care to inmates;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Corrections and a local mental health authority to cooperate to have certain offenders assessed for available community-based services, and to take steps to connect an offender to appropriate community-based services based on the results of the assessment; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Wildland Urban Interface Modifications
description: This bill addresses efforts to oversee wildfire risks associated with wildland urban interface property.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires counties to take certain actions related to wildland urban interface property, including assessing a fee;<hr><ltbullet>directs the fee to be retained by a county and deposited into the Wildland-urban Interface Prevention, Preparedness, and Mitigation Fund;<hr><ltbullet>addresses insuring wildland urban interface property;<hr><ltbullet>imposes notice requirements related to insuring wildland urban interface property;<hr><ltbullet>requires counties and municipalities to adopt the wildland urban interface building code standards;<hr><ltbullet>permits the Division of Forestry, Fire, and State Lands (division) to choose not to cover costs of local governments under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>directs the division to establish a program for wildland urban interface coordinators to evaluate, using a triage scale, high risk wildland urban interface property;<hr><ltbullet>addresses actions related to evaluating the high risk wildland urban interface property;<hr><ltbullet>provides for a database to be accessed by certain insurers related to evaluating high risk wildland urban interface property;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes rulemaking;<hr><ltbullet>addresses liability; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Cannabinoid Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to hemp and medical cannabis regulation.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTNAE", "name": "Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits certain cannabinoids from being used in cannabinoid products;<hr><ltbullet>allows the Department of Agriculture and Food to limit certain types of cannabinoids that are found in a cannabinoid product;<hr><ltbullet>amends background check requirements for cannabinoid processor licenses;<hr><ltbullet>amends qualifications for obtaining a cannabinoid processor license;<hr><ltbullet>requires industrial hemp retailers to maintain a video surveillance system;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to cannabinoid product enforcement;<hr><ltbullet>requires a person to have a cannabis processor license to transport hemp concentrate;<hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement that certain cannabinoid products be in a medicinal dosage form; <hr><ltbullet>allows for additional medical cannabis pharmacies;<hr><ltbullet>creates a new medical cannabis pharmacy license for independent medical cannabis pharmacies;<hr><ltbullet>creates ownership restrictions for independent medical cannabis pharmacies;<hr><ltbullet>adjusts fees for certain medical cannabis pharmacy licenses;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding cannabis production and sanitation;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to enforcement and appeals;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to closed-door medical cannabis pharmacies;<hr><ltbullet>allows a cannabis processing facility to have a website that includes product information;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding when the department may seize products and test products;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to information a medical cannabis pharmacy must have available to a patient purchasing medical cannabis;<hr><ltbullet>creates a reporting requirement for the department;<hr><ltbullet>repeals sections related to the state central patient portal; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill modifies how county officers and county legislative bodies maintain office space and hold meetings.

description: This bill amends provisions relating to civil commitment.

title: Residential Solar Panel Consumer Protection Amendments
description: This bill establishes additional protections for residential solar panel customers.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; <hr><ltbullet>creates additional disclosure language; <hr><ltbullet>mandates that a solar retailer's good faith estimate of energy production be within a specified percentage of the actual energy production;<hr><ltbullet>requires the solar retailer repair the solar panels if the actual energy production is not within a specified percentage of the good faith estimate of energy production;<hr><ltbullet>creates a registration and security requirement for a solar retailer to do business in Utah; <hr><ltbullet>provides an exception to the background check for a publicly traded corporation registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission;<hr><ltbullet>requires a solar retailer sales representative be employed by the solar retailer as a W-2 employee;<hr><ltbullet>delays a customer's financial obligation on a residential solar energy system until the system is active and producing usable energy; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Building Inspector Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions relating to building inspectors.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>directs the Uniform Building Code Commission to: <hr><ltbullet1>collect data pertaining to building inspectors;<hr><ltbullet1>publish gathered data on an annual basis; and<hr><ltbullet1>report the data annually to the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet>expands the scope for the Division of Professional Licensing to spend money from surcharges; <hr><ltbullet>adds unlawful and unprofessional conduct provisions for licensed building inspectors acting as qualified building officials;<hr><ltbullet>requires a local regulator to hire or contract with a qualified building official; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: State Tax Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions relating to the tax code.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>repeals obsolete language;<hr><ltbullet>provides the scope of the State Tax Commission's authority to share income tax return information with the Department of Workforce Services to determine eligibility for public assistance;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which there is an annual limit on the total amount of interest that the commission pays;<hr><ltbullet>requires a payment settlement entity, such as a marketplace facilitator, to file certain federal forms with the State Tax Commission; <hr><ltbullet>clarifies what is a commercial unit for purposes of claiming a commercial energy system tax credit;<hr><ltbullet>updates the circumstances under which an individual is exempt from individual income tax;<hr><ltbullet>creates a deduction for individuals who have to repay social security that is subject to income tax; <hr><ltbullet>provides for the repeal of the enterprise zone tax credit, which, by statute, automatically expired; <hr><ltbullet>extends the carry forward period for a tax credit available to a pass-through entity taxpayer who receives income from a pass-through entity that paid the income tax on the income;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances for the automatic removal of refundable individual income tax credits from the income tax return; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Tax Withholding Amendments
description: This bill modifies requirements for tax withholding.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet> provides penalty provisions that apply if a producer fails to file a Form 1099 for mineral production tax withholding or fails to file the Form 1099 on time;<hr><ltbullet>amends the percentage of the mineral production tax a producer withholds to align with the income tax rate;<hr><ltbullet>amends the information a producer is required to provide on a withholding return;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for a producer to file a form 1099 with the State Tax Commission; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Property Tax Act Modifications
description: This bill modifies provisions in the Property Tax Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes an application deadline for the residential property tax exemption;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the contents of the residential property declaration signed by an owner of residential property;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the circumstances under which land that is less than five acres in area may qualify for agricultural property tax assessment;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies a taxpayer's ability to appeal decisions related to tax deferral and tax abatement to the State Tax Commission;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Tax Commission to report to the Legislature if certain rules are promulgated; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Public Official Bonding Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to bonds required for public officials and employees to protect against malfeasance or misfeasance in office and replaces the requirement to post a bond with a requirement to obtain crime insurance.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>replaces requirements for bonds that a public official or employee is required to post in relation to the performance of duties with a requirement to obtain crime insurance;<hr><ltbullet>removes provisions relating to bonds that do not apply when replaced with crime insurance;<hr><ltbullet>removes provisions that make it difficult or impossible to obtain crime insurance;<hr><ltbullet>modifies, in certain circumstances, the scope of the coverage that relates to a bond that will be replaced with crime insurance;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements relating to crime insurance;<hr><ltbullet>addresses liability relating to certain public officials;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the setting of rates and record keeping for crime insurance;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the failure to obtain crime insurance;<hr><ltbullet>repeals certain provisions relating to actions on bonds; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Firefighter Cancer Amendments
description: This bill modifies the Utah Occupational Disease Act by expanding the rebuttable presumption for a firefighter diagnosed with cancer.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>expands the list of cancers that presumptively arise from service as a firefighter;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for the rebuttable presumption;<hr><ltbullet> excludes respiratory cancers related to the use of cigarettes, electronic cigarettes, tobacco products, or marijuana from the rebuttable presumption;<hr><ltbullet>provides a cancer screening to the firefighter;<hr><ltbullet>requires the fire department where a firefighter is working to cover the out-of-pocket cost of the cancer screening; and <hr><ltbullet>provides for the management of the cancer screening program.

title: Ritual Abuse Amendments
description: This bill addresses ritual abuse.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires current sexual assault and sexual abuse training for law enforcement officers to include training on sexual assault committed during a ritual and the impact of that conduct on the victim; <hr><ltbullet>creates an aggravating factor for certain offenses committed against an individual under 18 years old if the offense was committed as part of a ritual;<hr><ltbullet>contains a coordination clause to coordinate a substantive change between this bill and S.B. 24, Child Abuse and Torture Amendments, by adding the crime of child torture, which is newly created in S.B. 24, to the list of offenses that qualify for the aggravating factor created in this bill; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Government Records and Information Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to government records and information.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding the disclosure of voter history information;<hr><ltbullet>classifies as private a record or information regarding whether a voter returned a ballot with postage attached;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a government officer from accessing or using government records or information in a manner that is not related to a duty of the government officer;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a government officer from accessing or using government records or information for a primarily personal purpose, unless the government officer gains access to the records or information in the same manner as a member of the public;<hr><ltbullet>makes it a crime to intentionally violate the provisions described in the preceding paragraph;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions relating to the award of attorney fees; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Decommissioned Asset Disposition Amendments
description: This bill makes changes to the requirements related to the decommissioning and disposal of electrical generation facilities and equipment by a project entity.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTPUT", "name": "Public Utilities, Energy, and Technology Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a project entity from:<hr><ltbullet1>altering facilities that provide power to station service;<hr><ltbullet1>disconnecting from or modifying existing interconnections and critical switchyard equipment; and<hr><ltbullet1>taking actions that would require a new plant owner to make an interconnection request; and<hr><ltbullet>creates the Utah Energy Council (council);<hr><ltbullet>establishes council membership and duties;<hr><ltbullet>provides authority for the council to manage decommissioned electrical generation facilities;<hr><ltbullet>requires the council to select facility operators through a competitive process;<hr><ltbullet>establishes minimum qualifications and criteria for facility operators;<hr><ltbullet>repeals provisions related to the Decommissioned Asset Disposition Authority; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Public Education Revisions
description: This bill amends provisions and programs regarding the operation of the public education system.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>removes duplicative language regarding a college and career readiness plan;<hr><ltbullet>amends the Teacher Salary Supplement Program and the upcoming replacement Salary Supplement for Highly Needed Educators program to allow a local education agency (LEA) that experiences a carry forward or leftover balance to increase the amount the LEA provides to teachers under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>adds the Utah Schools for the Deaf and the Blind as an LEA that may participate in the Salary Supplement for Highly Needed Educators program;<hr><ltbullet>increases the portion of appropriated funding the State Board of Education (state board) is statutorily authorized to expend for administrative costs for early literacy software, including the cost of an independent software evaluator;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding kindergarten to:<hr><ltbullet1>allow a child to enroll in kindergarten if the child moves to Utah after having enrolled in kindergarten in another state with different age requirements for enrollment; and<hr><ltbullet1>repeal a requirement for the state board to create a process for an LEA to follow when an enrolled student in kindergarten is not toilet-trained;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding early learning plans to:<hr><ltbullet1>reduce requirements for the plans that LEAs submit to the state board; and<hr><ltbullet1>repeal a requirement for the state board to use a digital platform to communicate with LEAs regarding early learning;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to school fees to ensure that a school is not prohibited from charging a fee for a fine arts course; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Flag Display Amendments
description: This bill allows the display of certain flags on government property.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a government entity or employee of a government entity from displaying a flag in or on the grounds of government property except certain exempted flags;<hr><ltbullet>requires the state auditor to ensure compliance, including by imposing fines;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a cause of action for an alleged violation within the public education system;<hr><ltbullet>requires the attorney general to defend and the state to hold harmless an individual acting under color of state law to enforce the flag display statute within the public education system; and<hr><ltbullet>provides severability.

description: This bill addresses sentencing and criminal procedures for certain criminal offenses.

title: Child Welfare Modifications
description: This bill addresses search warrants and investigative warrants relating to child welfare.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding the issuance of warrants by a juvenile court;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a juvenile court to issue an investigative warrant related to the health, safety, or welfare of a child;<hr><ltbullet>states that a peace officer or child welfare caseworker who is executing a search warrant or an investigative warrant may request assistance in executing the warrant; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Environmental Permitting Modifications
description: This bill addresses provisions related to environmental permitting.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Air Quality (division) to:<hr><ltbullet1>develop and publish guidance and rules related to federal plantwide applicability limitations;<hr><ltbullet1>review the division's rules related to permit by rule registration;<hr><ltbullet1> include at least five new categories of sources in the division's permit by rule program; and<hr><ltbullet1>report to the Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Interim Committee the results of the division's review of the permit by rule program;<hr><ltbullet>adds a repeal date for the sections related to plantwide applicability limitations and permit by rule registration; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Homeowners' Association Requirements
description: This bill amends provisions relating to homeowners' associations.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>increases the monetary amount a unit or lot owner may request if an association fails to properly make records available for examination;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a declarant from using association funds in a legal action brought by a homeowner against the declarant before the end of the period of administrative control;<hr><ltbullet>defines "development right";<hr><ltbullet>amends the conditions for the termination of a period of administrative control for an association of lot owners;<hr><ltbullet>provides requirements for a declarant of a association of lot owners during the period of administrative control; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Private Individual Force and Detention Amendments
description: This bill concerns the ability of a private individual to use force or detain another individual.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends the circumstances under which a private individual may use force in defense of personal property;<hr><ltbullet>amends the circumstances under which a private individual may lawfully detain another individual, including removing the use of the term "arrest";<hr><ltbullet>provides a limitation on civil and criminal liability for a private individual who temporarily detains another individual under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>amends the force in arrest statute to provide that the statute applies to law enforcement officers and creates a new statute for when force can be used by a private individual when making a temporary detention; <hr><ltbullet>amends procedures that govern the subsequent arrest and transportation of an individual who has been temporarily detained by another private individual; <hr><ltbullet>adds a coordination clause between this bill and S.B. 79, Technical Code Amendments, to provide that the changes to Section 77-7-3 will supersede the changes to that section in S.B. 79; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: State Land Access Road Amendments
description: This bill requires certain state entities to identify and record notice of roads that traverse certain lands owned by the state.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the Public Lands Policy Coordinating Office (PLPCO) and the School and Institutional Trust Lands Administration (SITLA) to identify certain roads located on school and institutional trust lands and state lands, with initial focus within certain counties;<hr><ltbullet>requires PLPCO and SITLA to record with the relevant county recorder's office notice of the roads relevant to state lands and school and institutional trust lands;<hr><ltbullet>exempts class A, class B, and class C roads from the notice requirements; <hr><ltbullet>provides requirements for the Division of Wildlife Resources to identify roads within wildlife management areas;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Division of Wildlife Resources may not permanently close a road without consent of the legislative body of the county in which the road is located; and<hr><ltbullet>codifies a provision to ensure that title to a class D road abandoned by a county remains with the state, and provides a process for abandonment of a class D road or R.S. 2477 right-of-way.

description: This bill addresses firearm safety instruction in public schools.

description: This bill makes changes to criminal offenses in Title 76, Utah Criminal Code.

title: Health Education Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to health education.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Board of Education to establish curriculum requirements that include instruction in:<hr><ltbullet1>sexual assault resource strategies;<hr><ltbullet1>sexual violence behavior prevention; and<hr><ltbullet1>the legal implications of electronically distributing sexually explicit images;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to when a student receives health education instruction; <hr><ltbullet>requires a local education agency (LEA) to:<hr><ltbullet1>review data, including data on sexual assault, for each county in which the LEA is located;<hr><ltbullet1>use the reviewed data to inform the LEA's policies on health education; and<hr><ltbullet1>as appropriate, incorporate the data into health education; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Military Affairs Amendments
description: This bill makes changes to the code addressing military affairs.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends resident student status eligibility for veterans who use veteran benefits to pay for tuition;<hr><ltbullet>amends how much money the Interstate Commission on Educational Opportunity for Military Children may assess, levy, or collect from Utah legislative appropriations;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the Department of Veterans and Military Affairs:<hr><ltbullet1>is required to provide service benefits to service members, veterans, and the families of service members and veterans; and<hr><ltbullet1>serves as the State Approving Agency for Utah under United States Code, Title 38, Veterans Benefits;<hr><ltbullet>allows the Department of Veterans and Military Affairs to receive gifts, contributions, and donations to support service members, veterans, and the families of service members and veterans;<hr><ltbullet>allows the Department of Veterans and Military Affairs to enter into an intergovernmental support agreement with a military installation or entity, including the National Guard, to provide support services to the military installation or entity;<hr><ltbullet>repeals Title 63M, Chapter 6, Military Base Easements Act, and enacts sections in Title 71A, Veterans and Military Affairs, related to easements; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Education Industry Employee Privacy
description: This bill provides for the personal privacy of local education agency employees.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>enacts restrictions on a local education agency (LEA) selling or transferring certain contact information without consent;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits requiring use of certain technologies on personal devices;<hr><ltbullet>requires an LEA to provide accommodations for mandatory technology use under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>allows an employee to file written complaints with the State Board of Education about violations;<hr><ltbullet>permits the State Board of Education to investigate complaints; and <hr><ltbullet>allows for consequences for violations.

title: Murdered and Missing Indigenous Relatives Amendments
description: This bill reestablishes the Missing and Murdered Indigenous Relatives Task Force.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>reestablishes the Murdered and Missing Indigenous Relatives Task Force, with the membership consisting of nine members from government and community organizations;<hr><ltbullet>requires that any vacancy in the task force be filled in the same manner as the original appointment;<hr><ltbullet>designates the appointees from the Senate and House of Representatives as the cochairs of the task force;<hr><ltbullet>establishes that a quorum of the task force consists of five members and that majority action of the quorum is required for task force decisions;<hr><ltbullet>establishes compensation requirements for both legislator members and non-legislator members of the task force;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel provide staff support to the task force;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the responsibilities of the task force;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the task force must report its findings to the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee; and<hr><ltbullet>provides for the repeal of the task force.

title: Unauthorized Use of Residential Real Property Modifications
description: This bill addresses the consequences of unauthorized use of residential real property by providing a limited alternative remedy to remove a trespasser from a residential dwelling and providing a criminal penalty for the fraudulent sale or rental of residential real property.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>authorizes property owners or their agents to request assistance from the sheriff for the immediate removal of a trespasser from a residential dwelling under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>requires an owner seeking removal of a trespasser, or the owner's authorized agent, to submit a complaint;<hr><ltbullet>specifies requirements for the complaint;<hr><ltbullet>provides requirements for the sheriff;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a sheriff to arrest a trespasser for legal cause;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a sheriff is entitled to a specified fee for service of notice to vacate;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the owner or agent to request that the sheriff stand by while the owner or agent takes possession of the property; <hr><ltbullet>authorizes the sheriff to charge a reasonable hourly rate;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the sheriff is not liable to any party for loss, destruction, or damage;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the property owner or agent is not liable to any party for the loss or destruction of, or damage to, personal property unless it was wrongfully removed;<hr><ltbullet>provides civil remedies;<hr><ltbullet>imposes criminal penalties for unlawfully detaining, occupying, or trespassing of, a residential dwelling intentionally and causing a specified amount of damage; imposes criminal penalties for any person who knowingly and willfully presents a false document purporting to be a valid lease agreement, deed, or other instrument conveying real property rights;<hr><ltbullet>imposes criminal penalties for fraudulently listing or advertising for sale, or renting or leasing, residential real property under certain circumstances; and provides criminal penalties for committing perjury.

title: Dangerous Weapons Recodification and Cross References
description: This bill modifies provisions in the Utah Code addressing dangerous weapons by redrafting statutes into a new structure, reorganizing applicable criminal statutes into a new standardized format, and clarifying existing law.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>restructures and makes technical changes to sections in the Utah Code dealing with dangerous weapons to bring the sections into a standardized format;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions detailing the current law surrounding the carrying of firearms;<hr><ltbullet>for clarity, places certain contents of Title 76, Chapter 10, Part 5, Weapons, into Title 53, Public Safety Code;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies criminal provisions regarding who is required to have a concealed carry permit in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>includes coordination clauses coordinating technical changes between this bill and H.B. 183, Noncitizen Restricted Person Amendments, H.B. 227, Restricted Person Amendments, H.B. 21, Criminal Code Recodification and Cross References, and S.B. 14, Private Sale of a Firearm Sunset Review Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Adoption Records Access Amendments
description: This bill addresses access to adoption records.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allows an individual who is adopted as a minor child to access records associated with the individual's adoption if the individual is 18 years old or older;<hr><ltbullet>amends the jurisdiction of the juvenile court;<hr><ltbullet>allows a pre-existing parent to petition a court to keep the records associated with an individual's adoption sealed;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to address substantive and technical conflicts if this bill and S.B. 119, Domestic Relations Recodification, both pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Dangerous Weapons Amendments
description: This bill addresses statutes throughout the Utah Code dealing with dangerous weapons.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>restructures and makes technical changes to sections in the Utah Code dealing with dangerous weapons to bring the sections into a standardized format as part of a larger effort to recodify the criminal code;<hr><ltbullet>makes amendments to existing statutes dealing with firearms;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that an individual who may otherwise lawfully possess a firearm may:<hr><ltbullet1>possess a firearm at the individual's residence;<hr><ltbullet1>openly possess a firearm in most public locations; and<hr><ltbullet1>conceal a firearm in most public locations without a concealed carry permit;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies criminal provisions regarding who is required to have a concealed carry permit in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>removes the criminal provision for law-abiding citizens to possess a loaded rifle, shotgun, or muzzle-loading rifle in a vehicle;<hr><ltbullet>removes the crime of carrying a loaded firearm on a public street;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause coordinating technical changes with this bill and S.B. 14, Private Sale of a Firearm Sunset Review Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a purchaser to sign an affidavit of intent to occupy when buying a single-family home within the first 30 days the single-family home is on the market, unless the seller incurs an exigent circumstance;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a purchaser record an affidavit of intent to occupy with a county recorder; and <hr><ltbullet>prohibits the bulk sale of foreclosed single-family homes.

title: Hunting Amendments
description: This bill addresses the taking of wildlife through the use of a guide, outfitter, or spotter.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Guide, Outfitter, and Spotter Fund;<hr><ltbullet>provides when the use of a guide, outfitter, or spotter is unlawful; <hr><ltbullet>requires registration with the Division of Wildlife Resources (division);<hr><ltbullet>provides for rulemaking;<hr><ltbullet>permits the division to take action related to an applicant or registrant;<hr><ltbullet>outlines prohibited activities and penalties for violations;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the operations of a guide, outfitter, or spotter;<hr><ltbullet>repeals regulation by the Division of Professional Licensing; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: State Sovereignty Amendments
description: This bill addresses state sovereignty.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>declares that an international organization does not have any power, jurisdiction, or legal authority in this state;<hr><ltbullet>provides that, if an international organization issues a rule, resolution, tax, policy, or mandate that purports to have the force and effect of law, then the state, or a political subdivision of the state, may not implement or enforce the rule, resolution, tax, policy, or mandate;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the governor or the chief executive officer of a political subdivision from declaring a state of emergency exclusively in response to an international organization's proclamation declaring a state of emergency; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Adult Probation and Parole Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to the Division of Adult Probation and Parole within the Department of Corrections.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes the Division of Adult Probation and Parole in the code;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions throughout the code regarding the responsibility of the Department of Corrections to supervise individuals on probation or parole; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Vehicle Accident Liability Amendments
description: This bill clarifies that a vehicle operator intending to turn left is not required to yield the right-of-way to a vehicle operator approaching from the opposite direction that fails to stop when required by a stop sign or steady red signal.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that a vehicle operator intending to turn left is not required to yield the right-of-way to a vehicle operator approaching from the opposite direction that fails to stop when required by a stop sign or steady red signal at the intersection; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Process for Submitting Nonbinding Opinion Question
description: This bill modifies the Election Code to establish a procedure for the Legislature to submit a nonbinding opinion question to the voters of Utah.

title: Offender Reintegration Amendments
description: This bill concerns the reentry and reintegration of offenders and former offenders into the general public.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that a local mental health authority shall, to the extent feasible, coordinate with the Department of Corrections (department) to ensure the continuity of mental health services for county residents on probation or parole;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a criminal justice coordinating council shall identify strategies for connecting county residents on probation, parole, or leaving jail or prison, with certain county-based services; <hr><ltbullet>adds an expunged conviction and an arrest that occurred as a juvenile to the circumstances when a public employer may not exclude an applicant from an initial interview;<hr><ltbullet>reduces the amount of time following an individual's incarceration for purposes of defining unprofessional conduct in certain circumstances and expands the exceptions under which a conviction would not qualify;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the department may procure or adopt technology to coordinate services with outside organizations involved in supporting individuals on probation or parole;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Rehabilitation and Reentry Services Special Revenue Fund, which:<hr><ltbullet1> allows the department to accept donations and other funds; and<hr><ltbullet1>restricts funds for specified purposes relating to the successful reintegration of offenders and former offenders into the general public; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Initiatives and Referenda Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions relating to statewide initiatives and statewide referenda.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel to draft an impartial petition summary of:<hr><ltbullet1>a law proposed by a statewide initiative; or<hr><ltbullet1>a law that a statewide referendum seeks to overturn;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements and procedures for drafting and for challenging a petition summary;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the petition summary is included with the signature packets for a statewide initiative or a statewide referendum and provides that a petition signer may read the petition summary rather than the entire text of the law that is the subject of the petition;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an individual who signs an initiative packet or a referendum packet must read the entire statement included with the packet;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the attestation relating to reading a statement provided with an initiative packet or a referendum packet or reading the law to which the initiative or referendum relates, does not require an attestation that the individual understands the statement or law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Victim Privacy Changes
description: This bill addresses the privacy of a victim in a criminal investigation or action.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>addresses access by a defendant and a defendant's attorney to nonpublic electronic data related to a victim; and<hr><ltbullet>provides a victim in a criminal proceeding with a right to privacy in any nonpublic electronic data related to the victim that is collected during the course of the criminal investigation or action.

description: This bill addresses emissions from railroad locomotives.

description: This bill modifies the payment of wages provisions.

title: Dry Needling Amendments
description: This bill provides requirements for dry needling by a physical therapist or an occupational therapist.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>moves the registration requirement for a physical therapist using dry needling from an exception to unlawful and unprofessional conduct to a requirement for licensing;<hr><ltbullet>expands the definition of both physical therapy and occupational therapy to include dry needling; <hr><ltbullet>clarifies that no referral is needed for physical therapy or occupational therapy;<hr><ltbullet>creates a registration requirement for an occupational therapist to engage in dry needling; <hr><ltbullet>allows occupational therapists to assist with mental wellness; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Public Education Course Grade Requirements
description: This bill prohibits a local education agency (LEA) from requiring student attendance at an off-campus event.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an LEA from requiring a student to attend an off-campus event as a condition for grades or academic credit;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits adverse effects on a student's grades or academic standing due to non-attendance at an off-campus event; and<hr><ltbullet>requires an LEA to provide optional transportation, a fee waiver, and alternative options for students to meet academic requirements.

description: This bill defines terms and prohibits certain maneuvers related to the operation of a motorcycle.

title: Ballot Signature Amendments
description: This bill amends the signature-gathering process for an individual seeking the nomination of a political party.

title: Criminal Conduct Amendments
description: This bill amends the crime of enticing a minor and provisions related to the Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends the crime of enticing a minor;<hr><ltbullet>adds factors that a sentencing court must consider in making a determination regarding whether an individual under 21 years old used force or coercion when committing a registrable offense for purposes of determining registration length on the Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies which prosecuting agency is required to receive a petition from an offender petitioning to be removed from the Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry and the responsibilities of that agency in notifying the victim regarding the petition; <hr><ltbullet>requires an offender on the Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry who is required to register on the registry because of an offense committed in another jurisdiction to be removed from the other jurisdiction's registry in order to be removed from the Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry;<hr><ltbullet>contains a coordination clause to coordinate technical changes between this bill and S.B. 41, Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Highway Expansion Impacts on Signage Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to the relocation of a billboard due to road construction or other highway changes.

title: Substance Use Treatment and Enforcement Amendments
description: This bill addresses treatment and enforcement issues related to substance use.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a local substance abuse authority to include in the authority's annual plan a list of available substance use service providers, in a form and format usable by first responders; <hr><ltbullet>requires a local mental health authority to include in the authority's annual plan a list of available mental health service providers, in a form and format usable by first responders;<hr><ltbullet>allows and encourages first responders to offer a referral to substance use or mental health services to an individual who experiences an intentional or accidental overdose;<hr><ltbullet>addresses requirements for syringe exchange programs and information collected relating to syringe exchange programs;<hr><ltbullet>allows an opioid treatment program to operate a mobile unit to provide medication to treat substance use withdrawal symptoms or an opioid use disorder, and provides certain requirements for operation of a mobile unit;<hr><ltbullet>grants rulemaking authority to the Department of Health and Human Services regarding the requirements for operating a mobile unit to provide medication to treat substance use withdrawal symptoms or an opioid use disorder; <hr><ltbullet>amends criminal provisions of the Utah Controlled Substances Act;<hr><ltbullet>creates the crime of maintenance of a drug-involved premises;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding civil nuisance actions, including provisions that relate to a nuisance caused by unlawful actions related to a controlled substance;<hr><ltbullet>repeals intent language;<hr><ltbullet>adds a coordination clause between this bill and H.B. 355, Critical Infrastructure Materials Amendments, to provide that changes made to Section 76B-6-1101 in H.B. 355 are incorporated into changes this bill makes to that section; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Cannabis Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to medical cannabis.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>allows for additional medical cannabis pharmacies;<hr><ltbullet>creates a new medical cannabis pharmacy license for independent medical cannabis pharmacies;<hr><ltbullet>creates ownership restrictions for independent medical cannabis pharmacies;<hr><ltbullet>adjusts fees for certain medical cannabis pharmacy licenses;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding cannabis production and sanitation;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to enforcement and appeals;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to closed-door medical cannabis pharmacies;<hr><ltbullet>allows a cannabis processing facility to have a website that includes product information;<hr><ltbullet>limits the number of licenses that the Department of Agriculture and Food (department) may issue for cannabis processing facilities;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding when the department may seize products and test products;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to information a medical cannabis pharmacy must have available to a patient purchasing medical cannabis;<hr><ltbullet>creates a reporting requirement for the department;<hr><ltbullet>repeals sections related to the state central patient portal;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the creation of patient product information inserts;<hr><ltbullet>moves the repeal date for the Cannabis Research Review Board earlier one year;<hr><ltbullet>extends the repeal date for the Medical Cannabis Governance Structure Working Group; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill modifies provisions related to mailed ballots and ballot drop boxes.

title: Sexual Offense Revisions
description: This bill changes certain sexual offenses and sentencing for sexual offenses.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends sentencing provisions concerning repeat and habitual sex offenders, including requiring mandatory imprisonment;<hr><ltbullet>provides a definition of a female breast for purposes of certain sexual and sexual exploitation offenses that includes a breast that is undeveloped or partially developed;<hr><ltbullet>expands the definition of "child sexual abuse material" to include a minor observing or being used for sexually explicit conduct;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the definition of "sexual explicit conduct" concerning certain bodily functions;<hr><ltbullet>changes the mental state necessary to commit the offense of sexual exploitation of a minor;<hr><ltbullet>expands the offense of sexual exploitation of a minor to include when an actor accesses child sexual abuse material with the intent to view;<hr><ltbullet>provides a safe harbor provision for certain employees and independent contractors who are required to access or view child sexual abuse material within the scope of employment;<hr><ltbullet>changes the mental state necessary to commit the offense of aggravated sexual exploitation of a minor;<hr><ltbullet>amends the offense of aggravated sexual exploitation of a minor to remove a lesser penalty for circumstances when the child sexual abuse material depicts an individual who is 14 years old or older and pubescent; <hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to merge the changes to Section 76-3-406 if both this bill and H.B. 78, Criminal Offenses Amendments, both pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Homeschool Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to home school affidavits.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>clarifies when a letter of intent to homeschool is required from parents;<hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement for parents to submit an affidavit for students who begin homeschooling at the start of an academic year;<hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement for parents to attest to criminal background history;<hr><ltbullet>establishes procedures for local school boards to process letters of intent;<hr><ltbullet>removes liability from local school boards after student unenrollment; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Voting Revisions
description: This bill amends provisions relating to elections and voting.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that, beginning in 2026:<hr><ltbullet1>elections will be conducted both in person and by mail, rather than primarily by mail; and<hr><ltbullet1>a ballot will only be mailed to a voter who requests mailing or who is covered by the Uniform Military and Overseas Voters Act;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a voter may request to receive a ballot by mail in 2026 and beyond by making the request to a poll worker at the time the voter votes in person, making the request in a voter registration form, or making the request by submitting a separate form;<hr><ltbullet>modifies voter registration forms, and temporarily modifies a ballot return envelope, to permit a voter to request a mailed ballot in future elections using those documents;<hr><ltbullet>provides that, beginning in 2026, a ballot will not be mailed to a voter if the voter:<hr><ltbullet1>requests that a ballot not be mailed;<hr><ltbullet1>does not indicate a desire to receive a ballot when asked in person or via a form; or<hr><ltbullet1>fails to vote in a regular general election;<hr><ltbullet>subject to certain exceptions relating to military and overseas voters, provides that, for a ballot to be valid, the ballot must be received before the close of polls on the day of the election;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for notifying active voters of the requirement to request a mailed ballot for future elections;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a request to receive a mailed ballot must be remade if a voter fails to vote in a regular general election; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Office of Legislative Auditor General Provisions
description: This bill amends provisions governing the duties and powers of the legislative auditor general.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>restates the legislative auditor general's constitutional authority;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions governing information that maybe subject to federal law and is requested by the legislative auditor general from an entity, including the State Tax Commission;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the legislative auditor general to provide certain information to an audited entity;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions governing criminal interference with a legislative audit;<hr><ltbullet>amends the definition of "chief officer" for purposes of an entity responding to a legislative audit;<hr><ltbullet>permits the legislative auditor general to identify an individual other than a chief officer to respond to a legislative audit; <hr><ltbullet>amends provisions governing an audit response plan and an update to a plan;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the legislative auditor general to review and monitor the Utah System of Higher Education; and<hr><ltbullet>makes other technical and conforming changes.

title: Income Tax Revenue Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions relating to state income tax revenue.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Tax Commission, the Office of the Legislative Fiscal Analyst, and the Governor's Office of Planning and Budget to annually determine by consensus whether federal tax law changes will likely result in a material increase in state income tax revenue;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Tax Commission to submit a report to the Revenue and Taxation Interim Committee if a determination is made by consensus that federal tax law changes will likely result in a material increase in state income tax revenue;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Revenue and Taxation Interim Committee, upon receiving a report, to recommend legislative action for the next general session to negate the material increase in state income tax revenue;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Tax Commission to submit a report to the Division of Finance following the general session if a determination is made by consensus that a material increase in state income tax revenue is still expected;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Income Tax Surplus Restricted Account (account);<hr><ltbullet>specifies purposes for which revenue deposited into the account may be used; and<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Finance, upon receiving a report, to deposit the estimated amount of the material increase in state income tax revenue into the account.

title: Homeowners' Association Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to homeowners' associations.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the Office of the Homeowners' Association Ombudsman;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the duties, jurisdiction, and functions of the Office of the Homeowners' Association Ombudsman;<hr><ltbullet>requires that Office of the Homeowners' Association Ombudsman issue an advisory opinion under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which an advisory opinion of the Office of the Homeowners' Association Ombudsman is admissible in a subsequent proceeding;<hr><ltbullet>makes void and unenforceable a homeowners' association transfer fee under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements that a homeowners' association shall meet before imposing a fee or charge;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for a homeowners' association to impose a reinvestment fee;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a homeowners' association notify an owner in writing of a denied unit or lot plan;<hr><ltbullet>restricts a homeowners' association from making certain rules;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Department of Commerce to set and impose an annual registration fee on a homeowners' association;<hr><ltbullet>requires a homeowners' association to renew the homeowners' association's registration with the Department of Commerce annually;<hr><ltbullet>sets limits on the amount a homeowners' association may charge as a late fee;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a homeowners' association provide, upon request, certain documents;<hr><ltbullet>increases the monetary amount a homeowners' association may charge an owner when producing certain documents;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a declarant from selling a part of a common area during the period of administrative control under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>provides new requirements to amend a homeowners' association's governing documents;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a declarant from using association funds in a legal action brought by a homeowner against the declarant before the end of the period of administrative control;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a homeowners' association from restricting, denying, or delaying a plan due to the plan's inclusion of a fire-resistant material in an area with a heightened risk of wildfire;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a homeowners' association from charging any costs associated with the electronic transmission of certain documents;<hr><ltbullet>increases the monetary amount an owner may request from a homeowners' association if the homeowners' association fails to make documents available to the owner under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>amends the conditions for the termination of a period of administrative control for an association of lot owners;<hr><ltbullet>provides requirements for a declarant of an association of lot owners during the period of administrative control; and<hr><ltbullet>provides a repeal date for the Office of the Homeowners' Association Ombudsman and requires legislative review before the repeal.

title: Inmate Reentry, Finances, and Debt Modifications
description: This bill concerns inmate and former inmate reentry, finances, and debts.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires, with a delayed implementation date, a county jail to notify certain state agencies that may have information concerning an inmate's existing debts when an inmate is incarcerated in the county jail for more than 90 days and when the inmate is released from the county jail;<hr><ltbullet>requires, with a delayed implementation date, the Office of State Debt Collection to suspend the accrual of interest on certain accounts receivable during periods of at least 90 days of incarceration and for an additional period after release;<hr><ltbullet>expands the duties of the reentry division created by the Department of Corrections (department); <hr><ltbullet>requires the department to provide information to an inmate on a regular basis concerning:<hr><ltbullet1> the inmate's known debts;<hr><ltbullet1>incentives for paying certain debts while incarcerated; and<hr><ltbullet1>information on how to access additional information concerning debts and resources on financial literacy and money management;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department:<hr><ltbullet1>with a delayed implementation date, to notify certain state agencies that may have information concerning an inmate's existing debts when an inmate enters and leaves incarceration; and<hr><ltbullet1>to provide educational resources to individuals designated by an inmate concerning incentives for repaying certain debts while incarcerated; <hr><ltbullet>amends provisions concerning when incarceration may not be considered by the Office of Recovery Services (office) as voluntary unemployment for purposes of a child support order;<hr><ltbullet>requires the office to suspend child support orders and money judgments in certain circumstances relating to incarceration;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the office shall resume a suspended child support obligation after the offender has been released for 90 days; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Criminal Amendments
description: This bill addresses criminal offenses and repercussions from those offenses
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires a county sheriff to notify and coordinate with the relevant federal immigration authority when preparing to release from the county jail an individual who:<hr><ltbullet1>is being released after serving the individual's jail sentence for certain class A misdemeanors or a felony; and <hr><ltbullet1>is unlawfully present in the United States;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Corrections to notify and coordinate with the relevant federal immigration authority when preparing to release an inmate who:<hr><ltbullet1>is being released after serving a term of imprisonment for a felony; and<hr><ltbullet1>is unlawfully present in the United States;<hr><ltbullet>amends the sentence of imprisonment for a class A misdemeanor to one year for certain offenses;<hr><ltbullet>amends certain pretrial release provisions to add a rebuttable presumption that an individual is a flight risk if the individual is not lawfully present in the United States; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Restricted Person Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to those who are restricted persons regarding dangerous weapons.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>makes a person a restricted person if the person has been found not guilty by reason of insanity for any criminal offense not just a felony level offense;<hr><ltbullet> makes a person a restricted person if the person has been found mentally incompetent to stand trial for any criminal offense not just a felony level offense; and<hr><ltbullet>contains a coordination clause to coordinate technical changes between this bill and H.B. 133, Dangerous Weapon Amendments.

title: Primary Election Amendments
description: This bill addresses primary elections.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that, for certain primary election races, the person who wins the nomination will be determined by conducting a runoff election between the two candidates who received the most votes in the initial primary election if: <hr><ltbullet1>no candidate receives more than 50% of the votes in the race; and<hr><ltbullet1>the candidate who receives the highest number of votes does not receive at least 10% more of the total votes cast in the race than the candidate who receives the second highest number of votes;<hr><ltbullet>describes deadlines, notice requirements, and procedures relating to a runoff election, including party affiliation deadlines and procedures for a military or overseas voter to cast a ballot in a runoff election; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.
