title: Candidate Nomination Procedures Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to nominating candidates for elective office and placing candidates on a ballot.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>repeals provisions relating to a qualified political party;<hr><ltbullet>establishes two types of registered political parties:<hr><ltbullet1>a primary nominating party that nominates candidates through signature-gathering only, participates in the regular primary election, and has the name of the primary nominating party listed on the regular general election ballot in association with the party's candidates; and<hr><ltbullet1>a convention nominating party that nominates candidates using a method that does not involve the signature-gathering process described in the preceding paragraph or participation in the regular primary election, and whose candidates are listed on the regular general election ballot without an indication of the convention nominating party that nominated the candidates;<hr><ltbullet>requires a registered political party to choose whether to be a primary nominating party or a convention nominating party;<hr><ltbullet>modifies signature gathering thresholds; and<hr><ltbullet>  makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Rollback Tax Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to property taxes and fees imposed when land is no longer used for agricultural purposes.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the county to use 100% of the rollback tax or fee-in-lieu revenue collected within the county when land is no longer used for agricultural purposes for open land and agricultural use;<hr><ltbullet>directs the unused rollback tax or fee-in-lieu revenue from the county where the land is located to the LeRay McAllister Working Farm and Ranch Fund after five years;<hr><ltbullet>updates the sources of revenue to the LeRay McAllister Working Farm and Ranch Fund to include the rollback tax and fee-in-lieu revenue; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Disaster Funds Revisions
description: This bill concerns disaster funds.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to the State Disaster Recovery Restricted Account to change the amounts that may be expended by the Division of Emergency Management under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>renames the Response, Recovery, and Post-disaster Mitigation Restricted Account as the Disaster Response, Recovery, and Mitigation Restricted Account (account);<hr><ltbullet>modifies the amounts of funds available from the account for disaster response and recovery under specified circumstances; <hr><ltbullet>modifies the available uses for funds in the account to include pre-disaster mitigation under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>modifies standards relating to disaster response and recovery grants;<hr><ltbullet>grants rulemaking authority to the Division of Emergency Management regarding the use of funds from the account for pre-disaster mitigation purposes;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Finance to transfer certain funds from the State Disaster Recovery Restricted Account into the account under certain conditions; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Urban Farming Assessment Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to property tax assessment under the Urban Farming Assessment Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allows for land to qualify for urban farming assessment based on gross sales in addition to qualifying based on agricultural production;<hr><ltbullet>provides for land to continue to qualify for urban farming assessment based on gross sales upon failing to meet certain timing requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires an applicant for urban farming assessment to submit documentation to the county assessor demonstrating the land meets the agricultural production or gross sales requirements;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that a portion of land may qualify for urban farming assessment even if other portions of the land do not qualify;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the requirement for an owner of land approved for urban farming assessment to submit an annual renewal application;<hr><ltbullet>establishes circumstances under which a county assessor may request additional information from an owner of land approved for urban farming assessment; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Presidential Electors Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to the distribution of electoral votes.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>in an election for president and vice president of the United States:<hr><ltbullet1>allocates one electoral vote for the presidential and vice presidential candidates that receive the highest number of votes in a Congressional district;<hr><ltbullet1>allocates two electoral votes for the presidential and vice presidential candidates that receive the highest number of statewide votes; and<hr><ltbullet1>requires a registered political party, an unaffiliated candidate, or a write-in candidate to notify the lieutenant governor if there is a vacancy in the office of presidential elector; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill creates the Nuclear Energy Consortium and the Utah Energy Council, establishes a process for designating energy development zones, and creates the Energy Development Investment Fund.

title: Public Employee Gender-specific Language Requirements
description: This bill prohibits certain employment action against a public employee in relation to gender-specific language.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet> prohibits the State Board of Education, a local education agency, or a public employer from taking disciplinary action against an employee for using gender-specific language in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>requires a public employer that has a rule or policy requiring an employee to use gender-specific language to accommodate another individual to exempt the employee from disciplinary action in certain circumstances; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Agriculture and Food Amendments
description: This bill addresses issues related to the regulation, oversight, or encouragement of agriculture and food.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies the definition of "qualified veterinarian";<hr><ltbullet>changes references to the National Council on Weights and Measures;<hr><ltbullet>changes the Utah Fertilizer Act to the Utah Plant Food Act, including modifying definitions and making conforming references;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the Utah Agriculture Certificate of Environmental Stewardship Program;<hr><ltbullet>changes the time frames for annual fees under the Agricultural and Wildlife Damage Prevention Act;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the expiration of livestock brands;<hr><ltbullet>modifies information to be provided to operate a livestock market;<hr><ltbullet>amends the Domesticated Elk Act to address licensing, record retention, health information, and marking of domesticated elk;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that money in the LeRay McAllister Working Farm and Ranch Fund Program is nonlapsing;<hr><ltbullet>changes the Agriculture Conservation Easement Account to an expendable special revenue fund;<hr><ltbullet>addresses use of money in the Agriculture Resource Development Fund to pay administrative costs;<hr><ltbullet>addresses regulation of livestock by political subdivisions;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the earmarking of sales and use taxes related to the Division of Conservation within the Department of Agriculture and Food;<hr><ltbullet>addresses grants under the agricultural water optimization program; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Waste Classification Amendments
description: This bill relates to nuclear waste classification.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies the definition of high-level nuclear waste and low-level radioactive waste; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Local Land Use Modifications
description: This bill modifies provisions related to minor subdivisions of agricultural land in a county of the third, fourth, fifth, or sixth class.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes an owner of at least 50 contiguous acres of agricultural land in a county of the third, fourth, fifth, or sixth class to create a new parcel that, after the division, is separate from the remainder of the original 50 contiguous acres of agricultural land; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Municipal and County Zoning Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to the authority of municipalities and counties regarding short-term rentals.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that a municipality or county that regulates short-term rentals may use a listing or offering on a short-term rental website as evidence that a short-term rental took place so long as the municipality or county has additional information to support its position that an owner or lessee violated a municipality or county ordinance;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a municipality or county may require the owner of a short-term rental to obtain a business license or other permit from the municipality or county to operate a short-term rental in the municipality or in an unincorporated area of the county;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a municipality or county may request a short-term rental website remove a listing or offering that violates business licensing requirements or zoning requirements;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a municipality or county that imposes transient room tax on short-term rentals may provide a listing or offering on a short-term rental website to the county auditor as evidence that a short-term rental owner or lessee may be subject to the transient room tax; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: First Credential Program
description: This bill replaces the PRIME program to create the First Credential program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires designated pathway development positions to perform certain duties; <hr><ltbullet>repeals the PRIME program;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a first credential program;<hr><ltbullet>requires development of a master plan for scaling credentialing programs;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a master credential list of approved industry-recognized credentials;<hr><ltbullet>ensures credits are transferable to higher education institutions and technical colleges;<hr><ltbullet>provides a scholarship for students who complete the first credential program;<hr><ltbullet>requires annual review and updates based on labor market needs;<hr><ltbullet>provides a grant for implementation and incentives for outcomes;<hr><ltbullet>mandates partnerships between schools, employers, and apprenticeship programs;<hr><ltbullet>promotes stackable credentials that lead to career advancement;<hr><ltbullet>coordinates language with other legislation contingent upon passage;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Towing Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions related to the towing and impoundment of vehicles.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to impounded or towed vehicles to allow a state impound yard or tow yard to release a vehicle to certain individuals beside the owner if certain requirements are met;<hr><ltbullet>requires a private property owner who contracts with a tower to patrol a parking lot to publish information about the agreement with the tower for the public to view;<hr><ltbullet>allows signage for towing and parking restrictions to remain valid if the signage substantially conforms with the statutory standards;<hr><ltbullet>requires a tow truck motor carrier or impound yard to allow an individual to remove personal items from a vehicle if the individual has paid the towing fee;<hr><ltbullet>requires a tow truck motor carrier to provide to the Department of Transportation information about each towing dispatch rotation that includes the tow truck motor carrier;<hr><ltbullet>allows the Department of Transportation to require the removal from a towing dispatch rotation a tow truck motor carrier that has violated relevant towing laws and regulations;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a local government from imposing a maximum rate that deviates from the towing rates established by the Department of Transportation in administrative rule; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: HOA Board Education Amendments
description: This bill establishes education requirements for members of a homeowners' association board.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a homeowners' association board member complete education requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a homeowners' association board member or secretary maintain a record of completing the education requirements for at least four years;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a homeowners' association board member report completion of the education requirements to the homeowners' association;<hr><ltbullet>provides a remedy for an owner for when a homeowners' association board member fails to meet the education requirements;<hr><ltbullet>describes how a homeowners' association board member may remedy noncompliance with education requirements;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a board of a homeowners' association to remove a board member who fails to remedy noncompliance;<hr><ltbullet>creates a standard for a person that offers education requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the Department of Commerce maintain a list of persons authorized to offer education requirements; and<hr><ltbullet>provides that the requirements enacted by this bill do not take effect until after the period of administrative control.

title: Election Record Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to records created or used during an election.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>makes the recorded video of ballot processing a public record for purposes of the Government Records Access and Management Act (GRAMA);<hr><ltbullet>specifies that an election officer shall retain and preserve ballot chain of custody documentation created during an election;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that an election officer shall package and retain the election database, cast vote record, and other materials used in the programming of automatic tabulating equipment;<hr><ltbullet>for an election administered by a county clerk:<hr><ltbullet1>directs the county clerk to make, preserve, and retain for at least 12 years an electronic copy of certain election material;<hr><ltbullet1>authorizes, in certain circumstances, the county clerk or county legislative body to examine the electronic copy of election material to conduct research related to an election;<hr><ltbullet1>requires the county clerk to grant certain governmental entities access to the electronic copy of election material to conduct research related to an election; and<hr><ltbullet1>creates a process for a governmental entity to conduct a multi-county review of the electronic copy of election material;<hr><ltbullet>specifies that an electronic copy of election material is not a record for purposes of GRAMA;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that an election officer's obligation to seal official ballots and election returns does not prohibit a county clerk, an auditor, or the lieutenant governor from accessing the electronic copy of election material;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that an election officer shall retain and preserve the election database, cast vote record, and other materials for 22 months after an election;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions relating to information an election officer is required to report in a ballot reconciliation report and board of canvassers report;<hr><ltbullet>reduces the amount of time that an election officer has to publicize the certified board of canvassers report from seven to three days;<hr><ltbullet>requires an election officer to make a copy of the certified board of canvassers report available to members of the public in portable document format; <hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to reflect the changes made to certain voter registration provisions in H.B. 270, Voter Registration Records Amendments, if this bill and H.B. 270 both pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Higher Education Strategic Reinvestment
description: This bill enacts and amends provisions regarding the strategic approach of and investment in certain programs in the higher education system.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires certain reporting to and a study by the Higher Education Appropriations Subcommittee;<hr><ltbullet>provides for disbursement of certain reinvestment funds that are dedicated to a given degree-granting institution for reallocation to certain strategic investments under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>requires each degree-granting institution to create a strategic reinvestment plan to reallocate funding from certain programs and divisions of the institution to certain programs and divisions that merit additional investment;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Utah Board of Higher Education (board) to report to the Higher Education Appropriations Subcommittee and the Executive Appropriations Subcommittee regarding each institution's strategic reinvestment plan and execution of the plan over the upcoming three fiscal years;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes declining use of reinvestment funds to phase out reduced or eliminated programs or divisions of institutions over the upcoming three fiscal years;<hr><ltbullet>limits the number of credit hours a degree-granting institution may require between general education and degree-specific requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires the board to develop a process to grant conditional approval of accelerated three-year degrees;<hr><ltbullet>allows the board to transfer certain appropriations as an exception to the prohibition on line-item transfers in the Budgetary Procedures Act;<hr><ltbullet>coordinates with H.B. 51, Higher Education Reporting Amendments, to address subcommittee reports; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Public Sector Labor Union Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions governing public employee, public safety, and public fire labor organizations.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a labor organization for which a public employer collects union dues to provide an annual accounting to the labor organization members and to the Labor Commission;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a public employer from recognizing a labor organization as a bargaining agent for public employees;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a public employer from entering into collective bargaining contracts;<hr><ltbullet> prohibits using public money or public property to assist, promote, or deter union organizing or administration;<hr><ltbullet>excludes new labor organization employees from participating in Utah Retirement Systems;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the state risk manager to acquire and administer professional liability insurance for:<hr><ltbullet1> disputes between a K-12 personnel and a public employer; and<hr><ltbullet1>other public employees if there is a sufficient demand; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Privacy Protections in Sex-designated Areas
description: This bill modifies provisions regarding sex-designated privacy spaces in education and government facilities.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Utah Board of Higher Education to provide guidance regarding student housing that degree-granting institutions own or control;<hr><ltbullet>provides a definitional change for nonprofit exceptions to and broadens the scope of a nonprofit educational institution exception to the Utah Fair Housing Act;<hr><ltbullet>narrows an exception for a prohibition on sex-based distinctions to apply only to a determination of the School Activity Eligibility Commission and a student's participation in a certain gender-designated interscholastic activity;<hr><ltbullet>removes an ambiguous medical treatment documentation provision from certain lists of evidence supporting an individual's access to certain sex-designated privacy spaces;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding government entity facility compliance to specify which government entity bears certain duties;<hr><ltbullet>requires degree-granting institutions to comply with sex designations in assigning students to dwelling units within the institution's sex-designated student housing; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Voter Registration Records Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to voter registration records.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>modifies and recodifies provisions relating to:<hr><ltbullet1>the information in a voter registration record that is available to a person based on the capacity in which the person requests the information; and<hr><ltbullet1>the requirements to obtain additional privacy protection for a voter registration record;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a voter's voter registration record that, before January 1, 2027, was classified as private without requiring a reason for the classification will be reclassified as a public voter registration record, unless the voter takes certain action to obtain additional protection for the voter's voter registration record;<hr><ltbullet>requires an election officer to notify a voter whose voter registration is subject to reclassification as described in the preceding paragraph in order to give the voter an opportunity to apply for additional protection for the voter's voter registration record;<hr><ltbullet>requires the assignment of new voter identification numbers;    <hr><ltbullet>modifies the voter registration form to reflect the changes made in this bill and to give a voter the option of opting into receiving electronic communications from a political party with which the voter affiliates;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a voter registration subscription service for a state political party and provides the ability for a state political party to verify membership in the party;<hr><ltbullet>provides for release to a political party of information relating to the number of at-risk voters in the state and in individual state House of Representatives districts;<hr><ltbullet>establishes additional requirements to ensure the removal of deceased individuals from voter registration records;<hr><ltbullet>modifies penalties that may be imposed in relation to the unlawful disclosure of a voter registration record;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes;<hr><ltbullet>coordinates this bill with S.B. 191, Protective Orders Amendments, to, by reference, adopt a definition added in S.B. 191; and<hr><ltbullet>coordinates this bill with H.B. 69, Government Records and Information Amendments, to technically merge language in both bills.

title: Water Amendments
description: This bill addresses regulations related to water.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides circumstances of when a municipality may set different water rates based in part on water conservation;<hr><ltbullet>addresses special district fees;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>addresses rate setting by a retail water supplier and public water systems;<hr><ltbullet>provides for how revenues from retail rates may be spent;<hr><ltbullet>creates a presumption regarding the reasonableness of certain water rates that include water conservation as an element in determining the rate; <hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to the Board of Water Resources;<hr><ltbullet>addresses tiered rates for secondary water; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Commitment Revisions
description: This bill addresses the commitment of individuals in relation to civil, criminal, and juvenile proceedings.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends the definitions of "intellectual disability" and "intermediate care facility for people with an intellectual disability" as used in the Utah Code;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to the rights and privileges to which an individual is entitled when under commitment to the custody or to the treatment services of a local mental health authority;<hr><ltbullet>provides that if a right of a patient of a local mental health authority is limited or denied, including for the welfare of the patient or caretakers, the nature, extent, and reason for that limitation or denial shall be entered in the patient's treatment record;<hr><ltbullet>requires a designated examiner to conduct an examination of a proposed patient by telehealth except in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>requires a court to hold a hearing on an application for involuntary commitment remotely unless the court finds good cause not to hold the hearing remotely;<hr><ltbullet>amends standards and processes related to the involuntary civil commitment of an individual with an intellectual disability or related condition;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a court may only order the Department of Health and Human Services (department) to provide an initial evaluation and progress toward competency evaluation for a defendant or minor if the defendant or minor is located within the state;<hr><ltbullet>requires a court to dismiss a petition for involuntary civil commitment if both designated examiners determine that the proposed patient does not meet the criteria for involuntary commitment;<hr><ltbullet>provides that when there is a conflict in the opinions of forensic evaluators, if a party seeks an additional competency evaluation then the party is responsible for selecting the evaluator and paying the cost of the evaluator;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding the release of a defendant determined to be incompetent to proceed from a secured setting;<hr><ltbullet>addresses when the department is required to provide an updated juvenile competency evaluation after an extended attainment period; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Massage Therapy Amendments
description: This bill modifies licensing requirements for performing massage therapy, including creating a registration requirement for massage therapy establishments.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends the licensure requirements for massage therapy;<hr><ltbullet>specifies requirements for a criminal background check for an individual performing massage therapy;<hr><ltbullet>specifies requirements for a massage establishment to register;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which an individual must perform massage therapy in a registered massage establishment;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the expiration and renewal of licensure;<hr><ltbullet>specifies identification, signage, and disclosure requirements;<hr><ltbullet>creates standards for unlawful and unprofessional conduct by a massage establishment;<hr><ltbullet>requires penalties for a massage establishment that engages in unlawful or unprofessional conduct;<hr><ltbullet>specifies when a massage establishment can be denied registration;<hr><ltbullet>specifies requirements for a criminal background check for massage establishment owners;<hr><ltbullet>creates a safe harbor provision for a licensed individual renting or leasing to a sole practitioner;<hr><ltbullet>allows the Division of Professional Licensing to inspect a massage establishment;<hr><ltbullet>requires standards for the inspection of a registered massage establishment;<hr><ltbullet>provides exemptions from licensure requirements;<hr><ltbullet>schedules the repeal of provisions related to a massage assistant and massage assistant-in-training; <hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to coordinate enactment of provisions with S.B. 44, Professional Licensure Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Health Curriculum and Procedures Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions regarding health instruction and physical and mental health procedures in the public education system.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; <hr><ltbullet>requires any health care provider to obtain informed parental consent before providing or facilitating telehealth or another health care service to a student within a public school;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for certain restricted services, including:<hr><ltbullet1>identifying who may and may not provide a restricted service; and<hr><ltbullet1>requiring informed parental consent and certain parental notification;<hr><ltbullet>ensures that a local or state rule or policy does not create an exemption for otherwise prohibited endorsement, promotion, or disparagement of a certain religious belief or viewpoint;<hr><ltbullet>modifies required health instruction, including:<hr><ltbullet1>establishing statutory purposes for the curriculum the state board establishes;<hr><ltbullet1>adding situational awareness and the "success sequence";<hr><ltbullet1>reorganizing duties and prohibitions regarding instruction, discussion, and advocacy of certain concepts;<hr><ltbullet>amends the effect of prior informed written parental consent and the allowable subjects in sex education instruction; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Child and Family Services Amendments
description: This bill addresses child and family services, such as child placement, custody, and records.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>addresses bedroom sharing by foster children;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the Division of Child and Family Services (division) from:<hr><ltbullet1>withholding certain information from a child's parent, guardian, or custodian;<hr><ltbullet1>creating or changing division records in certain ways without written consent from the child's parent, guardian, or custodian;<hr><ltbullet1>initiating certain medical treatment or care on behalf of a child in the division's custody; and<hr><ltbullet1>placing a child with a foster parent or taking adverse action against a foster parent if the foster parent expresses discomfort with caring for a child;<hr><ltbullet>allows the division to share certain records concerning a child with an adoptive parent of the child or an individual who has been awarded permanent custody and guardianship of the child;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a parent's approval or disapproval of a child's sexual orientation, in itself, may not be the basis for:<hr><ltbullet1>removal of the child from the parent's custody; or<hr><ltbullet1>discrimination when a court is determining child custody as part of a divorce or other family law proceeding;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a juvenile court may not determine that reunification services should not be provided based solely on a parent's agreement or disagreement with the child's sexual orientation or gender identity; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: International Money Transmission Amendments
description: This bill enacts a tax and income tax credit related to international money transmissions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>imposes a tax on international money transmissions on or after a certain date;<hr><ltbullet>exempts an international money transmission from the tax if the customer requesting the transaction presents valid identification;<hr><ltbullet>requires the tax to be stated separately on an invoice or receipt;<hr><ltbullet>requires licensed money transmitters to remit collected taxes quarterly and report annually to the State Tax Commission;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the State Tax Commission's administration of the tax;<hr><ltbullet>enacts a nonrefundable income tax credit for individuals who pay the tax;<hr><ltbullet>requires the commissioner of the Department of Financial Institutions to annually provide a list of all licensed money transmitters to the State Tax Commission; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Water Infrastructure Modifications
description: This bill addresses funding and planning for water infrastructure.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>repeals the Water Resources Cities Water Loan Fund and provides that loan repayments go into the Water Infrastructure Fund;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes transfers of money in water funds and accounts to and from the Water Infrastructure Fund;<hr><ltbullet>requires capital asset management plans and reserve funding under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>modifies definitions, including the definition of "relevant agency";<hr><ltbullet>addresses the water infrastructure prioritization process, including exemptions from the process;<hr><ltbullet>repeals outdated language; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Health Care Malpractice Amendments
description: This bill addresses statutes of limitation for health care malpractice actions.

title: Mayoral Recall Election Amendments
description: This bill establishes a procedure to conduct a recall election for the office of mayor.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a procedure to require a recall election for a mayor;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements to file a recall application and petition;<hr><ltbullet>describes requirements for a petition for a recall election, gathering and submitting signatures, removing signatures, and evaluating signatures;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for holding a recall election and determining the results of a recall election;<hr><ltbullet> establishes ballot requirements for a recall election;<hr><ltbullet>establishes criminal penalties for misconduct relating to a petition for a recall election; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Political Signs Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to political signs.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines a term;<hr><ltbullet>for a political advertisement that is required to disclose certain campaign finance information, reduces the size dimensions of a lawn sign that is exempt from the disclosure requirement;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a person from:<hr><ltbullet1>attaching a political sign to a utility pole, light pole, an electric utility box, or any road sign; or <hr><ltbullet1>affixing an object to a political sign to block, conceal, or misrepresent the message or image on a political sign;<hr><ltbullet>creates a criminal offense for a person who engages in the conduct described above;<hr><ltbullet>creates an exception to the criminal offense described above for a government employee who removes a political sign in accordance with the government employee's duties;<hr><ltbullet>specifies that a person does not commit a criminal offense related to a political sign if the person:<hr><ltbullet1>removes an object described above; <hr><ltbullet1>removes a lawn sign described above; or<hr><ltbullet1>removes a political sign attached to a utility pole, light pole, an electric utility box, or road sign; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Municipal Services Fees and Political Subdivision Lien Amendments
description: This bill authorizes municipalities to place a political subdivision lien on property for certain past due services.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a municipality that sets a fee schedule by ordinance or resolution for water, sewer, or utility-related services provided by the municipality, or a third-party contracted by the municipality, to bill a customer receiving the water, sewer, or utility-related services, directly or through a third-party contracted by the municipality;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a municipality to hold a political subdivision lien on a property for past due water, sewer, or utility-related service fees;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a municipality or special district to: <hr><ltbullet1>charge interest on a past due fee; and<hr><ltbullet1>charge and collect a one-time penalty on a past due fee; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Expungement Amendments
description: This bill addresses expungement.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms for expungement;<hr><ltbullet>allows the Department of Public Safety to make rules regarding the procedure for notifying the Bureau of Criminal Identification of an order of expungement;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the list of offenses that are not eligible for automatic expungement;<hr><ltbullet>allows the Bureau of Criminal Identification to request the vacation of an order for automatic expungement in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the requirements for a certificate of eligibility to address registration as a sex offender, kidnap offender, or child abuse offender or a protective order or criminal stalking injunction in effect against the individual;<hr><ltbullet>modifies venue for a petition seeking expungement of criminal records;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that a certificate of eligibility has to be valid at the time that the petition for expungement was filed for a court to grant expungement;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the effect of an expungement on a civil protective order;<hr><ltbullet>modifies venue for a petition seeking expungement of juvenile records; <hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to address a technical conflict if this bill and S.B. 41, Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry Amendments, both pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill amends provisions relating to deadlines and the calculation of time in the Election Code.

title: Amendments to Election Law
description: This bill amends provisions relating to elections.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires the lieutenant governor to:<hr><ltbullet1>develop a procedure to evaluate voter registration records based on addresses to identify potential anomalies;<hr><ltbullet1>develop procedures to investigate the validity of a voter registration when a ballot mailed by the county clerk is returned as undeliverable; and<hr><ltbullet1>register with the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements program;<hr><ltbullet>requires the lieutenant governor to seek to enter into an agreement with the federal courts where, in exchange for receiving certain information from the state for the purpose of maintaining federal jury lists, the courts will notify the state of individuals who are disqualified from jury service due to criminal convictions or non-citizen status; <hr><ltbullet>for voting by mail:<hr><ltbullet1>requires a registered voter who has a Utah driver license or a state identification card to place to last four digits of the card's number on the return envelope, and permits a voter to enter the last four digits of the voter's social security number as an alternate form of identification;<hr><ltbullet1>until 2029, permits a voter's identity to be verified using signature comparison, if the voter doesn't enter the digits described in the preceding paragraph;<hr><ltbullet1>beginning in 2029, provides that if a voter does not have a Utah driver license, a Utah state identification card, or a social security card, the voter may provide identification by including a photocopy of certain forms of identification in the return envelope;<hr><ltbullet1>beginning in 2029, if a voter does not have a type of identification described in the preceding two paragraphs, requires the voter to vote in person, unless the voter qualifies for certain exceptions;   <hr><ltbullet>subject to certain exceptions, provides that, beginning in 2029, a voter will not receive a ballot by mail unless the voter requests to receive a ballot by mail;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a request to receive a ballot by mail remains in effect for eight years unless the voter takes certain action that results in termination of the request;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a voter may request, or renew a request, to receive a ballot by mail when the person:<hr><ltbullet1>registers to vote;<hr><ltbullet1>makes a request online;<hr><ltbullet1>applies to receive or renew a Utah driver license or Utah state identification card; or<hr><ltbullet1>votes at a polling place; <hr><ltbullet>amends voter registration forms relating to:<hr><ltbullet1>requesting to receive ballot notifications; and<hr><ltbullet1>requesting to receive a mailed ballot;<hr><ltbullet>modifies requirements for an individual to assist a voter to vote at a polling place;<hr><ltbullet>modifies a return envelope consistent with the requirements of this bill and to provide certain warnings to a voter;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions relating to obtaining and returning an emergency ballot;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions for the processing of ballots, consistent with the provisions of this bill;<hr><ltbullet>creates an exception to the requirement that the bulk of ballots initially mailed to voters must be mailed from a location in Utah, if the jurisdiction mailing the ballots is assigned to a United States Postal Service area distribution center outside of Utah;<hr><ltbullet>expands the duties of the lieutenant governor in relation to maintaining the voter registration database; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Ambulance Provider Payment Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to ambulance billing and charges.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>codifies a base rate for ground ambulance transports;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a ground ambulance provider from charging rates that exceed established rates;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits balance billing;<hr><ltbullet>requires an insurer and workers' compensation to allow for established rates;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Office of the Legislative Auditor General to conduct an audit if prioritized; and<hr><ltbullet>creates a repeal date.

title: Minors in State Custody Amendments
description: This bill addresses federal benefits for minors who are in the custody of the Department of Health and Human Services.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Health and Human Services (department) to apply for a Medicaid waiver to ensure that minors in the custody of the department who receive federal benefits will maintain resource-eligibility for Medicaid;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department to evaluate whether a minor in the custody of the department is receiving or is eligible to receive federal benefits;<hr><ltbullet>provides that, as appropriate, the department shall apply for federal benefits on behalf of a minor in the custody of the department, and may accept appointment as the representative payee for a minor's federal benefits;<hr><ltbullet>provides accounting, reporting, and administrative requirements for the department concerning a federal benefit provided to a minor in the custody of the department;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department to offer financial literacy training for a minor who received a federal benefit while in the custody of the department, or for a successor representative payee;<hr><ltbullet>grants rulemaking authority to the department relating to the administration of federal benefits for minors in the custody of the department;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department to report annually to the Health and Human Services Interim Committee regarding federal benefits received on behalf of minors in the custody of the department; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Wildfire Funding Amendments
description: This bill addresses wildfires.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>merges several funds into the Utah Wildfire Fund (fund);<hr><ltbullet>modifies references to the funds merged into the fund;<hr><ltbullet>amends definition provisions;<hr><ltbullet>addresses delegation of fire management authority;<hr><ltbullet>addresses elements of the fund such as what is deposited into the fund and how money in the fund is used;<hr><ltbullet>requires reporting;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes rulemaking; <hr><ltbullet>moves provisions related to community wildfire preparedness plans addressing wildland-urban interface; <hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause with H.B. 48 to address the transition to the Utah Wildfire Fund; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: Wildlife Amendments
description: This bill addresses state activities related to wildlife.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>addresses night hunting of nonprotected wildlife;<hr><ltbullet>imposes requirements for holding a hunting or combination license for service on the Wildlife Board or a regional advisory council;<hr><ltbullet>addresses definition of and access to wildlife management areas;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions concerning the Department of Agriculture and Food's activities related to livestock depredation and big game protection;<hr><ltbullet>addresses compensation for damage to livestock;<hr><ltbullet>corrects a definition of "big game"; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill addresses wraparound services for certain individuals with a disability.

title: Criminal Justice Amendments
description: This bill modifies statutory provisions related to criminal justice.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to the release of individuals due to overcrowding of correctional facilities;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to contracting with federal and county entities to house individuals, and establishes reporting requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires a county sheriff who permits probation to establish probation standards and procedures adopted by the Utah Sheriffs' Association;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the use of state funds for a syringe exchange program;<hr><ltbullet>adds "detention removal officer" to the definition of federal officers who have statewide law enforcement authority;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the Department of Corrections from housing inmates in a private correctional facility, unless the purpose is federal immigration detention or civil detention;<hr><ltbullet>modifies definitions related to the state daily incarceration rate;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to the definition and calculation of the state daily incarceration rate;<hr><ltbullet>modifies permitted uses for funds in the Adult Probation and Parole Employment Incentive Program;<hr><ltbullet>adds strangulation or choking as a criminal offense included with the crime of commission of domestic violence in the presence of a child;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the definition of habitual offender and makes conforming changes;<hr><ltbullet>requires a county sheriff to report statistics on releases due to overcrowding and pretrial release;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to a county sheriff's release of individuals on their own recognizance;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a county jail official from fixing a financial condition for an individual with a misdemeanor charge for certain domestic violence and driving under the influence offenses;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to a magistrate's orders for pretrial release or detention;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to interlocal agreements regarding release of incarcerated or supervised individuals;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the Subcommittee on County Correctional Facility Contracting and Reimbursement;<hr><ltbullet>repeals outdated provisions; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill amends and enacts provisions relating to efficiency improvement processes and certain funding requirements in the Governor's Office of Planning and Budget.

title: Municipal Ordinance Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to the imposition of a civil penalty for a municipal ordinance violation.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allows a municipality to impose a civil fine that exceeds the maximum class B misdemeanor fine under Section 76-3-301 if:<hr><ltbullet1>the fine is imposed for violation of an ordinance that regulates occupancy, the provision of off-street parking, or the operation of a rental dwelling or short-term rental;<hr><ltbullet1>the municipality has previously imposed a fine on the individual for the same violation three or more times within the past 12 months; and<hr><ltbullet1>the fine does not exceed the applicable maximum amount described in this bill.

title: Child Actor Regulations
description: This bill enacts provisions related to minors involved in entertainment.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a parent or guardian establish a trust for a minor involved in entertainment;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which a child of a content creator is not subject to trust and compensation requirements;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which a parent or guardian may serve as the trustee of a trust for a minor involved in entertainment;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for a performer's employer when depositing a percentage of the earnings of a minor involved in entertainment into a trust;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a right of action for a minor involved in entertainment;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a content creator maintain a record that relates to a minor featured in the content creator's content;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a content creator inform a minor's parents that the minor is featured in the content creator's content;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a minor's parent or guardian establish a trust for the minor featured in social media content under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>establishes limitations related to the trust established for a minor featured in social media content;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a formula for a content creator to calculate the percentage of any earnings from social media that feature a minor and to transfer the earnings to the minor's trust;<hr><ltbullet>provides exemptions from the trust and compensation requirements;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a right of action for an individual featured in social media content as a minor;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a process by which a content creator may petition a court for an exception to the requirement to divide earnings from social media featuring a minor;<hr><ltbullet>grants an individual featured in social media content as a minor a right of deletion;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a social media company maintain a readily available process by which an individual featured in social media content as a minor may request that a content creator delete content featuring the individual featured in social media content as a minor;<hr><ltbullet>provides a process by which an individual may petition a court to require that a content creator delete the individual's content; <hr><ltbullet>provides for an award of attorney fees and damages; and<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which the provisions of this bill supersede a contractual provision related to disputes.

title: Special Group License Plate Amendments
description: This bill changes the allocation of money from a historical support special group license plate.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allows an individual to request, for an additional fee, a set of two license plates;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Motor Vehicle Division to design and distribute a white, classic license plate.<hr><ltbullet>allows a corporate brand sponsored special group license plate and a special group license plate for major league sports teams;<hr><ltbullet>allows the consolidation of license plate types for purposes of meeting the minimum circulation requirements;<hr><ltbullet>provides the allocation of money from the voluntary contribution for a historical support special group license plate, allocating revenue to the sponsoring agency and to the Transportation Investment Fund of 2005;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Motor Vehicle Division to provide notice regarding the allocation of the money from the historical support special group license plate; <hr><ltbullet>provides that a vintage vehicle is not required to make the voluntary contribution to obtain the historical support special group license plate;<hr><ltbullet>allows contributions for collegiate special group license plates to be used for the institution's compensation to student athletes for the use of the student athlete's name, image, or likeness;<hr><ltbullet>amends the definition of a vintage vehicle to exclude the requirement regarding the type of license plate to be displayed;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Tax Commission to provide a report regarding special group license plates; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Parent Access to Learning Materials Pilot Program
description: This bill creates the Parent Access to Learning Materials Pilot Program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates a three-year pilot program for parent access to learning materials;<hr><ltbullet>directs the state board to select local education agencies (LEAs) to participate;<hr><ltbullet>requires participating LEAs to implement teacher incentives;<hr><ltbullet>starts with elementary schools in 2025-26 school year;<hr><ltbullet>allows expansion to secondary schools in 2026-27 school year; and<hr><ltbullet>requires program reports.

title: Pregnant and Postpartum Inmate Amendments
description: This bill addresses statutes regarding pregnant and postpartum inmates.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Corrections (the department) and the county jails to ensure that each female individual admitted to a correctional facility is tested for pregnancy;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department and each county jail to collect certain parental information on inmates;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department and each county jail to report to the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice:<hr><ltbullet1>the number of known pregnant inmates in custody; and<hr><ltbullet1>the number of inmates in custody who are parents to a minor child;<hr><ltbullet>amends the membership of the Correctional Postnatal and Early Childhood Advisory Board (the board);<hr><ltbullet>extends the repeal date of the board; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill amends provisions relating to homeowners' and condominium owners' associations.

title: Water Usage Amendments
description: This bill addresses the use of overhead spray irrigation under specified circumstances.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>directs a municipality or county to require compliance with a prohibition on use of overhead spray irrigation as part of land use approvals;<hr><ltbullet>requires a municipality or county to give notice of the prohibition on use of overhead spray irrigation;<hr><ltbullet>encourages a municipality or county to review certain plans, act on the plans, inspect for compliance, and address noncompliance; and<hr><ltbullet>prohibits for new development and redevelopment the use of overhead spray irrigation except under certain circumstances.

title: Homeless Services Amendments
description: This bill amends and enacts provisions related to homelessness.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Shelter Counties Advisory Board to make recommendations to the Utah Homeless Board (board) regarding homeless services;<hr><ltbullet>requires the board to collect and report on certain data;<hr><ltbullet>provides that funds from the Homeless to Housing Reform Restricted Account may be used for certain transportation costs to connect the individual with a support network outside of the state; <hr><ltbullet>modifies the process by which the board approves funding requests from the Homeless Shelter Cities Mitigation Restricted Account;<hr><ltbullet>amends certain provisions of the winter response task force;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions requiring service providers to design certain services to assist homeless individuals in progressing and transitioning from struggling with homelessness to personal thriving;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions requiring certain safety requirements for homeless shelters, including winter response shelters; <hr><ltbullet>provides for penalties if a service provider that receives state or federal funds refuses to comply with certain safety requirements;<hr><ltbullet>provides certain exceptions under the COVID-19 grant program for licensed residential vocational and life skills programs; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Olympics Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions of the Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>codifies requirements that relate to a sale or transfer of part of an Olympic facility, which requirements were previously approved by the Legislature via joint resolutions;<hr><ltbullet>codifies requirements that must be met before any portion of an Olympic facility may be sold or transferred;<hr><ltbullet>requires the governor, or the governor's designee, and an Olympic facility manager to meet with the Legislative Management Committee in connection with approving a sale of a part of an Olympic facility; and<hr><ltbullet>requires an Olympic facility manager to give prior notice of certain structural changes in the organization to the Legislative Management Committee.

title: Amendments to Voting Provisions
description: This bill addresses provisions relating to voting and voter registration data.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires certain reporting to the Government Operations Interim Committee;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies reporting requirements for the lieutenant governor and county clerks;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the lieutenant governor's authority to cooperate or enter into an agreement with another state or third-party to share voter registration information;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for the maintenance of voter registration records;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the lieutenant governor to contract with a third-party to maintain voter rolls;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the lieutenant governor to enter into agreements with the federal courts;<hr><ltbullet>requires the lieutenant governor to register with the federal Systemic Alien Verification for Entitlements Program for voter registration and voter list maintenance;<hr><ltbullet>requires county clerks to investigate certain registered voters in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>addresses ballot video surveillance requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires proof of United States citizenship to vote in a state election;<hr><ltbullet>provides for a ballot relating to only federal elections if a voter does not provide proof of United States citizenship;<hr><ltbullet>provides for removing an individual from the voter registration roll if evidence is discovered, and not refuted, that the individual is not a citizen of the United States; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: Guardianships and Supported Decision-Making Agreements Amendments
description: This bill addresses guardianships and supported decision-making agreements.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>repeals a provision that provides for the future repeal of statutory language concerning when counsel is not required for an allegedly incapacitated person;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions concerning the rights of certain individuals who are under a court-ordered guardianship;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions concerning the procedure for determining incapacity and appointing a guardian for an incapacitated person;<hr><ltbullet>prescribes the principles by which provisions related to supported decision-making agreements should be interpreted;<hr><ltbullet>describes the requirements for a supported decision-making agreement;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the use of a supported decision-making agreement by certain individuals, subject to the permission of the individual's guardian, conservator, or other qualified person, as applicable;<hr><ltbullet>describes the duties of an individual who is a supporter under a supported decision-making agreement;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a supported decision-making agreement may be revoked or terminated, with certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>describes how a supported decision-making agreement interacts with and affects other laws and principles;<hr><ltbullet>provides protections for a person who relies, in good faith, on the provisions of a supported decision-making agreement; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Property Manager Requirements
description: This bill modifies the Utah Real Estate Licensing and Practices Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>grants the Real Estate Commission (commission) authority to make administrative rules relating to property managers;<hr><ltbullet>requires an individual to hold a license as a property manager before engaging in property management;<hr><ltbullet>exempts certain individuals from licensure under this act;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the commission and Division of Real Estate determine the qualifications and requirements for an applicant for a property manager license;<hr><ltbullet>allows an individual with an active broker, associate broker, or sales agent license to obtain a property manager license without meeting certain examination and education requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires that an applicant for a property manager license pay a licensing fee;<hr><ltbullet>repeals provisions authorizing certain individuals to act as a property manager;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a property manager to fill out any form or document related to property management;<hr><ltbullet>provides parameters for what a property manager may do when engaging in property management; <hr><ltbullet>requires that a property manager associate with a real estate trust account;<hr><ltbullet>exempts a property manager with a security bond that protects at least 30% of estimated client funds from the requirement to associate with a real estate trust account; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Commitment Amendments
description: This bill addresses the commitment of individuals in relation to civil, criminal, and juvenile proceedings.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to the rights and privileges to which an individual is entitled when under commitment to the custody or to the treatment services of a local mental health authority;<hr><ltbullet>provides when there is a conflict in the opinions of forensic evaluators, if a party seeks an additional competency evaluation then that party is responsible for selecting the evaluator and paying the cost of the evaluator;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions and clarifies the process regarding the release from a secured setting of a defendant determined to be incompetent to proceed;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies when the Department of Health and Human Services is required to provide an updated juvenile competency evaluation after an attainment period; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill addresses the activation and use of body-worn cameras by law enforcement officers.

title: School Fees Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to school fees.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a local education agency (LEA) to, beginning for the 2026-2027 school year:<hr><ltbullet1>ensure that a student has at least one option at the student's school to complete all required courses and credits without paying a fee or a waiver; and<hr><ltbullet1>clearly disclose any fee related to a course or activity in the description of the course or activity in the LEA's registration materials;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an LEA from:<hr><ltbullet1>charging a student a fee for certain non-fee courses; or<hr><ltbullet1>charging a general fee or charging or increasing a fee to a student to supplement or supplant a fee the LEA is prohibited from charging;<hr><ltbullet>allows an LEA to charge a student a fee for certain expenses, under certain circumstances, including for:<hr><ltbullet1>expenses beyond the common delivery of instruction;<hr><ltbullet1>fee courses;<hr><ltbullet1>instructional supplies;<hr><ltbullet1>extracurricular activities;<hr><ltbullet1>a discretionary project; and<hr><ltbullet1>other additional expenses;<hr><ltbullet>repeals duplicative language regarding fees for textbooks; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Insect Terminology Amendments
description: This bill addresses the naming convention for the insect species Anabrus simplex.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires state entities referencing the species Anabrus simplex in state materials to use:<hr><ltbullet1>the scientific name; or<hr><ltbullet1>a common name as adopted by the Entomological Society of America;<hr><ltbullet>requires state entities to encourage national insect naming institutions to adopt the naming convention of Anabrus simplex:<hr><ltbullet1>the scientific name; or<hr><ltbullet1>a common name as adopted by the Entomological Society of America;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Commissioner of the Department of Agriculture and Food to submit a petition to the Entomological Society of America for a new common name for Anabrus simplex; <hr><ltbullet>provides for the automatic repeal of provisions related to the petition for a new common name; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill addresses public awareness of organ donation and opportunities for individuals to register as organ donors.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires or encourages information about the option and process to register as an organ donor, to be provided in connection with or in certain circumstances related to:<hr><ltbullet1>the Division of Wildlife Resources' website;<hr><ltbullet1>intake at a health care facility; and<hr><ltbullet1>individual income tax instructions booklets and the State Tax Commission's website;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Health and Human Services to convene a coalition of life-saving programs and create a comprehensive plan for communicating about those programs through state-owned channels; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill modifies the High Cost Infrastructure Development Tax Credit Act to include district energy systems.

description: This bill establishes Election Day as a state holiday.

description: This bill addresses violations related to geologic carbon storage.

title: Criminal Code Amendments
description: This bill concerns certain criminal offenses.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires certain state agencies to regularly review and make recommendations concerning certain statutory criminal offenses;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice to receive, compile, and submit a report on state agency reviews of statutory criminal offenses; <hr><ltbullet>lowers the penalty for criminal violations concerning an unauthorized use of a name in a charity solicitation; <hr><ltbullet>repeals the criminal offense relating to abuse of the flag; <hr><ltbullet>contains a coordination clause to coordinate technical changes between this bill and H.B. 21, Criminal Code Recodification and Cross References, due to the repeal of Section 76-10-604 in H.B. 21;<hr><ltbullet>contains a coordination clause coordinating technical changes between this bill, H.B. 21, Criminal Code Recodification and Cross References, and H.B. 38, Criminal Offenses Modifications;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and clarifying changes to Section 76-9-803; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Criminal Justice Revisions
description: This bill creates certain requirements for criminal justice agencies and entities working with criminal justice agencies.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>adds county attorney offices in counties of the second and third class to the statute requiring certain prosecutorial data collection and reporting regarding criminal cases and modifies requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires a county jail to:<hr><ltbullet1>collect biometric and other personal information for individuals brought to the county jail for processing or booking into custody regardless of whether the county jail retains custody of the individual; and<hr><ltbullet1>to the extent possible, connect an individual in custody with the individual's state identification number and use the state identification number in association with any records regarding the individual;<hr><ltbullet>amends the membership of the Public Safety Data Management Task Force;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice (the commission) to include certain DUI crash data in an annual DUI report;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Public Safety's Criminal Investigations and Technical Services Division to collect certain DUI crash data and provide the data to the commission;<hr><ltbullet>establishes law enforcement agency requirements concerning:<hr><ltbullet1>the collection and reporting of certain DUI crash data;<hr><ltbullet1>the sharing of information with the Department of Public Safety's statewide criminal intelligence system;<hr><ltbullet1>the collection and reporting of certain lost, stolen, and untraceable firearms; and<hr><ltbullet1>the collection and reporting of the disposition of firearms in the custody of a law enforcement agency;<hr><ltbullet>requires the commission to receive, compile, and publish law enforcement agency data concerning firearms;<hr><ltbullet>requires law enforcement agencies to supply certain law enforcement officers with a portable biometric capture device;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the public safety data portal is the repository for statutorily required data concerning:<hr><ltbullet1>certain DUI crash data;<hr><ltbullet1>law enforcement agency reporting requirements for certain firearms data; and<hr><ltbullet1>prosecutorial data collection regarding prosecutions of false sexual assault accusations;<hr><ltbullet>imposes certain requirements for software service vendors if the software service is for use by a criminal justice agency and collects and stores data required by statute to be reported to the commission;<hr><ltbullet>requires prosecutorial agencies and courts to report to the commission data concerning enhancements to criminal charges; <hr><ltbullet>requires all prosecutorial agencies in the state to submit data to the commission concerning certain prosecutions, dismissals, and declinations to prosecute;<hr><ltbullet>exempts certain reporting requirements from law enforcement grant eligibility requirements; <hr><ltbullet>modifies pretrial release data reporting requirements from the Administrative Office of the Courts; <hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Corrections to conduct a risk assessment for every individual convicted of a sex offense that would require the individual to register on the Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Corrections, until January 1, 2030, to submit the results of risk assessments for sex offenders to the commission; <hr><ltbullet>includes coordination clauses to:<hr><ltbullet1> merge the changes to Sections 63I-2-277 and 77-41-115 in this bill if this bill and S.B. 41, Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry Amendments, both pass and become law, including to address the repeal and replacement of Section 77-41-115 in S.B. 41 with a newly enacted statute; and<hr><ltbullet1>merge the changes to Sections 53-25-104 and 63A-16-1002 if this bill and H.B. 436, Impaired Driving Amendments, both pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: County Governance Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions relating to forms of county government.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that in a county of the third through sixth class with a council-manager form of government, each council member must be elected by a voter district;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a process for a county of the third through sixth class with a council-manager form of government to create voter districts;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the composition of a study committee formed to study changing the form of county government; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Medical Cannabis Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions related to medical cannabis.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>repeals provisions related to qualified medical providers and limited medical providers in the medical cannabis program;<hr><ltbullet>allows certain health care providers to recommend medical cannabis without first registering with the Department of Health and Human Services;<hr><ltbullet>repeals continuing education requirements related to medical cannabis;<hr><ltbullet>moves enforcement of advertising and payment requirements related to medical cannabis from the Department of Health and Human Services to the Division of Professional Licensing; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Juvenile Justice Amendments
description: This bill amends statutory provisions related to juvenile justice.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends the notification requirements for an offense committed by a student on school grounds;<hr><ltbullet>recodifies and amends requirements related to the notification of an offense committed by a student on school grounds, including statutory provisions addressing investigations, searches, and immunity;<hr><ltbullet>addresses a minor's eligibility for a nonjudicial adjustment when a referral to a juvenile court involves certain offenses;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a court may not grant a petition for expungement of a juvenile record if the petitioner has been adjudicated or convicted of certain drug offenses within two years before the petition for expungement is filed; <hr><ltbullet>repeals statutes regarding notification and reporting of prohibited acts by students; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Housing Attainability Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to affordable housing.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies and defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a closed meeting may be held under certain circumstances by a political subdivision; <hr><ltbullet>provides that a city of the first or second class, under certain conditions, may qualify for funds from the Utah Homes Investment Program (program) to rehabilitate attainable homes within the city of the first or second class boundaries; <hr><ltbullet>extends the sunset date for the program by one year;<hr><ltbullet>allows for certain uses of school surplus lands for affordable housing;<hr><ltbullet>provides that among the trustees appointed to the Utah Housing Corporation that no more than two trustees are from the same county;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the sunset date for the Utah Housing Corporation; <hr><ltbullet>provides that the Department of Transportation may make rules regarding the sale of surplus real property to a state agency under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>allows the Utah Housing Corporation to return deposits made by the state treasurer for loan financing for certain attainable homes upon certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes; and<hr><ltbullet>provides a coordination clause with H.B. 412, Boards and Commissions Revisions, regarding Section 63H-8-201.

title: Drug Overdose Training Amendments
description: This bill addresses training and education concerning drug overdose recognition.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Integrated Healthcare within the Department of Health and Human Services to create training and educational materials regarding recognizing a drug overdose;<hr><ltbullet>requires an alcohol training and education seminar to include, for certain trainees, the drug overdose training and educational materials created by the Division of Integrated Healthcare;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the receipt of the drug overdose training and educational materials does not create or increase liability for the individual who receives them; and  <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Homeless Rights Amendments
description: This bill describes the rights of homeless individuals.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>describes a homeless individual's rights, including the right to:<hr><ltbullet1>receive equal treatment by the state and a political subdivision of the state in the same manner as any other individual;<hr><ltbullet1>register to vote and to vote in elections; and<hr><ltbullet1>the protection of personal information; <hr><ltbullet>provides that a homeless individual has a right of action against a person who violates the homeless individual's rights; and<hr><ltbullet>provides a statute of limitations for a homeless individual to bring a right of action against a person who violates the homeless individual's rights.
