title: Maternal and Infant Amendments
description: This bill addresses newborn infant testing.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Corrections and the county jails to ensure that each female individual admitted to a correctional facility is tested for pregnancy;<hr><ltbullet>amends the membership of the Correctional Postnatal and Early Childhood Advisory Board (the board);<hr><ltbullet>extends the repeal date of the board;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Health and Human Services (department) to publish a privacy consent form pertaining to newborn infant testing;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the privacy consent form be provided to a newborn infant's parent or guardian prior to conducting a newborn infant heelstick screen;<hr><ltbullet>makes hearing loss a required newborn infant test, regardless of the number of annual births that occur at the hospital or setting where the infant was born; <hr><ltbullet>provides for giving a parent or guardian the option to consent to the department's retention policy for biological samples or genetic data collected through newborn infant testing;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department to destroy a biological sample or any genetic data collected through newborn infant testing; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

description: This bill amends the Governmental Immunity Act.

title: Access to Communication Device Location Information Amendments
description: This bill concerns access to communication device location information.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a mobile telecommunications service shall provide communication device location information as quickly as possible under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>adds certain law enforcement warrants that are prioritized as urgent regarding a missing individual in danger to the list of circumstances under which a mobile telecommunications service shall provide communication device location information as quickly as possible;<hr><ltbullet>requires, if a mobile telecommunications service establishes procedures for providing communication device location information, a method for a law enforcement agency to identify different types of requested information; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Local Land Use Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to land use.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies and modifies statutes regarding municipal annexation and municipal boundary adjustments;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers and amends Title 10, Chapter 2, Part 4, Annexation, to Title 10, Chapter 2, Part 8, Annexation and Title 10, Chapter 2, Part 9, Municipal Boundary Adjustments;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers and amends the process by which a municipality or county conducts certain plan reviews;<hr><ltbullet>modifies notice requirements before a public hearing on a proposed land use regulation;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a municipality or county may not require a private individual or entity, including a community association or homeowners association, to permanently maintain or be responsible for a public access amenity or water utility unless certain conditions apply;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the process by which a municipality or county inspects and approves or rejects the performance of warranty work;<hr><ltbullet>modifies a municipality's or county's process in regulating landscaping;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the process for a municipality or county to allow transferable development rights;<hr><ltbullet>creates a process by which an applicant may submit an identical floor plan to a municipality for an expedited review;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a municipality or county may not require a public hearing for a request for a variance or another land use appeal;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the ability of a municipality or county to enforce an ordinance by withholding a building permit or certificate of occupancy;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the State Fire Code Act;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to special districts and land use;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a process by which a person may convey real property by deed to a public entity; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Elections Office
description: This bill addresses issues relating to Utah's election system.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides for the appointment of a conflict of interest elections officer to act in the place of the lieutenant governor if a complaint or election controversy arises that has any connection to a race for office in which the governor or lieutenant governor is, or seeks to be, a candidate;<hr><ltbullet>describes the terms of service and authority of the conflict of interest elections officer; and <hr><ltbullet>creates the Elections Oversight Task Force and establishes the task force's:<hr><ltbullet1>membership;<hr><ltbullet1>duties; <hr><ltbullet1>reporting requirements; and<hr><ltbullet1>repeal date.

title: State Holiday Modifications
description: This bill modifies the day on which Juneteenth National Freedom Day is recognized in Utah.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that June 19, called Juneteenth National Freedom Day, is a legal holiday in Utah;<hr><ltbullet>consistent with other legal holidays in Utah, provides for recognition of Juneteenth National Freedom Day on the preceding Friday or subsequent Monday if the holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, respectively; and<hr><ltbullet>amends parent-time schedules in relation to Juneteenth National Freedom Day.

title: Signature Collection Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to nominations for elective office.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes a process for a voter to have the voter's signature removed from a petition to nominate a candidate of a registered political party that is not a qualified political party to elective office;<hr><ltbullet>requires an election official to post on the lieutenant governor's website the name and date of signature of each voter who signs a nomination petition;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an election official from removing a voter's signature from a nomination petition if the election official has already verified the voter's signature;  <hr><ltbullet>requires an election official to notify the county or district attorney if a person whose signature appears on a nomination petition notifies the election official that the person did not sign the nomination petition;<hr><ltbullet>describes deadlines and procedures related to the processes described above;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause that adds an hourly deadline to Sections 20A-9-405 and 20A-9-408 to reflect the time computation changes made in H.B. 299, Election Code Time Computation Revisions, if both bills pass and become law; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Department of Natural Resources Funding Amendments
description: This bill addresses revenue and expenditures related to funding state accounts within the Department of Natural Resources.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires counties to remit to the state money calculated based on certain new transmission facilities for deposit into the Species Protection Account;<hr><ltbullet>expands resources to be deposited into the Species Protection Account;<hr><ltbullet>requires reporting by the Division of Wildlife Resources and a study by the Office of Energy Development;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the payment of a tax on gross receipts of a radioactive waste facility derived from the disposal of concentrated depleted uranium and containerized waste, including having certain revenue be deposited into the Species Protection Account;<hr><ltbullet>imposes a tax related to certain wind or solar electric generation facilities to be deposited into the Species Protection Account; <hr><ltbullet>imposes an assessment on renewable energy parent entities to be deposited into the Species Protection Account;<hr><ltbullet>modifies calculation of centrally assessed new growth;<hr><ltbullet>requires counties to remit to the state a portion of centrally assessed new growth for deposit into the Species Protection Account;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes rulemaking; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: Population Data Amendments
description: This bill addresses population data.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>in circumstances where a population estimate is available from the Utah Population Committee and the United States Bureau of the Census, requires the use of the census or census estimate only if the Utah Population Committee estimate is unavailable; <hr><ltbullet>requires the Utah Population Committee to annually provide an adjusted sub-county population estimate for each municipality and unincorporated area within the state;<hr><ltbullet>requires government entities to share information with the Utah Population Committee that is necessary for the committee to prepare population estimates; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Presumption of State Jurisdiction Amendments
description: This bill addresses state sovereignty and establishes a presumption of state jurisdiction.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the principles of state sovereignty, including the presumption that jurisdiction over subject matters not enumerated to the federal government in the United States Constitution remains with the state;<hr><ltbullet>provides that any presumption against state jurisdiction may be overcome only by federal demonstration of specific constitutional authorization;<hr><ltbullet>places the burden on the federal government in jurisdictional conflicts between the state and federal government;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Federalism Commission to coordinate with federal agencies and state entities to help to resolve jurisdictional conflicts; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Court Fine Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to compensatory service and credits toward criminal fines.

title: Child Support Requirements
description: This bill  amends provisions related to child support obligations for a child in state custody.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that a parent or other obligated individual is not responsible to pay the state child support for a child who is in state custody, which includes custody of the Division of Child and Family Services and the Division of Juvenile Justice and Youth Services;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the juvenile court system from ordering child support to be paid to the state because a child is in state custody;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Office of Recovery Services to cease collection of past due amounts of child support ordered in connection with a child being in state custody and to forgive any outstanding balances owed for such child support obligations;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the duties of the Office of Recovery Services in relation to collection of child support for a child who is in state custody;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the duties of the attorney general in relation to collection of child support for a child who is in state custody;<hr><ltbullet>repeals provisions that permit and regulate child support while a child is in state custody; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Emergency Medical Services Revisions
description: This bill addresses emergency medical services.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>grants certain enforcement authority to the Bureau of Emergency Medical Services (bureau);<hr><ltbullet>requires the Trauma System and Emergency Medical Services Committee (committee) to make an annual recommendation to the bureau regarding the schedule of potential fines that the bureau should assess and collect;  <hr><ltbullet>requires the bureau to consider the committee's annual recommendation, and to adopt, publish, and enforce a schedule of potential fines for violations by a licensed emergency medical service provider;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Emergency Medical Services Critical Needs Account;<hr><ltbullet>requires fines collected to be deposited into the Emergency Medical Services Critical Needs Account; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Banning Foreign Funding in Ballot Propositions and Elections
description: This bill establishes provisions related to foreign financial influence in ballot propositions and elections.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a foreign national from making or attempting to make a contribution or an independent expenditure for a political purpose;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a candidate, officeholder, or entity subject to campaign finance reporting requirements from knowingly soliciting, accepting, or receiving a contribution from a foreign national;<hr><ltbullet>requires a candidate, officeholder, or entity that receives contributions to annually certify to the lieutenant governor that the candidate, officeholder, or entity did not knowingly accept a contribution from a foreign national;<hr><ltbullet>requires each corporation or labor organization subject to campaign finance reporting requirements to certify that the corporation or labor organization is not a foreign national;<hr><ltbullet>requires a candidate, officeholder, or entity that receives a contribution from a foreign national to:<hr><ltbullet1>immediately notify the lieutenant governor; <hr><ltbullet1>return the contribution to the foreign national; and<hr><ltbullet1>if the foreign national refuses to accept the return of the contribution, disperse the value of the contribution into the state's General Fund<hr><ltbullet>prohibits any person from aiding or facilitating a violation of the prohibitions described above; <hr><ltbullet>establishes a criminal penalty for a person who violates the provisions described above;<hr><ltbullet>requires the lieutenant governor to impose a civil penalty against a foreign national that makes a contribution or independent expenditure; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: LEA Reporting Requirements
description: This bill requires the State Board of Education (state board) to study and make recommendations regarding local education agency (LEA) reporting of costs associated with implementing new legislation.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the state board to study methods for LEAs to report on the costs of implementing new legislation;<hr><ltbullet>outlines the required elements of the report;<hr><ltbullet>requires the state board consult with LEAs;<hr><ltbullet>requires the state board to report findings and recommendations to the Education Interim Committee;<hr><ltbullet>requires legislative committees to review and consider the recommendations; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Blood Transfusion Amendments
description: This bill addresses blood transfusions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>except in certain situations, disallows a health care facility or provider from prohibiting a patient from providing the patient's own blood product or the blood product of the patient's directed donor for any potential transfusion related to the patient's health care; and<hr><ltbullet>provides immunity from liability to health care providers and facilities for a patient's injury, damages, or death occurring in connection with a transfusion of blood product provided by the patient.

title: SNAP Funds Amendments
description: This bill enacts provisions related to the Supplement Nutrition Assistance Program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions related to Supplement Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP); <hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Workforce Services (department) to request a waiver from the federal government regarding the use of SNAP benefits for certain foods;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department to: <hr><ltbullet1>submit the waiver before July 1, 2025;<hr><ltbullet1>implement the waiver within a certain period of time upon approval of the waiver; and<hr><ltbullet1>if the waiver is denied, reapply until a waiver is approved; and<hr><ltbullet> has reporting requirements.

title: Public Asset Ownership Amendments
description: This bill addresses the state ownership of certain environmental assets.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a state entity selling or exchanging an environmental commodity to report a digital identification number to the Office of Energy Development;<hr><ltbullet>exempts from reporting requirements an environmental commodity created from activities on school and institutional trust lands; <hr><ltbullet>declares that an environmental commodity created from activities receiving state funds is the property of the state in proportion to the state funds contributed to create the environmental commodity; <hr><ltbullet>clarifies that an environmental commodity created or purchased by a state entity remains under the control of the state entity; and<hr><ltbullet>establishes duties for the state treasurer in managing an environmental commodity.

title: Child Custody Proceedings Amendments
description: This bill addresses situations related to child custody.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a peace officer or child welfare caseworker may not take specific actions related to the custody of a child based on certain actions of the child's parent;<hr><ltbullet>provides that in a proceeding where custody and parent-time of a minor child are at issue, the court may not apply a negative inference against a parent based on certain actions of the parent; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill addresses enforcement steps with regard to raw milk, including when raw milk is suspected in a food borne illness outbreak.

description: This bill prohibits a municipality from regulating an open house.

title: School Activity Eligibility Commission Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions regarding the School Activity Eligibility Commission (commission).
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>broadens the scope of available appointees to the commission;<hr><ltbullet>modifies quorum requirements for the commission;<hr><ltbullet>modifies a requirement to establish certain baseline ranges;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an eligibility determination of the commission is for a given school year;<hr><ltbullet>provides a standard of proof for eligibility determinations of the commission;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits public schools from participating with an athletic association that does not provide administrative staff support to the commission;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the scheduling of commission meetings throughout the school year with certain submission deadlines and ad-hoc meetings for students who do not meet certain deadlines; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Department of Public Safety Fee Amendments
description: This bill addresses fees collected by the Bureau of Criminal Identification.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>increases the fee for a concealed firearm permit for out-of-state applicants assessed before July 1, 2026;<hr><ltbullet>amends fee provisions related to concealed firearm permits assessed after July 1, 2026, allowing the Bureau of Criminal Identification to set related fees in accordance with the procedures specified in Section 63J-1-504;<hr><ltbullet>amends when funds from the Concealed Weapons Account are transferred to the Suicide Prevention and Education Fund;<hr><ltbullet>increases the annual fee for offenders on the Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry assessed before July 1, 2026;<hr><ltbullet>amends fee provisions related to the Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry assessed after July 1, 2026, allowing the Department of Public Safety to set related fees in accordance with the procedures specified in Section 63J-1-504; and<hr><ltbullet>contains a coordination clause coordinating changes between this bill and S.B. 41, Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry Amendment.

title: Used Electric Vehicle Battery Disclosure Amendments

description: This bill amends provisions relating to security.

title: Tobacco and Electronic Cigarette Enforcement Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions related to tobacco and electronic cigarette products.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>repeals the ban on flavored electronic cigarette products;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the sale of flavored electronic cigarette products if they do not meet certain tracking requirements;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the nicotine content limit for electronic cigarette products;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to electronic cigarette product enforcement;<hr><ltbullet>excludes flavored electronic cigarette products from the requirement that electronic cigarette products obtain premarket authorization from the federal Food and Drug Administration;<hr><ltbullet>creates a temporary registry for flavored electronic cigarette products;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the electronic cigarette product registry;<hr><ltbullet>creates a flavored electronic cigarette product registry;<hr><ltbullet>creates requirements for what type of flavored electronic cigarette products may be sold in the state;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Public Safety to create systems to improve enforcement of tobacco and electronic cigarette laws;<hr><ltbullet>creates penalties for general retail tobacco businesses that sell flavored electronic cigarette products;<hr><ltbullet>raises permit fees for general tobacco retailers;<hr><ltbullet>for retail tobacco specialty businesses:<hr><ltbullet1>raises permit fees;<hr><ltbullet1>creates identification scanning requirements; and<hr><ltbullet1>creates surveillance footage requirements;<hr><ltbullet>creates a tobacco handling permit for retail tobacco specialty business employees and operators;<hr><ltbullet>creates a tax on flavored electronic cigarette products;<hr><ltbullet>amends criminal penalties regarding the illegal sale of tobacco and electronic cigarette products;<hr><ltbullet>creates a criminal penalty for the use of certain flavored electronic cigarettes;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits retail tobacco specialty businesses from selling a product containing nicotine to a restricted nicotine individual;<hr><ltbullet>requires the court to designate an individual as a nicotine restricted individual if the individual is convicted of providing certain products containing nicotine to a minor; and<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause with H.B. 21, Criminal Code Recodification and Cross References, to ensure the policy changes made in this bill are accurately reflected if both bills pass.

title: Health and Human Services Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to the Department of Health and Human Services.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>repeals outdated language;<hr><ltbullet>updates code references;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Department of Health and Human Services (department) may examine and audit the expenditures of public funds provided to a local health department;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the required qualifications for the department's executive director and deputy directors;<hr><ltbullet>updates the name of a division and an office within the department;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the executive director of the department may create committees within the department, subject to certain conditions and requirements;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the department to access certain records of individuals licensed or certified by the Division of Professional Licensing for specific purposes;<hr><ltbullet>adds additional items to the list of duties of the department;<hr><ltbullet>updates language to be consistent with the transfer of certain emergency medical services responsibilities from the department to the Department of Public Safety;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the administration of stock albuterol by a qualified adult;<hr><ltbullet>updates references from "targeted case management" to "case managers";<hr><ltbullet>allows the Office of Public Guardian to have access to certain documents and information, including private, controlled, or protected information, when reasonably necessary to fulfill the office's duties and responsibilities;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Division of Services for People with Disabilities must determine the most appropriate, least restrictive setting for an individual with an intellectual disability within the division's system;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding fetal death certificates and certificates of early term stillbirth;<hr><ltbullet>updates code references to reflect the current name of the Office of Substance Use and Mental Health within the department;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Office of Recovery Services to review child support guidelines and submit a summary of the review to the Judiciary Interim Committee; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Impaired Driving Amendments
description: This bill concerns the collection and reporting of certain DUI information.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice (the commission) to include certain DUI crash and arrest data in an annual DUI report;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Public Safety's Criminal Investigations and Technical Services Division to collect certain DUI crash and arrest data and provide the data to the commission;<hr><ltbullet>establishes law enforcement agency reporting requirements concerning the collection and reporting of certain DUI crash and arrest data;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the public safety data portal is the repository for the statutorily required DUI crash and arrest data; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Interdicted Person Amendments
description: This bill provides that an individual convicted of driving under the influence may be designated as an interdicted person.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that a person convicted of driving under the influence may be designated as an interdicted person and is prohibited from purchasing alcohol for a certain time period;<hr><ltbullet>requires a court to designate an individual as a interdicted person if the person is convicted of an extreme DUI;<hr><ltbullet>allows the court to determine the time period of interdiction;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Services to provide training on verification of whether a person is an interdicted person, including inspection of the person's identification card or driver license;<hr><ltbullet>requires a person designated as an interdicted person to obtain a unique driver license or identification card with security features indicating that the person is an interdicted person;<hr><ltbullet>allows a person to voluntarily obtain a unique driver license or identification card with security features indicating that the person is an interdicted person;<hr><ltbullet>provides relevant definitions; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Franchisee Protection Act
description: This bill establishes protections for franchisees.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a franchisor from requiring a franchisee to open on a when operating conflicts with the franchisee's sincerely held religious belief; <hr><ltbullet>provides exceptions under which a franchisor may require a franchisee to open a franchise despite a conflict with the franchisee's sincerely held religious belief;<hr><ltbullet>provides a remedy for a franchisee if the franchisor violates the prohibition without an exception; and<hr><ltbullet>provides a civil penalty for a franchisor that violates the prohibition without an exception.

description: This bill modifies requirements for construction trade licenses.

title: Candidate Disclosure Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to conflict of interest disclosures.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires a candidate for local elective office to file a conflict of interest disclosure statement at the time the candidate files a declaration of candidacy; <hr><ltbullet>creates an exception to the disclosure requirement described above if the candidate is seeking reelection to the same office and already, that same year, filed a conflict of interest disclosure statement;<hr><ltbullet>requires an election official to post the candidate's disclosure statement on the political subdivision's website;  <hr><ltbullet>subject to certain exceptions, requires state and local candidates and officeholders to annually disclose any misdemeanor or felony offense for which the candidate or officeholder has been convicted by a court located within or outside of this state;<hr><ltbullet>for purposes of laws governing when a public employer may ask a question about a job applicant's criminal history, specifies that a candidate or officeholder described above is not an applicant for a job with a public employer;<hr><ltbullet>creates deadlines and procedures related to the processes described above; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Revisions to Election Law
description: This bill amends provisions relating to elections.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>changes the voter registration deadline to 21 days before the day of an election for all methods of voter registration;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a deadline for a voter:<hr><ltbullet1>who will not otherwise receive a ballot by mail in the upcoming election to request to receive a ballot by mail; or<hr><ltbullet1>who will receive a ballot by mail in the upcoming election to change the address to which the ballot will be mailed; <hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions relating to information an election officer is required to report in relation to ballot processing;<hr><ltbullet>provides deadlines for tabulating ballots and publishing tabulation results;<hr><ltbullet>requires an election officer to post unofficial election results on the Monday after the day of the election;<hr><ltbullet>requires a ballot drop box to remain open until the polls close on election day;<hr><ltbullet>requires the lieutenant governor to award a contract, via a request for proposals, to designate a voting system, including equipment and software, that will be used throughout the state;<hr><ltbullet>requires that, as election officers replace voting equipment and software, the election officers replace the voting equipment and software with voting equipment and software that is part of the election system designated under the preceding paragraph; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Statewide Catalyst Campus Model
description: This bill establishes a grant program to help local education agencies create or expand catalyst centers.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates the Catalyst Center Grant Program (program) to support local education agencies (LEA) in creating or expanding catalyst centers; <hr><ltbullet>allows for multi-year grants and capital expenditures;<hr><ltbullet>requires alignment with labor market needs, LEA strategic plans, and state career and technical education goals;<hr><ltbullet>establishes accountability measures, including limits on carryforward funds and annual reporting;<hr><ltbullet>requires Talent Ready Utah and the Utah Leading through Effective, Actionable, and Dynamic Education to create a marketing campaign for the program;<hr><ltbullet>exempts certain individuals from educator licensing requirements;<hr><ltbullet>amends the Public Education Economic Stabilization Restricted Account to fund the program; <hr><ltbullet>creates requirements related to art and fine arts credits; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

description: This bill allows a victim of a crime to have the victim's initials used instead of the victim's name in publicly available criminal justice documents.

title: Local Government Fees Modifications
description: This bill modifies and enacts provisions related to municipal and county fees.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a city from imposing a fee on the general public for broadband or public safety service, with exceptions;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a town from imposing a fee on the general public for public safety service, with exceptions;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a municipality or county to impose a transportation utility fee if the municipality or county complies with certain requirements;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a process and requirements for a municipality or county to impose a transportation utility fee; <hr><ltbullet>provides that property owned by a religious organization may, under certain circumstances, be exempt from a transportation utility fee;<hr><ltbullet>provides a process to hold a referendum on the imposition of a transportation utility fee or an increase to an existing transportation utility fee; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Utah Fits All Scholarship Program Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to the Utah Fits All Scholarship Program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>strengthens residency requirements and income verification process;<hr><ltbullet>amends the definition of the program manager;<hr><ltbullet>creates a financial administrator to process payments and fund expenditures from a scholarship account;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits contracted entities from charging processing fees to families;<hr><ltbullet>establishes deadlines for scholarship acceptance or denial;<hr><ltbullet>limits extracurricular expenses to 20% of the scholarship amount;<hr><ltbullet>limits physical education expenses to an additional 20% of the scholarship amount;<hr><ltbullet>creates procedures for students with special needs;<hr><ltbullet>enhances program manager accountability through audits and transparency;<hr><ltbullet>adds requirements for a local education agency acting as qualified providers;<hr><ltbullet>allows for scholarship amount rollovers;<hr><ltbullet>creates a Utah Fits All Scholarship Restricted Account (the account);<hr><ltbullet>allows funds within the account to accrue interest and be invested;<hr><ltbullet>allows for rollover amounts of unused scholarship awards;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the State Tax Commission's role in income verification; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Transient Room Tax Amendments
description: This bill modifies the transient room tax and creates the Outdoor Recreation Mitigation Grant Program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the acceptable uses of transient room tax revenue;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a county to enter into an interlocal agreement with a municipality within the county to share county transient room tax revenue;<hr><ltbullet>modifies reporting requirements on counties that impose transient room tax;<hr><ltbullet>provides that certain municipalities may appoint board members to a tourism tax advisory board;<hr><ltbullet>requires the state auditor to review a county's report on transient room tax and determine if the report is sufficient and compliant;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the maximum county tax rate on short-term rentals of tourist home, hotel, motel, or trailer court accommodations and services for counties of the second, third, fourth, fifth, and sixth class;<hr><ltbullet>extends an earmark on certain transient room tax revenue for a county of the first class; <hr><ltbullet>modifies the state tax rate on short-term rentals of tourist home, hotel, motel, or trailer court accommodations and services;<hr><ltbullet>imposes an additional state tax on short-term rentals of tourist home, hotel, motel, or trailer court accommodations and services that take place within a county of the first class;<hr><ltbullet>directs the State Tax Commission to distribute certain revenue the state collects on short-term rentals of tourist home, hotel, motel, or trailer court accommodations and services;<hr><ltbullet>extends the sunset on the State Search and Rescue Advisory Board; <hr><ltbullet>creates a sunset review;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the uses of the Transient Room Tax Fund;<hr><ltbullet>establishes an outdoor recreation mitigation grant program within the Division of Outdoor Recreation;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Outdoor Recreation Mitigation Grant Fund;<hr><ltbullet>describes the criteria to apply for and receive an outdoor recreation mitigation grant;<hr><ltbullet>describes the acceptable uses of an outdoor recreation mitigation grant;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Outdoor Recreation to provide a written report annually to the Revenue and Taxation and Political Subdivisions Interim committees; <hr><ltbullet>repeals the sunset date on the Volunteer Emergency Medical Service Personnel Health Insurance Program; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Signature Verification Amendments
description: This bill amends provision related to signature verification.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>for a registered voter who manually signs a petition to nominate a candidate for elective office, requires the election officer to post the voter's name and other voter-related information on the lieutenant governor's website for at least 90 days;<hr><ltbullet>if a voter's information in the voter registration database contains a valid email address, requires an election officer to send an email to the voter notifying the voter that:<hr><ltbullet1>the voter's name and other voter-related information is posted on the website described above; and<hr><ltbullet1>the voter may request to have the voter's signature removed from the petition by submitting a written statement to the election officer;<hr><ltbullet>amends the information appearing on a nomination petition form to notify a voter of the posting and signature removal process described above;<hr><ltbullet>implements the posting and signature removal processes in relation to a candidate for elective office who is not affiliated with a political party;<hr><ltbullet>establishes and amends deadlines relating to signature submission, verification, and candidate certification; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Candidate Petition Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to ballot access.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>for a candidate for elective office seeking the nomination of a political party by manually gathering the signatures of registered voters on a nomination petition:<hr><ltbullet1>prohibits a county clerk from verifying the signature of a voter if the county clerk is not the county clerk of the voter's residence; and<hr><ltbullet1>if an elective office's political division crosses the boundary of two or more counties, requires the county clerk to verify each signature and to certify the total number of verified signatures to the lieutenant governor; <hr><ltbullet>for an elective office described above, requires the lieutenant governor to:<hr><ltbullet1>count the verified signatures received from each county clerk where the candidate submitted signatures for verification; and<hr><ltbullet1>if the total number of signatures is sufficient for the candidate to qualify for placement on the ballot, certify the signatures;<hr><ltbullet>implements the signature verification and certification processes described above for a candidate who is not affiliated with a political party;  <hr><ltbullet>amends the form of a nomination petition to specify that only a registered voter of the county where a candidate will submit signatures for verification is eligible to have the voter's signature verified; <hr><ltbullet>establishes and amends deadlines relating to signature verification and certification of a petition described above; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Animal Crime Victim Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to the release and forfeiture of an animal that is being held because of abuse or involvement in a crime.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides a process to permit, while legal resolution of a crime is ongoing, the release or transfer of an animal being held in a shelter because the animal was abused or was involved in a crime;<hr><ltbullet>permits a peace officer in possession of a warrant to enter premises or a vehicle to aid or take custody of an animal that is being criminally mistreated or is associated with a crime;<hr><ltbullet>requires notice to the owner or possessor of the animal;<hr><ltbullet>permits a shelter or government counsel to file a motion to have a court review whether an animal being held in a shelter due to criminal activity should be forfeited or transferred to alternative care;<hr><ltbullet>provides procedures for the hearing and the court's determination, and permits the animal's owner to be heard as part of the hearing;<hr><ltbullet>provides procedures for placement of the animal if the court orders ownership of the animal to be forfeited;<hr><ltbullet>permits a court to order an animal owner to pay for the costs of sheltering an animal due to the owner's criminal activity;<hr><ltbullet>permits a court to order an individual who has abused an animal or involved an animal in criminal activity to complete an educational or animal cruelty prevention program;<hr><ltbullet>provides cross references for the forfeiture procedure; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Child Support Modifications
description: This bill modifies provisions related to child support and family law.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates a rebuttable presumption that an order terminating parental rights shall state the amount of any child support arrears and permit collection of arrears;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a divorce decree provide information about the Office of Recovery Services (office);<hr><ltbullet>beginning July 1, 2026, creates a rebuttable presumption that a child support order shall include a provision requiring an obligor parent to pay a recurring amount as an ongoing expense for child care;<hr><ltbullet>requires the office to study and prepare a proposed method for calculating the amount of an ongoing expense for child care and report the office's findings to the Health and Human Services Interim Committee;<hr><ltbullet>requires the office to propose to the Health and Human Services Interim Committee procedural and statutory considerations that are necessary to move from a receipt-based child care payment model to a model where all new or modified child support orders would instead require an ongoing expense for child care as the primary means for sharing child care costs; and<hr><ltbullet>gives reporting requirements to the office.

title: Public Safety Amendments
description: This bill addresses provisions related to public safety.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions requiring a law enforcement agency of a city that is the seat of government for a county of the first class to enter into an interagency agreement related to public safety concerns with the Department of Public Safety (the department) and repeals the provisions, subject to a review by an interim committee, on July 1, 2027;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions requiring a law enforcement agency that has entered into an interagency agreement with the department to submit a report to the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee regarding the interagency agreement and repeals the provisions, subject to a review by an interim committee, on July 1, 2027;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions allowing the Division of Facilities Construction and Management to use eminent domain to condemn unincorporated property owned by a city that is the seat of government for a county of the first class in certain circumstances that are repealed on July 1, 2027;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions taking effect on July 1, 2026, related to procedures that are required to be undertaken by a law enforcement agency before the law enforcement agency may take an adverse decision regarding a law enforcement officer's employment; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Uniform Antitrust Pre-Merger Notification Act Amendments
description: This bill enacts the Uniform Antitrust Pre-Merger Notification Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a pre-merger notification is a notification filed with the Federal Trade Commission accompanied by a Hart-Scott-Rodino form;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a person filing a pre-merger notification file an electronic copy of a Hart-Scott-Rodino form and additional documentary material with the attorney general;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the attorney general from charging a fee connected with filing a Hart-Scott-Rodino form;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the attorney general from disclosing a Hart-Scott-Rodino form and other relevant information;<hr><ltbullet>classifies a Hart-Scott-Rodino form and other relevant information as a private record under the Government Records Access and Management Act;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the attorney general to disclose a Hart-Scott-Rodino form and other relevant information if relevant to an administrative proceeding or a judicial action;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the provisions enacted by this bill do not impact preexisting obligations of the attorney general;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the attorney general to disclose a Hart-Scott-Rodino form with the attorney general of another state under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the attorney general to seek the imposition of a civil penalty for noncompliance with the provisions of this bill;<hr><ltbullet>requires a court to promote uniformity among jurisdictions that enact the provisions of this bill;<hr><ltbullet>limits the provisions of this bill to a pre-merger notification filed after the effective date of the bill; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: School Digital Materials Amendments
description: This bill amends and enacts provisions regarding the accessibility of sensitive material through digital instructional material in a school setting.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>includes information regarding sensitive material in the information the state board provides through a certain parent portal;<hr><ltbullet>requires each local education agency (LEA) to:<hr><ltbullet1>provide certain information to parents at the time of student registration each year; and<hr><ltbullet1>maintain a section on the homepage of the LEA's website regarding sensitive material reporting;<hr><ltbullet>allows the state board, an LEA, or the Utah Education and Telehealth Network (UETN) to rescind certain contracts if a vendor does not remove access to digital sensitive material after a number of instances;<hr><ltbullet>requires the state board, an LEA, or UETN to:<hr><ltbullet1>remove access to digital instructional material that a vendor provides after a certain threshold of violations;<hr><ltbullet1>provide certain notice to each vendor with which the entity contracts to provide digital instructional material in a school setting; and<hr><ltbullet1>ensure that any database or school-provided device which a student may access uses a filter or other software to prohibit access to sensitive material; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Regulatory Oversight Amendments
description: This bill provides additional mechanisms for the oversight of state executive agencies.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>directs the Office of Professional Licensure Review (office) to create a mechanism to gather feedback regarding existing occupational regulations;<hr><ltbullet>directs the office to include the feedback regarding existing occupational regulations that the office gathers in the office's written report to the Business and Labor Interim Committee;  <hr><ltbullet>provides a limit on the cost of implementing an agency generated rule; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Tax Return Donation Amendments
description: This bill creates a School Meals Debt Relief Fund and provides for the fund's administration.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates a School Meals Debt Relief Fund;<hr><ltbullet>allows individual taxpayers to designate contributions to the fund on tax returns;<hr><ltbullet>establishes reporting requirements for local education agencies regarding school meals debt;<hr><ltbullet>provides for a distribution process based on each local education agency's proportion of total statewide school meals debt;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Board of Education to collect and verify school meals debt data;<hr><ltbullet>delegates rulemaking authority to the State Board of Education for program administration; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Brine Mining Amendments
description: This bill addresses the mining of brine within the state.

title: Student Athlete Revisions
description: This bill mandates policies on abusive coaching and addresses student-athlete compensation for name, image, or likeness.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes;<hr><ltbullet>allows an institution of higher education to use certain funds to compensate a student athlete directly for the use of the student athlete's name, image, or likeness;<hr><ltbullet>provides certain protections to institutions and student athletes;<hr><ltbullet>creates an audit requirement for the Board of Higher Education;<hr><ltbullet>requires a degree-granting institution to:<hr><ltbullet1> adopt a policy addressing abusive coaching practices; and<hr><ltbullet1>report to the Education Interim Committee; and<hr><ltbullet>requires a degree-granting institution's board of trustees to review and approve a degree-granting institution's policy on abusive coaching practices.

description: This bill amends provisions relating to owners and tenants.

title: School and Institutional Trust Lands Administration Modifications
description: This bill addresses provisions related to school and institutional trust lands.

title: State Purchasing Reserve Funding
description: This bill modifies provisions related to state purchasing.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes an administrative fee on state cooperative contracts that the division awards on behalf of an executive branch procurement unit;<hr><ltbullet>deposits revenue from the administrative fee into a restricted account called the State Purchasing Reserve Restricted Account (account);<hr><ltbullet>directs the state treasurer to invest money in the account in precious metals; and<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the money in the account to be used for the purpose of offsetting the cost of procuring goods and services for state entities and ensuring continuity in the state's procurement of goods and services, if certain inflation metrics are met.

title: Federalism Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to federalism.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>expands the membership of the Federalism Commission (commission) and modifies the manner in which members are appointed;<hr><ltbullet>increases the number of committee bill files the commission is permitted to open each year;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Center for Constitutional Studies (center) at Utah Valley University, in consultation with the commission, to:<hr><ltbullet1>develop a continuing education and training program for state and local government employees regarding federalism issues;<hr><ltbullet1>organize an annual federalism conference and study the creation of a state-led national federalism organization;<hr><ltbullet1>coordinate with private sector actors to conduct out-of-state outreach; and<hr><ltbullet1>establish informal working groups as necessary and report to the commission;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Herbert Institute (institute) at Utah Valley University, in consultation with the commission, to: <hr><ltbullet1>serve as a liaison between the commission, the center, and government entities on federalism issues; and<hr><ltbullet1>conduct outreach and coordination to support the commission's federalism efforts; and<hr><ltbullet1>coordinate with private organizations on local and national outreach efforts and report to the commission;<hr><ltbullet>requires the commission to:<hr><ltbullet1>make recommendations to the center and to the institute regarding the entities' federalism-related duties; and<hr><ltbullet1>report annually to the Legislative Management Committee regarding the entities' progress;<hr><ltbullet>requires executive branch agencies to designate a contact person to coordinate with the commission regarding education and training; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical corrections.

title: State Parks Modifications
description: This bill addresses the Division of State Parks.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>removes a requirement for the Division of State Parks (division) to comply with the Utah Procurement Code in selecting concessionaires in state parks;<hr><ltbullet>requires the division to operate, to the extent possible, from money and revenue collected as fees and charges;<hr><ltbullet>requires the director to implement a comprehensive plan for the long-term use of state parks developed by the division;<hr><ltbullet>grants rulemaking authority to the division to administer the state parks system;<hr><ltbullet>renames the State Parks Restricted Account;<hr><ltbullet>repeals sections related to boating accounts and river enhancement grants; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Behavioral Health Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions relating to behavioral health.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a behavioral health receiving center to comply with licensing requirements from the Department of Health and Human Services;<hr><ltbullet>grants the Department of Health and Human Services authority to enact rules and assess and collect fees in relation to the licensing of behavioral health receiving centers;<hr><ltbullet>addresses Medicaid directed payments for the Utah State Hospital and the Huntsman Mental Health Institute;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Public Safety to:<hr><ltbullet1>survey all law enforcement agencies in the state and publish a publicly searchable registry that will allow the public to see whether each law enforcement agency is or is not available to receive a voluntarily committed firearm in accordance with safe harbor provisions; and<hr><ltbullet1>subject to available funding, create and implement a marketing plan to educate law enforcement agencies and the public about safe harbor options for firearms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Drinking Water Utilities Amendments
description: This bill addresses security at drinking water facilities.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a community water system to: <hr><ltbullet1>complete a security plan; and<hr><ltbullet1>report a security breach to the Utah Cyber Center within two hours of discovering the security breach;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Drinking Water to report annually to two legislative committees on security at community water systems;<hr><ltbullet>classifies a community water system's security plan as a protected record; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Revisor's Technical Corrections to Utah Code
description: This bill makes technical corrections to the Utah Code.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies parts of the Utah Code to make technical corrections, including:<hr><ltbullet1>eliminating or correcting references involving repealed provisions;<hr><ltbullet1>eliminating redundant or obsolete language;<hr><ltbullet1>making minor wording changes;<hr><ltbullet1>updating cross-references; and<hr><ltbullet1>correcting numbering and other errors;<hr><ltbullet>amends the Sunset Act and the Repeal Dates by Title Act to repeal sunset and repeal dates that have passed and taken effect; and<hr><ltbullet>adds a coordination clause to subordinate changes in this bill that are in conflict with other legislation during the 2025 General Session.

title: Public Education Compliance
description: This bill amends and enacts provisions expanding the authority of the State Board of Education (state board) to address transparency and local education agency compliance.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the state board to:<hr><ltbullet1>use an existing compliance framework to address reports or allegations of noncompliance;<hr><ltbullet1>develop a system to address complaints to the Utah Professional Practices Advisory Commission in a timely and expedient manner; and<hr><ltbullet1>publish information related to state board meetings on the state board's website;<hr><ltbullet>may require the state board to issue a report;<hr><ltbullet>requires a school district or charter school to provide information to the state board that is necessary for the state board to fulfill a statutory data gathering, compliance, or reporting requirement; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Transportation and Infrastructure Funding Amendments
description: This bill allocates funds in the County of the First Class Highway Projects Fund and provides other transportation funding.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allocates funds in the County of the First Class Highway Projects Fund to various projects and purposes;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Department of Transportation to issue a general obligation bond, with the bond proceeds being distributed to a grant program, and provides revenue to service the bond;<hr><ltbullet>creates an affordable housing infrastructure grant program to provide grants to local governments to construct infrastructure to facilitate affordable housing projects in a county of the first class;<hr><ltbullet>provides funding, loans, and grants to certain transportation projects; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Medical Malpractice Modifications
description: This bill addresses malpractice actions against health care providers.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>with respect to a medical malpractice action:<hr><ltbullet1>repeals requirements related to affidavits of merit;<hr><ltbullet1>prohibits prejudicing a defendant in an adjudication of a claimant's claims;<hr><ltbullet1>prohibits pursuing or collecting on a judgment against a health care provider's personal income or assets, with exceptions;<hr><ltbullet1>grants access to the court's Xchange database to the Division of Professional Licensing (division);<hr><ltbullet1>establishes data collection and reporting requirements for the division;<hr><ltbullet1>amends procedure pertaining to prelitigation review panels and panel reviews;<hr><ltbullet1>makes a prelitigation review panel's recommendations or findings advisory; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Financial and Conflict of Interest Disclosures by Candidates Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to campaign finance and conflict of interest disclosures.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires a candidate for elective office in a county, municipality, or special district to file a conflict of interest disclosure statement at the time the candidate files a declaration of candidacy;<hr><ltbullet>requires a candidate seeking to fill a midterm vacancy in an office described above to file a financial report of contributions and expenditures;<hr><ltbullet>for a midterm vacancy in an office described above, or for a midterm vacancy in a statewide, state school board, or state legislative office, requires a candidate seeking to fill the vacancy to file a conflict of interest disclosure statement;<hr><ltbullet>requires an election officer who receives a conflict of interest disclosure statement to make the disclosure available for public inspection on the state's or political subdivision's website;<hr><ltbullet>if a midterm vacancy occurs in an office for which a registered political party is entitled to declare a nominee to fill the vacancy, requires the registered political party to notify the election officer of the date, time, and location of the meeting to select the nominee;<hr><ltbullet>requires a candidate seeking to fill a midterm vacancy on the state school board to file an interim financial report with the lieutenant governor;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies when a vacancy occurs in an elective office described above;<hr><ltbullet>for a midterm vacancy in certain county offices and in a municipal office, requires the county or municipal legislative body to notify, respectively, the county or municipal clerk;<hr><ltbullet>establishes deadlines related to the processes described above; <hr><ltbullet>for state and legislative office candidates seeking appointment to fill a midterm vacancy, amends the deadline to file a campaign finance report with the lieutenant governor;<hr><ltbullet>amends conflict of interest disclosure provisions to:<hr><ltbullet1>eliminate a disclosure related to a candidate's or officeholder's spousal information;<hr><ltbullet1>require the disclosure of certain household adult information only in certain circumstances; and<hr><ltbullet1>permit the candidate or officeholder making the disclosure to request the redaction of certain personally identifiable information from the disclosure if the candidate, officeholder, or the candidate's or officeholder's spouse is an at-risk government employee;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to reflect changes made in Section 20A-1-504 in S.B. 300, Election Amendments, with cross-referencing changes made to Sections 20A-11-204, 20A-11-303, and 20A-11-1303 in this bill, if both bills pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: School Data Amendments
description: This bill requires the State Board of Education (state board) to study and make recommendations regarding local education agency (LEA) data collection, retention, student information systems, and reporting requirements.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;    <hr><ltbullet>creates a Data Systems and Reporting Advisory Committee;     <hr><ltbullet>requires the state board to study LEA practices for collection and retention of student personally identifiable information;    <hr><ltbullet>requires analysis of LEA student information system costs and capabilities;     <hr><ltbullet>requires examination of LEA reporting requirements and potential sunset provisions;     <hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for stakeholder input and coordination;     <hr><ltbullet>requires the state board to report findings and recommendations to the Education Interim Committee; and     <hr><ltbullet>requires legislative review of recommendations.

title: Agricultural Amendments
description: This bill creates a requirement for the Department of Agriculture and Food to study issues related to local food availability.

title: Judicial Retention Changes
description: This bill addresses judicial retention.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies the ballot requirements for judicial retention elections;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the information contained in the voter information pamphlet for judicial retention elections;<hr><ltbullet>requires the lieutenant governor to transmit a retention recommendation from the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance to a county clerk;<hr><ltbullet>amends the ballot language for a judicial retention election to address a retention recommendation from the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance;<hr><ltbullet>provides that certain records for the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance are private;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Judicial Conduct Committee to provide records to the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms related to judicial performance evaluations;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Judicial Performance Evaluation Commission to provide the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance with a list of judges who are subject to a retention election in the next scheduled regular general election;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the membership, length of appointment, selection of the chairs, quorum requirements, and compensation for the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance;<hr><ltbullet>allows the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance to evaluate a judge and provide a recommendation to the public as to whether the judge should be retained for another term;<hr><ltbullet>provides the evaluation and recommendation process for the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance, including requiring the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance to:<hr><ltbullet1>hold any committee meeting to evaluate a judge before August 15 of the year in which the judge is subject to a retention election in a regular general election; and<hr><ltbullet1>provide a retention recommendation for a judge to the lieutenant governor on or before August 15 of the year in which the judge is subject to a retention election in a regular general election; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Utah Commission for Earthquake Preparedness
description: This bill creates the Utah Commission for Earthquake Preparedness.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates the Utah Commission for Earthquake Preparedness, addressing:<hr><ltbullet1>membership;<hr><ltbullet1>quorum requirements;<hr><ltbullet1>vacancies; and<hr><ltbullet1>compensation for commission members;<hr><ltbullet>permits the commission to invite officials from certain state and executive agencies to participate in the commission's meetings as nonvoting members;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Natural Resources to staff the commission;<hr><ltbullet>specifies duties and responsibilities of the commission;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a January 1, 2031, sunset date for the commission;<hr><ltbullet>subject to an exception, provides that money appropriated to the commission by the Legislature is nonlapsing; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Vehicle Registration Changes
description: This bill amends vehicle registration notification requirements and provides an option for a two-year registration period for certain vehicles.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allows a person to select a mail option for notification of vehicle registration;<hr><ltbullet>provides an option for a two-year vehicle registration period for a trailer, off-highway vehicle, street-legal all-terrain vehicle, or electric motor vehicle; <hr><ltbullet>provides for the calculation and deposit of registration and various other fees and taxes due at the time of registration to account for a 24-month vehicle registration period;<hr><ltbullet>provides coordination clauses to coordinate this bill with H.B. 277, Vehicle Registration Amendments, and H.B. 272, Vehicle Assessment Amendments, to ensure the three bills work together technically; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Sexual Abuse Material Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions relating to liability for commercial entities.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a commercial entity from knowingly or intentionally publishing or distributing obscene material or child sexual abuse material on the Internet;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a commercial entity from knowingly or intentionally engaging in the purchase or distribution of a child sex doll;<hr><ltbullet>provides a cause of action for an individual against a commercial entity that distributes or publishes unlawful materials;<hr><ltbullet>provides the relief a court may grant if an individual brings a cause of action against a commercial entity that distributes or publishes unlawful materials;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a commercial entity is not liable for unlawful content on the commercial entity's services, if the commercial entity did not create the unlawful material;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the attorney general to seek relief against a commercial entity that distributes or publishes unlawful materials;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the attorney general develop and publish guidance relating to liability for commercial entities; and<hr><ltbullet>authorizes individuals with claims under the provisions this bill enacts to combine the individuals' claims.

title: Water Entity Amendments
description: This bill addresses various water entities including their relationship with the Department of Natural Resources
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>removes certain water agencies from a definition of an independent entity;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions governing the water trust for the Great Salt Lake, including expanding the duties of the Great Salt Lake Trust Council;<hr><ltbullet>requires the state water agent to coordinate with the Department of Natural Resources (department);<hr><ltbullet>moves the Great Salt Lake commissioner and the Office of the Great Salt Lake Commissioner to be within the department;<hr><ltbullet>requires the review by the Great Salt Lake Trust Council of certain expenditures of the Great Salt Lake commissioner; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: Automotive Repair Business Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to automotive repairs.

title: Government Records Access and Management Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions of the Government Records Access and Management Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that the government records ombudsman shall provide resources and services related to a fee dispute in relation to a records request;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions regulating costs chargeable by a governmental entity for employee time in processing a records request under the Government Records Access and Management Act;<hr><ltbullet>adds provisions to regulate the disclosure of records and fee information regarding work-related contact information for an employee of a local education agency;<hr><ltbullet>requires a governmental entity to provide an itemized estimate of costs and fees expected to be incurred before the governmental entity begins to process a request or requires payment or deposit when fees are expected to exceed a certain amount;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions of the Government Records Access and Management Act to make an appeal to a chief administrative officer an optional process for appealing an estimate of fees that exceeds a certain amount;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a State Records Committee review of an agency access denial, fee waiver denial, or fee estimate dispute is de novo;<hr><ltbullet>requires a political subdivision to permit an optional appeal of an estimate of fees that exceeds a certain amount directly to the State Records Committee;<hr><ltbullet>modifies existing procedures; and<hr><ltbullet>makes conforming changes and style corrections.

title: County Formation Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to the creation of a new county.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes a threshold for petitioners and creates an opportunity for municipal legislative bodies to initiate a process to create a new county;<hr><ltbullet>imposes certain viability requirements on the formation of a new county, including the completion of a feasibility study;<hr><ltbullet>allows certain rural property to remain in the original county, in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the continuation of property taxation between an existing county and new county to satisfy general obligation or revenue bond indebtedness;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies provisions regarding the division of taxes, assets, and liabilities between an existing county and new county; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Criminal Justice Modifications
description: This bill amends statutory provisions related to criminal justice.

title: Municipal Incorporation Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions relating to the incorporation of a preliminary municipality.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that:<hr><ltbullet1>a person may not apply to incorporate an area as a preliminary municipality after February 15, 2025;<hr><ltbullet1>a person who applies to incorporate an area as a preliminary municipality by filing a feasibility request on or before February 15, 2025, may proceed in accordance with Title 10, Chapter 2a, Part 5, Incorporation of a Preliminary Municipality, after February 15, 2025;<hr><ltbullet1>a preliminary municipality may not annex an unincorporated area; and<hr><ltbullet1>a municipality may not annex an area if the area was included in a feasibility request to incorporate the area into a preliminary municipality; and<hr><ltbullet>requires:<hr><ltbullet1>a proposed preliminary municipality to agree that initial landowners will fully compensate the county for damages to county property or infrastructure before the preliminary municipality can transition into a town;<hr><ltbullet1>a preliminary municipality located in the fourth through sixth class to comply with terms, conditions, or restrictions that were established in a development agreement between the initial landowners and the county before the feasibility request was filed; <hr><ltbullet1>a preliminary municipality to comply with county standards for infrastructure; and<hr><ltbullet1>that a petition to transition a preliminary municipality into a town shall certify that damages to county property or infrastructure have been paid in full.

title: Olympic Legacy Liability Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to the Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games Act and winter sports activities.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides public policy considerations;<hr><ltbullet>provides definitions;<hr><ltbullet>establishes limitations on liability for claims against the operator of a specified winter sports area;<hr><ltbullet>requires a specified winter sports area to give notice of the liability limitations;<hr><ltbullet>permits a winter sports area operator to enter into a contract with a winter sports participant to limit the operator's liability;<hr><ltbullet>specifies the amount of liability caps and provides for adjustment of the liability caps; and<hr><ltbullet>makes conforming changes.

title: Worker Protection Modifications
description: This bill modifies the Utah Labor Code.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an employer from compelling an employee to attend a meeting or listen to communication of an employer's opinion about a religious or political matter;<hr><ltbullet>provides exceptions to the prohibition;<hr><ltbullet>provides a remedy for an employee who is compelled to attend a meeting or listen to communication of an employer's opinion about a religious or political matter;<hr><ltbullet> requires an employer to: <hr><ltbullet1>implement heat risk precautions and cold risk precautions; <hr><ltbullet1>implement recordkeeping requirements pertaining to heat stoke, hypothermia, frostbite, or temperature-related fatalities;<hr><ltbullet1>notify employees with a written description of quotas, adverse actions that may result for failing to obtain a quota, and incentives for meeting a quota;<hr><ltbullet1>provide data pertaining to quotas to a requesting employee;<hr><ltbullet1>implement recordkeeping requirements pertaining to quotas; and<hr><ltbullet1>maintain a workplace safety program for managing risks related to the temperature of the worksite;<hr><ltbullet>provides standards for tracking quotas;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits retaliation against an employee who requests records or files a complaint with the Labor Commission (commission); and<hr><ltbullet>provides for commission enforcement.

title: Genetic Information Amendments
description: This bill addresses the use of genetic sequencing tools and the storage of genetic sequencing data.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the use of certain genetic sequencers and genetic sequencing software;<hr><ltbullet>prescribes requirements and restrictions related to the storage of genetic sequencing data;<hr><ltbullet>requires relevant entities to certify compliance with genetic sequencing requirements;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the attorney general to investigate alleged violations of genetic sequencing requirements, and initiate civil actions for those violations; and<hr><ltbullet>provides protections for an employee who reports a suspected violation of genetic sequencing requirements to the attorney general.
