description: This bill modifies provisions related to law enforcement and criminal justice.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires that counties offering probation services adopt certain probation standards and practices;<hr><ltbullet>modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Office of State Debt Collection has the authority to collect civil accounts receivable or a civil judgment of restitution and interest thereon;<hr><ltbullet>provides that administrative garnishments also apply to a debtor's property or wages that are under control of a third party;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Office of State Debt Collection to provide an accounting of the unpaid balance of a defendant's criminal accounts receivable at the time of termination of the defendant's sentence;<hr><ltbullet>provides repayment procedures for any unpaid balance of a defendant's criminal accounts receivable upon termination of a sentence;<hr><ltbullet>provides circumstances that constitute a material change in circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>adds requirements for temporary pretrial status orders of detention;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions relating to factors for pretrial release requirements;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a request for a pretrial release at an initial appearance does not constitute a pretrial detention hearing;<hr><ltbullet>requires a court to make findings of fact when making a determination regarding pretrial release;<hr><ltbullet>adds a financial condition schedule to aid a court in determining the amount of a fixed financial condition;<hr><ltbullet>requires a judge to take certain actions if the judge is unable to hold a pretrial detention hearing before a certain deadline;<hr><ltbullet>provides for required procedures when a no bail hold is requested;<hr><ltbullet>provides that certain Board of Pardons and Parole decisions on restitution are final and not subject to judicial review;<hr><ltbullet>codifies order of restitution procedures that apply to certain offenders sentenced before July 1, 2021;<hr><ltbullet>provides procedures for the accounting and payment of restitution owed to various state governmental entities;<hr><ltbullet>permits a sentencing court to authorize the deposit of funds in certain interest-bearing accounts when distribution to a victim is pending;<hr><ltbullet>permits the Board of Pardons and Parole to order recovery of fees incurred on behalf of a sentenced offender in addition to the existing ability to recover costs;<hr><ltbullet>makes coordinating modifications related to docket entry and interest assessments;<hr><ltbullet>permits a court to set restitution for a juvenile sentenced to prison;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause that requires changes to a section of this bill supersede the changes to that section in H.B. 312, Criminal Justice Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and grammatical changes.

title: Concurrent Resolution Urging Changes to Federal Homelessness Regulations
description: This resolution urges federal government housing and homelessness agencies to implement reforms to housing assistant programs.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>urges the Department of Housing and Urban Development to implement reforms to certain federal housing assistant programs; <hr><ltbullet>recognizes that:<hr><ltbullet1>state and local governments seek to fund and implement programs that are more effective than the current alternatives to reduce the number of people living on the street and include approaches and strategies that are more responsive to local priorities and circumstances;<hr><ltbullet1>the Homeless Management Information System is costly, burdensome, and fails to meet the information and data needs of state and local governments; and<hr><ltbullet1>block grant funding provides the state with needed discretion on how to use federal funding for direct services to the state's homeless population;<hr><ltbullet>calls on the federal government to reform certain agency rules and federal laws to provide state and local governments greater latitude in administering homelessness; and<hr><ltbullet>provides for copies of the resolution to be distributed among certain federal agencies and other individuals.

title: Concurrent Resolution on State Innovation for Transition from Government Benefits to Self-reliance
description: This resolution urges the federal government to give more flexibility and autonomy to states to allow for greater innovation and experimentation to help families who receive government benefits more successfully transition off of welfare programs and into work-based self-reliance.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>articulates the strength of Utah's economy and nation-leading upward mobility; <hr><ltbullet>establishes Utah's track record as an innovative leader already showcasing the successes and advantages of state-driven approaches to work and welfare;<hr><ltbullet>identifies evidence of families in Utah who still struggle to fully realize the American Dream due to perceived or actual disincentives in the social safety net in the form of the "benefits cliff" and "benefits plateau"; and<hr><ltbullet>urges the federal government to increase flexibility and autonomy to allow states the ability to innovate through experiments and pilots to better transition families off of federally funded safety net programs and into work-based self-reliance.

title: Concurrent Resolution Regarding State Parks
description: This resolution encourages the Division of State Parks to work with federal agencies to transfer ownership or management of properties suitable for a state park, monument, or campground, back to the state.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>requests that the Division of State Parks (division) petition the Bureau of Land Management to transfer title to the state of Utah for the creation of the Little Sahara State Park;<hr><ltbullet>requests that the division negotiate with the United States Forest Service to transfer the Antelope Flat Campground for the creation of the Flaming Gorge State Park;<hr><ltbullet>encourages the division to work with federal agencies to acquire, lease, or manage any other properties considered suitable for a state park, monument, or campground; <hr><ltbullet>urges the division to study the feasibility of a Davis County Skyline Drive state park or state campground; and<hr><ltbullet>requests that the division update the Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Interim Committee on the division's progress.

title: House Concurrent Resolution on State Management of Federal Public Lands
description: This resolution urges the federal government and state entities to identify public lands for the state to manage for outdoor recreation.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>urges Congress to enact legislation establishing a framework for state operation of federal public lands to improve public land management and reduce federal expenditures;<hr><ltbullet>highlights the need to develop and maintain state parks, monuments, and campgrounds to provide the people of Utah with outdoor recreational opportunities; <hr><ltbullet>encourages the Division of State Parks (division) to work with federal agencies to acquire, lease, or manage properties considered suitable for a state park, monument, or campground;<hr><ltbullet>suggests land that the division may consider for a potential state park or campground; <hr><ltbullet>requests that the division petition the Bureau of Land Management to transfer title to the state of Utah for the creation of the Little Sahara State Park;<hr><ltbullet>requests that the division negotiate with the United States Forest Service to transfer the Antelope Flat Campground for the creation of the Flaming Gorge State Park; and<hr><ltbullet>requests that the division update the Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Interim Committee on the division's progress.

title: Concurrent Resolution Regarding Religious Freedom
description: This resolution supports and encourages practices that exemplify religious freedom in public spaces.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>acknowledges the historical context that supports the inclusion of religion in government and education; <hr><ltbullet>supports the right of public school students and teachers to openly express their faith;<hr><ltbullet>encourages the accommodation of religious observances in government and community settings;<hr><ltbullet>supports the protection of religious symbols in public spaces; and<hr><ltbullet>encourages the fostering of respectful dialogue among diverse faith traditions.

title: Joint Rules Resolution - Legislative Process Amendments
description: This joint rules resolution modifies legislative processes and procedures.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement that the Senate and House Rules committees meet annually to review joint rules;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the process to direct a roll call vote during an electronic meeting;<hr><ltbullet>modifies legislative staff offices' reporting requirement related to performance measures;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Executive Appropriations Committee to meet annually to approve legislative staff offices' budgets and certify the Legislature's budget to the governor;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the right of legislators to attend joint committee meetings, subject to certain restrictions;<hr><ltbullet>modifies specific bill format requirements;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies how requests for legislation, priority request designations, and legislation are treated when the chief sponsor is:<hr><ltbullet1>unable to serve in the next annual general session; or<hr><ltbullet1>elected or appointed to serve in the opposite chamber;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the circumstances under which the Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel removes a committee note;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the order in which the Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel numbers legislation;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the days of the week the Senate and House give preference for the other chamber's legislation;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits transferring sponsorship on legislation more than twice;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the consideration of an amendment or substitute legislation made in the other chamber;<hr><ltbullet>modifies deadlines related to the passage of the final appropriations bill and fiscal note bills;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies reimbursement procedures related to legislative travel;<hr><ltbullet>requires that when a legislative committee creates a subcommittee, the members must include at least one senator and one representative;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the chairs of the Legislative Process Committee and the Rules Review and General Oversight Committee to independently open a committee bill file, subject to certain requirements;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the chief sponsor of a committee bill from altering the bill before the bill is numbered for introduction, except altering to make a technical correction; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Public Education Base Budget Amendments
description: This bill supplements or reduces appropriations otherwise provided for the support and operation of public education for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2024, and ending June 30, 2025, and appropriates funds for the support and operation of public education for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2025, and ending June 30, 2026.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Board of Education (state board) to:<hr><ltbullet1>provide information necessary to calculate certain budgetary adjustments by a given date each year; and<hr><ltbullet1>establish certain budgetary data reporting requirements and deadlines;<hr><ltbullet>allows the state board to adjust per-teacher amounts for classroom supplies and materials if ongoing funding is insufficient;<hr><ltbullet>amends the state guarantee on local property tax levies to ensure that a hold harmless provision only applies in the case of a change in property valuation;<hr><ltbullet>provides appropriations for the use and support of school districts, charter schools and state education agencies;<hr><ltbullet>sets the value of the weighted pupil unit (WPU) initially at $4,674 for fiscal year 2025-2026;<hr><ltbullet>Adjusts the number of weighted pupil units (WPUs) in certain programs for student enrollment changes and statutory formula calculations;<hr><ltbullet>appropriates funds to the Uniform School Fund Restricted - Public Education Budget Stabilization Account;<hr><ltbullet>Makes an appropriation from the Uniform School Fund Restricted - Trust Distribution Account to the School LAND Trust program to support educational programs in the public schools;<hr><ltbullet>Adjusts the revenue targets and estimates tax rates for the statewide Basic Rate and WPU Value Rate according to statutory provisions;<hr><ltbullet>provides appropriations for other purposes as described; and<hr><ltbullet>approves intent language.

title: Property Tax Notice Amendments
description: This bill modifies the property tax valuation notice requirements.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that the county discretionary deferral program is available to an indigent individual;<hr><ltbullet>requires a county auditor to include on the property tax valuation notice: <hr><ltbullet1>a statement that a property owner who is 65 years old or older, disabled, or experiencing an extreme hardship, may be eligible for a deferral on the property owner's primary residence; and <hr><ltbullet1>a telephone number to obtain information about how to apply for a deferral;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical corrections; and<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to provide that the changes to S.B. 197, Property Tax Amendments, supersede the changes to this bill.

title: Services for Department of Defense Civilian Employees
description: This bill addresses certain benefits for a United States Department of Defense employee and the employee's family.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet> provides certain exemptions from occupational and professional licensure in a variety of occupations and professions for:<hr><ltbullet1>a United States Department of Defense employee if the employee has a valid license in another jurisdiction; and<hr><ltbullet1>a spouse of a United States Department of Defense employee if the spouse has a valid license in another jurisdiction;<hr><ltbullet>provides in-state residency for tuition purposes at an institution of higher education for a United States Department of Defense employee and the employee's family;<hr><ltbullet>addresses k-12 requirements for a child of a United States Department of Defense employee;<hr><ltbullet>contains a coordination clause to coordinate technical changes between this bill and H.B. 142, Service Member and Veteran Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Election Fundraising Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to prohibited campaign contributions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>exempts a campaign contribution for federal office, made by a person other than a lobbyist or principal, from the prohibition on campaign contributions during a legislative session or the time period when the governor may veto a bill;<hr><ltbullet>makes it a crime to make a federal contribution with the intent to influence the governor or a state official to take or not take an action or to reward the governor or a state official for taking or not taking an action; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Utah Retirement Systems Amendments for Military Personnel
description: This bill modifies the vesting requirements for employer contributions made to a defined contribution plan.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that employer nonelective contributions made on behalf of an employee to a defined contribution plan vest upon the member's termination of employment, if the member or the member's spouse is a military service member who receives permanent change of station or relocation orders outside the state;<hr><ltbullet>allows specified Utah National Guard personnel, including the adjutant general, to elect to be exempt from the retirement systems, allowing employer contributions to vest immediately; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill modifies the contribution provisions of the New Public Employees' Tier II Contributory Retirement Act.

title: Long-Term Disability Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to public employee long-term disability benefits.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies the definition of objective medical impairment for purposes of the Public Employees' Long-Term Disability Act;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to the application for and determination of long-term disability benefits;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies which employees are eligible for a disability benefit for a total disability due to a mental objective medical impairment through June 30, 2026;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the exclusions for monthly disability benefits;<hr><ltbullet>directs the Public Employees' Long-Term Disability program to administer the existing basic long-term benefit for volunteer emergency medical services personnel; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: State Employee Benefit Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to public employee benefits.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies the definition of gainful employment for purposes of the Public Employees' Long-Term Disability Act;<hr><ltbullet>includes pay for time that exceeds an eligible employee's regular schedule in the calculation of the eligible employee's regular monthly salary;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a death benefit for employees receiving long-term disability benefits;<hr><ltbullet>makes life assistance counseling that the Utah State Retirement Office offers available to employees receiving long-term disability benefits;<hr><ltbullet>increases the state-paid basic life insurance benefit for exempt state employees;<hr><ltbullet>creates additional state-paid basic life insurance benefit tiers for exempt state employees; and<hr><ltbullet>directs savings from a reduction in long-term disability premium rates be used to pay for the cost of the changes in this bill.

title: Child Abuse and Torture Amendments
description: This bill concerns child abuse and torture.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTLAW", "name": "Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates a new criminal offense for child torture and provides penalties;<hr><ltbullet>adds the offense of child torture to the list of offenses for which imprisonment is mandatory;<hr><ltbullet>amends existing definitions relating to the offenses of child abuse and aggravated criminal child abuse;<hr><ltbullet>modifies child abandonment, abuse or neglect of a child with a disability, and other statutes that rely on certain definitions concerning criminal child abuse;<hr><ltbullet>includes the offense of child torture in statutes that reference child abuse or aggravated child abuse, including statutes concerning background checks, murder and aggravated murder, child abuse homicide, bigamy, jail release agreements and orders, and adoption, parent-time, and custody statutes;<hr><ltbullet>adds the offense of child torture to the definition of "violent felony";<hr><ltbullet>includes the offense of child torture as a registrable offense on the Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the definition of "severe type of child abuse or neglect" in the juvenile code to refer to the amended definition of serious injury in the criminal child abuse statute; <hr><ltbullet>adds coordination clauses:<hr><ltbullet1>to merge the changes to Section 76-3-406 if both this bill and H.B. 78, Criminal Offenses Amendments, both pass and become law; <hr><ltbullet1>to merge the changes to Section 77-41-102 in this bill if this bill, S.B. 41, Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry Amendments, both pass and become law, and H.B. 21, Criminal Code Recodification and Cross References, does not pass and become law, due to Section 77-41-102 being repealed and replaced with newly enacted statutes in S.B. 41; and<hr><ltbullet1>to merge the changes to Section 77-41-102 in this bill if this bill, S.B. 41, Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry Amendments, and H.B. 21, Criminal Code Recodification and Cross References, all pass and become law, due to Section 77-41-102 being repealed and replaced with newly enacted statutes in S.B. 41; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Housing and Transit Reinvestment Zone Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to the Housing and Transit Reinvestment Zone Act.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTEDW", "name": "Economic Development and Workforce Services Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to the Housing and Transit Reinvestment Zone Act;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to the Hotel Impact Mitigation Fund and distribution of funds;<hr><ltbullet>amends the allowable use of a certain sales and use taxes to be used for convention center revitalization;<hr><ltbullet>allows certain sales and use tax revenue distributed to a county to be used for convention center revitalization; <hr><ltbullet>creates a process to propose a convention center reinvestment zone to facilitate revitalization of a convention center and surrounding areas within a county of the first class to:<hr><ltbullet1>allow capture of sales and use tax increment related to state and certain local sales and use taxes;<hr><ltbullet1>allow capture of property tax increment; and<hr><ltbullet1>provide for distribution of funds to enable bonding;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions to exclude remote sales tax revenue for the capture of sales and use tax increment; <hr><ltbullet>amends the median gross income for a certain percentage of proposed dwelling units within the housing and transit reinvestment zone to the county median gross income for households of the same size;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the collection of a tax increment for a housing and transit reinvestment zone project may be triggered no more than three times per project;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to housing and transit reinvestment zones within certain transit stations or hubs; <hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to mixed-used development;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the requirement that a proposal for a transit reinvestment zone includes a mix of dwelling units with at least 25% of the dwelling units having more than one bedroom;<hr><ltbullet>amends the date by which a tax increment collection notice is sent to certain entities to no later than December 31 of the year before the year tax increment is to take place;<hr><ltbullet>requires certain limitations on use of funds in certain convention center reinvestment zones;<hr><ltbullet>requires the base year to be updated in certain circumstances regarding existing community reinvestment projects; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Professional Licensure Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to professional licensure.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>standardizes the requirements for a criminal background check for licensure in certain professions;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the circumstances under which the Division of Professional Licensing (division) revokes a license, as that revocation applies to a criminal background check;<hr><ltbullet>renames the Physicians Education Fund to the Physicians Education and Enforcement Fund (fund);<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the director of the division to make distributions from the fund under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the division deposit administrative penalties imposed for unprofessional or unlawful conduct into the fund; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Juvenile Court Procedures Amendments
description: This bill addresses petitions to modify orders of permanent custody and guardianship.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>describes circumstances under which a parent may file a petition to modify an order of permanent custody and guardianship;<hr><ltbullet>addresses whether a district court or juvenile court retains jurisdiction over an order of permanent custody and guardianship;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a juvenile court shall order a parent to file an order of permanent custody and guardianship with the district court in certain circumstances; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>repeals the existing chapter dealing with insurance investments;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a minimum financial security benchmark for insurers;<hr><ltbullet>describes the authorized investments an insurer may make;<hr><ltbullet>establishes prudence evaluation criteria;<hr><ltbullet>requires that an insurer establish and follow a written investment policy;<hr><ltbullet>describes the authorized classes of investments an insurer may make;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the limitation of classes of investments;<hr><ltbullet>requires that an insurer doing business in different currencies have securities in each currency that meet the requirements of this chapter;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an insurer from making certain types of investments;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the effect of investment restrictions on insurers;<hr><ltbullet>provides insurers guidelines for the required reports and replies under this chapter;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the commissioner to retain experts when analyzing an insurer's investments;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the commissioner to issue orders regarding an insurer's investment practices;<hr><ltbullet>describes how a commissioner should conduct an administrative hearing under this chapter;<hr><ltbullet>exempts an investment policy subject to this chapter from the definition of "record" under the Government Records Access and Management Act;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which this chapter prevails over any conflicting statute that relates to insurance investments; and<hr><ltbullet>grants the commissioner rulemaking authority regarding insurance investments.

title: Vehicle Registration Modifications
description: This bill allows the State Tax Commission to contract with a designated agent to assist in address verification for vehicles and vessels insured in the state.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>allows the State Tax Commission (commission) to contract with a designated agent to determine the address for which a vehicle's or vessel's insurance is tied, to assist the commission in determining whether the owner is a resident of this state;<hr><ltbullet>based on information provided by the designated agent, allows the commission to investigate whether the owner is a resident for vehicle or vessel registration purposes or otherwise in compliance with relevant registration and tax laws; <hr><ltbullet>for a person found in violation of certain tax and fee requirements, allows the person 60 days to cure the violation before being subject to a penalty;<hr><ltbullet>allows the commission to impose penalties in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>allows funds in the Uninsured Motorist Identification Restricted Account to be used to cover the costs of the designated agent for address verification; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Election Code Amendments
description: This bill amends the Election Code and related provisions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>standardizes language related to a voter who, after signing a petition, seeks to remove the voter's signature from the petition;<hr><ltbullet>reduces the amount of time that the sponsors of a petition for incorporation that passes have to determine certain features of the new municipal government from 60 to 30 days; <hr><ltbullet>clarifies the deadline for a candidate for mayor or municipal council of a newly incorporating municipality to file a declaration of candidacy;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the county clerk determines whether to remove a voter's signature from a petition for incorporation of a municipality; <hr><ltbullet>repeals the in-state residency requirement for a signature-gatherer who circulates a petition on behalf of:<hr><ltbullet1> an organization of registered voters seeking to become a registered political party; or<hr><ltbullet1> a candidate for elective office seeking the nomination of a registered or qualified political party;<hr><ltbullet>repeals provisions related to the in-state residency requirement described above;<hr><ltbullet>for a regular primary or presidential primary election, or for certain regular general or statewide special elections, requires a board of canvassers to immediately transmit to the lieutenant governor certain vote total information;<hr><ltbullet>eliminates the requirement that a board of canvassers make the transmission described above by telephone, fax, or mail;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a process for a voter who signs a petition on behalf of a candidate for elective office seeking the nomination of a registered political party to have the voter's signature removed from the petition; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Appearance of Candidate Name on Ballot
description: This bill addresses the manner in which a candidate's name may appear on a ballot.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes criteria for permitting a candidate to:<hr><ltbullet1>use the candidate's middle name instead of the candidate's first name on a ballot;<hr><ltbullet1>use the candidate's nickname on a ballot; or<hr><ltbullet1>use the candidate's initial on a ballot;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a procedure for a candidate to request that the candidate's name appear on a ballot as described in the preceding paragraph; and<hr><ltbullet>provides for an appeal of a rejection of a request described in the preceding paragraph.

title: Unauthorized Use of Real Property Amendments
description: This bill addresses the consequences of unauthorized use of real property by providing a limited alternative remedy to remove a trespasser from real property and providing a criminal penalty for the fraudulent sale or rental of real property.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>authorizes property owners or their agents to request assistance from law enforcement for the immediate removal of a trespasser from real property under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>requires an owner seeking removal of a trespasser, or the owner's authorized agent, to submit a complaint;<hr><ltbullet>specifies requirements for the complaint;<hr><ltbullet>provides requirements for law enforcement;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes law enforcement to arrest a trespasser for legal cause;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the owner or agent to request that law enforcement stand by while the owner or agent takes possession of the property; <hr><ltbullet>provides that law enforcement is not liable to any party for loss, destruction, or damage;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the property owner or agent is not liable to any party for the loss or destruction of, or damage to, personal property unless it was wrongfully removed;<hr><ltbullet>provides civil remedies;<hr><ltbullet>imposes criminal penalties for unlawfully possessing of, occupying on, or trespassing on real property intentionally and causing a specified amount of damage;<hr><ltbullet>imposes criminal penalties for any person who knowingly and willfully presents a false document purporting to be a valid lease agreement, deed, or other instrument conveying real property rights;<hr><ltbullet>imposes criminal penalties for fraudulently listing or advertising for sale, or renting or leasing, residential real property under certain circumstances; and <hr><ltbullet>provides criminal penalties for committing perjury.

description: This bill provides a process by which a city council may retain or employ staff to assist the city council.

title: Mobile Crane Amendments
description: This bill addresses the use of mobile cranes.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires that an owner of real property on which a mobile crane will be used to:<hr><ltbullet1>obtain a geotechnical report; and<hr><ltbullet1>take certain precautions if the geotechnical report states that the conditions of the real property cannot support the maximum crane load;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an owner from using a mobile crane on the owner's property under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>creates a presumption of negligence in a civil action resulting from an owner failing to take certain precautions when using a mobile crane; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Waste Tire Recycling Amendments
description: This bill makes changes to the Waste Tire Recycling Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies and defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>exempts landfills from restrictions on accepting waste tires if the landfill uses a mobile facility to reduce the size of waste tires;<hr><ltbullet>allows certain shredded waste tires to be disposed of in a landfill;<hr><ltbullet>allows an owner or operator of a landfill in a county of the third through sixth class to apply for reimbursement for waste tires disposed of in the owner or operator's landfill; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Medical Cannabis Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to medical cannabis.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends surveillance requirements; <hr><ltbullet>allows the Cannabis Production Establishment and Pharmacy Licensing Advisory Board (licensing board) to renew or approve medical cannabis courier licenses;<hr><ltbullet>allows the licensing board to renew licenses as necessary instead of only in December; <hr><ltbullet>allows a cannabis processing facility to operate at a second location under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>amends reporting requirements;<hr><ltbullet>limits the number of licenses that the Department of Agriculture and Food (department) may issue for cannabis processing facilities;<hr><ltbullet>allows the department to issue letters of concern;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a medical cannabis pharmacy from allowing the recommendation of medical cannabis near the pharmacy under certain circumstances; <hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement that pharmacy and courier agent registration cards include the agent's employer on the card;<hr><ltbullet>allows for medical cannabis cardholders to bring their own opaque bag or box to transport medical cannabis from the pharmacy;<hr><ltbullet>requires medical cannabis pharmacies and couriers to report a change in ownership at least 45 days before the change occurs;<hr><ltbullet>requires qualified medical provider employee proxies to complete a course on health information privacy;<hr><ltbullet>removes certain information from the medical cannabis card;<hr><ltbullet>repeals provisions related to the Division of Finance and the medical cannabis program;<hr><ltbullet>aligns continuing education provisions of qualified medical providers and pharmacy medical providers;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the creation of patient product information inserts;<hr><ltbullet>moves the repeal date for the Cannabis Research Review Board earlier one year;<hr><ltbullet>extends the repeal date for the Medical Cannabis Governance Structure Working Group;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause with H.B. 21, Criminal Code Recodification and Cross References, to align a definition and cross reference; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill addresses certain crimes committed against child welfare workers.

title: Corrections Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions related to corrections.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends which individuals in the custody of the Department of Corrections (the department) may petition to have a sex designation change on a birth certificate;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an individual in the custody of the department from filing a petition in district court to legally change the individual's name;<hr><ltbullet>includes individuals on parole on the list of individuals to whom a government entity is not required to respond regarding certain records requests;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the department may independently investigate criminal allegations against:<hr><ltbullet1>individuals in the custody of the department; and<hr><ltbullet1>subject to certain limitations, employees of the department;<hr><ltbullet>amends the prison telephone surcharge account to allow revenue generated from offenders using department tablets and other electronic devices to be placed in the account;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding the substances administered by the department when carrying out a judgment of death by lethal intravenous injection; <hr><ltbullet>requires an individual on probation or parole who is required to undergo drug testing as a condition of probation or parole to sign a waiver allowing the provider undertaking the testing to notify the individual's supervising officer regarding the results of the testing; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Technical Code Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions to modify gender-specific language.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions to modify gender-specific language;<hr><ltbullet>enacts changes to conform with legislative drafting standards;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to address conflicts with any other legislation; and<hr><ltbullet>makes other technical and conforming changes.

title: Water Fee Amendments
description: This bill allows state agencies to develop a fee schedule for water consumption.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Environmental Quality (department) to establish a fee schedule;<hr><ltbullet>allows the Water Development Coordinating Council (state council) to establish a fee schedule beginning on July 1, 2026, subject to approval by the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet>exempts a special district from certain fee requirements to pay the fees established by the department and state council; <hr><ltbullet>outlines requirements related to the fee schedules;<hr><ltbullet>allows the department to establish a financial incentive to comply with certain criteria;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the collection of fees by the department and, pending approval by the Legislature, the collection of fees by the state council;<hr><ltbullet>creates an exemption for a wholesale water supplier and agricultural water from the fees;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the deposit of fees into the Water Infrastructure Fund less the department's costs;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department and state council to report on the fee schedule to the Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Interim Committee;<hr><ltbullet>requires monitoring of fees; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Funeral Services Amendments
description: This bill addresses natural organic reduction.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>allows a funeral service establishment to offer natural organic reduction;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a funeral service director meet certain requirements if the funeral service director offers natural organic reduction;<hr><ltbullet>grants immunity to a funeral service establishment that relies on a natural organic reduction authorization form in carrying out natural organic reduction;<hr><ltbullet>updates a funeral service establishment's recordkeeping requirements;<hr><ltbullet>provides requirements for accepting remains for natural organic reduction;<hr><ltbullet>limits liability for a funeral service establishment providing natural organic reduction;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for authorizing natural organic reduction;<hr><ltbullet>describes the procedure for natural organic reduction;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for the final disposition of remains from the natural organic reduction process;<hr><ltbullet>categorizes the use of remains from natural organic reduction to grow food as unlawful; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Estate Planning Recodification
description: This bill recodifies and amends statutes related to estate planning.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>coordinates definitions between Title 75, Utah Uniform Probate Code, Title 75A, Fiduciaries, and Title 75B, Trusts;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the definitions for Title 75, Utah Uniform Probate Code;<hr><ltbullet>recodifies and clarifies a statute regarding the effective date of Title 75, Utah Uniform Probate Code;<hr><ltbullet>recodifies Title 75, Chapter 7, Utah Uniform Trust Code, to Title 75B, Chapter 2, Uniform Trust Code;<hr><ltbullet>recodifies Title 75, Chapter 12, Uniform Directed Trust Act, to Title 75B, Chapter 3, Uniform Directed Trust Act;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to explain that certain definitions will not be enacted in Title 75A, Chapter 9, Uniform Health-Care Decisions Act, if this bill and S.B. 134, Health-Care Decisions Act Amendments, both pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to address a technical conflict with a cross-reference change if this bill and H.B. 334, Guardianships and Supported Decision-Making Agreements Amendments, both pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Dog Related Liability Amendments

highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that a dog owner is not liable for injury or death caused by the owner's dog to a trespasser; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill enacts provisions regarding a student's reasonable expectation of individual privacy and personal modesty in the public education system.

title: Utah-Ireland Trade Commission
description: This bill creates the Utah-Ireland Trade Commission within the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates the Utah-Ireland Trade Commission (trade commission) within the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity (office);<hr><ltbullet>describes the membership, purpose, and duties of the trade commission;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the office staff the trade commission;<hr><ltbullet>requires an annual report; <hr><ltbullet>authorizes the office to solicit funds for certain purposes and to account for those funds; and<hr><ltbullet>provides a sunset date of July 1, 2030.

title: Education Scholarship Amendments
description: This bill amends the Carson Smith Opportunity Scholarship Program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires scholarship granting organizations to verify Utah residency through multiple forms of documentation;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits scholarship granting organizations from charging any fees to families;<hr><ltbullet>mandates independent audits of all scholarship granting organizations regardless of scholarship amount;<hr><ltbullet>requires public disclosure of all third-party contracts and associated fees;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a formal appeals process for denied expense reimbursements;<hr><ltbullet>limits extracurricular and physical education expenses to 20% of the scholarship amount;<hr><ltbullet>requires specific deadlines be created for scholarship notification and acceptance;<hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement for home school affidavit documentation; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Veteran Access to State Parks
description: This bill addresses a program that offers a discounted annual pass to state parks for qualified veterans.

title: Uniform Family Law Arbitration Act
description: This bill enacts the Uniform Family Law Arbitration Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides the scope of the Uniform Family Law Arbitration Act (act);<hr><ltbullet>addresses the law that is applicable to arbitration in a family law dispute;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for an arbitration agreement for a family law dispute;<hr><ltbullet>allows a party to initiate arbitration by giving notice to the other party in accordance with the arbitration agreement or the laws governing contractual arbitration;<hr><ltbullet>provides the framework for motions for judicial relief involving a family law arbitration;<hr><ltbullet>provides the qualification and selection requirements for an arbitrator;<hr><ltbullet>requires certain disclosures by an arbitrator, the parties, and the attorneys representing the parties;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the disqualification of an arbitrator;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the participation of, and a communication by, an attorney or other individual in family law arbitration;<hr><ltbullet>allows a court or arbitrator to make a temporary order when there is an arbitration of a family law dispute;<hr><ltbullet>addresses protection orders in family law arbitration;<hr><ltbullet>provides the powers and duties of an arbitrator;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the recording of an arbitration hearing;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for an award by an arbitrator in a family law arbitration;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the confirmation or correction of an award in a family law arbitration;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the vacation or amendment of an award in a family law arbitration by a court;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the requirements for a party seeking to clarify a confirmed award;<hr><ltbullet>requires a court to enter a judgment for a family law arbitration award;<hr><ltbullet>allows a court to seal or redact a document that was part of the family law arbitration;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the modification and enforcement of a confirmed award or judgment from a family law arbitration;<hr><ltbullet>addresses when an appeal from a family law arbitration may be taken;<hr><ltbullet>addresses immunity of an arbitrator in a family law arbitration;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the uniformity of application and construction of the act;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act; and<hr><ltbullet>provides a transitional provision.

title: Domestic Relations Recodification
description: This bill recodifies and amends statutes related to domestic relations.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the jurisdiction of the juvenile and district courts with regards to adoptions;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies and coordinates definitions related to domestic relations;<hr><ltbullet>recodifies and amends Title 78B, Chapter 15, Utah Uniform Parentage Act, to Title 81, Chapter 5, Uniform Parentage Act, including changing the term, "support-enforcement agency" to "child support services agency";<hr><ltbullet>recodifies and amends Title 78B, Chapter 14, Utah Uniform Interstate Family Support Act, to Title 81, Chapter 8, Uniform Interstate Family Support Act, including:<hr><ltbullet1>defining terms to coordinate with the definitions in Title 81, Chapter 5, Uniform Parentage Act; and<hr><ltbullet1>changing the term, "support-enforcement agency" to "child support services agency";<hr><ltbullet>recodifies Title 78B, Chapter 20, Uniform Deployed Parents Custody, Parent-time, and Visitation Act, to Title 81, Chapter 10, Uniform Deployed Parents Custody, Parent-time, and Visitation Act;<hr><ltbullet>recodifies Title 78B, Chapter 13, Utah Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act, to Title 81, Chapter 11, Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act;<hr><ltbullet>recodifies Title 78B, Chapter 6, Part 1, Utah Adoption Act, to Title 81, Chapter 13, Adoption;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies provisions regarding adoption, including: <hr><ltbullet1>definitions related to adoption;<hr><ltbullet1>access to adoption records by a potential birth father that is allowed to intervene in an adoption proceeding;<hr><ltbullet1>that a petitioner's home includes a temporary place of abode in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet1>clarifying the time periods associated with adoption; and<hr><ltbullet1>requirements for adopting an adult; <hr><ltbullet>allows an adoption proceeding to be brought in a judicial district rather than a county;<hr><ltbullet>repeals a requirement requiring a petition for adoption of a minor child to be filed within 30 days of the minor child being placed in the home of the prospective adoptive parents;<hr><ltbullet>repeals a statute requiring a person filing a petition for the adoption of an alien child to include written evidence of lawful admission of the alien child;<hr><ltbullet>recodifies Title 78B, Chapter 24, Uniform Unregulated Child Custody Transfer Act, to Title 81, Chapter 14, Uniform Unregulated Child Custody Transfer Act;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to address a technical conflict with a reference if this bill and H.B. 329, Homeless Services Amendments, both pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to coordinate changes to statutes related to adoption documents if this bill and H.B. 129, Adoption Records Access Amendments, both pass and become law; <hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to change the reference in a statute if this bill and H.B. 30, Indian Family Preservation Act Amendments, both pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to modify a definition due to the repeal of a statute if this bill and H.B. 21, Criminal Code Recodification and Cross References, both pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to address inconsistent terminology if this bill and H.B. 141, Adoption Modifications, both pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to address inconsistent terminology if this bill and H.B. 283, Child and Family Services Amendments, both pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Eviction Amendments
description: This bill addresses provisions relating to owners and renters.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a new owner of a multifamily unit building provide notice of the change in ownership and any rent increase of 10% or greater than the monthly rent;<hr><ltbullet>permits a renter in a multifamily unit building to terminate an existing lease agreement if the renter provides written notice to the owner at least 60 days before the day on which the renter terminates the lease agreement;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an owner from imposing a rent increase for the first 90 days an owner owns a multifamily unit building;<hr><ltbullet>allows a jury or court to exercise discretion when entering a judgment for actual damages a jury or court in a proceeding involving a tenant and an owner; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Higher Education Development Areas
description: This bill enacts provisions relating to the development of property owned by certain higher education institutions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>authorizes certain higher education institutions to designate a development area consisting of property owned by the institution;<hr><ltbullet>provides a process for an institution to adopt a resolution designating a development area;<hr><ltbullet>requires an institution to establish a fund for revenue from the development area and provides for uses of money in the fund;<hr><ltbullet>provides limitations on a member of the board of trustees regarding participation in development actions and requires a member of a board of trustees to disclose a conflict before the board of trustees approves a development agreement;<hr><ltbullet>requires payment of privilege tax on leased property within a development area and describes the method for a county treasurer to distribute privilege tax revenue to the institution; and<hr><ltbullet>requires the board of trustees to provide an annual report to the Higher Education Appropriations Subcommittee for each development area.

title: Firearm and Firearm Accessory Modifications
description: This bill addresses firearms and firearm accessories.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires, beginning on January 1, 2027, a manufacturer or seller of gas-operated semiautomatic firearms that is manufacturing or selling the firearms to the government of the United States, a state, or a federally recognized tribe, to mark on the firearm that the firearm may only be used by a government employee in accordance with government policy;<hr><ltbullet>amends offenses related to a restricted person in possession of a dangerous weapon to include ammunition;<hr><ltbullet>makes possession of a firearm on which the identifying marks have been altered or removed a crime;<hr><ltbullet>makes possession of a firearm without identifying marks a crime;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions requiring the Bureau of Criminal Identification to inform local law enforcement when a prohibited person attempts to purchase a firearm from a firearm dealer;<hr><ltbullet>creates a criminal offense, beginning on January 1, 2027, for an adult to possess a machinegun firearm attachment;<hr><ltbullet>creates a waiting period, with certain exemptions, between the purchase of a firearm from a dealer and the delivery of the firearm to the purchaser;<hr><ltbullet>creates a criminal offense, beginning on January 1, 2027, for a person to import, sell, manufacture, transfer, receive, or possess, in certain circumstances, a gas-operated semiautomatic firearm;<hr><ltbullet>requires a firearm dealer to post a written notice of potential liability for the negligent storage of a firearm and provides a penalty for failure to post the notice;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Public Safety to create a system for individuals who possess certain gas-operated semiautomatic firearms before January 1, 2027, to register the firearm with the department;<hr><ltbullet>creates a criminal offense beginning on January 1, 2027, for a person to import, sell, manufacture, transfer, receive, or possess, in certain circumstances, a large-capacity ammunition feeding device;<hr><ltbullet>expands the criminal offense of altering a serial number on a pistol or revolver beginning on January 1, 2027, to include all firearms and large-capacity ammunition feeding devices; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Electric Utility Amendments
description: This bill creates requirements for providing electrical service to large-scale electrical loads.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes alternative processes for providing electric service to customers with large electrical loads;<hr><ltbullet>exempts service provided under this chapter from certain rate regulation requirements while maintaining safety and reliability standards;<hr><ltbullet>creates procedures for submitting, evaluating, and contracting for large-scale electrical service requests;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for qualified electric utilities and large-scale generation providers serving large load customers;<hr><ltbullet>creates accounting and operational transparency requirements to protect retail customers;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a framework for closed private generation systems and connected generation systems;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Public Service Commission (commission) to investigate the feasibility of a large load flexible tariff; and<hr><ltbullet>requires the commission to conduct periodic reviews of the program and report to the Legislature.

title: Metal Purchase and Theft Amendments
description: This bill concerns the purchase and theft of metal including catalytic converters.

title: Health Care Decisions Act Amendments
description: This bill enacts the Uniform Health Care Decisions Act.

title: Course Choice Empowerment
description: This bill establishes a private online course choice program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes standards for educational software and hardware procurement;<hr><ltbullet>removes references to a contractor from the Statewide Online Education Program statute;<hr><ltbullet>creates an online course choice program specifically for private school students;<hr><ltbullet>requires the program be administered by an independent program manager contracted by the State Board of Education;<hr><ltbullet>allows eligible students to earn credits through online courses, including courses in blended-learning environments;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a contract administrator role to oversee program implementation; <hr><ltbullet>authorizes the state board to contract with multiple entities for different program functions; <hr><ltbullet>provides for state oversight while maintaining program independence; <hr><ltbullet>creates transition provisions if program manager contracts end;<hr><ltbullet>requires separate funding from public education programs;<hr><ltbullet>requires the program manager to:<hr><ltbullet1>approve and oversee course providers;<hr><ltbullet1>approve and oversee courses offered;<hr><ltbullet1>establish payment structure for courses; and <hr><ltbullet1>annually report on program performance; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Law Enforcement DNA Amendments
description: This bill addresses the collection and analysis of DNA by law enforcement.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends when a DNA specimen for an individual taken at the time of booking may be processed to include, among other circumstances, to allow the processing of the individual's DNA 60 days after the day on which any warrant of arrest has been issued for the individual if the warrant is still outstanding;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the level of offense that must be charged or convicted before an individual who had the individual's DNA specimen taken may be assessed a fee;<hr><ltbullet>requires a prosecutor to notify an individual charged with an offense requiring collection of the individual's DNA of the individual's rights regarding the destruction of the individual's DNA specimen in certain circumstances; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: App Store Accountability Act
description: This bill enacts provisions governing app store operations and creates requirements for age verification and parental consent.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires app store providers to:<hr><ltbullet1>verify a user's age category;<hr><ltbullet1>obtain parental consent for minor accounts;<hr><ltbullet1>notify users and parents of significant changes;<hr><ltbullet1>share age category and consent data with developers; and<hr><ltbullet1>protect age verification data;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits app store providers from:<hr><ltbullet1>enforcing contracts against minors without parental consent; and<hr><ltbullet1>misrepresenting parental content disclosures;<hr><ltbullet>requires developers to:<hr><ltbullet1> verify age category and consent status through app stores; and<hr><ltbullet1>notify app stores of significant changes;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits developers from:<hr><ltbullet1>enforcing contracts against minors without verified parental consent; and<hr><ltbullet1>misrepresenting parental content disclosures;<hr><ltbullet>designates violations of certain provisions as deceptive trade practices;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Consumer Protection to establish standards for age verification methods;<hr><ltbullet>creates a private right of action for parents of harmed minors;<hr><ltbullet>provides a safe harbor for compliant developers; and<hr><ltbullet>includes a severability clause.

title: Legislative Activities Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to the Legislative Management Committee (LMC), the State Capitol Preservation Board, and the Legislature.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that LMC oversees workplace harassment and discrimination policy governance and updates references to that policy;<hr><ltbullet>provides that LMC shall oversee and develop policies governing branch-wide internal administrative matters for the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet>eliminates certain administrative duties of the presiding officer and the majority and minority leaders of each house and the chairman of LMC;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the LMC Subcommittee on Oversight;<hr><ltbullet>eliminates the Legislature's responsibility to print, store, and distribute the Utah Code Annotated;<hr><ltbullet>repeals a provision governing legislators who attend meetings of the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet>updates the definition of a legislative procurement unit to include the House, Senate, or a staff office of the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet>repeals certain quinquennial reporting requirements applicable to legislative boards and the Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel; <hr><ltbullet>for the State Capitol Preservation Board:<hr><ltbullet1>specifies certain rules that the board shall promulgate to govern, administer, and regulate capitol hill;<hr><ltbullet1>provides that the board's authority to promulgate a rule described above does not restrict LMC from adopting a similar policy on behalf of the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet1>provides that if there is a conflict between a board rule and an LMC policy the LMC policy prevails; and<hr><ltbullet1>directs the executive director of the board to notify and consult with the president of the Senate and the speaker of the House of Representatives when a person appeals an administrative denial of a requested activity in the legislative area;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a bill summary prepared by a staff member of the Senate or the House of Representatives, or by a staff office for the Legislature, is not evidence of legislative intent;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the control and use of office spaces on Capitol hill; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Sexual Crimes Amendments
description: This bill addresses sexual crimes.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides a definition of a female breast for certain sexual and sexual exploitation offenses that includes a breast that is undeveloped or partially developed;<hr><ltbullet>expands the definition of "child sexual abuse material" to include a minor observing or being used for sexually explicit conduct;<hr><ltbullet>expands the definition of "sexually explicit conduct" concerning certain bodily functions for certain offenses;<hr><ltbullet>changes the mental state necessary to commit the offense of sexual exploitation of a minor;<hr><ltbullet>expands the offense of sexual exploitation of a minor to include when an actor accesses child sexual abuse material with the intent to view;<hr><ltbullet>provides a safe harbor provision for certain employees and independent contractors who are required to access or view child sexual abuse material within the scope of employment;<hr><ltbullet>changes the mental state necessary to commit the offense of aggravated sexual exploitation of a minor;<hr><ltbullet>amends the offense of aggravated sexual exploitation of a minor to remove a lesser penalty for circumstances when the child sexual abuse material depicts an individual who is 14 years old or older or pubescent; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Natural Resources Modifications
description: This bill modifies provisions related to hunting and public lands under the Department of Natural Resources.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Guide, Outfitter, and Spotter Fund;<hr><ltbullet>establishes when the use of a guide, outfitter, or spotter is unlawful;<hr><ltbullet>requires registration of a guide, outfitter, and spotter with the Division of Wildlife Resources (division);<hr><ltbullet>provides for division rulemaking related to guides, outfitters, and spotters;<hr><ltbullet>outlines prohibited activities and penalties for violations related to guides, outfitters, and spotters;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the provisions related to guides, outfitters, and spotters do not apply to private land;<hr><ltbullet>removes a requirement for the Public Lands Policy Coordinating Office (PLPCO) to prepare and submit a constitutional defense plan;<hr><ltbullet>renames the executive director of PLPCO as the advisor on public lands;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the advisor of PLPCO and director of the Office of Energy Development:<hr><ltbullet1>are appointed by the governor with the advice and consent of the Senate; and<hr><ltbullet1>report to the executive director of the Department of Natural Resources, upon the executive director's request;<hr><ltbullet>repeals a committee required to inventory and map R.S. 2477 rights-of-way;<hr><ltbullet>repeals regulation related to hunting guide registration by the Division of Professional Licensing; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill addresses the Notice of Intent to Sell Nonpublic Personal Information Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the liability and remedy under the Notice of Intent to Sell Nonpublic Personal Information Act (act) is an individual action and not a class action or action in a representative capacity;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the statute or limitations;<hr><ltbullet>finds that the act's prohibition of class actions since January 1, 2004, is a remedy provision and not procedural; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: Income Tax Contributions Amendments
description: This bill provides for taxpayer contributions for statewide hunger relief on the income tax return.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes the Statewide Hunger Relief Fund (fund);<hr><ltbullet>allows taxpayers, through the individual income tax return, to contribute to the fund to support the Utah Food Bank in fighting hunger statewide;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Tax Commission to make annual disbursements from the fund to the Utah Food Bank;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the removal of the contribution from the income tax return if the contribution does not generate a certain amount of money each year for a specified period; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Local Land Use Regulation Restrictions

title: Public Utility Expenditures Amendments
description: This bill  prohibits a qualified utility from recovering in rates expenses related to advertising, lobbying, and political activities.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a qualified utility from recovering in rates certain advertising, lobbying, and political influence expenses;<hr><ltbullet>requires a qualified utility to file an annual report detailing prior year expenses related to advertising, lobbying, and political activities;<hr><ltbullet>specifies information that must be included in the annual report; and<hr><ltbullet>establishes penalties for a qualified utility that improperly recovers prohibited expenses.

title: Legislative Audit Amendments
description: This bill enacts and amends provisions governing the duties and powers of the legislative auditor general.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>restates the authority of the legislative auditor general; <hr><ltbullet>amends provisions governing information that may be subject to federal law and is requested by the legislative auditor general from an entity, including the State Tax Commission;<hr><ltbullet>excludes certain information provided to the legislative auditor general from the definition of "record";<hr><ltbullet> permits an entity to provide certain privileged items to the legislative auditor general; <hr><ltbullet>requires an entity that withholds certain privileged items from the legislative auditor general to expressly assert a privilege;<hr><ltbullet>permits the legislative auditor general to contest a privilege claim;<hr><ltbullet>requires, in certain circumstances, an entity to submit privileged items to an arbitrator to determine a privilege claim;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the legislative auditor general to provide certain information to an audited entity;<hr><ltbullet>amends the definition of "chief officer" for purposes of an entity responding to a legislative audit;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions governing an audit response plan and an update to a plan;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the legislative auditor general to review and monitor the Utah System of Higher Education;<hr><ltbullet>coordinates enactment of provisions with S.J.R. 4, Joint Resolution Amending Court Rules on Attorney Confidentiality; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical corrections.

title: Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Adjustments
description: This bill amends provisions related to the Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>reduces the amount of time that must elapse before an offender who is on the Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry for an offense requiring lifetime registration is:<hr><ltbullet1>able to first petition for early removal from the registry; and<hr><ltbullet1>able to file an additional petition for early removal if the offender's previous petition is denied;<hr><ltbullet>contains a coordination clause to coordinate changes between this bill and S.B. 41, Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Pari-mutuel Horse Racing
description: This bill creates the Pari-mutuel Horse Racing Commission and allows for pari-mutuel horse racing and wagering.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Pari-mutuel Horse Racing Commission (commission);<hr><ltbullet>provides for the commission's membership, authority, and duties;<hr><ltbullet>requires the state auditor to audit the commission's accounting;<hr><ltbullet>allows the commission to issue licenses and permits for pari-mutuel events;<hr><ltbullet>allows the commission to enforce fines and penalties for permit and license violations;<hr><ltbullet>requires voters to approve pari-mutuel horse racing and wagering within a county before the commission issues permits in the county; <hr><ltbullet>requires a permittee other than a political subdivision to post a bond or other financial assurance;<hr><ltbullet>provides for simulcasting and advance deposit pari-mutuel wagering;<hr><ltbullet>provides for takeouts of certain percentages from the winning wagers for certain purposes;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits bribery, touting, and wagering involving minors;<hr><ltbullet>requires the identification of horses;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits certain treatment of animals in relation to pari-mutuel events; and<hr><ltbullet>creates restricted accounts.

title: Nonjudicial Adjustment Amendments
description: This bill modifies the provisions of the Indigent Defense Act in relation to nonjudicial adjustments and access to legal counsel.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a minor from declining to enter into a nonjudicial adjustment agreement unless the minor has received advice from legal counsel, with exceptions;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the duties of the Indigent Defense Commission to include encouraging the provision of resources for minors to receive access to legal advice when considering a nonjudicial adjustment;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the duties of the Office of Indigent Defense Services to require the office to provide no-cost legal advice for minors considering a nonjudicial adjustment;<hr><ltbullet>permits the Office of Indigent Defense Services to employ or contract with an attorney to provide legal advice to minors considering a nonjudicial adjustment;<hr><ltbullet>creates procedures for giving notice of requirements before declining a nonjudicial adjustment agreement; and<hr><ltbullet>makes clarifying amendments.

title: Talent Connect
description: This bill establishes a statewide talent portal for high-demand jobs and creates a cooperative education program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates a statewide talent portal for high-demand jobs in Utah;<hr><ltbullet>defines high-demand jobs based on growth rate, wages, and societal impact;<hr><ltbullet>requires a platform that connects Utah employers with qualified candidates from higher education institutions;<hr><ltbullet>mandates mobile access to the talent portal;<hr><ltbullet>requires integration with state labor market data and workforce systems;<hr><ltbullet>establishes regular updates of high-demand job categories based on market trends;<hr><ltbullet>creates requirements for data analytics and employer verification systems;<hr><ltbullet>requires annual reporting on portal metrics and outcomes;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a cooperative education pilot program;<hr><ltbullet>creates a strategic partnerships between Utah universities and engineering efforts;<hr><ltbullet>requires participating employers to provide full-time paid cooperative education work experiences;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a dual mentorship structure with academic and industry advisors;<hr><ltbullet>creates a framework for granting academic credit for cooperative education experiences;<hr><ltbullet>requires development of an electronic management system for program administration;<hr><ltbullet>establishes data collection and analysis requirements for program evaluation;<hr><ltbullet>mandates annual reporting on program effectiveness and workforce impact;<hr><ltbullet>establishes liability and risk management protocols for participating institutions; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Government Records Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to the Government Records Access and Management Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a summary of government records requirements to be developed and provided to employees of a governmental entity;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions relating to fees charged in relation to a record request;<hr><ltbullet>modifies requirements for responding to a record request, including:<hr><ltbullet1>deadlines;<hr><ltbullet1>a request for an expedited response;<hr><ltbullet1>appeals; and<hr><ltbullet1>other requirements;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions relating to the State Records Committee;<hr><ltbullet>requires a governmental entity to conduct an annual review of records retention requirements and compliance with those requirements;<hr><ltbullet>amends requirements for an ordinance or policy adopted by a political subdivision in relation to public records;<hr><ltbullet>makes it a crime to destroy a record with the intent to avoid disclosure in response to a pending record request; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Modifications to Election Law
description: This bill modifies provisions relating to elections.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a county clerk to coordinate with local post offices to ensure the optimal handling of ballots;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a poll watcher may observe the signature-verification process for a petition to qualify a candidate for a primary election ballot (candidate petition) or for a written request to remove a signature from a candidate petition;<hr><ltbullet>makes it unlawful for a poll watcher to reveal certain information observed during the process described in the preceding paragraph;<hr><ltbullet>requires an election officer to conduct an audit of signature comparisons made for a candidate petition;<hr><ltbullet> requires an election officer who engages in the signature-verification process for a candidate petition to certify a certain percentage of signatures submitted beyond the required signature-gathering threshold;<hr><ltbullet>addresses viewing by a candidate or a candidate's campaign representative of a complete, unredacted signature packet, or a request to remove a signature from a signature packet, relating to a candidate petition for the candidate's election race;<hr><ltbullet>provides the ability for a voter to track a candidate petition recently signed by the voter and certain information relating to verification of the signature;    <hr><ltbullet>in relation to a signature packet for a candidate petition, establishes requirements for:<hr><ltbullet1>submitting the packet;<hr><ltbullet1>maintaining a chain of custody for a packet; and<hr><ltbullet1>storing a packet;<hr><ltbullet>grants rulemaking authority to the director of elections within the Office of the Lieutenant Governor;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to deadlines and the calculation of time in the Election Code;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies and modifies deadlines in the Election Code;<hr><ltbullet>includes coordination clauses:<hr><ltbullet1>adding Election Day as a legal holiday, to the repeal and reenactment of Section 63G-1-301 in this bill, if this bill and H.B. 351, Election Day Amendments, both pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>adding Easter Sunday as a legal holiday, to the repeal and reenactment of Section 63G-1-301 in this bill, if this bill and S.B. 259, State Holy Days, both pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet1>in the coordination clause described above, adding other changes made to Section 63G-1-301 in S.B. 259 to the repeal and reenactment of that section in this bill; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Municipal Broadband Service Amendments
description: This bill addresses a municipality's provision of a broadband service.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements and limitations in relation to a municipality providing a broadband service;<hr><ltbullet>addresses bonding, reporting, and public disclosure relating to the provision of a broadband service by a municipality; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Point of the Mountain State Land Authority Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to the Point of the Mountain State Land Authority.
