title: Guardianship Modifications
description: This bill addresses guardianships.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>for a guardianship proceeding on and after May 7, 2025, requires the court to make a finding regarding whether an incapacitated person is mentally incompetent and is not permitted to vote in an election or hold office in this state under Utah Constitution, Article IV, Section 6;<hr><ltbullet>for an incapacitated person for whom a guardian was appointed before May 7, 2025, creates a presumption in certain circumstances that the incapacitated person is mentally incompetent and is not permitted to vote in an election or hold office in this state under Utah Constitution, Article IV, Section 6; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Public Employee Negotiation Amendments
description: This bill addresses collective bargaining for public employees.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the Labor Relations Board (board);<hr><ltbullet>describes the composition and duties of the board;<hr><ltbullet>describes the entities the board may employ;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the board's rulemaking authority;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the board to subpoena witnesses and administer oaths;<hr><ltbullet>establishes who may serve as counsel for public employers and the board;<hr><ltbullet>creates protections for public employees regarding self-organization;<hr><ltbullet>allows a public employer to deduct an employee's dues for a collective bargaining unit from an employee's pay;<hr><ltbullet>requires that labor organizations represent employees without discriminations;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the board investigate a petition on a representation question under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>establishes criteria and the function of a representation election at the direction of the board;<hr><ltbullet>establishes who may represent a public employer in collective bargaining;<hr><ltbullet>establishes management rights of a public employer;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a duty to bargain collectively for both the public employer and an exclusive representative;<hr><ltbullet>describes what a collective bargaining agreement shall contain;<hr><ltbullet>permits and describes the mediation of disputes relating to collective bargaining;<hr><ltbullet>describes how to initiate fact finding relating to a dispute regarding collective bargaining;<hr><ltbullet>establishes fact finding proceedings in a dispute related to collective bargaining;<hr><ltbullet>allows arbitration for a dispute resulting from collective bargaining;<hr><ltbullet>requires the board to establish an education course for fact finders and arbitrators;<hr><ltbullet>describes an unfair labor practice of a public employer;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the process by which an unfair labor practice is investigated and resolved;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a hearing process for an unfair labor practice complaint hearing;<hr><ltbullet>describes the process of the court enforcement and review of a board order;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits police officers from engaging in strikes;<hr><ltbullet>establishes criteria for mediation of a dispute under certain circumstances; and<hr><ltbullet>establishes the criteria for arbitration under certain circumstances.

title: Governmental Immunity Act Amendments
description: This bill amends the Governmental Immunity Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines a term;<hr><ltbullet>requires a governmental entity to file a statement with Division of Corporations and Commercial Code containing:<hr><ltbullet1>any doing-business-as name the governmental entity utilizes;<hr><ltbullet1>the office or agent designated to receive service of a summons and complaint; and<hr><ltbullet1>the physical address to which service of a summons and complaint is to be delivered by hand or transmitted by mail;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a governmental entity from challenging the validity of a notice of claim, or the sufficiency of service of a summons and complaint, if the governmental entity:<hr><ltbullet1>fails to file or update the statement described above; and<hr><ltbullet1>has actual notice of the notice of claim or the summons and complaint;<hr><ltbullet>if a challenge described above is not prohibited, requires a claimant to prove that the claimant used reasonable diligence in attempting to discover the identity of a governmental entity using a doing-business-as name; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: School Discipline Amendments
description: This bill regulates the use of emergency safety interventions on a student in a school.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>consolidates and clarifies existing school physical intervention provisions into a single section of code;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Board of Education to establish administrative rules for physical intervention in schools;<hr><ltbullet>establishes standards for use of physical restraint in schools;<hr><ltbullet>defines allowed incidences of seclusion in schools;<hr><ltbullet>requires local education agencies to collect and report data on incidents of student confinement;<hr><ltbullet>provides for investigation and enforcement requirements;<hr><ltbullet>outlines liability protections and exceptions; <hr><ltbullet>establishes consequences for violations of the law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Local Health Department Amendments
description: This bill addresses provisions related to local health departments and the Department of Environmental Quality.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Environmental Quality (department) and each local health department to enter into a cooperative agreement for providing environmental health services;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the governance committee comprised of department and local health department personnel:<hr><ltbullet1>review all department funding;<hr><ltbullet1>review whether funds allocated by contract or cooperative agreement are subject to requirements meeting or exceeding the minimum performance standards created by the department; and<hr><ltbullet1>create a process for exempting certain applications for federal funding from committee review;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department to reimburse a local health department for all costs associated with collecting a civil penalty under Title 19, Environmental Quality Code; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Law Enforcement Usage of Artificial Intelligence
description: This bill concerns the use of artificial intelligence by law enforcement.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a law enforcement agency to have a policy concerning the law enforcement agency's use of generative artificial intelligence;<hr><ltbullet>requires a police report or other law enforcement record to include a disclaimer if the report or record was created wholly or partially by using generative artificial intelligence; and<hr><ltbullet>requires the author of a police report or other law enforcement record that was created wholly or partially by using generative artificial intelligence to certify that the author has read and reviewed the report or record for accuracy.

title: Diesel Emissions Reduction Amendments
description: This bill creates a voluntary registry for certain non-road diesel engines.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>directs the Division of Air Quality (division) to create a voluntary registry for certain non-road diesel engines;<hr><ltbullet>prevents the division from paying a replacement incentive to an owner of a non-road diesel engine not on the registry;<hr><ltbullet>requires a registrant of a non-road diesel engine to pay a registration fee;<hr><ltbullet> requires the division to deposit registration fees into the Environmental Mitigation and Response Fund;<hr><ltbullet>grants the division rulemaking authority to implement the provisions; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: School District Modifications
description: This bill addresses creation of new school districts and the transition process from divided to new school districts.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>enacts dates regarding the redistricting of local school board districts after the creation of certain new school districts;<hr><ltbullet>amends the duties of the Office of the Legislative Auditor General to include receiving and providing certain information during the transition process from divided to new school districts;<hr><ltbullet>extends, by an additional year, the rights of transferred employees regarding salary and benefits;<hr><ltbullet>reduces the body of voters whose approval is required to create a new school district to voters within the proposed new school district;<hr><ltbullet>reduces the threshold for interlocal participants to propose a new school district to a majority of municipalities that are participants in the interlocal agreement;<hr><ltbullet>amends certain dates regarding election cycles following the creation of a new school district;<hr><ltbullet>amends certain deadlines for the duties of municipal legislative bodies, county legislative bodies, local school boards, and other entities under certain circumstances after the creation of a new school district;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions regarding the transition from a divided school district to new and reorganized new school districts, including:<hr><ltbullet1>school district employee and other personnel issues;<hr><ltbullet1>records of the divided school district;<hr><ltbullet1>the actual transfer of funds, property, assets, and liabilities;<hr><ltbullet1>retrospectively voiding certain agreements or policies; and<hr><ltbullet1>resolution of disputes between school districts through an agreed upon or appointed arbiter;<hr><ltbullet>requires a government entity to send an invoice before requiring payment of past fees before processing a new request; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Protective Orders Amendments
description: This bill addresses protective orders.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms for cohabitant abuse protective orders; <hr><ltbullet>provides that a court may treat a petition for a protective order as a request for a no-fault cohabitant abuse protective order only if the petitioner and the respondent agree to the order and the terms of the order;<hr><ltbullet>allows a court to grant a no-fault cohabitant abuse protective order if the parties agree to the terms of the order;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the modification of a no-fault cohabitant abuse protective order;<hr><ltbullet>requires a no-fault cohabitant abuse protective order include a credible threat finding;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a no-fault cohabitant abuse protective order may not be introduced as evidence in a civil or criminal proceeding that the respondent committed domestic violence or abuse;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that a no-fault cohabitant abuse protective order does not prevent a petitioner from obtaining an ex parte cohabitant abuse protective order or a cohabitant abuse protective order;<hr><ltbullet>modifies a cross-reference regarding the provisions of a cohabitant abuse protective order that are civil offenses; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Defendant Access to Evidence Amendments
description: This bill addresses a criminal defendant's access to evidence in a county jail.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the county sheriff to ensure that a jail inmate awaiting trial, sentencing, or disposition of criminal charges has:<hr><ltbullet1>a space to review discovery and other evidence or documents in the jail inmate's criminal case with the jail inmate's counsel; and<hr><ltbullet1>the means to access and review discovery and other evidence or documents in the jail inmate's criminal case;<hr><ltbullet>addresses how the jail inmate may access or review discovery, evidence, or other documents in jail;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a jail inmate's counsel has to ensure that certain discovery, evidence, or other documents are not left with the jail inmate at the jail; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Transportation Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to transportation items, transportation mobility plans, and adherence to proposed phases of certain transportation developments.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires cities and metropolitan planning organizations to identify transportation connectivity impediments and provide a report on plans to address transportation connectivity;<hr><ltbullet>requires periodic reporting and follow up on certain station area plans;<hr><ltbullet>requires property acquired by the Department of Transportation for a public transit purpose remain under the ownership of the Department of Transportation;<hr><ltbullet>designates certain legislative committees as recipients for certain required reports;<hr><ltbullet>creates requirements for air ambulance dispatch services;<hr><ltbullet>adjusts a sales and use tax earmark percentage to increase funding for transportation;<hr><ltbullet>extends a deadline for certain sales and use taxes to be allocated for public transit innovation grants;<hr><ltbullet>reinstates certain funding to the Department of Transportation for litter mitigation that was reduced due to the COVID-19 pandemic;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Transportation to adhere to phasing of projects if required by the environmental impact statement;<hr><ltbullet>repeals certain outdated language and makes other technical changes;<hr><ltbullet>allocates revenue for certain road projects;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Transportation and Salt Lake City to coordinate on certain traffic studies and planning;<hr><ltbullet>repeals certain highway-related name designations;<hr><ltbullet>provides maintenance responsibilities for certain street light infrastructure; and<hr><ltbullet>makes other technical changes.

title: Property Tax Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to property tax.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits taxpayers from receiving the homeowner's credit unless the taxpayer received the credit within the previous two years, beginning in 2026;<hr><ltbullet>removes requirements for annual inflation adjustments for the homeowner's credit;<hr><ltbullet>increases the household income limits and maximum credit amounts allowed for a renter's credit;<hr><ltbullet>changes the qualifications, scope, duration, and rates of interest applicable to the discretionary and nondiscretionary property tax deferral programs;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits taxpayers from receiving indigent abatement unless the taxpayer received the abatement within the previous two years, beginning in 2026;<hr><ltbullet>requires a county auditor to include information on the property tax valuation notice regarding the availability of tax deferral programs;<hr><ltbullet>requires a county treasurer to include information on the tax notice regarding the amount of outstanding taxes and interest for taxpayers who receive a deferral;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits taxpayers from receiving more than one of certain forms of property tax relief;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to address substantive and technical conflicts if this bill and H.B. 20, Property Tax Code Recodification, both pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Federal Guidance Letter Amendments

title: Guardianship Amendments
description: This bill addresses a guardianship for an individual with a severe intellectual disability.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms for guardianship;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies court jurisdiction for guardianships;<hr><ltbullet>enacts a guardianship proceeding for an individual with a severe intellectual disability;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the applicability of a guardianship proceeding for an individual with a severe intellectual disability;<hr><ltbullet>enacts certain rights for an individual with a severe intellectual disability for which a full guardianship is imposed;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for a guardianship proceeding for an individual with a severe intellectual disability, including the requirements for the petition, venue, and in-person hearings;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the appointment of:<hr><ltbullet1>an attorney for a respondent in a guardianship proceeding for an individual with a severe intellectual disability;<hr><ltbullet1>a physician, psychologist, physician assistant, or court visitor to examine the respondent; and<hr><ltbullet1>an emergency or temporary guardian while guardianship proceedings are pending;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a court may appoint a guardian for a respondent if the court makes certain findings;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the court shall prefer a full guardianship for an individual with a severe intellectual disability;<hr><ltbullet>requires the court to include certain provisions in an order of appointment;<hr><ltbullet>provides who may be a guardian for an individual with a severe intellectual disability;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the duties, powers, and rights of a guardian for an individual with a severe intellectual disability in a full guardianship;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the removal or resignation of a guardian for an individual with a severe intellectual disability;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the termination of a guardianship for an individual with a severe intellectual disability; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Real Estate Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to real estate.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>authorizes an association to establish by rule a minimum lease term of six months or less;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a homeowners' association fee for rentals does not apply to certain exempt persons;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a homeowners' association may only charge a fee to an owner that owns a rental within the homeowners' association once every 12 months;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a homeowners' association hold a meeting and approve a fee before imposing a fee on an owner that owns a rental within the homeowners' association;<hr><ltbullet>provides a remedy by which an owner may contest a fee a homeowners' association imposes for a rental;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a representative of a homeowners' association to act as attorney-in-fact for the owners in a homeowners' association for any disposition of common areas;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the circumstances under which a homeowners' association can prohibit or restrict the conversion of a grass park strip to water-efficient landscaping;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a homeowner to designate an individual other than the homeowner as the primary contact for the homeowner;<hr><ltbullet> defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a condominium owner provide the developer notice and an opportunity to repair any alleged design or construction defect before filing a lawsuit; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Property Tax Revisions
description: This bill modifies provisions in the Property Tax Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires counties to annually provide the State Tax Commission (commission) with a preliminary assessment book before delivery to the county auditor;<hr><ltbullet>requires the commission to take corrective action upon a county officer's noncompliance with assessment duties;<hr><ltbullet>describes forms of corrective action that the commission may take against a county officer;<hr><ltbullet>requires commission assistance upon a county officer's noncompliance with assessment duties for a certain period of time;<hr><ltbullet>increases the costs paid by counties that request and receive appraisal assistance from the commission;<hr><ltbullet>repeals newspaper publication requirements applicable to certain property tax increase proposals;<hr><ltbullet>requires taxing entities holding a public hearing for certain property tax increase proposals to allow for in-person or virtual participation;<hr><ltbullet>requires the property tax valuation notice provided by county auditors to include taxpayer instructions for appealing a property's valuation;<hr><ltbullet>removes tax payment information from the property tax valuation notice provided by county auditors;<hr><ltbullet>requires the commission to provide education and training to specified county officers in addition to hearing officers;<hr><ltbullet>requires county officers subject to the education and training requirements to complete the education and training before performing valuation-related work;<hr><ltbullet>allows the commission to require education and training for other county officers involved in property valuation;<hr><ltbullet>requires counties to ensure taxpayers have the ability to submit property valuation appeals through electronic means;<hr><ltbullet>requires counties to annually report appeals information to the commission for reporting to the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet>requires the tax notice provided by county treasurers to include information regarding payment options;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Multicounty Appraisal Trust to use trust funds to:<hr><ltbullet1>develop and maintain a statewide web portal for uniform access to property characteristics and features;<hr><ltbullet1>develop and maintain a statewide web portal for the uniform electronic filing of property valuation appeal applications; and<hr><ltbullet1>assist counties in reporting appeals information to the commission;<hr><ltbullet>establishes timing requirements for counties to complete a review of certain applications for farmland and urban farming property tax assessment required after land changes ownership; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Right to Appeal Amendments
description: This bill addresses a right to an appeal of an injunctive order.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and Court of Appeals;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms related to a civil action in which a trial court grants an injunctive order restraining the execution or enforcement of a state law or any part of a state law;<hr><ltbullet>grants a right to an appeal of an injunctive order in certain circumstances; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Estate Planning Amendments
description: This bill addresses issues related to estate planning.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates and amends definitions related to estate planning;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the requirements for making a will, including the requirements for testamentary capacity;<hr><ltbullet>amends the rule against perpetuities for a power of appointment;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the legal standard of proof for a guardianship;<hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement that a person alleged to be incapacitated be present at the guardianship hearing;<hr><ltbullet>allows a trustee to decant a trust in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the capacity to make a power of attorney;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the capacity to appoint an agent for purposes of an advanced health care directive;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the capacity required for a custodian for Title 75A, Chapter 8, Uniform Transfers to Minors Act;<hr><ltbullet>recodifies Title 75B, Chapter 1, Part 3, Asset Protection Trust;<hr><ltbullet>defines asset protection trust to include an irrevocable trust for which the settlor may be made a beneficiary by the act or action of another person;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an affidavit of solvency for an asset protection trust is discretionary;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a person may only bring a cause of action or claim for relief regarding a fraudulent or voidable transfer for assets transferred to the asset protection trust within the limitations period;<hr><ltbullet>provides that, if a trustee makes multiple transfers to an asset protection trust, a distribution is considered to be made from the most recent transfer;<hr><ltbullet>allows a trustee to convey property held in the asset protection trust to the settlor or beneficiary to secure financing;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the property has to be reconveyed to the trustee within a certain time period to not be considered a transfer for purposes of the limitations period;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to address a technical conflict with a cross-reference change if this bill and H.B. 334, Guardianships and Supported Decision-Making Agreements Amendments, both pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to coordinate technical and substantive changes if this bill and S.B. 100, Estate Planning Recodification, both pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Local Impact Mitigation Amendments
description: This bill enacts a local impact mitigation tax for oil and gas production.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>imposes a local impact mitigation tax on oil and gas that is produced within the state within a certain period and is saved, sold, or transported;<hr><ltbullet>provides for certain exemptions from the tax;<hr><ltbullet>requires quarterly payment of the tax from oil and gas producers;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Tax Commission to distribute tax revenue within a certain time to the counties from which the revenue was collected;<hr><ltbullet>provides for certain tax revenue distribution requirements for a county that receives tax revenue;<hr><ltbullet>limits the use of tax revenue to certain transportation-related mitigation projects;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Tax Commission to collect an administrative charge from the collected tax revenue;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits counties from imposing certain oil or gas mitigation fees;<hr><ltbullet>requires any county that receives tax revenue to report to the Legislature regarding the county's use of the tax revenue; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Parent-time and Custody Amendments
description: This bill addresses parent-time and custody.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that a court may not require a parent to disclose the parent's address if the parent relocated due to domestic violence or family violence by the other parent;<hr><ltbullet>addresses a change of custody or parent-time for a minor child who turns five years old;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the establishment and modification of a parent-time schedule;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the parent-time requirements upon the relocation of a parent;<hr><ltbullet>addresses telephone contact and virtual parent-time for a noncustodial parent when a parent relocates;<hr><ltbullet>requires the time periods for extended parent-time by a parent for summer break or off-track time to be consecutive;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the parent-time schedules to address consistency among the schedules;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the parent-time schedules for Mother's Day and Father's Day;<hr><ltbullet>removes Columbus Day and Veterans Day as holidays in the parent-time schedules;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to address a substantive conflict with the parent-time schedule for Juneteenth National Freedom Day if this bill and H.B. 370, State Holiday Modifications, both pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Emergency Medical Services
description: This bill addresses emergency medical services.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes that 911 ambulance services are essential services;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the respective duties of the Department of Health and Human Services, the Department of Public Safety, and the Bureau of Emergency Medical Services (bureau);<hr><ltbullet>where applicable, indicates the proper government agency or division, where an incorrect entity or agency is indicated;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Emergency Medical Services Critical Needs Account;<hr><ltbullet>for an emergency medical services grant in a rural county, increases the maximum allowable amount that the grant recipient may receive for use toward the purchase of vehicles;<hr><ltbullet>directs available but undistributed grant funds at the end of the year to be deposited into the Emergency Medical Services Critical Needs Account created under Section 53-2d-109;<hr><ltbullet>requires the bureau to establish designation requirements for training centers;<hr><ltbullet>modifies a notice requirement to require the bureau to provide a class A notice;<hr><ltbullet>subjects training centers to the disciplinary jurisdiction of the bureau;<hr><ltbullet>subjects an issuance of a notice of violation or order under the Emergency Medical Services Act to Title 63G, Chapter 4, Administrative Procedures Act;<hr><ltbullet>grants investigative authority to the bureau;<hr><ltbullet>makes it a class B misdemeanor to willfully disobey a valid subpoena or cease and desist letter from the bureau; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Municipal Land Use Exemption Amendments

title: Emergency Medical Services Modifications
description: This bill addresses ground ambulance interfacility transport services.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>grants authority to and requires municipalities and counties to ensure that a minimum level of ground ambulance interfacility transport services are provided within the respective municipality or county;<hr><ltbullet>requires a municipality or county to conduct a review and evaluation of emergency medical service provider's sevices every four years;<hr><ltbullet>requires a municipality or county to request competitive sealed proposals for the purpose of evaluating alternative qualified emergency medical service providers;<hr><ltbullet>removes the Bureau of Emergency Medical Services Management (bureau) from involvement in the process by which a municipality or county selects emergency medical service providers, except verifying and providing notice that an applicant emergency medical service provider meets minimum requirements; <hr><ltbullet>recognizes the bureau's jurisdiction to discipline non-911 ambulance service providers;<hr><ltbullet>requires a county or municipality to:<hr><ltbullet1>offer a first right to provide interfacility transports to the current 911 ambulance service provider;<hr><ltbullet1>conduct formal reviews of 911 service providers and interfacility transport service providers;<hr><ltbullet>grants investigative authority to the bureau;<hr><ltbullet>makes it a class B misdemeanor to willfully disobey a valid subpoena or cease and desist letter from the bureau; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Environmental Quality Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to the licensing and taxation of radioactive waste.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the requirements for a waste facility to renew or amend a radioactive waste license;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Tax Commission to deposit into an energy-related fund the portion of new tax revenue derived from a radioactive waste facility receiving radioactive waste from a new generator;<hr><ltbullet>creates a radioactive waste facility expansion tax on a radioactive waste facility that submits an application to the Division of Waste Management and Radiation Control to construct a new radioactive waste facility or expand an existing facility;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the payment and deposit of the radioactive waste facility expansion tax;<hr><ltbullet>implements a sunset date for the radioactive waste facility expansion tax; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Recycling and Waste Amendments
description: This bill addresses issues related to the disposal and recycling of electronic and solid waste.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines "community collection event";<hr><ltbullet>requires a manufacturer of a consumer electronic device to develop a public education program about a collection, reuse, or recycling program for a consumer electronic device;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Environmental Quality (department) to develop a public education program related to electronic and other waste;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department to publish information related to recycling programs and recycling resources on the department's website;<hr><ltbullet>removes an exception for the department to charge more than one fee for the same solid waste; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Voter Information Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to voter registration records.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that if a voter with a voter registration record that is classified as private signs a petition, the voter's name, address, and other information relating to the petition may be publicly disclosed to the same extent, and in the same manner, as a voter signing the petition who does not have a private voter registration record;<hr><ltbullet>requires a petition to contain a warning regarding the provision described in the preceding paragraph; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Financial Institution Tax Amendments
description: This bill modifies the formula for apportioning business income of financial institutions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>grants rulemaking authority to the State Tax Commission to establish the sales to include in the sales factor fraction for financial institutions; and<hr><ltbullet>provides that sales from Utah investment and trading activities of financial institutions are not sourced to Utah.

title: Child Care Revisions
description: This bill modifies provisions related to caring for children.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires licensure for a residential child care provider when providing child care for a certain number of qualifying children;<hr><ltbullet>requires certification for a residential child care provider when providing child care for a certain number of qualifying children;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions authorizing the Department of Health and Human Services to inspect the home of a certified child care provider under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a certified residential child care provider from providing child care to more than two qualifying children under certain ages;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions of criminal background check requirements for a child care provider; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Vehicle Emission Inspection Program Revisions
description: This bill amends provisions related to vehicle emissions inspections to enhance the ability to investigate whether an individual has avoided a required emissions inspection.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allows the Motor Vehicle Division to revoke the vehicle owner's registration if the vehicle owner has provided a false or an improper address to register a vehicle to avoid an emissions inspection; <hr><ltbullet>prohibits the Motor Vehicle Division from registering a motor vehicle if the owner of the motor vehicle has failed to pay a civil penalty for registering with a false or improper address;<hr><ltbullet>allows the State Tax Commission to recover costs of investigation or administration; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Electricity Supply Amendments
description: This bill creates requirements for providing electrical service to large-scale electrical loads.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes alternative processes for providing electric service to customers with large electrical loads;<hr><ltbullet>exempts service provided under this chapter from certain rate regulation requirements while maintaining safety and reliability standards;<hr><ltbullet>creates procedures for submitting, evaluating, and contracting for large-scale electrical service requests;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for qualified electric utilities and large-scale generation providers serving large load customers;<hr><ltbullet>creates accounting and operational transparency requirements to protect retail customers;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a framework for closed private generation systems and connected generation systems;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Public Service Commission (commission) to establish a large load flexible tariff;<hr><ltbullet>directs the commission to establish rules for allocating transmission costs between large load customers and retail customers; and<hr><ltbullet>requires the commission to conduct periodic reviews of the program and report to the Legislature.

title: Severance Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions relating to severance of oil, gas, and minerals.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>repeals and reenacts the severance tax credit for mining exploration to create an agreement and post-performance certificate process;<hr><ltbullet>schedules the repeal of the severance tax credit for mining exploration but requires legislative review before the repeal;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a taxpayer to claim the high cost infrastructure tax credit against severance tax liability instead of income tax liability;<hr><ltbullet>allows a taxpayer to claim the high cost infrastructure credit against severance tax liability during the 2025 taxable year for costs incurred during the 2024 taxable year;<hr><ltbullet>creates a new severance tax credit part and moves existing tax credits to the new part;<hr><ltbullet>addresses federal agency consultation before certain acts related to federal designations and minerals; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Inland Port Authority Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to the Utah Inland Port Authority.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Utah Inland Port Authority (authority) may facilitate and provide funding for the development of land in a project area, land related to land in a project area, and land adjacent to a project area, including: <hr><ltbullet1>the development of public infrastructure and improvements in a project area and directly adjacent to a project area; and <hr><ltbullet1>other infrastructure and improvements, including environmental sustainability projects, on or related to land in a project area;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the authority to provide funding through grant or agreement to another governmental entity to help fulfill the authority's duties and responsibilities;<hr><ltbullet>provides that contaminated land or land within a remediation project area may be used for a distribution center if the contaminated land is owned by a private landowner;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the authority executive director may make policies to allow the authority to classify a business proposal submitted to the authority by a nongovernment party as protected under Section 63G-2-305, for as long as is necessary to evaluate the proposal and determine whether to proceed or not proceed;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Utah Inland Port Authority Board (board) to conduct a review of the authority's statutory authority at least annually and, if necessary, recommend statutory changes to the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the structure of the board; <hr><ltbullet>provides that the authority may use funding to pay for all of or part of development of land within or adjacent to a project area; <hr><ltbullet>modifies the timeline for an optional extension of nonmunicipal differential payments and municipal deferential payments to the authority; <hr><ltbullet>provides that the authority may use primary municipality differential funds on environmental projects within or adjacent to authority jurisdictional land and economic development activities within or adjacent to authority jurisdictional land; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Congregate Care Modifications
description: This bill addresses congregate care programs.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Health and Human Services (department) to make reasonable effort to determine within seven days after receiving a completed report from the Bureau of Criminal Identification about an individual whether to grant direct patient access to the individual;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the department to establish fees for applications for certification for direct patient access;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the Office of Licensing (office) from:<hr><ltbullet1>placing a restriction or prohibition on new admissions based on the sole fact that the program is operating under a conditional license; or<hr><ltbullet1>altering or restricting the rights of a congregate care program based on the sole fact that the program has appealed an agency action or an appeal or adjudicative proceeding is pending;<hr><ltbullet> requires the office, if conditions are met, to:<hr><ltbullet1>inspect a congregate care program;<hr><ltbullet1>provide notice to a congregate care program; or <hr><ltbullet1>remove restrictions and conditions on a congregate care program's license; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Limited Purpose Local Government Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions affecting special districts.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a property owner special district may pledge all or a portion of revenue collected from an impact fee or other fee toward payment of a general obligation bond;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a basic special district to create a public infrastructure district;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a basic special district to fund:<hr><ltbullet1>the acquisition and construction of certain facilities; and <hr><ltbullet1>affordable housing projects;<hr><ltbullet>modifies requirements for determining consent of surface property owners within a public infrastructure district;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to the appointment or election of board members for a public infrastructure district;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to the annexation of property to, or withdrawal of property from, a public infrastructure district;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a public entity or private person may not receive funds from any portion of a public infrastructure district's property tax revenue without a resolution of the public infrastructure district's board authorizing the public entity or private person to receive the funds;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the process for a public infrastructure district to issue a bond; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Community Development Modifications
description: This bill deals with the use of certain funding to promote home ownership and provisions related to community reinvestment agencies.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Utah Inland Port Authority to provide general differential revenue from a project area to a non-profit housing fund to assist low-income individuals and families to achieve home ownership within a 15 mile radius of the project area that generated the general differential revenue;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a community reinvestment agency to pay all or any portion of the agency's housing allocation to a nonprofit housing fund for use in assisting individuals or families within the community to achieve or retain homeownership; <hr><ltbullet>requires a participation agreement to have a provision authorizing an agency to use funding that would otherwise be provided to a participant under the participation agreement to pay a participant's delinquent property tax or privilege tax or resolve a political subdivision lien against the participant;<hr><ltbullet>requires an agency to confirm with the county that a participant is not delinquent on property tax or privilege tax or subject to a political subdivision lien before providing the participant with funding under a participation agreement;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a county treasurer, in consultation with a community reinvestment agency, to use funding that would otherwise be distributed to a private participant under a participation agreement to resolve past-due property taxes, privilege taxes, or a political subdivision lien; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Digital Information Seizure Amendments
description: This bill concerns digital information contained on a computer or portable communication device seized by law enforcement.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>provides specific procedures and requirements regarding the copying and return of digital data on certain seized computers or portable communication devices;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a law enforcement agency or prosecuting agency from conditioning the return of digital data from a seized computer or portable communication device on the owner consenting to a search of the computer or portable communication device or providing the owner's password or otherwise unlocking the computer or portable communication device; <hr><ltbullet>requires a prosecuting attorney to notify the agency with custody of a seized computer or portable communication device within a specific time period when the prosecuting attorney determines that the computer or portable communication device no longer needs to be retained as evidence; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>repeals the Rural Health Care Facilities restricted account;<hr><ltbullet>appropriates money to the State Tax Commission (tax commission) for distribution to certain counties and municipalities to improve the delivery of health care in rural areas of the state;<hr><ltbullet>requires the insurance commissioner to update the state's essential health benefits plan with benefits mandated since January 1, 2012;<hr><ltbullet>allows the insurance commissioner to update the plan described above to incorporate federally mandated benefits under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the tax commission's reporting requirements related to the tax commission's collection of the beer excise tax;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Labor Commission (commission) to use certain restricted account funds to pay the salary and benefits of a compliance officer for the commission's Division of Occupational Safety and Health; <hr><ltbullet>grants the Department of Government Operations (department) the authority to operate the department as an internal service fund agency to provide certain government-related services;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a process for an internal service fund agency to compensate the agency's employees at a rate that is equivalent to state agency employees by submitting a proposed increased rate schedule to the rate committee after the annual legislative session;<hr><ltbullet>requires the rate committee to convene a meeting within 30 days of receiving the rate schedule described above to review and approve or reject the increased rate schedule;<hr><ltbullet>repeals an outdated reference to the former Department of Administrative Services; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Medicaid Accounts Amendments
description: This bill addresses budgeting for the Medicaid program and Medicaid expansion.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms, including "Medicaid shortfall";<hr><ltbullet>establishes the conditions under which a Medicaid shortfall occurs;<hr><ltbullet>requires that appropriations for costs related to the Medicaid program and Medicaid expansion, respectively, be funded from a specific dedicated account or fund; and<hr><ltbullet>establishes a protocol of cost control measures to implement relative to the Medicaid program and Medicaid expansion in the event of a Medicaid shortfall; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical corrections.

title: State Holy Days
description: This bill amends provisions relating to certain days and commemorative periods recognized by the state.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>designates certain days and time periods of special religious significance as state holy days;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a state holy day is not a legal holiday, unless expressly provided otherwise;<hr><ltbullet>designates Easter Sunday as a legal holiday, but one that is not recognized on the preceding Friday or the following Monday; and<hr><ltbullet>provides that a state employee may use the state employee's personal preference day to recognize a state holy day or for any other purpose.

title: Tourism Related Tax Reporting Amendments
description: This bill deals with reporting requirements for a county that imposes a transient room tax or a tourism, recreation, cultural, convention, and airport facilities tax.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the Office of the Legislative Fiscal Analyst (office) to analyze a county's written report on the county's use of transient room tax revenue and tourism, recreation, cultural, convention, and airport facilities tax revenue and make a determination;<hr><ltbullet>requires the office to provide a summary of the office's analysis to the Revenue and Taxation and Political Subdivisions Interim committees and the state auditor;<hr><ltbullet>requires the state auditor to review the office's determination that a county's written report does not sufficiently demonstrate the county is complying with statutory requirements for a transient room tax or a tourism, recreation, cultural, convention, and airport facilities tax and make an independent finding; <hr><ltbullet>if the state auditor finds the county's written report does not sufficiently demonstrate the county is complying with statutory requirements for a transient room tax or a tourism, recreation, cultural, convention, and airport facilities tax, allows the state auditor to withhold funds generated by a transient room tax or a tourism, recreation, cultural, convention, and airport facilities tax from the county until the county complies with county report requirements; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Housing Affordability Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions related to affordable housing.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions allowing revenue from a home ownership promotion zone to be used for certain purposes;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions allowing legislative bodies to settle certain litigation through a consent agreement;<hr><ltbullet>allows a county and municipality to use home ownership promotion zone funds for all or part of water exaction, street lighting, and environmental remediation costs;<hr><ltbullet>requires a county to comply with land use provisions for all pending and new land use applications;<hr><ltbullet>directs the Utah Housing Corporation to make rules regarding: <hr><ltbullet1>procedures, qualifications, and requirements for private financial institutions that offer certain mortgage loans to first-time homebuyers; and<hr><ltbullet1>the creation of an incentive program for qualified buyers to assist certain borrowers with the purchase of liability insurance for certain qualifying projects;<hr><ltbullet>provides that first-time home buyers may use certain mortgage loans for specified purposes; <hr><ltbullet>creates a subordinate shared appreciation loan program to be administered by the Department of Workforce Services to assist borrowers for certain purposes; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Revisor's Corrections to Utah Code - Title 10
description: This bill makes code revisions in Title 10, Utah Municipal Code.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>replaces the term "this act" in Title 10, Utah Municipal Code, with a citation to the relevant title, chapter, or legislation;<hr><ltbullet>replaces certain effective date language with the effective date of the referenced legislation;<hr><ltbullet>establishes subsection structuring within code sections without structure;<hr><ltbullet>repeals obsolete language; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Higher Education Certification Amendments
description: This bill creates the Child Care Center Business Management Certificate Program at Utah State University.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates the Child Care Center Business Management Certificate Program (program) at Utah State University;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the program is managed by Utah State University;<hr><ltbullet>requires the program to teach students best practices, licensing requirements, and management skills to:<hr><ltbullet1>become a regulated provider;<hr><ltbullet1>establish certain child care centers; and<hr><ltbullet1>maintain a small business;<hr><ltbullet>allows the program to contract with a third party to develop curricula; and<hr><ltbullet>requires that the program report to certain committees regarding certain program data.

title: Utah Constitutional Sovereignty Act Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions in the Utah Constitutional Sovereignty Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>expands the definition of "government officer" under the Utah Constitutional Sovereignty Act (Sovereignty Act) to include employees of public school districts and institutions of higher education;<hr><ltbullet>replaces a concurrent resolution with legislation as the format for legislative action under the Sovereignty Act;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the time at which notice is provided to tribal governments regarding legislative action;<hr><ltbullet>addresses requirements for amending or repealing legislation passed under the Sovereignty Act; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Ethylene Oxide Litigation Amendments
description: This bill creates a civil cause of action for ethylene oxide exposure.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates an exclusive, civil cause of action for ethylene oxide exposure;<hr><ltbullet>provides immunity from suit to individuals or businesses in the healthcare industry in relation to the use of ethylene oxide, with limited exceptions;<hr><ltbullet> provides requirements and procedures for claims and pleadings;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the enacted chapter is the exclusive remedy for ethylene oxide exposure actions;<hr><ltbullet>provides transitional language;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the enacted chapter supercedes other personal injury or related laws; and<hr><ltbullet>provides that the enacted chapter does not affect workers' compensation claims or programs.

description: This bill modifies provisions related to charter school authorization and funding.

title: Unauthorized Artificial Intelligence Impersonation Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions relating to the unauthorized use of an individual's personal identity, including use through artificial intelligence technology.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>expands the scope of what constitutes abuse of personal identity to include unauthorized commercial use of simulated or artificially recreated personal identities;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the distribution of technology primarily designed for unauthorized creation of content using personal identities for commercial purposes;<hr><ltbullet>creates exemptions for certain fair uses of personal identity; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Government Records Management Amendments
description: This bill creates the Government Records Office (the office) within the Division of Archives and Records Service (the division), and replaces the State Records Committee (the committee) with the director of the office, who is an attorney with knowledge and experience relating to government records law and makes other changes relating to government records.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates the office within the division and describes the functions of the office;<hr><ltbullet>requires the governor to appoint the director of the office, in consultation with the executive director of the department, and with the advice and consent of the Senate;<hr><ltbullet>describes the term of office, qualifications, and duties of the director;<hr><ltbullet>directs the Division of Human Resource Management to conduct a performance survey and evaluation of the director on a specified schedule;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the committee;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the director will replace the committee in fulfilling the duties currently assigned to the committee, including the duty to decide appeals under the Government Records Access and Management Act;  <hr><ltbullet>makes the government records ombudsman an employee of the office;<hr><ltbullet>grants rulemaking authority to the director of the office;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the transition from the committee to the director of the office;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an individual in an executive branch management position is subject to the record amendment or retention policy created by the governor;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes; and<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to resolves conflicts between this bill and S.B. 163, Government Records Amendments, to allow the changes in S.B. 163 to work within the provisions of this bill that replace the State Records Committee with the director of the Government Records Office.

title: State Debt Collection Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to state debt collection.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies the duties of the Office of State Debt Collection (office);<hr><ltbullet>allows the office to hold title to real property or dispose or acquire surplus property, if doing so is incidental to execution or collection proceedings;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Department of Health and Human Services may enforce certain rights to recovery against a decedent's estate regardless of any contrary provisions in the Utah Uniform Probate Code;<hr><ltbullet>requires notice to the office when a person files an application or a petition for probate;<hr><ltbullet>exempts proceedings to enforce or collect a criminal account receivable, civil judgment of restitution, or civil account receivable from certain time limitations in the Utah Uniform Probate Code;<hr><ltbullet>addresses enforcement of a civil judgment of restitution or civil account receivable; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Funds Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to state accounts.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allows the State Tax Commission to use money in the State Tax Commission Administrative Charge Account to offset general operational expenses;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Department of Cultural and Community Engagement disburses money from the Nonprofit Capacity Fund;<hr><ltbullet>allows the Utah Board of Higher Education to move money across specified line items;<hr><ltbullet>provides circumstances under which an internal service fund agency may charge a rate, fee, or other charge that is less than the rate, fee, or other charge the Legislature approved;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a fee agency from charging a fee amount that is different from the amount the Legislature approved, unless the amount is less than the approved amount and the fee agency satisfies specified notice requirements; <hr><ltbullet>addresses a fee agency's obligations if the fee agency charges a fee that exceeds the amount the Legislature approved;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the following unfunded accounts:<hr><ltbullet1>the Utah Natural Resources Legacy Fund; <hr><ltbullet1>the Intermountain Weatherization Training Fund; and<hr><ltbullet1>the Utah Children's Outdoor Recreation and Education Fund;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the Mathematical Equations Act; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Employment Investigation Records Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to certain employment records of alleged misconduct.

title: Lobbying Amendments
description: This bill amends and enacts provisions relating to lobbying.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>modifies and clarifies the definitions of lobbyist, lobbying, and a principal;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the limits for certain expenditures;  <hr><ltbullet>prohibits consideration, a reward, or an incentive for lobbying that is contingent on certain government action and provides criminal and civil penalties for violation of the prohibition;<hr><ltbullet>replaces the offense of employing or soliciting a person to lobby for contingent compensation with the offense described in the preceding paragraph;<hr><ltbullet>creates an exception to the definition of "expenditure" in relation to certain sporting events, performances, or exhibitions of a state institution of higher education or a private, nonprofit institution of higher education;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to lobbying by a former state official; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Ticketing Delivery Amendments
description: This bill enacts provisions relating to the delivery of an e-ticket.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that it is unlawful for a primary ticket seller or reseller to fail to deliver an e-ticket to an event before the event begins;<hr><ltbullet>grants an individual a cause of action against a person that engages in a prohibited practice related to ticket sales;<hr><ltbullet>provides for an award of damages; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Finance Amendments
description: This bill enacts provisions related to finance.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies the exclusions to the definition of title loan;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the scope of the Uniform Special Deposits Act;<hr><ltbullet>allows parties to an agreement under the Uniform Special Deposits Act to choose a forum in Utah for settling a dispute, regardless of whether the dispute occurred in Utah;<hr><ltbullet>provides that sections of the Uniform Special Deposits Act may vary by agreement or amendment;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for a special deposit;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a special deposit serve a permissible purpose;<hr><ltbullet>provides the conditions under which a bank shall pay a beneficiary funds in the balance of a special deposit;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the interest of a depositor or beneficiary in a special deposit;<hr><ltbullet>allows a court to grant relief to prevent a bank from paying a depositor or beneficiary of a special deposit if a payment would result in fraud;<hr><ltbullet>provides that except in certain circumstances, a bank may not exercise a right of recoupment or set off against a special deposit;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the duties and liabilities of a bank in regards to a special deposit;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a special deposit terminates five years after the date on which the special deposit was first funded;<hr><ltbullet>describes the application of governing law over special deposits;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the provisions of this act only apply to an agreement executed after the effective date of this bill, unless the parties to a special deposit amend the agreement;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the provisions of this act are severable if a provision of the act is found invalid;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the scope of the Uniform Mortgage Modification Act;<hr><ltbullet>codifies the types of modifications that may be made to a mortgage loan that will not materially prejudice interest holders; and<hr><ltbullet>contains safe harbor provisions for mortgage modifications that do not materially prejudice the holders of a junior interest.

title: Property Tax Modifications
description: This bill modifies the Property Tax Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allows a taxing entity that reduces the taxing entity's budget below the previous year's budgeted revenue to increase, for a period of five years, the budget up to the base year budget without complying with the truth in taxation notice and public hearing requirements; <hr><ltbullet>repeals the requirement for a portion of revenue generated by the statewide multicounty assessing and collecting levy to be set aside for county distributions through the Property Tax Valuation Fund and redirects the set aside amount to the Multicounty Appraisal Trust; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

description: This bill modifies provisions relating to the Supreme Court.

title: Congregate Care Amendments
description: This bill addresses congregate care programs.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Congregate Care Advisory Committee (committee);<hr><ltbullet>authorizes and directs the Office of Licensing (office), in consultation with the committee, to:<hr><ltbullet1>set minimum safety requirements for congregate care programs;<hr><ltbullet1>review proposed admissions criteria that a program submits in connection with an application for or renewal of licensure;<hr><ltbullet1>deny or accept a program's proposed admissions criteria;<hr><ltbullet>creates the position of congregate care ombudsman (ombudsman);<hr><ltbullet>authorizes and directs the ombudsman to receive and investigate reports regarding congregate care programs;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Licensed Provider Civil Money Penalty Fund;<hr><ltbullet>denies direct access qualified status for certain individuals;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for congregate care programs, including that the programs:<hr><ltbullet1>adopt admissions criteria by which to determine whether an individual child is a qualified candidate for the program;<hr><ltbullet1>maintain a list of a child's authorized contacts who may contact the child if the child is in crisis;<hr><ltbullet1>notify the authorized contacts and the parent or guardian of a child who is in crisis;<hr><ltbullet1>post notice within the program regarding the ombudsman;<hr><ltbullet1>provide a dedicated telephone from which a child or staff may contact the ombudsman at any time;<hr><ltbullet1>provide disclosures to a child, the child's parent or guardian, and the child's authorized contacts;<hr><ltbullet>establishes responsibility for payment to a health care facility that provides services to a child, including transportation costs; and<hr><ltbullet>establishes whistleblower protections for individuals who report a concern to, or who facilitate or cooperate with, the ombudsman; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Election Amendments
description: This bill modifies the procedures for filling certain candidate and officeholder vacancies.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>describes the circumstances under which a political party is permitted to fill a candidate vacancy;<hr><ltbullet>for the candidate vacancies described in this bill, provides that the candidate vacancy is filled by the applicable political party appointing one individual selected by a majority vote of the applicable political party delegates;<hr><ltbullet>for the midterm vacancies described in this bill, provides that the vacancy is filled, or in certain circumstances temporarily filled, by the governor appointing one of three individuals determined by a majority vote of the applicable political party delegates;<hr><ltbullet>requires the party liaison to communicate the result of a vote of delegates described in the preceding paragraphs; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Strategic Lawsuit Against Public Participation Protections
description: This bill modifies the Uniform Public Expression Protection Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies the scope of the Uniform Public Expression Protection Act (act) to apply only to causes of action for defamation or slander in relation to a claim involving exercise of a constitutional right;<hr><ltbullet>permits a party to issue a subpoena for testimony at a hearing conducted pursuant to the act, with some limitations;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a cause of action be dismissed without prejudice instead of with prejudice in some circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>removes the ability to seek costs, attorney fees, and expenses in some circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions addressing attorney fees and the precedential effects of a voluntary dismissal of a cause of action;<hr><ltbullet>provides that trial proceedings on discovery and certain causes of action are not stayed while an appeal is pending; <hr><ltbullet>modifies standards required to obtain a reward of costs, attorney fees, and expenses in some circumstances; and<hr><ltbullet>modifies language related to broadly construing the purpose of the act.

title: Limitations on Liability Modifications
description: This bill provides liability protection in some circumstances in relation to transportation provided for behavioral health care.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides definitions;<hr><ltbullet>provides limitations on liability, in some circumstances, for a behavioral health care provider that provides transportation services for a minor for the purposes of providing access to treatments;<hr><ltbullet>permits a behavioral health care provider to contract with a parent of a minor who is receiving services from the behavioral health provider in order to limit the behavioral health care provider's liability, with some limitations; and<hr><ltbullet>provides exceptions to liability limitations.

title: Private Investigator Regulation Modifications
description: This bill modifies provisions related to licensure of private investigators.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires notice of the cancellation of a private investigator's license or disciplinary action against the licensee to an agent sponsoring the licensee;<hr><ltbullet>requires a licensee to complete 16 hours of continuing education to renew a license beginning in 2027; <hr><ltbullet>modifies the information that appears on a licensee's identification card and the circumstances under which a licensee shall provide identifying information to a person verifying validity of the license;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Bail Bond Recovery and Private Investigator Licensure Board to take action when the agent for a licensed agency is incapacitated or dies;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to disciplinary action against a licensee;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which a member may serve more than one term on the Bail Bond Recovery and Private Investigator Licensure Board; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Transportation Utility Fee Amendments
description: This bill deals with a municipality's or county's ability to impose a transportation utility fee.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a municipality or county may impose and collect a transportation utility fee under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>describes the notice and public hearing requirements to establish a transportation utility fee;<hr><ltbullet>requires a municipality or county to establish different rates within a transportation utility fee for different classifications of users, if the rates and classifications have a reasonable basis;<hr><ltbullet>requires a municipality or county to exempt a religious organization from a transportation utility fee; and<hr><ltbullet>provides that if a municipality or county has a transportation utility fee that is not in compliance with statutory requirements, the municipality or county shall modify or repeal the transportation utility fee by July 1, 2027.

title: Military Installation Development Authority and Other Development Zone Amendments
description: This bill deals with the Military Installation Development Authority and the distribution of certain sales tax revenues related to certain authorities and zones.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes an eligible basic special district to use tax revenue under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>provides a formula for the State Tax Commission to distribute local revenue from the sale of construction materials within a qualified development zone;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the distribution of tax revenue generated by a Schedule J sale;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies provisions related to the resort communities tax and the additional resort communities tax;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the authority may enter into an agreement with the state or an agency of the state, including an agreement to use revenue generated from a project area outside the project area, if the project area is on land owned by the state or the state armory board;<hr><ltbullet>states that a public infrastructure district created by the authority may be a subsidiary of the authority; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Dietitian Licensing Amendments
description: This bill enacts the Dietitian Licensure Compact Act (compact).
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>describes the purpose of the compact;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes member state requirements for the compact;<hr><ltbullet>describes requirements to receive a compact privilege license, which allows a licensee to practice in states that are members of the compact;<hr><ltbullet>describes requirements to change the state of an individual license;<hr><ltbullet>provides for an active military member and the spouse of an active military member to retain a license while the military member is on active duty;<hr><ltbullet>establishes what adverse action a home state and another member may take against an individual licensee;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the Dietitian Licensure Compact Commission (commission);<hr><ltbullet>directs for a coordinated data system;<hr><ltbullet>establishes rulemaking procedures for the commission;<hr><ltbullet>establishes oversight, dispute resolution, and enforcement under the compact;<hr><ltbullet>establishes when the compact comes into effect, how a state may withdraw, and how the compact is amended; and<hr><ltbullet>provides that the compact supersedes conflicting state law.

title: Prosecutorial Misconduct Amendments
description: This bill creates a commission to address prosecutorial misconduct.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that certain records of the Prosecutor Conduct Commission are protected;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Prosecutor Conduct Commission (commission) within the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice;<hr><ltbullet>provides the membership of the commission;<hr><ltbullet>addresses terms, vacancies, and compensation for members of the commission;<hr><ltbullet>allows the commission to select a chair for a two-year term;<hr><ltbullet>addresses staffing for the commission;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the duties and functions of the commission;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the complaint and investigation process for the commission;<hr><ltbullet>allows a prospective employer to inquire as to whether there is a pending investigation regarding a prosecuting attorney;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for a finding of professional misconduct by a prosecuting attorney;<hr><ltbullet>provides reporting requirements when the commission makes a finding of professional misconduct;<hr><ltbullet>enacts an annual reporting requirement to the Legislature regarding complaints and investigations by the commission; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Municipality Annexation and Incorporation Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to municipal annexation and incorporation.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires an annexation policy plan to include a statement regarding: <hr><ltbullet1>the current county zoning of an unincorporated area proposed for annexation; and<hr><ltbullet1>the zoning likely to be applied, should the unincorporated area be annexed to the municipality, to the unincorporated area proposed for annexation; <hr><ltbullet>prohibits a municipality from zoning in an affected area in a manner that results in the affected area being utilized in a more restrictive way than before the affected area was annexed into the municipality, for at least one year following the date of annexation;<hr><ltbullet>requires a municipal legislative body to establish by ordinance a process to compensate a property owner for a reduction in property value following an annexation or incorporation and subsequent zoning for a more restrictive use of the property; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Transportation Condemnation Amendments
description: This bill provides certain requirements that the Department of Transportation is required to meet when exercising eminent domain powers.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms related to eminent domain;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Transportation (department) to meet certain requirements when exercising eminent domain powers, including:<hr><ltbullet1>identification of the rights and interests being acquired, including the value assigned to each right or interest;<hr><ltbullet1>limiting the department's ability to construct an improvement that interferes with the visibility of the owner for a certain time period;<hr><ltbullet1>requiring just compensation before the department may obtain real property; and<hr><ltbullet1>requiring written certification acknowledged by the condemnee indicating that each interest acquired has been assigned a separate value; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Judgment Renewal Modifications
description: This bill modifies provisions of the Judgment Renewal Act and provisions relating to entering and renewing a judgment.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies statute of limitations provisions to provide that a statute of limitations runs from the date of renewal of a judgment, not only from the original date of a judgment;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a renewal of a judgment maintains the date of the original judgment, maintains the priority of collection of the original judgment, and unless specifically excepted, resets any time limitation for action upon the judgment;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a judgment may be renewed multiple times; and<hr><ltbullet>makes conforming changes.
