title: Alcohol Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to alcohol.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>permits a local government to authorize an outlet or restaurant with an alcohol license to be in proximity to a public park under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the Alcoholic Beverage Services Commission's authority when granting or denying an application for a retail license;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a hotel may serve spirituous liquor in a container that is not the spirituous liquor's original container;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a patron of a facility with multiple licenses may transport beer between the premises under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes staff of a retail licensee that are 21 years old or older to test the quality and taste of liquor using the "straw test";<hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement that dispensing locations under an equity license be connected by a private roadway;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an equity license applies to all locations owned by an equity licensee;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an amphitheater qualifies for a banquet license;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Services may approve multiple locations in or on the licensed premises of an on-premise banquet licensee;<hr><ltbullet>lowers the seating capacity threshold for a sport facility or concert venue for purposes of receiving an on-premises beer retailer license;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which an off-premise beer retailer may sell beer at a loading area or a designated parking stall;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a person applying for an event permit post a surety bond; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Deferred Deposit Lending Modifications
description: This bill modifies provisions related to deferred deposit, or payday, lending.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>extends the time period during which a person may rescind a deferred deposit loan;<hr><ltbullet>requires a deferred deposit lender to provide a notice of default in the language in which the deferred deposit loan transaction occurs; <hr><ltbullet>requires a deferred deposit lender to have a notice of default available in English upon request for a person who receives a notice of default in another language; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Cosmetology Modifications
description: This bill restructures the licensing standards for the Cosmetology and Associated Professions Licensing Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates a scope of practice for professionals regulated by the Cosmetology and Associated Professions Licensing Act;<hr><ltbullet>restructures the existing Cosmetology and Associated Professions Licensing Board;<hr><ltbullet>restructures the license classifications regulated by the Cosmetology and Associated Professions Licensing Act;<hr><ltbullet>restructures the qualifications for licensure for professionals regulated by the Cosmetology and Associated Professions Licensing Act;<hr><ltbullet>establishes standards for apprenticeship for professionals regulated by the Cosmetology and Associated Professions Licensing Act;<hr><ltbullet>addresses unprofessional conduct;<hr><ltbullet>allows a school to receive curriculum approval from the Division of Professional Licensing; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Major Sporting Event Venue Financing Amendments
description: This bill enacts the Major Sporting Event Venue Zone Act and related provisions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes objectives and requirements for a municipality or county to create a major sporting event venue zone to capture property tax increment and local sales and use tax increment within a defined area around a major sporting event venue;<hr><ltbullet>defines permitted uses and administration of property tax increment and local sales and use tax increment generated pursuant to a major sporting event venue zone;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a creating entity of a major sporting event venue to impose, under certain circumstances: <hr><ltbullet1>a resort communities sales and use tax within a major sporting event venue zone; and<hr><ltbullet1>an additional resort communities sales and use tax within a major sporting event venue zone;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a county of the third class with three or more major sporting event venues may implement a resort communities tax in unincorporated areas, the same as if the county of the third class were an eligible municipality, and use the revenue from the tax on public infrastructure or transit;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a creating entity of a major sporting event venue zone to designate a community reinvestment agency or a public infrastructure district as a fiscal agent for major sporting event venue zone funds;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a creating entity to enter into an agreement with a person to utilize major sporting event venue zone funds in regard to owning, leasing, or operating a major sporting event venue;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a creating entity to utilize major sporting venue zone funds to bond;<hr><ltbullet>provides a sales and use tax exemption for construction materials used for the remodeling, or refurbishing of a major sporting event venue;<hr><ltbullet>requires a municipality or county to submit a major sporting event venue zone proposal to the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity; <hr><ltbullet>creates and defines the membership of a committee to review a proposed major sporting event venue zone;<hr><ltbullet>requires the committee to evaluate the proposed major sporting event venue zone and, if certain criteria are met, approve the proposal with or without modifications;<hr><ltbullet>requires participation from local taxing entities if the major sporting event venue zone meets statutory requirements;<hr><ltbullet>provides procedures for a major sports event venue that overlaps with a community reinvestment project, a housing and transit reinvestment zone, a first home investment zone, or a revitalization zone; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Medical Malpractice Revisions
description: This bill addresses malpractice actions against health care providers.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>with respect to a medical malpractice action:<hr><ltbullet1>removes the requirement that a claimant submit an affidavit of merit;<hr><ltbullet1>establishes data collection and reporting requirements for the Division of Professional Licensing and the Administrative Office of the Courts;<hr><ltbullet1>addresses the calculation of noneconomic losses;<hr><ltbullet1>limits, subject to state constitutional protection, the combined amount to which a claimant is potentially entitled for economic and noneconomic losses;<hr><ltbullet1>obligates a plaintiff, in certain circumstances, to pay the reasonable attorney fees and costs incurred by a defendant;<hr><ltbullet1>precludes liability from attaching, in certain circumstances, to a medical facility, clinic, or organization;<hr><ltbullet1>amends the authority of prelitigation review panels and the process for conducting panel reviews; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Utah Fairpark Area Investment and Restoration District Modifications
description: This bill modifies provisions relating to the Utah Fairpark Area Investment and Restoration District.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>broadens permissible uses for a fair park land lease;<hr><ltbullet>modifies taxing authority provisions related to the fairpark district or a host municipality;<hr><ltbullet>modifies land use authority provisions relating to land located within the fairpark district;<hr><ltbullet>enables a public infrastructure district created by the fairpark district to:<hr><ltbullet1>levy property taxes;<hr><ltbullet1>use bond proceeds for the development and maintenance of public utility infrastructure; and<hr><ltbullet1>pay for specified development and improvements;<hr><ltbullet>provides funding for the fairpark district;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a process for a member of the fairpark board to annually file a conflict of interest disclosure;<hr><ltbullet>designates the fairpark district as a qualifying jurisdiction that can receive tax information from the State Tax Commission;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to merge the changes to Section 59-12-103 in this bill and S.B. 27, Motor Vehicle Division Amendments, if both pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Land Use and Development Amendments
description: This bill creates the Beehive Development Agency and authorizes the commissioner of the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity to propose significant community impact project plans and associated project areas to the Beehive Development Agency.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>provides a severability provision;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Beehive Development Agency (agency) under Utah Constitution, Article XI, as a political subdivision of the state that is an independent, nonprofit, separate body corporate and politic, with perpetual succession, and a public corporation;<hr><ltbullet>provides that appropriations to the agency are nonlapsing;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the agency board and describes the agency powers and duties;<hr><ltbullet>describes the purposes of a significant community impact project;<hr><ltbullet>creates a revolving loan fund and establishes a loan committee;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the agency to create a public infrastructure district for a significant community project area;<hr><ltbullet>describes the potential revenue sources of a significant community impact project area, including property tax differential and revenue generated by certain taxes;<hr><ltbullet>repeals provisions establishing the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity (office) board of directors and the Unified Economic Opportunity Commission;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Economic Opportunity Coordinating Council (council);<hr><ltbullet>changes the executive director of the office to the commissioner of the office;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the commissioner of the office shall:<hr><ltbullet1>receive guidance from the council regarding statewide strategic objectives;<hr><ltbullet1>establish strategies for and actively recruit targeted industries identified by the council;<hr><ltbullet1>encourage a business to permanently relocate to, or significantly expand operations in, the state;<hr><ltbullet1>establish strategies for and actively support entrepreneurship and small business development;<hr><ltbullet1>coordinate economic development activities; and<hr><ltbullet1>coordinate with various departments and officials in order to consolidate certain state housing programs from the Division of Housing and Community Development within the office by July 1, 2026;<hr><ltbullet>removes the sunset on the Utah Housing Corporation; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Nonprofit Entities Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to nonprofit entities.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies the definition of "governmental nonprofit corporation" to exclude the Utah Association of Special Districts;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that a private nonprofit organization that is not a public employees' association is not required to post employee compensation information online; and<hr><ltbullet>requires a governmental nonprofit corporation to post financial information on the Utah Public Finance Website.

title: Protected Person Amendments
description: This bill enacts provisions relating to the construction of a security improvement to real property belonging to an individual who is certified to be at risk of harm.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a process for an individual at risk of harm to apply to the commissioner of public safety for certification to construct a security improvement on the individual's property;<hr><ltbullet>requires a land use authority to approve an individual's land use application to construct a security improvement on the individual's real property if the application complies with the state's construction and fire codes;<hr><ltbullet>exempts an individual's security improvement from county or municipal land use regulations;<hr><ltbullet>describes remedies available to an individual if a municipality or county unlawfully conditions, delays, or denies the individual's building permit for a security improvement; and<hr><ltbullet>provides for the confidentiality of records relating to certification of a security improvement or security improvement construction.

title: Election Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions relating to elections.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements and procedures addressing circumstances when the lieutenant governor may have a real or perceived conflict of interest in certain matters relating to the administration of elections, the regulation of campaign finance requirements or reporting requirements, or the regulation of lobbying, including:<hr><ltbullet1>requiring, or in certain circumstances permitting, the lieutenant governor to delegate certain duties to a county clerk that relate to a race where the governor or lieutenant governor are running for office;<hr><ltbullet1>requiring, or in certain circumstances permitting, the attorney general to act in the place of the lieutenant governor in relation to matters requiring factual determinations, interpreting or applying the law, or imposing penalties; and<hr><ltbullet1>provides that the state board of canvassers shall canvass regular primary election results and presidential primary election results; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Concurrent Resolution Supporting Federalism Principles and Utah's Control of its Energy Future
description: This resolution reaffirms Utah's sovereignty under the principle of federalism and asserts the state's right to determine its own energy policies.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>reiterates the powers afforded to states under the United States Constitution and its protections against federal overreach;<hr><ltbullet>affirms that the authority to determine energy policies affecting state residents is among the powers reserved to states under the Tenth Amendment;<hr><ltbullet>explains the significance of the United States Supreme Court's "Loper Bright" decision in preserving federalism;<hr><ltbullet>asserts Utah's right to play a primary role in determining energy policies within its borders;<hr><ltbullet>urges the federal government to limit its role in energy regulation to matters of interstate commerce and national security;<hr><ltbullet>requests meaningful consultation between federal agencies and states when developing energy-related policies; and <hr><ltbullet>calls for formal mechanisms for state input in federal energy policy decisions.

description: This resolution calls on the President of the United States to issue an executive order on federalism.

description: This resolution makes an application to Congress to call a convention for proposing amendments to the United States Constitution.

title: Senate Rules Resolution - Legislative Process Amendments
description: This rules resolution modifies Senate processes and procedures.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the duties of the secretary of the Senate related to technical corrections to legislation;<hr><ltbullet>repeals outdated language related to the daily order of business;<hr><ltbullet>modifies procedures for obtaining a citation;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that a senator may not impugn the motives of another senator or a senator's guest;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits certain items and activities in the Senate gallery;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a senator obtain permission to cosponsor Senate legislation;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the Senate Rules Committee, after sifting, makes recommendations about which legislation should be assigned to the second reading calendar;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies which legislation the Senate may pass without receiving a favorable recommendation from a Senate standing committee;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the circumstances under which a standing committee may recommend legislation for the consent calendar;  <hr><ltbullet>provides legislators the right to attend Senate committee meetings, subject to certain restrictions;<hr><ltbullet>provides an exception during a special session to the prohibition on legislation being read a third time until at least the day after it is placed on the third reading calendar;<hr><ltbullet>addresses procedures related to committee reports and Senate calendars;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies procedures for the disposition of legislation voted on third reading;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies procedures related to the consent calendar;<hr><ltbullet>requires legislation to remain on the concurrence calendar at least overnight for the first 42 days of an annual general session; <hr><ltbullet>clarifies the prohibition on senators speaking more than twice on the same legislation;<hr><ltbullet>allows senators participating by electronic means to be considered present for the purpose of voting;<hr><ltbullet>removes obsolete language; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Election Records Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to election records.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes retention and disposition requirements for certain election records;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes an election officer to share with certain individuals the record of voters contacted to cure a ballot;<hr><ltbullet>establishes and modifies provisions related to who, and the circumstances under which, an individual may view the video recordings of the processing of ballots and unattended ballot drop boxes;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the data reporting requirements and deadlines for ballot statistics published on an election officer's website during an election;<hr><ltbullet>eliminates certain ballot reconciliation reporting requirements;<hr><ltbullet>classifies certain election records as public records;<hr><ltbullet>for the board of canvassers' report that an election officer submits to the board of canvassers after an election:<hr><ltbullet1>specifies certain election-related data that the election officer must include in the report's statement of votes cast; and<hr><ltbullet1>requires the election officer to include in the report certain data from the election results database;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a process for an election officer who does not count ballots using automatic tabulating equipment to include certain data from the election results database in the board of canvassers' report;<hr><ltbullet>requires an election officer to: <hr><ltbullet1>publish a notice of the board of canvasser's report as a class A notice;<hr><ltbullet1>include with the notice a copy of the board of canvasser's report on the Utah Public Notice Website and the election officer's jurisdiction's website; and <hr><ltbullet1>make the board of canvassers' report available to the public in certain electronic file formats;<hr><ltbullet>requires the lieutenant governor to ensure that all voting equipment has the capability of generating an election results database;<hr><ltbullet>specifies the data that must be contained in an election results database; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: County Governance Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions relating to forms of county government.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a county council member in certain counties to represent a district, with exceptions;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a process for a county to create and implement a county council district map; <hr><ltbullet>establishes deadlines for certain counties to implement district maps;<hr><ltbullet>describes the circumstances in which a previously at-large county council member may represent a county council district in which the county council member does not live following the adoption of a district map;<hr><ltbullet>describes the circumstances in which certain counties may redistrict; <hr><ltbullet>describes the penalties for failure to create and implement a county council district map;<hr><ltbullet>provides a sunset date; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Election Amendments
description: This bill modifies election provisions relating to qualifying for placement on a primary election ballot.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>for the 2026 election year only, in relation to the office of United States representative only:<hr><ltbullet1>permits an individual who desires to circulate a petition to gather signatures to qualify for placement on the regular primary election ballot as a potential nominee of a political party for United States representative (a congressional signature petition) to file a notice of intent to gather signatures before filing as a candidate for United States representative;<hr><ltbullet1>until the deadline for filing a declaration of candidacy for United States representative, permits an individual to circulate a congressional signature petition, regardless of whether the individual is also running for an office other than United States representative;<hr><ltbullet1>requires that an individual who is running for an office other than United States representative must withdraw as a candidate for that office before filing a declaration of candidacy for United States representative;<hr><ltbullet1>provides that the declaration of candidacy filing period is March 9, 2026, through March 13, 2026; and<hr><ltbullet1>permits an individual who circulates a congressional signature petition to collect signatures from any resident of the state who is permitted by the political party to vote for the political party's candidates in a primary election, rather than only a resident of the congressional district for which the individual intends to run;<hr><ltbullet>grants rulemaking authority to regulate the circumstances under which an individual may submit a candidate signature packet; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the exclusive and original appellate jurisdiction of the Utah Supreme Court;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a final judgment in certain cases is appealable even if a motion or claim for attorney fees has not been entered by the district court;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the jurisdiction of the Utah Court of Appeals; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Public Education Base Budget Amendments
description: This bill supplements or reduces appropriations otherwise provided for the support and operation of public education for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2025 and ending June 30, 2026 and appropriates funds for the support and operation of public education for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends weighted pupil unit provisions for career and technical education programs to address eligibility for Career and Technical Education center funding;<hr><ltbullet>revises emergency funding provisions for students learning English;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to designating programs for annual funding from the Public Education Economic Stabilization Restricted Account;<hr><ltbullet>provides appropriations for the use and support of school districts, charter schools and state education agencies;<hr><ltbullet>sets the value of the weighted pupil unit (WPU) initially at $4,870 for fiscal year 2026-2027;<hr><ltbullet>adjusts the number of weighted pupil units (WPUs) in certain programs for student enrollment changes and statutory formula calculations;<hr><ltbullet>appropriates funds to the Uniform School Fund Restricted - Public Education Budget Stabilization Account;<hr><ltbullet>makes an appropriation from the Uniform School Fund Restricted - Trust Distribution Account to the School LAND Trust program to support educational programs in the public schools;<hr><ltbullet>adjusts the revenue targets and estimates tax rates for the statewide Basic Rate and WPU Value Rate according to statutory provisions;<hr><ltbullet>provides appropriations for other purposes as described; and<hr><ltbullet>approves intent language.

title: Municipal Services Fees and Political Subdivision Lien Amendments
description: This bill authorizes municipalities to place a political subdivision lien on property for certain past due services and makes related amendments.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a municipality that sets a fee schedule by ordinance or resolution for water, sewer, or utility-related services provided by the municipality, to bill a customer receiving the water, sewer, or utility-related services;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a municipality to place a political subdivision lien on property for certain past due service fees after providing notice of:<hr><ltbullet1>the past due fees; and<hr><ltbullet1>the municipality's intent to record a political subdivision lien if the past due fees remain unpaid;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a municipality or special district to:<hr><ltbullet1>charge interest on a past due fee; and<hr><ltbullet1>charge and collect a one-time penalty on a past due fee as an administrative cost; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill enacts provisions related to utility scale solar power plants.

title: Criminal Penalty Amendments
description: This bill addresses criminal penalties.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTLAW", "name": "Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>reduces the criminal offense of operating a vehicle at a speed greater than 20 miles per hour in a school zone from a class C misdemeanor to an infraction if the person is operating the vehicle from 21 miles per hour to 29 miles per hour;<hr><ltbullet>merges the criminal offenses of:<hr><ltbullet1>operating a motor vehicle without an owner's or operator's security; and<hr><ltbullet1>failing to carry evidence of owner's or operator's security to be carried when operating a motor vehicle;<hr><ltbullet>reduces the penalty for the criminal offense of careless driving from a class C misdemeanor to an infraction; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Candidate Petition Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to candidate nomination petitions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires a candidate who seeks the nomination for an elective office by gathering signatures of registered voters to submit the signatures to the county clerk of each registered voter's residence;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a county clerk may only certify the signature of a registered voter described above if the registered voter is a resident of the county clerk's county;<hr><ltbullet>for a signature gathering candidate who seeks the nomination for an office in a district where the officeholder is elected by the voters from more than one county, requires the county clerk of each county to which the candidate submits signatures to:<hr><ltbullet1>count the number of valid signatures submitted by the candidate; and<hr><ltbullet1>certify the number of valid signatures to the lieutenant governor; <hr><ltbullet> for an elective office described above, requires the lieutenant governor to:<hr><ltbullet1>count the total number of valid signatures received from each county clerk; and<hr><ltbullet1>if the aggregate number of valid signatures is sufficient for the candidate to qualify for placement on the ballot, certify the signatures;<hr><ltbullet>amends the candidate nomination petition forms to specify that only a registered voter residing in the county where a candidate submits signatures for verification should sign the candidate's nomination petition;<hr><ltbullet>for a candidate for elective office seeking the nomination of a qualified political party through signature-gathering, shortens the deadline for the candidate to submit signatures to an election official from 14 to 21 days before the day on which the party holds a convention to nominate a candidate for the same elective office; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Voting Equipment Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to voting equipment.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>except for an electronic pollbook or official register, requires an election officer to ensure that all voting equipment used in this state is not capable of wireless communication;<hr><ltbullet>repeals a provision governing the certification of voting equipment used in ranked-choice voting;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an election officer from acquiring voting equipment that is not part of the new voting equipment system selected for purchase by the lieutenant governor;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Voting Equipment Selection Committee shall assist the lieutenant governor in:<hr><ltbullet1>conducting a competitive procurement for a new voting equipment system; and<hr><ltbullet1>ensuring that the new voting equipment system complies with the requirements for casting a mechanical ballot; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Signature Verification Revisions
description: This bill amends provisions related to candidate nomination petitions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires an election official to post the name, voter precinct number, and date of signature of a registered voter who signs a candidate nomination petition on the lieutenant governor's website for at least 90 days after the date of an election;<hr><ltbullet>requires an election official to send an email notice to a registered voter described above informing the voter that:<hr><ltbullet1>the voter's name and voter-related information is posted on the lieutenant governor's website; and<hr><ltbullet1>the voter may request to have the voter's signature removed from the candidate nomination petition by submitting a written statement to the election official requesting removal of the signature;<hr><ltbullet>requires an election official to make the website posting described above regardless of whether the voter's voter registration record is classified as a private record;<hr><ltbullet>amends candidate nomination petition forms to include information notifying a voter of the posting and signature removal processes described above; <hr><ltbullet>for a candidate seeking the nomination of a qualified political party to an elective office through signature gathering, shortens the deadline for the candidate to submit signatures to an election official from 14 to 21 days before the day on which the qualified political party holds a convention to nominate a candidate for the same elective office; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Signature Gathering and Verification Amendments
description: This bill modifies requirements for petitions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends, standardizes, and makes technical revisions to the signature collector verification form included in petition packets;<hr><ltbullet>specifies how an individual may be paid for collecting petition signatures;<hr><ltbullet>beginning on July 1, 2027, requires a clerk who verifies signatures for a petition to send an email and text message notice to the signer of the petition notifying the signer of the status of the signer's signature;<hr><ltbullet>requires the lieutenant governor to develop and maintain an online training course to educate individuals who collect signatures for a petition;<hr><ltbullet>requires an individual who collects signatures for a petition to complete the training course described above before collecting any signatures for the petition;<hr><ltbullet>requires an election official to reject a signature packet if the individual who collects signatures for the petition did not complete the online training course described above;<hr><ltbullet>modifies requirements related to statewide initiative and referendum packets by:<hr><ltbullet1>removing the requirement that the county clerk deliver each packet to the lieutenant governor; <hr><ltbullet1>requiring the county clerk who verifies packets to certify certain statistical information to the lieutenant governor; and<hr><ltbullet1>directing the county clerk to retain and preserve each packet for at least 22 months;<hr><ltbullet>designates the existing initiative and referendum packet format as one packet type and creates an alternative packet type with different content and assembly requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires an alternative packet type to provide access to the text of a proposed or referable law through a QR code rather than a printed copy;<hr><ltbullet>for an alternative packet type, requires the initiative petition and each signature sheet to contain a brief, plain-language description of the principal provisions of the law proposed by the initiative;<hr><ltbullet>allows the sponsors of an initiative or referendum petition to circulate packets using a traditional packet type, an alternative packet type, or both;<hr><ltbullet>repeals provisions permitting an individual to optionally provide the individual's email address when signing an initiative or referendum signature sheet;<hr><ltbullet>updates the formatting and spacing requirements for initiative and referendum signature sheets;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the sponsors of an initiative or referendum petition from marking or redacting a signature sheet in a manner that obscures, conceals, or renders illegible a signer's date of signature or other voter information used for verification;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a county clerk may not certify a signature if the date of signature is later than the applicable deadline for submitting an initiative or referendum packet;<hr><ltbullet>on January 1, 2027, repeals provisions requiring the sponsors of an initiative petition to:<hr><ltbullet1>send an informational email to each initiative petition signer who provides a legible email address on a signature sheet; and<hr><ltbullet1>send a list to the lieutenant governor identifying the recipients of the email described above;<hr><ltbullet>beginning on January 1, 2027, requires an election officer to send the email described above to each eligible voter who signs an initiative petition within two business days of verifying the voter's signature;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical revisions to the required statements that appear on initiative and referendum signature sheets;<hr><ltbullet>modifies certain statements appearing on initiative and referendum packets to provide that:<hr><ltbullet1>the signer of the packet had an opportunity to read and understand the proposed or referable law; title: Political Signs Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to political signs.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>specifies the form and placement of the disclosure statement for political advertisements;<hr><ltbullet>creates an exception to political advertising disclosure requirements for certain candidate-paid political signs; <hr><ltbullet>reduces the size dimensions of a political sign that is exempt from disclosing, on the sign, the person who paid for the sign;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a person from:<hr><ltbullet1>attaching a political sign to a utility pole, light pole, an electric utility box, a traffic control device, or any railroad sign or signal; or<hr><ltbullet1>affixing an object to a political sign for the purpose of blocking, concealing, or misrepresenting the message or image on the political sign;<hr><ltbullet>expands existing criminal penalties for defacing political signs to cover the conduct described above, and specifies exceptions for:<hr><ltbullet1>a person who removes a political sign that does not contain the disclosure described above;<hr><ltbullet1>a person who removes a political sign that violates the prohibition on electioneering in or near a polling place;<hr><ltbullet1>a government employee who removes a political sign in the course of the government employee's duties;<hr><ltbullet1>a person who removes an object that blocks or conceals a political sign; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Local Government Amendments
description: This bill deals with provisions related to counties and special districts.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines the term "finance officer" and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>describes when a county legislative body shall submit the question of moving the county seat to the county's voters;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to the annexation or consolidation of counties and the creation of a new county;<hr><ltbullet>addresses pending criminal and civil proceedings following the creation of a new county;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a county shall hold an election on an optional plan to change the form of county government at the next regular general election that is no less than 180 days after the day on which the county attorney submits to the county clerk the attorney's report;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to county costs following a change of venue;<hr><ltbullet>repeals a requirement that a county financial officer be bonded;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the ability of a legislative body to investigate the actions of a county officer that impacts county business or operations;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to the consolidation of county offices;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the qualification requirements of a county assessor;<hr><ltbullet>provides that, if a county council delegates the provision of accounting services to a finance officer, the county auditor is not required to fulfill an accounting obligation described in statute unless statute explicitly states that the county auditor shall provide the accounting obligation;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to county surveyor duties;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the circumstances in which an election official is required to notify eligible voters via email about the disqualification of a candidate;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the manner in which a county recorder is required to index recorded instruments;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a county legislative body to set fees for services of the county recorder;<hr><ltbullet>increases certain statutorily provided fees for certain county recorder services;<hr><ltbullet>provides a method for an individual requesting a record related to military service to demonstrate that the individual is a lineal descendant of the individual who is the subject of the record;<hr><ltbullet>provides that, when a county contracts with a licensed professional land surveyor to fulfill certain county surveyor duties, the licensed professional land surveyor may utilize the county surveyor seal or a personal seal;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to survey monuments, corners, and boundaries;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a county surveyor to charge a plat fee to an infrastructure financing district or public infrastructure district;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a county treasurer to enter an agreement with a special district for the county treasurer to bill and collect assessments on behalf of the special district;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to merit system employment, including administrative appeals to a career service council or an administrative law judge;<hr><ltbullet>repeals a criminal penalty for individuals who willfully violate provisions related to county personnel management;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers authority for a county to expend county funds as considered advisable for the development of the county's resources;<hr><ltbullet>repeals sections related to the Title 17 recodification during the 2025 First Special Session;<hr><ltbullet>recodifies Title 17B, Chapter 2a, Part 13, Infrastructure Financing District, as Title 17D, Chapter 5, Infrastructure Financing District Act; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: School Cybersecurity Amendments
description: This bill directs the State Board of Education to establish minimum cybersecurity standards for local education agencies.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTLAW", "name": "Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>prohibits certain devices in schools;<hr><ltbullet>directs the Cybersecurity Commission to make rules establishing minimum cybersecurity standards for local education agencies (LEAs) aligned with industry recognized frameworks;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a phased implementation timeline for LEA compliance;<hr><ltbullet>requires coordination among the Utah Cyber Center, the State Board of Education, and the Utah Education and Telehealth Network;<hr><ltbullet>establishes reporting requirements for cybersecurity incidents;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Board of Education to provide implementation support and resources; <hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to incorporate changes made to Section 53G-7-227 with changes made to that section in S.B. 69, School Device Revisions; and<hr><ltbullet>makes conforming changes.

title: School Security Amendments
description: This bill creates the School Safety Support Program to provide funding for school safety requirements and infrastructure.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTLAW", "name": "Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates the School Safety Support Program (program) to fund school safety personnel, building standards, emergency protocols, and security infrastructure;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a distribution formula that allocates funding to charter schools and school districts based on enrollment and base amounts;<hr><ltbullet>requires local education agencies to submit safety plans and annual reports to receive funding;<hr><ltbullet>adds the program to the list of education programs eligible for annual inflation and enrollment growth adjustments;<hr><ltbullet>protects the program from funding reductions due to negative enrollment growth;<hr><ltbullet>directs the state board to collaborate with the School Safety Center and state security chief to establish rules and monitor implementation; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: School Security Personnel Standards
description: This bill provides amendments to school safety standards regarding requirements for various safety related personnel.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTLAW", "name": "Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allows county security chiefs to designate approved private security companies to administer required school safety personnel training;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Board of Education to administer stipends for a school guardian in coordination with the state security chief; <hr><ltbullet>requires a local education agency (LEA) to provide a panic alert device for certain school safety personnel; <hr><ltbullet>expands the definition of an armed school security guard to include a special function officer; <hr><ltbullet>clarifies requirements of a school guardian concealed carrying a firearm while on duty;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits certain devices in schools;directs the Cybersecurity Commission to make rules establishing minimum cybersecurity standards for local education agencies (LEAs) aligned with industry recognized frameworks;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a phased implementation timeline for LEA compliance;<hr><ltbullet>requires coordination among the Utah Cyber Center, the State Board of Education, and the Utah Education and Telehealth Network;<hr><ltbullet>establishes reporting requirements for cybersecurity incidents;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Board of Education to provide implementation support and resources;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to incorporate changes made to Section 53G-7-227 with changes made to that section in S.B. 69, School Device Revisions;<hr><ltbullet>provides protocols for a school guardian or armed school security guard for an incident using deadly force;<hr><ltbullet>establishes visitor management protocols for an LEA;<hr><ltbullet>removes duplicative language; and<hr><ltbullet>makes conforming changes.

title: Criminal and Juvenile Justice Changes
description: This bill amends statutory provisions related to the criminal and juvenile justice system.

title: Child Protection Ombudsman Amendments
description: This bill makes changes related to the child protection ombudsman.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allows the child protection ombudsman to receive a complaint with respect to a parent;<hr><ltbullet>requires the child protection ombudsman to:<hr><ltbullet1>provide information about a parent's and child's rights on the child protection ombudsman's website; and<hr><ltbullet1>annually report to the Child Welfare Legislative Oversight Panel and the Health and Human Services Interim Committee;<hr><ltbullet>requires a peace officer or child welfare caseworker who takes a child into protective custody to provide the child's parent or guardian with information about the child protection ombudsman; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Adoption Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to adoption and child-placing agencies.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to child-placing agencies including:<hr><ltbullet1>terms of licensing;<hr><ltbullet1>advertising requirements;<hr><ltbullet1>reporting requirements; and<hr><ltbullet1>disclosure of information to birth parents and adoptive parents;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the rights of birth parents and adoptive parents;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the types of payments and fees that are permissible in an adoption;<hr><ltbullet>addresses transportation of birth mothers to Utah from other states or countries;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to mental health therapy for a birth parent;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that a birth parent can revoke consent under limited circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>addresses adoption services in health care facilities;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes; and<hr><ltbullet>defines terms.

title: Tribal Endorsement of Utah Driver License Amendments
description: This bill allows an applicant for a driver license to request a notation on the driver license or identification card indicating that the individual is an enrolled member of a federally recognized Indian tribe.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>allows an applicant to request a notation of "Federally Recognized Tribal Member" on the driver license or identification card indicating that the individual is an enrolled member of a federally recognized Indian tribe;<hr><ltbullet>instructs the Driver License Division regarding satisfactory proof that an applicant is an enrolled member of a federally recognized Indian tribe; and<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the notation from identifying a specific Indian tribe.

description: This bill deals with requirements regarding purchasing from a community rehabilitation program and related provisions.

title: Privacy Compliance for Education Technology Vendors
description: This bill requires the termination of a contract with a third-party provider in certain circumstances involving a failure to comply with state or federal privacy laws.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires an education entity or a government agency contracting on behalf of an education entity to:<hr><ltbullet1>include certain provisions in a contract with a third-party contractor;<hr><ltbullet1>notify a third-party contractor of the contractor's unauthorized sale of student data or information in violation of state or federal privacy laws; and<hr><ltbullet1>terminate a contract with a third-party contractor that does not remedy the privacy violation after notification;<hr><ltbullet>repeals a provision allowing a third-party contractor to respond to a student's request for information or feedback; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Vehicle Registration Amendments
description: This bill allows the cancellation of vehicle registration and the refund of certain taxes and fees on a pro rata basis.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allows the owner of certain vehicles to cancel the registration of the vehicle;<hr><ltbullet>allows the owner of a vehicle that cancels the registration of the vehicle to receive a refund of the registration fees and uniform fees in lieu of ad valorem tax on a pro rata basis; <hr><ltbullet>provides an additional penalty for operating a vehicle for which the registration has been canceled by the vehicle owner;<hr><ltbullet>requires reporting on data related to refunds issued; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Motor Vehicle Division Amendments
description: This bill makes technical changes including standardization of vehicle weight definitions and usage, exempting street-legal all-terrain vehicles from certain provisions, correcting a sales tax earmark, and various technical and cleanup changes.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>standardizes terms used to refer to the weight of a vehicle for consistency throughout the code;<hr><ltbullet>allows alternative registration term provisions to apply to rental car fleets;<hr><ltbullet>discontinues the issuance of special interest vehicle license plates;<hr><ltbullet>amends the definition of "rack" to only include those in operation before a certain date;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to consignment sales of motor vehicles and motor vehicle auction licenses;<hr><ltbullet>strikes language requiring owner's or operator's security for a vehicle merely registered in the state but not operated on a highway;<hr><ltbullet>codifies a definition related to motor fuel tax;<hr><ltbullet>grants rulemaking authority to the Department of Transportation to accommodate vehicles registered for a two-year term to participate in the road usage charge program;<hr><ltbullet>exempts a street-legal all-terrain vehicle from certain emissions inspection fees and odometer requirements;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes to various code sections related to motor vehicles and license plates to provide clarity and correct mistakes;<hr><ltbullet>corrects a technical drafting error in a sales tax earmark; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Insurance Code Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions relating to insurance.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes an insurance fraud investigator that the Insurance Department (department) employs to investigate crimes committed by a department licensee;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to a captive insurance company that is organized as a risk retention group;<hr><ltbullet>provides the type of experts the Insurance Commissioner (commissioner) may hire to conduct an examination of a licensee;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an entity that is subject to examination (examinee) shall pay the costs of an examination;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the commissioner may use a deposit an examinee makes to pay an examination cost an examinee fails to pay;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a deposit an examine makes shall first be used to pay for an unpaid examination cost;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to the service of process through a state officer;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the commissioner to make rules governing the process for winding down the business of a resident agency title insurance producer;<hr><ltbullet>exempts a risk retention group from paying an annual fee with the department;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to money appropriated from the Captive Insurance Restricted Account;<hr><ltbullet>requires that an insurer file with the commissioner and the National Association of Insurance Commissioners a quarterly statement of the insurer's financial condition;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to the payment of dividends to include domestic mutual insurance holding companies;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a mutual insurer or mutual insurance company provide the commissioner with a notification before a dividend distribution;<hr><ltbullet>removes a civil penalty for a director or officer of an insurance holding company that commits certain violations;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an insurer may issue a group insurance policy offering life insurance to the trustees of a fund established, created, and maintained for the benefit of members of an association group;<hr><ltbullet>changes the day on which an insurer shall make an annual report;<hr><ltbullet>increases the liability coverage a title insurance producer shall maintain;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to the type of policies an individual title insurance producer and agency title insurance producer shall maintain;<hr><ltbullet>increases the amount of coverage an individual title insurance producer or agency title insurance producer shall maintain;<hr><ltbullet>provides that if an agency title insurance producer becomes aware of facts that indicate an electronic wire funds transfer did not reach the electronic wire funds transfer's intended recipient, the agency title insurance producer make a report of the facts;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a title insurer report to the commissioner the termination of an appointment of a title insurance producer;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a nonresident title insurance agency deposit a Utah home buyer's escrow in a depository institution's Utah branch;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an individual title insurance producer or agency title insurance producer notify the parties to a real estate transaction of a closing protection letter;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a title insurance licensee is not required to deposit money in a depository institution under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>repeals certain reporting requirements relating to licensee compensation;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an insurer shall pay each claim submitted by an insured and a provider;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to required contracts involving a public adjuster;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to the compensation of a public adjuster;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions that authorize a property insurance policy to prohibit the assignment of property insurance policy rights and benefits;<hr><ltbullet>provides requirements for the funds a public adjuster holds;<hr><ltbullet>establishes public adjuster standards of conduct;<hr><ltbullet>establishes record retention requirements for a public adjuster;<hr><ltbullet>amends the standards for the conduct of a hearing the commissioner undertakes while engaging in an administrative action against an insurer;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the applicability of certain statutes to a risk retention group;<hr><ltbullet>amends the definition of the excess surplus of a captive insurance company;<hr><ltbullet>expands the authority of the commissioner to suspend or revoke the certificate of authority of a captive insurance company to conduct business in this state;<hr><ltbullet>changes the day on which an agency title insurance producer is required to pay an assessment;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to the actions the commissioner may take against a licensee;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to who is required to complete continuing education requirements;<hr><ltbullet>repeals training requirements related to a resident producer;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an ambulance membership organization is a limited health plan under Title 31A, Chapter 8, Health Maintenance Organizations and Limited Health Plans;<hr><ltbullet>provides the registration requirements for an ambulance membership organization;<hr><ltbullet>provides the renewal process for an ambulance membership organization;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an ambulance membership organization shall submit an annual report to the commissioner;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an ambulance membership organization from selling, offering for sale, or providing an ambulance membership contract to an individual enrolled in Medicaid;<hr><ltbullet>enacts marketing requirements and required disclosures for an ambulance membership organization;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the commissioner to revoke or suspend an ambulance membership organization's license;<hr><ltbullet>exempts foreign ambulance membership organizations from certain sections of code;<hr><ltbullet>removes the director of the Department of Health and Human Services from an annual audit of internal quality control for an organization;<hr><ltbullet>repeals and amends provisions related to long-term care and long-term care insurance;<hr><ltbullet>addresses requirements for insurers that provide dental services to residents in Utah;<hr><ltbullet>requires insurers to allow dental providers to opt out of participation in dental plans under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>addresses a dental insurer's obligation when a paper check is sent to a provider and is returned to the insurer;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a dental insurer from imposing a fee for paying with a paper check;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an insurer from interfering with an agreement for service between a patient and dental provider;<hr><ltbullet>addresses claim form requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires an insurer to provide an explanation of benefits that addresses non-covered services to a patient and provider; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Identification Verification Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to identification verification.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that an authorized person shall verify proof of age for an individual who appears to be 35 years old or younger before the individual procures an alcoholic product at a restaurant;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an off-premise beer retailer, a state store, or a package agency shall request proof of age from each patron;<hr><ltbullet>requires that an off-premise beer retailer, a state store, or a package agency verify that an individual is not an interdicted person if the individual provides a Utah driver license as a proof of age;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an authorized person shall verify proof of age for each individual before the individual gains admittance to a bar or tavern or purchases beer from an off-premise beer retailer;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes an authorized person to temporarily confiscate a proof of age the authorized person determines is fake; <hr><ltbullet>provides that when a court designates an individual as an interdicted person, the court may require the individual to surrender the individual's Utah driver license or Utah identification card;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an individual who voluntarily applies for a driver license or an identification card with an interdicted person qualifier is not required to pay an administrative fee imposed by the Driver License Division;<hr><ltbullet>provides a coordination clause between this bill and H.B. 597, Alcohol Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: School and Institutional Trust Lands Amendments
description: This bill addresses the preservation of a culturally or scientifically significant site on school and institutional trust lands.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTNAE", "name": "Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates a process for a county to nominate a culturally or scientifically significant site located on school and institutional trust lands (trust lands) for potential preservation;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for the nomination of a proposed culturally or scientifically significant site;<hr><ltbullet>requires the director of the School and Institutional Trust Lands Administration (administration) to:<hr><ltbullet1>notify a county with trust lands of the opportunity to nominate a culturally or scientifically significant site;<hr><ltbullet1>approve a nomination for a culturally or scientifically significant site if the director determines that the nomination is consistent with the established requirements; and<hr><ltbullet1>maintain and periodically review a list of approved culturally or scientifically significant sites;<hr><ltbullet>allows the director of the administration to:<hr><ltbullet1>reject a nomination if the director determines the nomination is inconsistent with the established requirements; and<hr><ltbullet1>consider a preservation measure if the culturally or scientifically significant site is at risk; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Housing and Community Development Amendments
description: This bill creates the Division of Housing and Community Development within the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTEDW", "name": "Economic Development and Workforce Services Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates the Division of Housing and Community Development (HCD) within the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity by enacting, renumbering, and amending certain provisions from the Housing and Community Development Division within the Department of Workforce Services and the Governor's Office of Planning and Budget to HCD;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides for personnel transfer from the Housing and Community Development Division within the Department of Workforce Services to HCD;<hr><ltbullet>creates the state housing coordinator (housing coordinator) position within HCD, who is appointed by the governor with the advice and consent of the Senate;<hr><ltbullet>renames the Housing and Community Development Division within the Department of Workforce Services to the Division of Community Services within the Department of Workforce Services; <hr><ltbullet>repeals certain obsolete sections of code;<hr><ltbullet>repeals certain sections of code to consolidate with other code sections;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the Commission on Housing Affordability; <hr><ltbullet>requires coordination between the housing coordinator of HCD and the Utah Housing Corporation (UHC) under certain circumstances; <hr><ltbullet>amends the required fields of expertise of public trustees appointed to the UHC board of trustees; <hr><ltbullet>moves the Homeless Housing and Services Grant Program from the Office of Homeless Services into HCD; <hr><ltbullet>requires recipients of certain state or state-administered funds to report certain data to HCD; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Drinking Water Restructuring Amendments
description: This bill addresses violations of the Safe Drinking Water Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates and modifies terms;<hr><ltbullet>allows a court to:<hr><ltbullet1>appoint a receiver for a supplier of a public water system to implement a corrective or remedial action for a violation of the Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) or compliance order; and<hr><ltbullet1>require a violator to divest ownership of the public water system to ensure long-term compliance with SDWA;<hr><ltbullet>requires the director of the Division of Drinking Water to report to a legislative committee if the director brings a civil action that may result in a receivership or divestment for a public water system supplier; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Health and Human Services (department) to contract for a new electronic health record system for inmate care, based on recommendations of a working group;<hr><ltbullet>permits appropriations from the Medicaid Growth Reduction and Budget Stabilization Account for the electronic health record system;<hr><ltbullet>provides that money appropriated to the department to pay for unanticipated high-cost correctional health expenses is non-lapsing;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department, in consultation with the Department of Corrections, to prepare and implement a plan for providing opioid use disorder treatment to certain inmates who suffer from an opioid use disorder, and requires the Department of Corrections to cooperate with the department in providing medication assisted treatment in accordance with that plan;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Health Provider Directory and Access Amendments
description: This bill addresses provider directories and timely access to behavioral health services.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires covered insurers to:<hr><ltbullet1>assist enrollees in accessing behavioral health services in a timely manner; <hr><ltbullet1>facilitate an insured obtaining behavioral health services from an out-of-network provider if an in-network provider is not available in a timely manner; <hr><ltbullet1>publish health care provider directories; <hr><ltbullet1>regularly update health care provider directories; and<hr><ltbullet1>take certain steps to ensure the accuracy of provider directories; <hr><ltbullet>authorizes Utah's insurance commissioner (commissioner) to make rules to implement certain provisions of this bill; <hr><ltbullet>requires providers to respond to an insurer's request for verification of provider directory information within a certain period of time; <hr><ltbullet>requires insurers and the commissioner to issue an educational letter to a provider that demonstrates a pattern of violations of certain provisions;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Professional Licensing to convene a working group to study the feasibility and cost of creating and maintaining a statewide behavioral health provider directory (working group) and report to the Health and Human Services Interim Committee; <hr><ltbullet>provides a repeal date for the working group; and<hr><ltbullet>defines terms.

title: Criminal Use of Cryptocurrency Amendments
description: This bill creates cryptocurrency training requirements for law enforcement and consumer protections for digital asset kiosks.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTLAW", "name": "Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires specialized cryptocurrency investigation training for designated officers;<hr><ltbullet>requires local law enforcement agencies to report cryptocurrency investigation data to the Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice (commission);<hr><ltbullet>requires the commission to provide annual summary reports to the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet>establishes consumer protection requirements for virtual currency kiosks, including graduated transaction limits, disclosure requirements, fraud prevention warnings, annual location reporting, and recordkeeping requirements;<hr><ltbullet>provides enforcement authority to the Division of Consumer Protection, including administrative penalties and civil actions for violations of virtual currency kiosk regulations;<hr><ltbullet>provides for legislative sunset review of cryptocurrency investigation reporting requirements; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Signature Gathering Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions for initiative and referendum petitions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies certain forms to provide that:<hr><ltbullet1>for an individual who signs an initiative or referendum petition, the individual had an opportunity to read the entire statement included in the initiative or referendum packet; and<hr><ltbullet1>for an individual who gathers signatures for an initiative or referendum petition, the individual believes that the individual described above had an opportunity to read the law that is the subject of the petition;<hr><ltbullet>specifies that a person may use a spiral binder to bind together the pages that make up an initiative or referendum packet; <hr><ltbullet>provides that an individual who gathers signatures for an initiative or referendum petition may remove a signature sheet from the initiative or referendum packet for the purpose of gathering signatures; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Tax Modifications
description: This bill modifies tax provisions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>consolidates certain State Tax Commission reports in relation to federal tax law changes;<hr><ltbullet>provides penalty provisions that apply if a producer fails to file a Form 1099 for mineral production tax withholding or fails to file the Form 1099 on time;<hr><ltbullet>modifies filing requirements applicable to producers for mineral production tax withholding;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies assessment requirements for the common areas of a condominium or community association;<hr><ltbullet>increases property valuation thresholds for which county reporting to the State Tax Commission and the Revenue and Taxation Interim Committee is required;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the definition of "indigent individual," as applied to property tax relief, by removing language that limits a finding of extreme hardship to counties;<hr><ltbullet>allows a taxpayer to appeal a county's denial of the taxpayer's application for property tax relief on the basis of late filing;<hr><ltbullet>consolidates a list of all privilege tax exemptions within the privilege tax statute;<hr><ltbullet>consolidates certain tax credit review requirements applicable to the Utah low-income housing tax credit;<hr><ltbullet>expands the definition of "Utah unrelated business income," as applied to corporate income tax, to include allocated income;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the taxpayer tax credit to align with federal tax changes;<hr><ltbullet>extends provisions allowing for pass-through entities to pay taxes on behalf of individuals;<hr><ltbullet>expands the definition of "short-term rental," as applied to sales and use tax, to include rentals involving real property;<hr><ltbullet>requires a county that imposes the 1% local option sales and use tax to distribute revenue collected within a newly-incorporated municipality to that municipality for a certain period;<hr><ltbullet>increases the weight-based motor vehicle exemption for the motor vehicle rental tax;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the motor vehicle exemptions for the tourism, recreation, cultural, convention, and airport facilities tax to match the exemptions for the motor vehicle rental tax;<hr><ltbullet>requires a taxing entity to provide notice of the reauthorization of certain local option sales taxes to the State Tax Commission within a certain period before the reauthorization takes effect;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the State Tax Commission from enforcing a reauthorized local option sales tax unless the taxing entity provides timely notice of the reauthorization;<hr><ltbullet>repeals obsolete tax provisions, including the income tax credit for items using cleaner burning fuels and the inheritance tax; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Governmental Immunity Amendments
description: This bill amends the Governmental Immunity Act of Utah.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; <hr><ltbullet>provides that a governmental entity and the governmental entity's employees are immune from suit for engaging in the following activities: <hr><ltbullet1>responding to a disaster or potential disaster; or<hr><ltbullet1>if the employee is a first responder, providing emergency medical services;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that immunity from suit for providing emergency medical services is not limited to providing medical services resulting from emergencies of a certain type; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Dangerous Weapon Amendments
description: This bill addresses the carrying of dangerous weapons at an institution of higher education.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allows an individual 21 years old or older to conceal a dangerous weapon at an institution of higher education without a concealed carry permit;<hr><ltbullet>amends the offense of carrying a dangerous weapon at an institution of higher education by:<hr><ltbullet1>renaming the offense to "Openly carrying a dangerous weapon at an institution of higher education";<hr><ltbullet1>removing private institutions of higher education from locations where the offense is applicable; and<hr><ltbullet1>prohibiting an individual, including an individual with any type of concealed carry permit, from openly carrying a dangerous weapon at an institution of higher education unless the individual is lawfully responding to an active threat;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that an individual 18 years old or older but younger than 21 years old may carry, in an open manner, an unloaded firearm in any public location not prohibited by state statute or federal law;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that an individual who has a concealed carry permit that allows the individual to carry on the grounds of an elementary school or secondary school may not open carry a dangerous weapon on the grounds of an elementary school or secondary school unless the individual is lawfully responding to an active threat; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: State Sovereignty Amendments
description: This bill addresses state sovereignty.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the governor or the chief executive officer of a political subdivision from declaring a state of emergency exclusively in response to an international organization's proclamation declaring a state of emergency;<hr><ltbullet>declares that an international organization has no power, jurisdiction, or legal authority in the state;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the state, state agencies, and local governments from implementing or enforcing an international directive issued by an international organization; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

description: This bill amends provisions relating to those who are restricted persons regarding dangerous weapons.

title: Public Assistance Amendments
description: This bill addresses lawful presence for receipt of public benefits.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>removes authority for an agency or political subdivision of the state to skip verification of lawful presence for receipt of a state or local public benefit or a federal public benefit the state administers;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an agency or political subdivision of the state from providing state or local public benefits to an individual who is unlawfully present in the United States, with certain exceptions;  <hr><ltbullet>requires an agency or department to conduct certain audits;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Office of the Legislative Auditor General may conduct a certain audit under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>provides for criminal or civil penalties under certain circumstances; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Presumption of Indigency Amendments
description: This bill addresses a court's determination of indigency.

title: Presidential Electors Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions governing the distribution of electoral votes.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>in an election for president and vice president of the United States:<hr><ltbullet1>allocates one electoral vote for the presidential and vice presidential candidates who receive the highest number of votes in a Congressional district;<hr><ltbullet1>allocates two electoral votes for the presidential and vice presidential candidates who receive the highest number of statewide votes; and<hr><ltbullet1>requires a registered political party, or an unaffiliated candidate or a write-in candidate for president of the United States, to notify the lieutenant governor if a vacancy occurs in the office of a presidential elector; <hr><ltbullet>standardizes the deadlines to file a declaration of candidacy for the office of vice president of the United States and to choose presidential electors; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Firearm Background Check Amendments
description: This bill addresses background checks for firearms.

title: Underage Marriage Amendments
description: This bill addresses provisions related to underage marriage.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates the criminal offense of unlawfully marrying a minor;<hr><ltbullet>creates the criminal offense of transporting a minor out of state for an illegal marriage;<hr><ltbullet>creates the criminal offense of traveling out of state to marry a minor;<hr><ltbullet>moves to the criminal code the existing criminal offense for a parent or guardian to unlawfully consent or allow a minor to enter a marriage;<hr><ltbullet>moves to the criminal code the existing criminal offense for unlawfully solemnizing a marriage of a minor;<hr><ltbullet>moves to the criminal code the existing criminal offense of fraudulently acting as a minor's parent or guardian for the purpose of providing a false consent for the minor to get married;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the statute of limitations for a criminal prosecution for unlawfully marrying a minor, transporting a minor out of state for an illegal marriage, or traveling out of state to marry a minor is 15 years from the day on which a minor to the marriage turns 18 years old;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a marriage performed in another country, state, or territory, in which one of the parties to the marriage is a minor, is invalid in Utah unless the marriage meets certain requirements; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.
