title: Offender Modifications
description: This bill addresses provisions related to offenders.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allows a court to order the Division of Adult Probation and Parole to supervise an individual convicted of class B misdemeanors under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Board of Pardons and Parole (board), if considering whether to parole an offender who has previously been paroled and had the offender's parole revoked due to a new criminal offense, to consider the facts and circumstances of the new criminal offense in determining whether the offender should be paroled again;<hr><ltbullet>allows the board, with certain exceptions, to only consider a pardon for an offender who has committed an offense that requires the offender to register on the Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry (the registry) if:<hr><ltbullet1>for a sex offender required to register on the registry for 10 years, 10 years have passed from when the sex offender entered the community after the sex offender's conviction; or<hr><ltbullet1>for a sex offender required to register on the registry for the sex offender's lifetime, 20 years have passed from when the sex offender entered the community after the sex offender's conviction;<hr><ltbullet>does not allow an offender who has committed an offense that requires the offender to register on the registry at the time the offender is sentenced to receive a certificate of eligibility of expungement from the Bureau of Criminal Identification; and<hr><ltbullet>adds to the requirements for the board to meet before the board may parole an offender before the offender's minimum term of imprisonment has been met.

title: Wildlife Amendments
description: This bill addresses the management of wildlife resources and wildlife habitats.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>addresses who may provide verification of illness, injury, or disability in relationship to a license, certificate, or permit issued under the Wildlife Resources Act;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to notice of acquisition of real property;<hr><ltbullet>addresses rulemaking and penalties related to reporting hunt information;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the management of grizzly bears;<hr><ltbullet>grants rulemaking authority;<hr><ltbullet>addresses discharge of a dangerous weapon related to a waterfowl management area or wildlife management area; <hr><ltbullet>creates the Poaching Mitigation Fund;<hr><ltbullet>provides for restitution money to be deposited into the Poaching Mitigation Fund for use by the Division of Law Enforcement within the Department of Natural Resources;<hr><ltbullet>removes references to spotters;<hr><ltbullet>provides that money in the Guide and Outfitter Fund be used by the Division of Law Enforcement within the Department of Natural Resources;<hr><ltbullet>removes outdated language related to the Division of Professional Licensing;<hr><ltbullet>modifies definitions related to guide and outfitter provisions, including the definition of a guide or outfitter;<hr><ltbullet>modifies fee provisions;<hr><ltbullet>amends under certain circumstances the total number of individuals allowed to provide guide services or outfitting services at a time;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the relationship between guides and outfitters and the retention of outfitters;<hr><ltbullet>addresses unlawful activity of a pilot of an aircraft;<hr><ltbullet>requires certain reimbursements of investigatory expenses for violations of the wildlife resources title;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to unlawful taking of protected wildlife related to a guide or outfitter; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: Political Advertising Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to political advertising.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>specifies that an electioneering communication or a political advertisement includes a communication or advertisement disseminated on a social media platform;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes an election officer to impose a monetary fine against a person who violates certain provisions related to political advertising and reporting requirements;<hr><ltbullet>limits a fine described above to one per political advertisement for disclosure violations and one per act or omission for other violations;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to add a cross-reference to a subsection enacted in H.B. 33, Political Signs Amendments, that amends the same section that this bill amends; and   <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Emergency Reporting Abuse Amendments
description: This bill amends the criminal offense of emergency reporting abuse.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies the offense of emergency reporting abuse to include conduct in which an actor contacts a 911 emergency response service when the actor knows, or reasonably should know, that no actual or perceived emergency, crime, or other circumstance jeopardizing public safety exists;<hr><ltbullet>adds new penalties to the criminal offense of emergency reporting abuse; <hr><ltbullet>moves a definition to the statute in which the definition is referenced; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Adult-oriented Performance and Material Amendments
description: This bill addresses criminal offenses relating to adult-oriented performances and materials.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>removes unlawful pornographic performances from the offense of distributing pornographic material and places the conduct into a new stand-alone offense;<hr><ltbullet>removes aiding or abetting a minor in an unlawful pornographic performance from the offense of aiding or abetting a minor in distributing pornographic material and places the conduct into a new stand-alone offense; <hr><ltbullet>removes engaging in a performance that is harmful to minors while in the presence of a minor from the offense of distributing material harmful to minors and places the conduct into a new stand-alone offense;<hr><ltbullet>changes the mental state required to be convicted of engaging in a performance that is harmful to minors while in the presence of a minor;<hr><ltbullet>amends penalties for committing the offense of distributing material harmful to minors;<hr><ltbullet>removes aiding or abetting a minor to engage in a performance that is harmful to minors while in the presence of another minor from the offense of aiding or abetting a minor in distributing material harmful to minors and places the conduct into a new stand-alone offense;<hr><ltbullet>revises the criminal conduct referenced above for clarity, including penalty provisions;<hr><ltbullet>adds the new stand-alone offenses to statutes in which the current offenses are referenced, including:<hr><ltbullet1> the offense of creating, viewing, or accessing pornographic or indecent material on school property; and <hr><ltbullet1>statutes concerning patterns of unlawful activity, property subject to forfeiture, court orders for criminal investigations, and civil enforcement actions; <hr><ltbullet>adds a coordination clause to merge the changes to Section 76-5c-205 if this bill and S.B. 18, Criminal Offense Modifications, both pass and become law; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill amends provisions relating to automotive repairs.

title: Pregnant and Postpartum Inmate Amendments
description: This bill addresses issues related to inmates who are pregnant or in postpartum recovery.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Corrections (the department) and each county jail to report to the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice:<hr><ltbullet1>the number of known pregnant inmates in custody; and<hr><ltbullet1>the number of inmates in custody who are parents to a minor child;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the postpartum recovery period for pregnant inmates is 12 weeks after the day on which the inmate gives birth;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the restraining of an inmate during postpartum recovery unless an individualized determination of certain security risks is made that details why the restraints are necessary;<hr><ltbullet>increases the period of time that the department and each county jail is required to provide access to a social worker to an inmate who is pregnant, or who has recently given birth, from six weeks to 12 weeks, to help the inmate:<hr><ltbullet1>arrange childcare;<hr><ltbullet1>establish a reunification plan; and<hr><ltbullet1>establish a substance abuse treatment plan, if needed;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the department and each county jail is required to provide an inmate in postpartum recovery access to postpartum care for 12 weeks after the inmate gives birth;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that health care providers in general may make certain decisions regarding pregnant inmates; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Department of Natural Resources Related Modifications Amendments
description: This bill addresses provisions related to the Department of Natural Resources and related regulated areas.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>removes language related to determining the work period for certain Department of Natural Resources' employees;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms, including defining "invasive mussel";<hr><ltbullet>exempts an owner or operator of certain vessels from requirements related to invasive species and launching or operating the vessel on waters of the state;<hr><ltbullet>addresses vessels owned by government agencies;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to a required aquatic invasive species education course;<hr><ltbullet>addresses vessels rented or leased from a boat livery, including modifying recordkeeping requirements for a boat livery;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to collection of annual aquatic invasive species fees, including repealing outdated language;<hr><ltbullet>addresses responsibilities of the Division of Law Enforcement and the Division of Wildlife Resources;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to records kept by the Division of Water Rights, including to allow for the records to be kept in physical or electronic form;<hr><ltbullet>corrects citations;<hr><ltbullet>addresses funding of litigation;<hr><ltbullet>addresses treatment of water rights after termination or noncompliance of certain royalty contracts or mineral leases;<hr><ltbullet>removes a cap on low-interest loans related to secondary water metering;<hr><ltbullet>modifies when certain applications may be filed with the state engineer under instream flow provisions;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies rulemaking authority related to rules enforced by the Division of Law Enforcement;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the duties of the Utah Geological Survey;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the makeup of the Board of the Utah Geological Survey;<hr><ltbullet>changes the term "buffalo" to "bison" in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the section specifying funding sources of the Watershed Restoration Initiative;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the Alternative Energy Development Tax Credit Act; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: Use of Force Reporting Requirements
description: This bill addresses the justified use of force.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes that an individual is required to report, or cause another individual to report, the use of deadly force to 911 or law enforcement in order to receive a pretrial justification hearing;<hr><ltbullet>automatically provides a defendant with a prima facie claim of justification at a pretrial justification hearing if the defendant reported, or caused another individual to report, the defendant's use of force within 24 hours after using the force; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Offender Transfer Amendments
description: This bill addresses provisions related to the Interstate Compact for Adult Offender Supervision.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends the fee for an individual on probation or parole who is applying for a transfer of supervision to another state under the Interstate Compact for Adult Offender Supervision (the compact);<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that under the compact that an individual on probation or parole in this state who seeks a transfer of supervision to another state due to a felony or qualifying misdemeanor is required to be under the supervision of the Division of Adult Probation and Parole before the individual may apply for the transfer;<hr><ltbullet>enacts requirements for a court or the Board of Pardons and Parole when issuing an arrest warrant for an individual on probation or parole who has violated the terms of the individual's supervision and is being supervised in another state under the compact;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Bureau of Criminal Identification to submit any arrest warrant for an individual on probation or parole being supervised in another state under the compact to the National Crime Information Center;<hr><ltbullet>merges the reporting requirements applicable to the Bureau of Criminal Identification under Section 53-10-214 with the reporting requirements applicable to the Bureau of Criminal Identification under Section 53-10-213 and repeals Section 53-10-214; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Unlicensed Driver Amendments
description: This bill addresses drivers without a driver license, driving privilege card, or learner permit.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; <hr><ltbullet>modifies the circumstances in which law enforcement is required to impound a vehicle;<hr><ltbullet>addresses identification of an individual who operates a vehicle without a valid driving credential;<hr><ltbullet>allows certain fees to be waived in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>modifies certain fees and the allocation of fee revenue;<hr><ltbullet>amends certain penalties associated with driving without a driver license;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to administrative suspension of a driver license; <hr><ltbullet>requires a vendor providing software service for a fingerprint device to ensure the software is compatible with law enforcement database software; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Violent Crime Clearance Rate Amendments
description: This bill creates a grant program to assist a law enforcement agency in solving violent crimes.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Violent Crime Clearance Rate Fund, which:<hr><ltbullet1>includes legislative appropriations, contributions from private sources, and any interest earned on the fund;<hr><ltbullet1>is administered by the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice; and<hr><ltbullet1>is nonlapsing;<hr><ltbullet>directs the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice to award grants from the Violent Crime Clearance Rate Fund to law enforcement agencies to assist with efforts in solving violent crimes;<hr><ltbullet>describes how the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice shall allocate funds; and<hr><ltbullet>requires a law enforcement agency that receives a grant from the Violent Crime Clearance Rate Fund to use the money for purposes related to solving violent crimes.

title: International Money Transmission Amendments
description: This bill enacts provisions related to international money transmissions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>imposes a tax on international money transmissions on or after a certain date;<hr><ltbullet>exempts an international money transmission from the tax if the customer requesting the transaction presents valid identification;<hr><ltbullet>requires the tax to be stated separately on an invoice or receipt;<hr><ltbullet>requires licensed money transmitters to remit collected taxes quarterly and report annually to the State Tax Commission;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the State Tax Commission's administration of the tax;<hr><ltbullet>requires the commissioner of the Department of Financial Institutions to annually provide a list of each licensed money transmitter to the State Tax Commission; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Tax Return Donation Amendments
description: This bill creates a School Meals Debt Relief Fund and provides for the fund's administration.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates a School Meals Debt Relief Fund;<hr><ltbullet>allows individual taxpayers to designate contributions to the fund on tax returns;<hr><ltbullet>establishes reporting requirements for local education agencies regarding school meals debt;<hr><ltbullet>provides for a distribution process based on each local education agency's proportion of total statewide school meals debt;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Board of Education to collect and verify school meals debt data;<hr><ltbullet>delegates rulemaking authority to the State Board of Education for program administration; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Sexual Material Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions relating to liability for obscenity, a child sex doll, or child sexual abuse material.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an individual has a cause of action if a person exposes the individual to or depicts the individual in obscenity or child sexual abuse material;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an individual has a cause of action if a person depicts or intends to depict the individual's likeness as a minor on a child sex doll;<hr><ltbullet>provides requirements for an individual bringing an action under provisions this bill enacts;<hr><ltbullet>provides the relief a court may grant an individual bringing an action under the provisions this bill enacts;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an entity that provides access to the internet is not liable under the provisions this bill enacts, if the entity did not create the content;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes an individual to bring an action regardless of whether conduct has resulted in a criminal conviction;<hr><ltbullet>provides a severability clause; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Department of Natural Resources Amendments
description: This bill addresses provisions related to the Department of Natural Resources.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>removes language related to determining the work period for certain Department of Natural Resources' employees;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to records kept by the Division of Water Rights, including to allow for the records to be kept in physical or electronic form;<hr><ltbullet>corrects citations;<hr><ltbullet>addresses treatment of water rights after termination or noncompliance of certain royalty contracts or mineral leases;<hr><ltbullet>removes a cap on low-interest loans related to secondary water metering;<hr><ltbullet>modifies when certain applications may be filed with the state engineer under instream flow provisions;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies rulemaking authority related to rules enforced by the Division of Law Enforcement;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the duties of the Utah Geological Survey;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the makeup of the Board of the Utah Geological Survey;<hr><ltbullet>changes the term "buffalo" to "bison" in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>repeals section specifying funding sources of the Watershed Restoration Initiative;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the Alternative Energy Development Tax Credit Act; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: Unlawful Tracking Amendments
description: This bill addresses the unlawful tracking of an individual.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends the offense of unlawful installation of a tracking device by:<hr><ltbullet1>renaming the offense to unlawful use of a tracking device or tracking application;<hr><ltbullet1>broadening the offense to include placing a tracking device on certain personal property and using a tracking application to track another individual's movements;<hr><ltbullet1>clarifying that an actor commits the offense if the victim had previously given consent for the actor to use the tracking device or tracking application and later revoked that consent, and the actor continued to use the tracking device or tracking application; and<hr><ltbullet1>requiring statutory damages in a successful civil action brought by a victim if the victim elects to receive the statutory damages instead of compensatory damages; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Critical Infrastructure Amendments
description: This bill enacts provisions regarding foreign adversary threats to critical infrastructure.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>directs the Utah Cyber Center to develop guidance on foreign adversary threats to critical infrastructure;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits use of federally banned equipment in critical infrastructure;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes voluntary security assessments for critical infrastructure involving foreign adversary technology;<hr><ltbullet>provides for coordination between the Utah Cyber Center and governmental entities on critical infrastructure security;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits governmental entities and critical infrastructure providers from contracting for or deploying technology included on a prohibited list maintained by the Utah Cyber Center; <hr><ltbullet>requires the Utah Cyber Center to publish and maintain a prohibited list of foreign adversary technologies that pose a risk to critical infrastructure; <hr><ltbullet>prohibits entities with access to critical infrastructure from entering into agreements with foreign principals that would allow remote access to or control of critical infrastructure; and <hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Utah Cyber Center to approve exceptions to the prohibitions under specified circumstances.

title: Signature Collection Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions related to nominations for elective office.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires an election official to post the name and date of signature of a voter who signs a nomination petition on the lieutenant governor's website for at least 90 days;<hr><ltbullet>requires an election official to notify the county or district attorney if a person whose signature appears on a nomination petition notifies the election official that the person did not sign the nomination petition;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the deadlines for a voter who signs a nomination petition to submit a statement to an election official requesting that the voter's signature be removed from the petition; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Hunting and Fishing Amendments
description: This bill addresses practices related to hunting and fishing.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates the Poaching Mitigation Fund;<hr><ltbullet>provides for restitution money to be deposited into the Poaching Mitigation Fund for use by the Division of Law Enforcement within the Department of Natural Resources;<hr><ltbullet>removes references to spotters;<hr><ltbullet>provides that money in the Guide and Outfitter Fund be used by the Division of Law Enforcement within the Department of Natural Resources;<hr><ltbullet>removes outdated language related to the Division of Professional Licensing;<hr><ltbullet>modifies definitions related to guide and outfitter provisions, including the definition of a guide or outfitter;<hr><ltbullet>modifies fee provisions;<hr><ltbullet>amends under certain circumstances the total number of individuals allowed to provide guide services or outfitting services at a time;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the relationship between guides and outfitters and the retention of outfitters;<hr><ltbullet>addresses unlawful activity of a pilot of an aircraft;<hr><ltbullet>requires certain reimbursements of investigatory expenses for violations of title;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to unlawful taking of protected wildlife related to a guide or outfitter; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: Boating Insurance Amendments
description: This bill removes the requirement for boat insurance.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>repeals the statutory requirement for boat insurance; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: School Board Referendum Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to local referendums.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>subject to certain exceptions, establishes a process for voters who are residents of a school district to hold a referendum on a law passed by the school district's local school board, including a law that increases a tax or imposes a new tax;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to add a reference to a referable local school tax law being enacted in this bill to similar language being enacted in H.B. 32, Signature Gathering and Verification Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Public Funds and Political Activities Amendments
description: This bill addresses political activities of persons receiving public funds.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an entity from receiving a government contract or a state grant if:<hr><ltbullet1>the entity participates in a political campaign;<hr><ltbullet1>the entity devotes more than an insubstantial part of the entity's activities to attempting to influence legislation; or<hr><ltbullet1>the entity's primary objective can only be attained by legislative action or inaction and the entity advocates for that action or inaction;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a current or prospective government contractor or a current or prospective state grant recipient from making a contribution to a political entity or to another person for a political purpose; and<hr><ltbullet>provides enforcement of the provisions in this bill.

title: Milk Amendments
description: This bill addresses the regulation of milk or milk products.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies an exemption from certain dairy regulations;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>outlines general requirements related to raw milk or raw milk products;<hr><ltbullet>addresses prohibited counts in raw milk;<hr><ltbullet>prescribes labeling;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the suspension and reissuance of permits;<hr><ltbullet>addresses foodborne illness outbreaks;<hr><ltbullet>addresses cease and desist orders;<hr><ltbullet>addresses rulemaking;<hr><ltbullet>provides for fees;<hr><ltbullet>imposes penalties;<hr><ltbullet>exempts from certain requirements sales or deliveries of raw milk or raw products from a farm;<hr><ltbullet>provides for an exemption for small producers;<hr><ltbullet>provides for no severability; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Uniform Estate Planning Amendments
description: This bill enacts the Uniform Electronic Estate Planning Documents Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>enacts the Uniform Electronic Estate Planning Documents Act;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the scope of the provisions this bill enacts;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a non-testamentary estate planning document or an electronic signature may not be denied legal effect because the non-testamentary estate planning document or electronic signature is in electronic form;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a non-testamentary estate planning document or an electronic signature is attributable to a person if the non-testamentary estate planning document or the electronic signature was the act of the person;<hr><ltbullet>provides notarization and acknowledgment requirements for a non-testamentary estate planning document or an electronic signature on an electronic non-testamentary estate planning document;<hr><ltbullet>provides witnessing and attestation requirements for an electronic non-testamentary estate planning document;<hr><ltbullet>establishes retention requirements for an electronic non-testamentary estate planning document;<hr><ltbullet>provides the manner in which an individual may certify a paper copy of an electronic non-testamentary estate planning document;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an electronic non-testamentary estate planning document or an electronic signature on an electronic non-testamentary estate planning document may not be excluded from a proceeding solely because the electronic non-testamentary estate planning document or an electronic signature is in electronic form; and<hr><ltbullet>provides the manner in which the provisions this bill enacts relate to existing law.

title: Genetic Information Amendments
description: This bill addresses the use of genetic sequencing tools and the storage of genetic sequencing data.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the use of certain genetic sequencers and genetic sequencing software;<hr><ltbullet>prescribes requirements and restrictions related to the storage of genetic sequencing data;<hr><ltbullet>requires relevant entities to certify compliance with genetic sequencing requirements;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the attorney general to investigate alleged violations of genetic sequencing requirements, and initiate civil actions for those violations; and<hr><ltbullet>provides protections for an employee who reports a suspected violation of genetic sequencing requirements to the attorney general.

title: Sex Designation Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to sex and gender.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>replaces the term gender with sex; and<hr><ltbullet>requires agencies when making administrative rules, policies, and programs to refer to biological sex using the term sex instead of gender.

title: Small Lots and Starter Homes Amendments
description: This bill deals with regulation of certain land uses in residential zones located in counties of the first, second, and third class.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; <hr><ltbullet>provides that a person may make a request to a county of the first, second, or third class, or a municipality located in a county of the first, second, or third class, in regard to a proposed land use that conforms with a preferred land use regulation;<hr><ltbullet>requires the municipality or county to determine if a request conforms with a preferred land use regulation and provide notice of the determination to the applicant;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a planning commission or legislative body to deny a request, under certain conditions, that conforms with a preferred land use regulation;<hr><ltbullet>provides that if a planning commission or legislative body does not deny a request that conforms with a preferred land use regulation within 45 days, the request becomes a permitted use; <hr><ltbullet>provides that a person has two years from the day on which a request becomes permitted to submit a complete application; and<hr><ltbullet>provides that, after a request is denied, a person may make a subsequent request made within four years of the denial but the subsequent request requires the legislative body to expressly approve the request for the request to become a permitted use.

description: This bill amends provisions relating to the Judicial Conduct Commission.

title: Water Amendments
description: This bill addresses water in the lower basin as defined by the Colorado River Compact.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>exempts from provisions related to abandonment or forfeiture for nonuse certain water rights of a water conservancy district that are related to the lower basin; <hr><ltbullet>prohibits certain instream flow change applications related to the lower basin; <hr><ltbullet>provides a coordination clause between this bill and H.B. 348, Dedicated Water Amendments, to include dedicated water applications in certain prohibitions of instream flow applications related to the lower basin; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: Juvenile Justice Amendments
description: This bill amends statutory provisions related to juvenile justice.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires a school to refer a minor to a court after a minor has allegedly committed a drug possession offense for a third time;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms related to offenses committed at school;<hr><ltbullet>amends the notification requirements for an offense committed by a student on school grounds;<hr><ltbullet>recodifies and amends requirements related to the notification of an offense committed by a student on school grounds, including statutory provisions addressing investigations, searches, and immunity;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms for juvenile programming and data reporting requirements;<hr><ltbullet>addresses a minor's eligibility for a nonjudicial adjustment when a referral to a juvenile court involves certain offenses;<hr><ltbullet>repeals statutes regarding notification and reporting of prohibited acts by students;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes; and<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to address the cross-reference changes to drug offenses if this bill and H.B. 301, Drug Recodification, both pass and become law.

description: This bill modifies income tax credits for employer-provided child care.

title: Transgender Medical Procedures Amendments
description: This bill addresses the use of public employee insurance for certain transgender medical treatments and procedures.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>subject to a limited exception, prohibits public employee insurance from covering, or paying or reimbursing for the performance of, certain transgender medical treatments or procedures;<hr><ltbullet>provides that if, before May 6, 2026, public employee insurance paid or reimbursed for a procedure to transition an individual from the individual's biological sex, public employee insurance must offer the same type and amount of insurance coverage for a procedure to restore that individual, to the extent possible, to that individual's biological sex; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Utah State Board of Education Ethics Amendments
description: This bill establishes comprehensive ethics standards, complaint procedures, and enforcement mechanisms for members of the State Board of Education.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes a code of official conduct for State Board of Education members in statute;<hr><ltbullet>creates requirements for conflict of interest disclosures and ethics training;<hr><ltbullet>establishes procedures for filing ethics complaints against board members;<hr><ltbullet>creates an independent ethics commission to investigate complaints;<hr><ltbullet>establishes hearing procedures, evidentiary standards, and due process protections;<hr><ltbullet>provides for disciplinary actions for violations;<hr><ltbullet>establishes confidentiality requirements and contempt provisions; and<hr><ltbullet>provides authority for subpoenas and witness examination.

title: Health Data Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to the Department of Health and Human Services' health data authority.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies and amends provisions related to the Department of Health and Human Services' (department) health data plans;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies and amends provisions related to the All Payer Claims Database;<hr><ltbullet>repeals certain reporting requirements; <hr><ltbullet>allows the department to share data within the department and with public health authorities, local mental health authorities, and local substance use authorities;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions related to data security and privacy;<hr><ltbullet>extends the repeal date for the department's health data authority;<hr><ltbullet>creates a repeal date for the Health Data Committee; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Non-Compete Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to non-compete agreements.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an employer from enforcing a non-compete agreement against an employee under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a person from enforcing a non-compete agreement against an independent contractor;<hr><ltbullet>requires that an employer presenting an employee with an offer of employment include with the offer of employment a non-compete agreement if the employer intends to enter into a non-compete agreement with the employee;<hr><ltbullet>imposes requirements on an employer presenting an employee with a non-compete agreement;<hr><ltbullet>requires that an employer give an employee advance notice of a non-compete agreement;<hr><ltbullet>makes void a non-compete agreement under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a person that fails to comply with provisions that this bill enacts may not enforce a non-compete agreement;<hr><ltbullet>grants a right of action to an individual against a person that attempts to enforce an unlawful non-compete agreement; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Substance Use Intervention Amendments
description: This bill addresses substance use interventions in communities and for criminal justice involved individuals.

title: Competency Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to competency evaluations.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires that when a court orders two competency evaluations, the evaluations must be ordered in the same order; <hr><ltbullet>provides that a court may order the Department of Health and Human Services to conduct additional or updated competency evaluations under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>permits a defendant to be transferred to a clinical or inpatient setting for a competency evaluation;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that certain provisions do not apply to progress toward competency evaluations;<hr><ltbullet>amends a provision related to a report of a progress toward competency evaluation; <hr><ltbullet>provides for the portability of an involuntary medication order when an individual is transferred between facilities; <hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Voting Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to voting.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides a process for an election officer to independently determine whether a registered voter is not a citizen of the United States;<hr><ltbullet>provides a process to challenge a determination described in the preceding paragraph;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an individual from voting if an election officer independently determines that the voter is not a citizen of the United States and the individual does not successfully dispute the determination;<hr><ltbullet>creates a bifurcated ballot system where, for an election held on or after November 1, 2026:<hr><ltbullet1>a voter chooses whether to provide documentary proof of United States citizenship when registering to vote or before voting; and<hr><ltbullet1>a voter who does not provide documentary proof of United States citizenship may only vote in races for federal office;<hr><ltbullet>modifies voter registration forms and requirements consistent with the bifurcated ballot system;<hr><ltbullet>establishes procedures for administration of the bifurcated ballot system;<hr><ltbullet>establishes or modifies deadlines to cure a ballot or to provide proof of citizenship, as needed, for a rejected ballot or a provisional ballot;<hr><ltbullet>modifies voter registration list requirements in relation to the bifurcated ballot system; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill addresses tax penalties within the Individual Income Tax Act.

title: County Formation Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to the creation of a new county.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a process for the legislative body of a petitioning municipality to initiate a process to create a new county;<hr><ltbullet>imposes a threshold for petitioners and certain viability requirements on the formation of a new county, including the completion of a feasibility study;<hr><ltbullet>allows certain rural property to remain in a seceding county, in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the continuation of property taxation between a seceding county and a new county to satisfy general obligation or revenue bond indebtedness;<hr><ltbullet>requires a new county to levy local option sales and use taxes for transportation at the same rate and in the same manner as the seceding county for transactions within the new county;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies provisions regarding the division assets and liabilities between a seceding county and a new county; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Firearms Liability Amendments
description: This bill amends civil liability concerning firearms and firearm-related items.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and amends definitions;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions and requirements for certain claims arising from a firearm or firearm-related item brought against:<hr><ltbullet1>a seller or manufacturer of a firearm or a firearm-related item; or <hr><ltbullet1>a trade association;<hr><ltbullet>for certain claims arising from a firearm or a firearm-related item:<hr><ltbullet1>requires a court to dismiss claims that fail to meet specific requirements;<hr><ltbullet1>grants reasonable attorney fees and court costs to a prevailing defendant in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet1>allows a defendant to appeal an interlocutory order that denies the defendant's motion to dismiss certain claims; and<hr><ltbullet1>prevents a foreign nation from asserting specific exceptions that may allow a claim for civil liability;<hr><ltbullet>preempts a political subdivision from imposing civil liability on a manufacturer, seller, or trade association in certain circumstances; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Public Safety Data Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to public safety data.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>removes a report required to be submitted by the Bureau of Criminal Identification to the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee regarding attempted weapons purchases by individuals who are restricted from purchasing, possessing, or transferring a firearm as a result of a conviction for an offense involving domestic violence and requires the report to be submitted to the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice (commission) to be included in the public safety portal;<hr><ltbullet>removes a report required to be submitted by the Division of Juvenile Justice and Youth Services to the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee regarding data of sexual assaults in detention and secure care facilities and requires the report to be submitted to the commission to be included in the public safety portal;<hr><ltbullet>removes a report required to be submitted by the Department of Corrections to the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee regarding data of sexual assaults in correctional facilities and requires the report to be submitted to the commission to be included in the public safety portal;<hr><ltbullet>requires institutions of higher education to provide data of crime in student housing to the commission to be included in the public safety portal;<hr><ltbullet> requires the multi-agency strike force to combat violent and other major felony crimes to submit the strike force's annual report to the commission to be included in the public safety portal;<hr><ltbullet>requires the commission to include a report from the Board of Pardons and Parole regarding metrics of offenders in the public safety portal;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Prosecutor Conduct Commission to provide the Prosecutor Conduct Commission's annual report on prosecutorial complaints to the commission to be included in the public safety portal;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Public Safety and the Bureau of Forensic Services to provide an annual report on sexual assault kits to the commission to be included in the public safety portal;<hr><ltbullet>adds requirements for the commission regarding the public safety portal;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the commission is not required to provide records in response to a record request under the Government Records Access and Management Act for records received by the commission for the public safety portal; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical can conforming changes.

title: Coercion Amendments
description: This bill addresses criminal offenses related to coercive conduct.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates the criminal offense of aiding or encouraging suicide that:<hr><ltbullet1>contains current language regarding aiding suicide moved from the criminal offense of manslaughter; and<hr><ltbullet1>adds new elements of encouraging suicide in certain circumstances that can be charged criminally;<hr><ltbullet>separates the criminal offenses of sexual extortion and aggravated sexual extortion into two separate offenses;<hr><ltbullet>adds additional elements to the criminal offense of sexual extortion;<hr><ltbullet>adds the criminal offenses of sexual extortion and aggravated sexual extortion to the list of offenses that are eligible to be considered a domestic violence offense;<hr><ltbullet>requires a mandatory fine for certain convictions of:<hr><ltbullet1>aiding or encouraging suicide;<hr><ltbullet1>sexual extortion; and <hr><ltbullet1>aggravated sexual extortion; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Electronic Signature Collection Amendments
description: This bill amends the electronic signature gathering process.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines a term;<hr><ltbullet>requires the device used to electronically gather signatures for an initiative petition, a referendum petition, or a candidate nomination petition (collectively, "petition") to be capable of scanning and extracting certain data from a driver license, state identification card, or another form of valid voter identification;<hr><ltbullet>beginning on January 1, 2028, requires the device described above to be capable of operating in an offline environment;<hr><ltbullet>beginning on January 1, 2028, requires at least 10% of the signatures certified for a petition to be gathered using the electronic signature gathering process;<hr><ltbullet>beginning on January 1, 2030, requires at least 50% of the signatures certified for a petition to be gathered using the electronic signature gathering process;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the lieutenant governor to suspend the 10% electronic signature requirement if the electronic signature gathering system is not functioning in a manner that reasonably permits compliance; <hr><ltbullet>beginning on January 1, 2032:<hr><ltbullet1>requires the sponsors of an initiative or referendum petition, or an individual who circulates a candidate nomination petition, to gather signatures using the electronic signature gathering process; and<hr><ltbullet1>prohibits a person described above from gathering signatures manually;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies electronic signature-gathering security requirements by distinguishing between baseline device security configuration standards and ongoing cyber-security procedures governing system operation, monitoring, and maintenance, as established by the lieutenant governor;<hr><ltbullet>requires the lieutenant governor to submit an annual report to the Government Operations Interim Committee, beginning no later than October 1, 2026, and continuing no later than October 1 of each year through 2031;<hr><ltbullet>adds a January 1, 2032 repeal date for sections related to manual signature gathering;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to standardize a defined term in this bill with the same term in H.B. 32, Signature Gathering and Verification Amendments; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill modifies provisions related to energy balancing account cost recovery for electrical corporations.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes an energy cost baseline to be set by the Public Service Commission in general rate cases;<hr><ltbullet>creates a symmetrical sharing band requiring electrical corporations to share with customers 80% of variances between actual costs and the energy cost baseline for costs incurred on or after January 1, 2026; and<hr><ltbullet>maintains 100% cost recovery for energy balancing account costs incurred before January 1, 2026.

title: Offender Amendments
description: This bill concerns provisions relating to offenders.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires a county jail to assist certain county jail inmates in obtaining a current driver license or state-issued identification;<hr><ltbullet>requires a substance abuse treatment program to share the results of a participant's drug test with the participant's supervising probation or parole officer and other specified individuals under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Driver License Division to coordinate with a county jail in providing a county inmate with a driver license certificate or a temporary regular identification card;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Corrections (department) to:<hr><ltbullet1>identify and provide information and resources regarding post-incarceration housing; <hr><ltbullet1>within 12 months after the day on which the department implements a digital communications program for inmates, provide a secure digital portal that will facilitate attorney-client communications and document exchanges between inmates and attorneys; and<hr><ltbullet1>provide annual data to the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice concerning the types of, and usage of, various incentives offered to inmates;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Adult Probation and Parole to track and annually report information concerning the housing of offenders currently on parole; <hr><ltbullet>amends health information disclosure provisions for individuals who are on probation or parole; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Truth in Taxation Amendments
description: This bill addresses property tax increases through truth in taxation.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires fiscal year taxing entities proposing a property tax rate increase to make a preliminary statement in a public meeting regarding the taxing entity's consideration of a tax rate increase;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies notice and publication requirements for towns proposing a tax rate increase that do not have public websites;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the State Tax Commission's authority to deny a taxing entity's proposed tax rate increase for failing to meet truth in taxation requirements;<hr><ltbullet>provides for a one-year period in which the State Tax Commission is not required to deny a fiscal year taxing entity's proposed tax rate increase for failure to comply with certain truth in taxation requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires fiscal year taxing entities proposing a property tax increase to:<hr><ltbullet1>prepare and adopt an interim budget that includes a property tax impact schedule; and<hr><ltbullet1>reserve a certain amount of the taxing entity's general fund revenue in a restricted budget account for a limited period of time;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to incorporate changes made to Section 59-2-919 in S.B. 238, Property Tax Adjustments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill enacts provisions establishing requirements for Public Service Commission participation in regional transmission organizations and independent system operators.

description: This bill establishes the Commission on Unincorporated Areas of a County of the First Class.

title: Carbon Dioxide System Amendments
description: This bill concerns carbon dioxide systems.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Utah Fire Prevention Board (board) to establish a licensing and certification program for certain carbon dioxide systems;<hr><ltbullet>requires a person engaging in the business of servicing carbon dioxide systems to have a license from the state fire marshal;<hr><ltbullet>requires, with exceptions, an individual who services a carbon dioxide system to have a certification from the state fire marshal;<hr><ltbullet>requires the board to establish rules, application forms, and fees for carbon dioxide system licensing and certification; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Charter School Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to charter schools, including property disposition, governance requirements, and the Charter School Revolving Fund.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>gives charter schools parity with eligible entities to purchase decommissioned school property;<hr><ltbullet>establishes restrictions on charter school resale of acquired property;<hr><ltbullet>requires charter school governing board members to take an oath of office;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that charter schools are public schools;<hr><ltbullet>replaces the Charter School Revolving Account with the Charter School Revolving Fund; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Initiative and Referendum Signature Gathering and Removal Amendments
description: This bill addresses petition signature gathering and removal.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires an individual who gathers a statement requesting removal of a petition signer's signature to be at least 18 years old;<hr><ltbullet>beginning on May 6, 2026, requires a paid signature removal statement gatherer to: <hr><ltbullet1>display a badge disclosing certain information while gathering the statement; and<hr><ltbullet1>verify, on the statement, certain information about the individual who signs the statement;<hr><ltbullet>beginning on May 6, 2026, requires a signature removal statement, if collected by a paid gatherer, to include a notice that removing the signer's signature may prevent the initiative or referendum from appearing on the ballot;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a person from paying a person to gather a signature removal statement unless the payment is based on an hourly rate; <hr><ltbullet>prohibits a person from using an initiative or referendum petition signer's email address for any non-petition related purpose;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a voter from submitting a signature removal statement by mail using prepaid postage;<hr><ltbullet>creates an exception to the prohibition described above if a signature removal statement submitted by mail using prepaid postage is postmarked on or before the effective date of this bill;<hr><ltbullet>provides that, in certain circumstances, a county clerk may not refuse to certify an initiative or referendum petition signature solely because the date written next to the signature contains a one-calendar-year error;<hr><ltbullet>expands existing criminal penalties in relation to the initiative and referendum process by prohibiting an individual from:<hr><ltbullet1>making certain misrepresentations while the individual gathers petition signatures or signature removal statements; or<hr><ltbullet1>providing or offering to provide money, prepaid postage, or any direct financial benefit to an individual to remove the individual's signature from a petition;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause creating an exception to the prohibition in H.B. 32, Signature Gathering and Verification Amendments, on certifying a petition signature dated after the submission deadline when the date qualifies for the one-calendar-year error provision created by this bill; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill amends government entity drug testing provisions.

title: Great Salt Lake Related Amendments
description: This bill addresses activities that are related to the Great Salt Lake.

title: Family Law Modifications
description: This bill addresses family law issues related to spousal support, child support, custody, and parent-time.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the duties of the Office of Recovery Services with regard to spousal support;<hr><ltbullet>requires the director of the Office of Recovery Services to hold certain meetings for obligees and obligors and places a sunset date on the requirement;<hr><ltbullet>creates a reporting requirement for the director of the Office of Recovery Services and places a sunset date on the reporting requirement;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the collection of spousal support by the Office of Recovery Services after a child support obligation ends;<hr><ltbullet>allows a certain amount of money from a monthly child support payment to pass through to a family who is receiving public assistance on and after July 1, 2028;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the suspension of a driver license by the Office of Recovery Services, including the suspension of an individual's driver license when the individual is in arrears of at least $35,000;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the information provided by the Online Court Assistance Program;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a delinquent payment for child support accrues interest on and after July 1, 2027; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Federal Funds Modifications
description: This bill modifies provisions related to federal funds.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>directs the legislative fiscal analyst to submit to the Federalism Commission (commission) the portions of each budget stress test that relate to federal funds;<hr><ltbullet>requires the commission to review and, in the commission's discretion, make legislative recommendations regarding the federal funds portions of each budget stress test;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Utah State University Jon M. Huntsman School of Business to:<hr><ltbullet1>create and maintain a publicly available dashboard that visualizes state dependency on federal funds; and<hr><ltbullet1>model economic scenarios to inform federal funds contingency planning; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Utah Retirement Plan Exchange
description: This bill establishes a retirement plan exchange for private employers.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>directs the state treasurer's office (office) to establish and maintain a publicly accessible online exchange through which an eligible private employer may review, compare, and select one or more retirement plans for the benefit of the employer's employees;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for the exchange, including the types of available retirement plans, the manner in which the exchange presents the retirement plan options, and the information available for each retirement plan;<hr><ltbullet>provides a process by which a retirement plan provider can list a qualified retirement plan on the exchange;<hr><ltbullet>requires each retirement plan provider with a listing on the exchange to annually report to the office;<hr><ltbullet>allows the office to remove or suspend a listing under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>gives the office rulemaking authority related to the office's duties; and<hr><ltbullet>allows the office to contract with a third party to fulfill the office's duties related to the exchange.

title: Tariff Payment Tax Credit
description: This bill enacts an individual income tax credit for certain tariff payments.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>enacts a nonrefundable individual income tax credit for a business entity's payment of tariffs, the costs of which have not been passed to customers, in an amount that corresponds to the total amount of qualifying tariff payments made by the business entity during the taxable year;<hr><ltbullet>requires a qualifying claimant, before claiming a tax credit, to apply for and receive a written certification from the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity (office) certifying the qualifying claimant's eligibility for the tax credit and the tax credit amount;<hr><ltbullet>requires the office to annually report to the State Tax Commission on recipients of a written certification for the tax credit;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the office to make rules for administering the certification requirements for the tax credit; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: School District Elections Amendments
description: This bill makes the office of local school board member an office that is elected via a partisan election.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>makes the office of local school board member an office that is elected via a partisan election;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions relating to filling a midterm vacancy for the office of local school board member;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the election of a local school board member using the partisan primary election nomination process; <hr><ltbullet>modifies campaign reporting requirements and conflict of interest reporting requirements for a local school board office candidate or local school board officeholder;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the transition from a nonpartisan local board of education to a partisan local board of education; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Parental Access to Children's Medical Records Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to parent access to a minor's medical record.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>specifies that a parent has the right to access their child's medical record;<hr><ltbullet>requires a health care facility to ensure that a child's parent has access to the child's electronic health record unless certain circumstances are met;<hr><ltbullet>requires an electronic medical record system vendor to ensure a health care facility can provide access to parents;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the attorney general's office to bring enforcement actions; and<hr><ltbullet>requires a health care facility to provide medical records free of charge under certain circumstances.

title: Unauthorized Practice of Law Amendments
description: This bill addresses the unauthorized practice of law.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms related to the unauthorized practice of law;<hr><ltbullet>allows the court to take certain actions when a person is engaging in the unauthorized practice of law before the court;<hr><ltbullet>allows a civil action to be brought for the unauthorized practice law; <hr><ltbullet>establishes a criminal penalty for the unauthorized practice of law; <hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the statutory provisions regarding the unauthorized practice of law do not limit the Supreme Court's authority to regulate the practice of law;<hr><ltbullet>provides a three-year statute of limitations for a civil action for the unauthorized practice of law and the exceptions to the statute of limitations;<hr><ltbullet>reorganizes the three-year statute of limitations for certain actions; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Electronic Information Privacy Act Amendments
description: This bill amends the Electronic Information Privacy Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends and clarifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies and amends procedures and requirements for a law enforcement agency that seeks to obtain, use, copy, or disclose certain electronic information or records;<hr><ltbullet>revises liability provisions for a provider of an electronic communication service or a remote computing service;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the procedures and requirements described in the Electronic Information Privacy Act (act) are the only permissible methods for a law enforcement agency to obtain, use, copy, disclose, or otherwise access certain electronic information or records, with certain exceptions;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a law enforcement agency from contracting with or otherwise using a third party to obtain, use, copy, disclose, or otherwise access certain electronic information or records in a manner that the law enforcement agency would be prohibited from doing directly, with certain exceptions;<hr><ltbullet>provides that electronic information or records obtained in violation of the act, as well as any evidence derived from the electronic information or records, are subject to the same rules governing exclusion of evidence obtained in violation of constitutional requirements; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Non-nicotine Inhalation Product Amendments
description: This bill addresses non-nicotine inhalation products.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires a non-nicotine inhalation product and a non-nicotine inhalation substance to be registered;<hr><ltbullet>establishes civil penalties for selling an unregistered non-nicotine inhalation product or non-nicotine inhalation substance;<hr><ltbullet>creates the criminal offense of illegal distribution of a cannabinoid inhalation product or a cannabinoid inhalation substance;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that a cannabinoid product does not include an electronic cigarette;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>includes a clause coordinating this bill and H.B. 385, Specialized Product Sales Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Public Employee Compensation Amendments
description: This bill establishes limitations on school district administrator compensation.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet> defines terms related to district administrator compensation;<hr><ltbullet>caps annual salary increases for certain district administrators at the weighted pupil unit inflationary factor;<hr><ltbullet>requires a public hearing before a local school board may approve salary increases that exceed the weighted pupil unit inflationary factor;<hr><ltbullet>requires performance metric outcomes for salary increases that exceed the weighted pupil unit inflationary factor;<hr><ltbullet>limits certain administrator benefits;<hr><ltbullet>establishes compensation scale requirements for deputy administrators;<hr><ltbullet>establishes initial compensation requirements for new superintendents; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Towing Notice and Ownership Rights Modifications
description: This bill provides certain protections for an owner or lien holder of a towed vehicle if proper notice has not been provided to the owner or lien holder.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that, for a private-property tow, a possessory lien related to a vehicle that has been towed is not enforceable if required notice was not properly provided to the owner or lien holder;<hr><ltbullet>allows an owner or a lien holder to take possession of a vehicle without paying towing or storage fees if notice was not properly given;<hr><ltbullet>if an owner claims notice was not properly provided, creates a presumption of improper notice that may be rebutted by presenting, as applicable:<hr><ltbullet1>time-stamped evidence that notice was properly provided to the Motor Vehicle Division; or <hr><ltbullet1>evidence that notice was sent via certified mail;<hr><ltbullet>allows a party prevailing in an action related to lack of notice to be awarded attorney fees;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Department of Transportation to make rules to establish the process for an owner or a lien holder to make a claim for release of a vehicle; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Tourism Taxes Amendments
description: This bill addresses reporting requirements for tourism-related taxes.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>includes the the state auditor in the analysis conducted by the Office of the Legislative Fiscal Analyst to determine by consensus whether county expenditure reports sufficiently demonstrate compliance with the expenditure requirements for revenue generated by a transient room tax (TRT) or a tourism, recreation, cultural, convention, and airport facilities tax (TRCC);<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the state auditor to audit expenditures reported by counties as part of the analysis for county expenditure reports;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the state auditor's authority to prohibit counties from accessing revenue generated by a TRT or TRCC if the state auditor and the Office of the Legislative Fiscal Analyst determine a county's expenditure report does not sufficiently demonstrate compliance with the expenditure requirements; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Classroom Technology Amendments
description: This bill requires the State Board of Education to create model policies on the use of technology and artificial intelligence in a public school classroom.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Board of Education (state board) to include certain technology standards in core education standards;<hr><ltbullet>creates certain requirements for a local education agency (LEA) related to the use of technology in the classroom;<hr><ltbullet>requires the state board to create a model policy on:<hr><ltbullet1>the balanced use of technology in the classroom; and<hr><ltbullet1>the use of artificial intelligence in the classroom;<hr><ltbullet>creates certain requirements for specific grade levels when using technology in the classroom;<hr><ltbullet>exempts certain groups from the grade level requirements when using technology in the classroom;<hr><ltbullet>creates a reporting requirement;<hr><ltbullet>gives authority to the state board to create rules;<hr><ltbullet>requires LEAs to provide additional resources to certain students; and<hr><ltbullet>allows public high schools to create and offer a sandbox artificial intelligence course.

title: Sentencing Amendments
description: This bill amends statutory provisions related to sentencing.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies the membership of the Sentencing Commission;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Sentencing Commission to give consideration to certain objectives when determining a recommended sentence or supervision length for the adult sentencing and supervision length guidelines;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Sentencing Commission, before November 1, 2026, to revise and review the adult sentencing and supervision length guidelines for certain offenses;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the authorization process for the adult sentencing and supervision length guidelines and juvenile disposition guidelines;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the factors and information that a sentencing court is required to consider when sentencing an individual; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Artificial Intelligence Modifications
description: This bill enacts provisions related to counterfeit intimate images and digital content provenance standards.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Digital Voyeurism Prevention Act to address non-consensual generation and distribution of counterfeit intimate images;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits generation services and platforms from distributing counterfeit intimate images without obtaining and verifying consent from the depicted individual;<hr><ltbullet>establishes civil liability for violations of the act, with actual damages, punitive damages, attorney fees, and injunctive relief;<hr><ltbullet>establishes safe harbor protections for generation services and covered platforms that implement reasonable safeguards and respond appropriately to notices; <hr><ltbullet>establishes heightened pleading standards requiring plaintiffs to plead specific facts;<hr><ltbullet>requires platforms to implement notice and takedown procedures and disclosure requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires large online platforms to detect, disclose, and preserve provenance data in distributed content;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for capture device manufacturers regarding latent disclosures in captured content; <hr><ltbullet>requires covered providers to include disclosures in AI-generated content;<hr><ltbullet>provides exemptions for certain products and services;<hr><ltbullet>provides for enforcement by the Division of Consumer Protection; and<hr><ltbullet>provides a severability clause.

title: School Board Election Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to the State Board of Education.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>makes the office of State Board of Education member a nonpartisan office;<hr><ltbullet>repeals provisions making the office of State Board of Education member a partisan office;  <hr><ltbullet>requires the governor to fill a vacancy in the office of State Board of Education member by appointing, with the advice and consent of the Senate, an individual who meets the office's eligibility and residency requirements; <hr><ltbullet>beginning with the 2028 election cycle, requires a candidate for an office on the State Board of Education to participate in a nonpartisan primary election to narrow the number of candidates who participate in a nonpartisan general election; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Third Party Litigation Funding Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to maintenance funding agreements.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; <hr><ltbullet>distinguishes between consumer maintenance funding agreements and commercial maintenance funding agreements; <hr><ltbullet>requires maintenance funding providers to register with the Division of Consumer Protection; <hr><ltbullet>extends the right of rescission for a consumer maintenance funding agreement; <hr><ltbullet>imposes disclosure requirements in connection with consumer and commercial maintenance funding agreements; <hr><ltbullet>restricts certain relationships between attorneys and maintenance funding providers; <hr><ltbullet>prohibits maintenance funding arrangements involving foreign entities or persons of concern; <hr><ltbullet>establishes priority and assignability provisions relating to maintenance funding interests; <hr><ltbullet>restricts a commercial maintenance funding provider from directing or controlling litigation decisions; <hr><ltbullet>provides for enforcement, penalties, and rulemaking;<hr><ltbullet>provides a coordination clause to substantively and technically coordinate changes between this bill and S.B. 38, Consumer Protection Modifications, and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Artificial Intelligence Transparency Amendments
description: This bill enacts the AI Transparency Act relating to transparency and whistleblower protections for frontier artificial intelligence models.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires developers of certain artificial intelligence models to create, implement, and publish public safety and child protection plans;<hr><ltbullet>requires developers to publish summaries of risk assessments for certain artificial intelligence models;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits developers from making materially false or misleading statements about covered risks;<hr><ltbullet>requires developers to report certain safety incidents to the Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy (office);<hr><ltbullet>requires the office to provide annual assessments and legislative recommendations regarding regulation of certain artificial intelligence models;<hr><ltbullet>establishes civil penalties for violations;<hr><ltbullet>provides whistleblower protections for employees who report safety concerns of certain artificial intelligence models; <hr><ltbullet>establishes remedies for employees who suffer adverse action for whistleblower activities; <hr><ltbullet>creates the AI Transparency Enforcement Restricted Account to fund enforcement activities; and<hr><ltbullet>provides a severability clause.

title: Immigrant Driving Amendments
description: This bill repeals the driving privilege card program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>repeals the driving privilege card program;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the Driver License Division from issuing a driving privilege card on or after May 6, 2026;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes throughout the Utah Code related to the repeal of the driving privilege card program;<hr><ltbullet>requires law enforcement to report to the Immigration and Customs Enforcement Agency of the United States Department of Homeland Security if an individual who is unlawfully present in the United states is involved in a motor vehicle accident; and<hr><ltbullet>makes other technical changes.

title: Voting Registration Amendments
description: This bill addresses provisions related to voter registration.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates a process for an individual to receive a voter registration form and voter registration information when purchasing a hunting or fishing license; and<hr><ltbullet>permits the lieutenant governor or the legislative auditor general to contract with a third-party to assist in the review and identification of inaccuracies in the voter registration database.

title: Security and Land Restriction Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions dealing with the sale of land to restricted foreign entities.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>lowers the percentage of ownership a restricted foreign entity may maintain in a separate entity before the separate entity is considered a restricted foreign entity;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Department of Public Safety (department) shall send a letter to an entity the department suspects of being a restricted foreign entity;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an entity to which the department sends a letter shall provide evidence that demonstrates the entity is not a restricted foreign entity within 30 days after the day on which the entity receives the letter;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the attorney general shall coordinate with the Division of Facilities and Construction Management when conducting a sale of a restricted foreign entity's interest in land;<hr><ltbullet>provides that if an entity does not respond to a letter from the department, the department may impose a fine for each day the entity does not respond; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.
