title: Public Education Student Athlete Protections
description: This bill prohibits a public school from participating in an association that governs athletic interscholastic activities in certain circumstances.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a public school from participating in an association that governs athletic interscholastic activities (association) if the association does not:<hr><ltbullet1>include certain policies in the association's policies; or<hr><ltbullet1>sufficiently enforce the association's rules and policies;<hr><ltbullet>requires an association to report to the Rules Review and General Oversight Committee; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Overdose Amendments
description: This bill concerns criminal provisions relating to an overdose.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends the affirmative defense based on reporting an overdose event, including to clarify that the affirmative defense may apply to:<hr><ltbullet1>an individual who remains with the individual experiencing the overdose event; and<hr><ltbullet1>the individual experiencing the overdose event; <hr><ltbullet>creates an option for a dismissal of certain first-time drug offenses under circumstances applicable to the overdose affirmative defense;<hr><ltbullet>amends the sentencing mitigating factor based on reporting an overdose event, including to clarify that the mitigating factor may apply to:<hr><ltbullet1>an individual who remains with the individual experiencing the overdose event; and<hr><ltbullet1>the individual experiencing the overdose event; <hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to coordinate changes between this bill and H.B. 301, Drug Recodification, if both bills pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: School Design Amendments
description: This bill requires the State Board of Education (state board) to establish a library of school building designs.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes a school building design library maintained by the state board;<hr><ltbullet>requires the state board to develop standard designs for elementary, middle, high, and multi-level schools;<hr><ltbullet>requires school districts to own and submit building designs developed using public funds;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes school districts and charter schools to select designs from the library;<hr><ltbullet>establishes periodic review and update requirements for the design library;<hr><ltbullet>requires competitive bidding for architectural and engineering design fees;<hr><ltbullet>mandates life-cycle cost analysis in building designs;<hr><ltbullet>establishes public cost reporting and transparency requirements for school construction projects;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes design-build as an alternative project delivery method; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Drug Recodification
description: This bill technically reorganizes, revises, and clarifies provisions relating to drugs.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>technically reorganizes, revises, and clarifies provisions concerning drugs, including moving certain criminal offenses concerning drugs from Title 58, Occupations and Professions, into Title 76, Utah Criminal Code, and reorganizing remaining sections into organized structures; <hr><ltbullet>updates cross references; <hr><ltbullet>adds coordination clauses to:<hr><ltbullet1>coordinate changes between this bill and S.B. 117, Occupational and Professional Licensing Amendments, if both bills pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet1>ensure the statutory numbering and renumbering made in this bill will be reflected in any new language added to the Utah Code by legislation that passes in the 2026 General Session and becomes law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill addresses family law proceedings.

title: Homeless Services Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to homeless services.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines and amends terms;<hr><ltbullet>repeals certain obsolete sections of code;<hr><ltbullet>amends the duties of the Office of Homeless Services (office) and duties of the homeless services coordinator (coordinator);<hr><ltbullet>amends certain staffing requirements for certain boards or committees;<hr><ltbullet>amends certain reporting requirements; <hr><ltbullet>permits a service provider to temporarily expand a congregate shelter's bed capacity limit under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>changes provisions related to a participating local government's tax revenue distributions for homeless shelters; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Elections Study
description: This bill directs the Gary R. Herbert Institute for Public Policy at Utah Valley University and the Center for Constitutional Studies at Utah Valley University to conduct an elections study.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet> directs the Gary R. Herbert Institute for Public Policy at Utah Valley University  (the institute) and the Center for Constitutional Studies at Utah Valley University (the center) to conduct an elections study regarding:<hr><ltbullet1>the security of in-person voting versus voting by mail; and<hr><ltbullet1>best practices for conducting and implementing a process where identification must be presented before depositing a ballot in a ballot drop box; and<hr><ltbullet>directs the institute and the center to present the study to the Government Operations Interim Committee.

title: School Curriculum and Standards Modifications
description: This bill modifies requirements for social studies education and establishes open education resources.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the state superintendent to identify and develop high-quality open educational resource instructional materials;<hr><ltbullet>requires social studies instruction on American self-governance and comparative government systems;<hr><ltbullet>requires instruction from documents influencing America's founding and literary thought;<hr><ltbullet>requires sourcing of English language arts assessment passages from primary source documents where appropriate;<hr><ltbullet>requires instruction on the roles and responsibilities of government officials;<hr><ltbullet>allows local education agencies to determine whether applied crafts and technical arts courses meet fine arts credit requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires American constitutional government and citizenship to be taught as two distinct semester courses; <hr><ltbullet>requires United States history to be taught as two distinct semester courses; <hr><ltbullet>prohibits students from taking the same semester course twice to meet graduation requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires literacy coaches to support the integration of social studies content into literacy instruction;<hr><ltbullet>requires regular social studies instruction for elementary grades;<hr><ltbullet>allows social studies instruction to be delivered through integrated instruction with English language arts and mathematics;<hr><ltbullet>requires implementation of elementary social studies requirements by July 1, 2031;<hr><ltbullet>repeals an adult education citizenship test and certain required plans;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Human Development Instruction

title: Patient Nondisclosure Clauses
description: This bill addresses certain nondisclosure clauses.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>makes the validity of a nondisclosure clause precluding a patient from reporting the conduct of the patient's health care provider to the Division of Professional Licensing contingent on the provider having provided the division's model notice to the patient before the execution of the nondisclosure clause; and<hr><ltbullet>requires the division to make a model notice and publish the notice online for download.

title: Agency Fee Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to budgetary procedures.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires that, before billing another state agency for a good or service, an internal service fund agency provide specified rate data to the Governor's Office of Planning and Budget and to the Office of the Legislative Fiscal Analyst;<hr><ltbullet>requires an internal service fund agency to annually report the actual costs and revenue for each rate, fee, or other amount charged during the preceding fiscal year;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a fee agency from charging a fee unless the fee agency provides specified fee data to the Governor's Office of Planning and Budget and to the Office of the Legislative Fiscal Analyst;<hr><ltbullet>requires a fee agency to annually report the actual costs and revenue for each fee charged during the preceding fiscal year; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Solar Panel Disposal Amendments
description: This bill creates a study and a program for the testing and disposal of solar panel waste.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>mandates disclosure language by a solar retailer regarding state requirements for the testing and disposal of a solar panel;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Waste Management and Radiation Control Board to make rules, beginning on July 1, 2028, for the testing and disposal of solar panel waste;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Solar Panel Waste Restricted Account;<hr><ltbullet>imposes an assessment on renewable energy parent entities to be deposited into the Solar Panel Waste Restricted Account;<hr><ltbullet>imposes a distributed generation fee on small-scale solar entities;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the Division of Waste Management and Radiation Control (division) to require an owner or operator of a solar panel, beginning on July 1, 2028, to:<hr><ltbullet1>complete a hazardous waste analysis on the solar panel before disposal; and<hr><ltbullet1>dispose of hazardous solar panel waste at a solar panel waste disposal site or solar panel waste recycling facility;<hr><ltbullet>allows an operator of a landfill to submit an application to register with the division as a solar panel waste disposal site;<hr><ltbullet>establishes that the director of the division may enforce the solar panel waste requirements by bringing a civil action in a court;<hr><ltbullet>requires the division to report annually to two legislative committees;<hr><ltbullet>requires the division to complete a study on solar panel recycling in the state and report the findings and recommendations to two legislative committees;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the energy project assessment ends on December 31, 2027; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Government Records Classification Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to the classification of certain government records.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends the definition of "initial contact report" for purposes of the Government Records Access and Management Act;<hr><ltbullet>classifies as public any record that documents a governmental entity's receipt or expenditure of funds, including:<hr><ltbullet1>a record related to a financial account, budget, voucher, or grant;<hr><ltbullet1>a financial report or general ledger; and<hr><ltbullet1>a record documenting compensation a governmental entity pays to a vendor;<hr><ltbullet>if properly classified by the governmental entity, makes private any portion of a record that reveals whether a taxpayer receives a specified property tax exemption, deferral, abatement, or other relief; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Animal Depredation Amendments
description: This bill addresses provisions related to agricultural and wildlife damage from animal depredation.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines and modifies terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Department of Agriculture and Food (department) may issue an aerial hunting permit and aerial hunting license for the taking of a coyote from an aircraft;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Agricultural and Wildlife Damage Prevention Board (board) to make rules related to an aerial hunting permit and aerial hunting license;<hr><ltbullet>establishes that an aerial hunting permittee or licensee assumes all liability for an accident, injury, or damage arising from the aerial hunting activity;<hr><ltbullet>modifies how the department reviews the accounts of an organization that receives funds from the Agricultural and Wildlife Damage Prevention Account;<hr><ltbullet>grants authority to the board to set an annual predator control fee on certain sheep, goats, cattle, and turkey;<hr><ltbullet>modifies criminal penalties related to feral swine;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the seizure and forfeiture of a vehicle used in the commission of a crime related to feral swine; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: License Plate Reader Amendments
description: This bill amends requirements for the use of automatic license plate readers and processing of license plate data.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>repeals sections related to license plate readers, relocates provisions related to license plate readers in the Utah Code;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides authorized uses and purposes for license plate readers and license plate data by governmental entities and law enforcement;<hr><ltbullet>establishes reporting requirements regarding the use of license plate readers and processing of license plate data; <hr><ltbullet>creates standards for processing license plate data obtained from a license plate reader including:<hr><ltbullet1>data security; <hr><ltbullet1>data retention; and<hr><ltbullet1>data sharing; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: State Employee Maternity and Leave Amendments
description: This bill modifies policies related to paid leave and maternity.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>increases the amount of postpartum recovery leave that a state employer must provide a state employee from three to six weeks;<hr><ltbullet>requires certain state employers to provide six weeks of paid leave to a state employee who adopts a child under six years old;<hr><ltbullet>provides that paid leave for an adoption described above runs consecutive to the three weeks of paid leave that is currently available to a state employee who adopts a child under 18 years old;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that adoption leave may be used at any point during the adoption process and is not limited to the finalization of an adoption;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that a state employee's appointment as legal guardian of a child qualifies the state employee for parental leave;<hr><ltbullet>removes foster placement as an event making a state employee eligible for paid parental leave and creates a separate foster leave category with a four-week paid-leave duration;<hr><ltbullet>allows two state employees who jointly adopt or foster a child to share a single paid leave period rather than each receiving a separate leave entitlement;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that a state employee may not use foster leave after a child is no longer in foster care with the state employee;<hr><ltbullet>allows a state employee to use foster leave on an intermittent basis;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the combined use of parental leave, foster leave, and adoption leave for the same child; <hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Human Resource Management to make rules to administer the paid leave types described above; <hr><ltbullet>increases the amount of foster leave that an LEA must provide an LEA employee from three to four weeks;<hr><ltbullet>requires an LEA to provide three weeks of paid leave to an LEA employee who adopts a child under six years old;<hr><ltbullet>provides that paid leave for an adoption described above runs consecutive to the three weeks of paid leave that is currently available to an LEA employee who adopts a child under 18 years old;  <hr><ltbullet>amends the Breastfeeding Protection Act to include a woman's use of a breast pump; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Liability Limitations Amendments
description: This bill creates an affirmative defense.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates an affirmative defense in a civil action for conduct, an omission, or a condition authorized or required by a governmental entity;<hr><ltbullet>specifies the circumstances in which the affirmative defense described above does not apply, including in an action for products liability;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies when conduct, an omission, or a condition is considered to have occurred for purposes of the affirmative defense;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that lawful authorization to engage in an activity does not eliminate a duty to exercise reasonable care; <hr><ltbullet>specifies that the affirmative defense applies regardless of the theory of liability; and<hr><ltbullet>abrogates the common law to the extent the common law is inconsistent with the affirmative defense.

title: Criminal Offenses Modifications
description: This bill addresses criminal offenses.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends the offense of threat of terrorism by:<hr><ltbullet1>renaming the offense to terrorism; and<hr><ltbullet1>clarifying that the offense applies to certain completed acts in addition to threatened acts;<hr><ltbullet>creates the offense of unlawfully advancing foreign organizations and governments;<hr><ltbullet>creates the offense of intentional concealment of identity while committing an offense in public;<hr><ltbullet>creates the offense of unlawful deprivation of religious rights with a corresponding civil right of action by a victim that may be brought against the actor;<hr><ltbullet>amends the definition of unlawful activity applicable to the offense of prohibited conduct concerning a pattern of unlawful activity to include the offenses of aggravated disorderly conduct on a street or highway and unlawfully advancing foreign organizations and governments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Recovery Operations Amendments
description: This bill distinguishes recovery operations from normal towing operations and creates requirements for the operation and payment of recovery operators.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that an insurer who covers a vehicle that is recovered as part of a recovery operation is the insurer who pays the recovery operator;<hr><ltbullet>creates a process for an insurer and a recovery operator to dispute an amount due for a recovery operation;<hr><ltbullet>requires motor vehicle liability policies for commercial vehicles to include coverage for recovery operations;<hr><ltbullet>requires tow truck motor carrier rotations to identify tow truck motor carriers that are qualified to perform recovery operations; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Nicotine Product Tax Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to nicotine product taxes.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>increases the rates of the taxes levied on cigarettes, electronic cigarettes, and nontherapeutic nicotine devices;<hr><ltbullet>replaces the weight-based tax rate for alternative nicotine products with:<hr><ltbullet1>a per product tax rate, for alternative nicotine products that contain pouches; or<hr><ltbullet1>a tax rate based on a percentage of the manufacturer's sales price, for alternative nicotine products that do not contain pouches;<hr><ltbullet>imposes a transitional inventory tax on cigarettes subject to the tax increase described in this bill;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Finance to transfer the additional revenue generated by the tax increases described in this bill for electronic cigarettes, nontherapeutic nicotine devices, and alternative nicotine products to the General Fund; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: First Responder Health Amendments
description: This bill amends requirements for providing health coverage and resources to first responders.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends eligibility requirements for the Volunteer Emergency Medical Service Personnel Insurance Program;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Public Safety (department) to annually submit a report on first responder agencies' compliance with requirements to provide mental health resources to first responders and first responders' spouses to the:<hr><ltbullet1>Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee; and<hr><ltbullet1>State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice's public safety portal; <hr><ltbullet>amends eligibility for receiving mental health resources for separated first responders and separated first responders' spouses;                <hr><ltbullet>creates the Mental Health Resources for First Responders Restricted Account (account) to provide funding for the department to provide certain mental health resources to eligible small first responder agencies;<hr><ltbullet>provides a sunset date for grants to first responder agencies;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Statewide Water Storage
description: This bill addresses water storage within the state.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides a process for applying to the Board of Water Resources (board) to be considered for state funding for the construction of or increase in the capacity of water storage in the state;<hr><ltbullet>creates criteria for considering state funding for construction of water storage in the state;<hr><ltbullet>requires the board to annually review eligibility for consideration of state funding for construction of water storage in the state;<hr><ltbullet>requires the board to report recommendations related to state funding for construction of or increase in the capacity of water storage in the state; <hr><ltbullet>addresses rulemaking related to the processes implemented and the recommendations issued by the board; and<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that recommendations are nonbinding.

title: Elections Provisions Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to elections.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the conditions and requirements for a ballot to list a candidate using a variation of the candidate's name or a nickname;<hr><ltbullet>modifies, consolidates, recodifies, and adds provisions relating to:<hr><ltbullet1>notices of offices to be filled at upcoming elections;<hr><ltbullet1>notices of candidate filing periods;<hr><ltbullet1>notices of candidates to be included on a ballot and other instructions relating to a ballot;<hr><ltbullet1>notices of election; and<hr><ltbullet1>other notices relating to elections;<hr><ltbullet>modifies certain declaration of candidacy periods:<hr><ltbullet1>to coincide with the declaration of candidacy periods for municipal primary elections and municipal general elections; and<hr><ltbullet1>to make declaration of candidacy periods for all registered political parties the same, regardless of whether the registered political party is a qualified political party;<hr><ltbullet>beginning on January 1, 2027, prohibits a county clerk's or election officer's name from:<hr><ltbullet1>inclusion in the official endorsement for a ballot;<hr><ltbullet1>inclusion on a return envelope for a ballot; or<hr><ltbullet1>inclusion on a ballot, except to the extent that the county clerk or election officer is listed as a candidate on the ballot;<hr><ltbullet>modifies certain deadlines set at a specific date to instead occur on a business day;<hr><ltbullet>modifies and consolidates provisions relating to removing the names of deceased individuals from the list of registered voters;<hr><ltbullet>modifies requirements relating to the storage of election material, ballots, and election returns;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the deadline to file an objection to a declaration of candidacy;<hr><ltbullet>modifies and removes inconsistent provisions relating to participation in a regular primary election;<hr><ltbullet>grants rulemaking authority to the Office of the Lieutenant Governor to regulate the use and application of the Great Seal of the State of Utah or a replica of the seal;<hr><ltbullet>modifies and clarifies provisions relating to the crime of illegally using or defacing the Great Seal of the State of Utah; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Water Easement Amendments
description: This bill addresses provisions related to a prescriptive easement for water conveyance.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that a municipality has first priority to establish control of a prescriptive easement for water conveyance upon the holder of the easement filing a notice of intent to abandon;<hr><ltbullet>requires a political subdivision that desires to establish control of a prescriptive easement for water conveyance to file a notice describing the use and location of the prescriptive easement in the office of the county recorder in which the easement is located;<hr><ltbullet>allows a political subdivision to convert the use of a prescriptive easement for water conveyance if the political subdivision:<hr><ltbullet1>mails notice of the converted use of the easement to each affected landowner;<hr><ltbullet1>files a notice describing the converted use of the easement in the office of the county recorder;<hr><ltbullet1>waits 120 days from the day the political subdivision sends notice to each affected landowner;<hr><ltbullet1>receives no written objection to the converted use from an affected landowner; and<hr><ltbullet1>limits the modified use of the easement to not burden an affected landowner's use of land, interfere with an existing easement, or expand the size of the easement; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Certified Teacher Librarian Amendments
description: This bill requires a school district or regional education service agency to staff a full-time certified teacher librarian.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a school district or a regional education service agency to staff a certified teacher librarian to:<hr><ltbullet1>oversee the curation of materials in a school's library;<hr><ltbullet1>develop certain curricula;<hr><ltbullet1>assist schools in complying with certain state statutes; and<hr><ltbullet1>provide professional learning and mentorship; and<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Board of Education to:<hr><ltbullet1>distribute funds the Legislature appropriates; and<hr><ltbullet1>make relevant rules.

description: This bill modifies truth-in-taxation notice requirements for a fiscal year taxing entity when a mayor or budget officer proposes a property tax rate increase in a tentative budget.

title: Judicial Modifications
description: This bill addresses issues related to the judiciary.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the ballot language for a retention election;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the transfer of an action from the district court to the Business and Chancery Court;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the assignment of district court judges to cases a municipality files, appeals, or transfers to the district court;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the requirements for a three-judge panel in the district court;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the publication requirements for a final decision or order from the Business and Chancery Court;<hr><ltbullet>amends the tentative decision requirements for the Business and Chancery Court;<hr><ltbullet>contingent on statutory provisions being held invalid or enjoined:<hr><ltbullet1>establishes the Constitutional Court (court);<hr><ltbullet1>addresses the postjudgment interest rate for judgments of the court;<hr><ltbullet1>addresses a retention election for a judge of the court;<hr><ltbullet1>adds a judge of the court to the definition of "public official" for Title 63G, Chapter 23, Property Donated to State by Public Official;<hr><ltbullet1>addresses salaries for judges of the court;<hr><ltbullet1>provides that the court is not geographically divided into districts;<hr><ltbullet1>provides that the court consists of three judges;<hr><ltbullet1>amends the membership of the Judicial Council to include a member from the court;<hr><ltbullet1>amends provisions regarding the administration of the courts to address the creation of the court;<hr><ltbullet1>addresses a judicial hiring freeze for judges of the court;<hr><ltbullet1>amends the jurisdiction of the district court to allow a district court judge or Court of Appeals judge to preside over an action of the court for purposes of disqualification and recusal;<hr><ltbullet1>provides that the court is a trial court with statewide jurisdiction;<hr><ltbullet1>addresses the organization and status of the court;<hr><ltbullet1>addresses the jurisdiction of the court;<hr><ltbullet1>addresses the transfer of an action to the court;<hr><ltbullet1>addresses the administration, staff, and management of the court;<hr><ltbullet1>allows a district court judge or Court of Appeals judge to be appointed to the court without vacating the judge's appointment to the district court or Court of Appeals;<hr><ltbullet1>addresses the location and facilities of the court;<hr><ltbullet1>addresses the selection process for judges of the court, including the creation of the Constitutional Court Nominating Commission; and<hr><ltbullet1>makes changes to provisions regarding judgments, mileage, and lis pendens to address the creation of the court;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the right to appeal for an injunction of a state law; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Solar Power Utility Amendments
description: This bill enacts new provisions related to net metering of electricity.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Public Service Commission to establish an optional time-of-use export pricing tariff for net metering customers;<hr><ltbullet>requires differential pricing for customer-generated electricity based on time of day or real-time market conditions;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a minimum floor for export credits; and<hr><ltbullet>provides customer protections including voluntary participation and retention of existing options.

title: Agriculture and Food Amendments
description: This bill addresses provisions related to the Department of Agriculture and Food.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>updates the names of the members of the Agricultural Advisory Board;<hr><ltbullet>creates an expendable special revenue account for the weights and measures program administered by the Department of Agriculture and Food;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the percentage of funds from the Agriculture Resource Development Fund that the department may use for disaster relief programs;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the term "brand" to remove a tattoo as an identifiable mark and the brisket area as a brand location;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the commissioner of the Department of Agriculture and Food to remove a board member of a conservation district;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an applicant for an agricultural water optimization grant may consult with the Division of Water Rights regarding the necessity of a change application or quantification of saved water;<hr><ltbullet>transfers the obligation to report on the agricultural water optimization program to the Department of Agriculture and Food;<hr><ltbullet>repeals a provision that requires the registration of farm names with the commissioner of the Department of Agriculture and Food; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Sex Offender Oversight Amendments
description: This bill addresses oversight of sex offenders on the Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires local law enforcement agencies to have specific responsibilities for certain sex offenders;<hr><ltbullet>revises definitions concerning a residence for purposes of the Sex, Kidnap, and Child Abuse Offender Registry (registry);<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Public Safety (department) to:<hr><ltbullet1>create a monitoring program for sex offenders who are unable to provide a required residential address to the registry;<hr><ltbullet1>delegate monitoring oversight responsibility to a local law enforcement agency or to the Division of Adult Probation and Parole; <hr><ltbullet1>establish a process for a local law enforcement agency or the Division of Adult Probation and Parole to be notified of the need for an arrest warrant for certain sex offenders; and<hr><ltbullet1>develop and provide an online training program for certain individuals who work with sex offenders;<hr><ltbullet>requires specific entities to coordinate with the department regarding the monitoring of, or seeking an arrest warrant for, certain sex offenders;<hr><ltbullet>requires a sex offender to comply with the monitoring program;<hr><ltbullet>creates criminal penalties for a sex offender's failure to comply with the monitoring program;<hr><ltbullet>requires a court to consider and, if the court finds probable cause, issue an arrest warrant for certain sex offenders;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Adult Probation and Parole to have specific responsibilities for certain sex offenders; <hr><ltbullet>provides a presumption for the issuance of an arrest warrant in lieu of a summons for certain sex offenders; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Grazing Permits Amendments
description: This bill addresses grazing on school and institutional trust lands.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the director of the School and Institutional Trust Lands Administration (SITLA) to prioritize multiple use and sustained yield in the management of school and institutional trust lands (trust lands);<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the director of SITLA from issuing permits for the non-use of trust lands if the trust lands may be used for grazing; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Child Welfare Changes
description: This bill addresses guardians ad litem and consideration of a minor's best interest.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>makes modifications to the Guardian ad Litem Oversight Committee;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the responsibilities of the director of the Office of Guardian ad Litem;<hr><ltbullet>requires an attorney guardian ad litem to inform the court at each hearing:<hr><ltbullet1>whether the minor expressed a desire to attend the hearing; and<hr><ltbullet1>of the date of the attorney guardian ad litem's last interaction with the minor;<hr><ltbullet>addresses when a guardian ad litem is appointed;<hr><ltbullet>adjusts the responsibilities and obligations of an attorney guardian ad litem;<hr><ltbullet>directs a court to consider the best interest of a minor within the context of the principles and provisions in Sections 80-2a-201 and 80-4-104;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the report provided to the Child Welfare Legislative Oversight Panel and the chairs of the Health and Human Services Interim Committee by the fatality review committee within the Division of Continuous Quality and Improvement should not be fully redacted; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Higher Education Innovation
description: This bill creates a pilot grant program for higher education research funding.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding the Nucleus Institute, including:<hr><ltbullet1>authority regarding a facility on point of the mountain state land;<hr><ltbullet1>renaming the Utah Innovation Fund to the Nucleus Fund;<hr><ltbullet1>amending the appointment of certain positions and board members; and<hr><ltbullet1>amending compensation;<hr><ltbullet>allows the commissioner of higher education to undertake certain duties previously dedicated to the Utah Board of Higher Education (board);<hr><ltbullet>creates a pilot grant program for higher education research funding;<hr><ltbullet>requires the board to administer and approve funding grants, potentially through the Nucleus Institute, the Talent, Education, and Industry Alignment Board, or an ad hoc committee;<hr><ltbullet>requires the board to report on the research funding grant program; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Speech, Language, and Hearing Occupations Licensing Amendments
description: This bill modifies the regulations for hearing professionals.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>allows the division to create temporary working groups when no board is available to assist the division;<hr><ltbullet>allows an audiologist to supervise a hearing instrument specialist intern;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the creation of the Speech-language Pathologist and Audiologist Licensing Board;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the exemption permitting an individual to receive licensure as a speech-language pathologist or an audiologist from the State Board of Education;<hr><ltbullet>creates an alternative path for licensure as an audiologist and as a speech-language pathologist;<hr><ltbullet>aligns the unprofessional conduct standards of a hearing instrument specialist with the unprofessional conduct standards of audiologists; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Land Management Funding Amendments
description: This bill addresses funding for watershed restoration and forest health.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the Utah Forest Restoration Institute (institute) in connection with Utah State University;<hr><ltbullet>provides funding to the institute;<hr><ltbullet>requires the institute to:<hr><ltbullet1>conduct research as provided by state and federal law;<hr><ltbullet1>study how the state can improve forest and watershed health;<hr><ltbullet1>recommend mitigation strategies that reduce the risks and impact of wildfire;<hr><ltbullet1>coordinate with the Watershed Restoration Initiative to fund watershed and forest restoration projects;<hr><ltbullet1>review and respond to, in a timely manner, an emergency request for funding a watershed restoration project in response to a natural disaster; and<hr><ltbullet1>monitor the long-term effectiveness of watershed and forest restoration projects;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Watershed Restoration Initiative to:<hr><ltbullet1>coordinate funding decisions with the institute on partnership watershed restoration projects;<hr><ltbullet1>coordinate the long-term monitoring of a watershed restoration project with the institute;<hr><ltbullet1>collect data required by the institute; <hr><ltbullet1>provide research and learning opportunities for higher education students and faculty associated with the institute; and<hr><ltbullet1>submit an annual report to the institute and two legislative committees; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Real Estate Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to real estate.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires that the Department of Commerce make a recommendation to the Business and Labor Interim Committee regarding the jurisdiction of the Division of Real Estate and the Division of Consumer Protection over property management;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>extends the implementation date for the property manager license to January 1, 2027;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the division shall make rules for the licensing of a dual broker;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a dual broker may engage in property management without obtaining a property management license;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the scope of a property manager license;<hr><ltbullet>requires an individual who holds a property manager license who is employed by a person that is required to affiliate with a principal broker to also affiliate with the principal broker;<hr><ltbullet>provides the conditions under which a property manager is not required to affiliate with a principal broker;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to investigating a violation of Title 61, Chapter 2f, Real Estate Licensing and Practices Act;<hr><ltbullet>provides requirements for the records that a brokerage and a property manager that meets certain requirements is required to maintain;<hr><ltbullet>amends the circumstances under which a property manager is not required to maintain property management client funds in a trust account; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Electric Mobility Device Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions regarding electric assisted bicycles and other devices.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the definition of motorcycle includes a motorcycle being powered by an electric or combustion engine;<hr><ltbullet>makes it unlawful to consume alcohol while operating an electric assisted bicycle;<hr><ltbullet>addresses tampering with or modifying equipment beyond the manufacturer's original settings on an electric assisted bicycle or motorcycle;<hr><ltbullet>requires an individual under 21 years old to wear a helmet while operating certain devices on a highway;<hr><ltbullet>allows a peace officer to hold an individual's electric vehicle and release it to a parent if the peace officer observes a violation and the individual is under 18 years old;<hr><ltbullet>creates a safety course for the operation of certain electric devices on a highway and describes the circumstances under which the course is required; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Uniform Assignment for Benefit of Creditors Amendments
description: This bill enacts the Uniform Assignment for Benefit of Creditors Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes scope provisions, and eligibility requirements for assignors, assignees, and assignment agreements, including independence standards and fiduciary duties for assignees;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the legal effect of an assignment, filing and recording requirements, creditor notification procedures, and mandatory duties of both an assignor and an assignee throughout the administration of the assignment estate;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a process for submitting, allowing, disputing, and disallowing a creditor claim;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a comprehensive priority scheme for distributions from the assignment estate;<hr><ltbullet>grants an assignee defined powers to operate businesses, dispose of assets, pursue and defend claims, avoid certain transfers, and wind up the assignment, subject to fiduciary obligations and judicial oversight;<hr><ltbullet>addresses liability standards, assignee removal and replacement, final accounting and discharge, interstate recognition of assignments, and limits on contractual variation to ensure uniform application; and<hr><ltbullet>repeals the existing assignment for benefit of creditors code.

title: Department of Health and Human Services Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions of the Health and Humans Services code and related provisions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>removes rulemaking authority from the Primary Care Grant Committee;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the membership of the Compassionate Use Board;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the designation of a vice chair of the Utah Health Workforce Advisory Council;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the recommendations of the Utah Health Workforce Advisory Council are independent of the governor and the Department of Health and Human Services (department);<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to a qualified individual for purposes of the department's fatality review;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the department to make rules related to the congregate care ombudsman;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to Medicaid dental benefits and instructs the department to apply for waivers to provide dental services;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a rural hospital's contracted hiring group may provide education loan repayment assistance to a physician to qualify for a education loan repayment assistance contract with the department;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies provisions related to the transfer of an individual in the custody of the Department of Corrections to the state hospital;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the Division of Services for People with Disabilities (division) may use certain funds for individuals transitioning to home- and community-based services, rather than division services;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to the child protection ombudsman;<hr><ltbullet>updates the name of the Department of Health and Human Services in certain provisions; <hr><ltbullet>corrects code references; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill addresses executive branch agencies.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the Utah Office of Data Privacy is an office within the Department of Government Operations (department);<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the department exercises oversight of the state's comprehensive accounting system and executive branch payroll services;<hr><ltbullet>subjects the Division of Finance's establishment of the comprehensive state accounting system to departmental oversight;<hr><ltbullet>replaces the requirement that the director of the Division of Finance audit all claims against the state with a requirement that the director oversee internal controls relating to state financial transactions;<hr><ltbullet>updates the definition of "executive branch entity" for purposes of executive branch payroll services by: <hr><ltbullet1>removing a date-specific reference to participation in the Division of Finance's central payroll system; and<hr><ltbullet1>adding the Division of Technology Services as an entity included within the definition;<hr><ltbullet>changes the title of certain gubernatorial appointees to "commissioner," beginning on May 6, 2026; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Specialized Product Sales Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to specialized products.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates a license for persons that sell specialized products to be administered by the Department of Agriculture and Food (department);<hr><ltbullet>requires specialized product retailers to provide a list of specialized products offered for sale to the department;<hr><ltbullet>requires applicants for a specialized product retailer license to provide ownership information;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits issuing a license if certain individuals involved with the specialized product retailer have violated certain criminal laws;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Tax Commission to revoke certain tobacco and nicotine licenses if the licensee stores or sells illegally obtained controlled substances;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits advertising of electronic cigarette products and nicotine products in certain locations;<hr><ltbullet>creates fees and penalties related to the license;<hr><ltbullet>criminalizes the criminally negligent sale of tobacco, electronic cigarettes, and nicotine to minors; and<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to underage tobacco sales.

highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>repeals:<hr><ltbullet1>the Guest Worker Program and related employee verification provisions; and<hr><ltbullet1>the Utah Pilot Sponsored Resident Immigrant Program Act; <hr><ltbullet>eliminates the repeal of the Private Employer Verification Act that is scheduled to occur on the Guest Worker Program start date;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the Identity Theft Victims Restricted Account that would have gone into effect on the Guest Worker Program start date; <hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding exceptions to verification of lawful presence for the receipt of certain public assistance benefits; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Kratom Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions related to kratom.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a kratom processor and kratom retailer to register with the Department of Agriculture and Food;<hr><ltbullet>bans the sale of certain kratom products;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to penalties and fees;<hr><ltbullet>amends the age for who can purchase a kratom product; and<hr><ltbullet>suspends the operation of the Kratom Consumer Protection Act if every alkaloid found in the Mitragyna speciosa plant is a controlled substances under state law.

title: Cannabis Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to cannabis.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to hazardous waste and cannabinoid (hemp) disposal;<hr><ltbullet>requires industrial hemp retailers to check an individual's identification to ensure a purchaser is at least 21 years old;<hr><ltbullet>repeals video surveillance requirements for industrial hemp retailers;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to unlawful acts concerning hemp products;<hr><ltbullet>exempts medical cannabis processors from obtaining an additional license to process hemp products;<hr><ltbullet>creates a fee on medical cannabis purchases for use in enforcement of various laws;<hr><ltbullet>renames the Cannabis Production Establishment and Pharmacy Licensing Advisory Board to the Specialized Product Authority Licensing Board (licensing board);<hr><ltbullet>reconstitutes the licensing board's membership;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to labeling and packaging;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the licensing board's duties;<hr><ltbullet>moves control of the Qualified Patient Enterprise Fund to the Department of Agriculture and Food (UDAF);<hr><ltbullet>moves all Department of Health and Human Services duties related to the medical cannabis program to UDAF;<hr><ltbullet>allows medical cannabis processors to make cannabis products with a THC content below .3% (low THC products); <hr><ltbullet>allows medical cannabis pharmacies to sell low THC products;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to address a cross-reference in S.B. 121, Medical Cannabis Program Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause with H.B. 385, Specialized Product Sales Amendments, to address the movement of the Qualified Patient Enterprise Fund.

title: Veterans PTSD Clinical Research Amendments
description: This bill addresses psychedelic-assisted therapy for certain veterans.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Huntsman Mental Health Institute (Huntsman) to conduct a clinical study on the safety and feasibility of psychedelic-assisted therapy for veterans with treatment-resistant post-traumatic stress disorder;<hr><ltbullet>permits Huntsman to accept donations to fund the clinical study;<hr><ltbullet>requires Huntsman to begin the clinical study if legislative appropriations and donations combined are equal to or exceed an amount sufficient to begin the study;<hr><ltbullet>requires reporting to the Health and Human Services Interim Committee; <hr><ltbullet>provides a sunset date for the provisions related to the clinical study;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Vacancy Replacement Amendments
description: This bill addresses vacancies in elected office.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires certain vacancies in elected office to be filled by appointment of an individual selected by the political party of which the prior officeholder was a member at the time the prior officeholder was last elected or appointed, including:<hr><ltbullet1>a vacancy in the office of United States senator, state legislator, or State Board of Education member, to be appointed by the governor; and<hr><ltbullet1>a vacancy in a county office, to be appointed by a county legislative body; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: District Court Amendments
description: This bill addresses civil actions in the district court.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>grants the attorney general an unconditional right to intervene in a civil action in the district court upon notice that a party is challenging the constitutionality of a statute;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Utah Supreme Court has exclusive and original appellate jurisdiction over a judgment or order from a panel of three district court judges;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the attorney general, the governor, or the Legislature may file a notice to convene a three-judge panel in a civil action in the district court;<hr><ltbullet>requires a panel of three district court judges to be convened to hear and decide a civil action upon the filing of a notice to convene a district court panel;<hr><ltbullet>requires each judge of a district court panel to be randomly selected and from a different judicial district than the other judges on the panel;<hr><ltbullet> addresses the structure and voting process for a district court panel;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the statutory venue requirements for a civil action do not apply to an action before a district court panel;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Judicial Council to create a rule regarding the random selection process for a judge on a district court panel;<hr><ltbullet>addresses staffing of a district court panel; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Early Intervention for Dyslexia Amendments
description: This bill creates the Dyslexia Screening Pilot Program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Dyslexia Screening Pilot Program to:<hr><ltbullet1>provide dyslexia related resources to district and charter schools; and<hr><ltbullet1>create a dyslexia screener at the University of Utah College of Education and the University of Utah Education Policy Center;<hr><ltbullet>creates reporting requirements to the Education Interim Committee;<hr><ltbullet>requires the University of Utah Education Policy Center to:<hr><ltbullet1>develop a statewide dyslexia intervention plan; and<hr><ltbullet1>report to the State Board of Education (state board);<hr><ltbullet>requires the state board to:<hr><ltbullet1>administer and oversee the pilot program;<hr><ltbullet1>choose two schools participating in the program to receive dyslexia intervention;<hr><ltbullet1>procure an intervention provider; and<hr><ltbullet1>make certain rules related to the pilot program;<hr><ltbullet>provides a repeal date for the pilot program; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Real Estate Transaction Amendments
description: This bill enacts the Utah Real Estate Cybercrime Prevention Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>makes failing to use the real estate transaction communication network (network) unprofessional conduct for employees of appraisal management companies, appraisers, escrow agents, mortgage lenders, mortgage loan originators, real estate sales agents, real estate brokers, title insurance licensees, and title insurers;<hr><ltbullet>makes violating a rule from the real estate transaction communication utility (utility) unprofessional conduct for appraisal management companies, appraisers, escrow agents, mortgage lenders, mortgage loan originators, real estate sales agents, real estate brokers, title insurance licensees, and title insurers;<hr><ltbullet>requires covered individuals to use the network to send covered communications related to real estate transactions;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Real Estate Communication Commission (commission) within the Department of Commerce to oversee the network;<hr><ltbullet>assigns the commission duties such as selecting a utility and approving fee schedules;<hr><ltbullet>grants the commission the power to issue or revoke a certificate of authority and recommend enforcement actions to other regulatory agencies;<hr><ltbullet>mandates that any person operating a network obtain a certificate of authority from the commission;<hr><ltbullet>requires the utility to submit all user eligibility rules and fee schedules to the commission for review and approval;<hr><ltbullet>directs the commission to perform criminal background checks on individuals who own 10% or more of the utility;<hr><ltbullet>directs the commission to automatically revoke a certificate of authority if an owner fails to accurately disclose a criminal history involving fraud or deceit;<hr><ltbullet>establishes that a certificate of authority expires after two years and outlines the specific requirements for renewal; and<hr><ltbullet>defines unprofessional conduct as violating network rules or failing to use the network for covered communications.

title: Public Project Subcontractor Amendments
description: This bill modifies disclosure requirements for subcontractors.,
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>enacts a new workers' compensation insurance attestation requirement for an employer seeking a zero estimated exposure policy, including a mandatory signed statement and criminal fraud warning;<hr><ltbullet>shifts several fixed interest rates and penalty amounts under the Employment Security Act to amounts the division determines by rule;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies enforcement authority and penalty structures related to unemployment insurance reporting, collections, liens, and warrants;<hr><ltbullet>creates new compliance and disclosure obligations for a subcontractor working on a public construction project, including employee reporting and zero estimated exposure policy disclosures;<hr><ltbullet>requires a subcontractor on a public project to provide employee information to the division;<hr><ltbullet>requires a general contractor and a property owner to retain documentation for audit and enforcement purposes;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Division of Professional Licensing to make audit recommendations to the State Tax Commission;<hr><ltbullet>expands the definition of unprofessional conduct to include failure to comply with newly enacted subcontractor requirements;<hr><ltbullet>provides a coordination clause to substantively and technically coordinate changes between this bill and H.B. 40, Utah Construction Trades Licensing Act Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Prohibition Against Student Character Tracking and Grading Systems
description: This bill defines character education and creates restraints on certain entities regarding the use of character education.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>repeals certain requirements related to:<hr><ltbullet1>civics education; and<hr><ltbullet1>character education;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits administrative and instructional personnel from:<hr><ltbullet1>implementing character education;<hr><ltbullet1>measuring, quantifying, tracking, or grading a student's character education; and<hr><ltbullet1>collecting and distributing character education data about a student;<hr><ltbullet>outlines constitutional protections for a parent and the parent's children;<hr><ltbullet>requires the state auditor to:<hr><ltbullet1>receive certain reports;<hr><ltbullet1>conduct certain investigations; and<hr><ltbullet1>enforce the provisions of the section;<hr><ltbullet> creates a private right of action;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a public entity from creating certain rules related to character education; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Sex-Designated Housing Amendments
description: This bill creates an exemption in the Utah Fair Housing Act allowing a landlord to designate housing as single-sex based on biological sex.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>permits a landlord to restrict occupancy in single-sex housing to individuals of the designated biological sex;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that such restriction is not unlawful discrimination under the Utah Fair Housing Act; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: State Purchasing Reserve Funding
description: This bill modifies provisions related to state purchasing.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes an administrative fee on state cooperative contracts;<hr><ltbullet>deposits revenue from the administrative fee into a restricted account called the State Purchasing Reserve Restricted Account (account);<hr><ltbullet>directs the state treasurer to invest money in the account in precious metals; and<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the money in the account to be used for the purpose of offsetting the cost of procuring goods and services for specified public entities and ensuring continuity in the public entities' procurement of goods and services, if certain inflation metrics are met.

title: Homeowners' Association Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions relating to homeowners' associations.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the Office of the Homeowners' Association Ombudsman (office) make public each advisory opinion the office issues;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the office publish educational materials on the office's website;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an action by an attorney employed by the office does not create an attorney-client relationship;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the filing fee a person pays for an advisory opinion from the office is nonrefundable;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a homeowners' association may not require a person to engage in binding arbitration before obtaining an advisory opinion from the office;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for the contents of a request for an advisory opinion;<hr><ltbullet>amends the amount of the civil penalty a court may issue after qualifying conditions are met;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the requirement that the parties to an advisory opinion split the cost of the advisory opinion;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an administrative setup fee may not exceed $200;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the conditions under which Title 57, Chapter 8, Condominium Ownership Act, or Title 57, Chapter 8a, Community Association Act, applies;<hr><ltbullet>requires that an association of unit owners prepare and adopt an annual budget for the association;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to the applicability of Title 57, Chapter 8, Condominium Ownership Act, or Title 57, Chapter 8a, Community Association Act;<hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement that a board member and president of an association provide a physical address to the Department of Commerce for registration;<hr><ltbullet>provides that certain documents are considered property of an association;<hr><ltbullet>provides that if a person maintains a document considered property of an association, the person shall provide the document to the association upon request;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a declarant may sell a part of the common areas during the period of administrative control to certain persons; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Public Education Information System
description: This bill modifies provisions related to student information systems for local education agencies.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes data compliance requirements for local education agency student information systems;<hr><ltbullet>requires local education agencies to meet state board data standards and interoperability requirements; <hr><ltbullet>requires student information systems to capture school safety and threat assessment data; <hr><ltbullet>authorizes the state board to provide technical assistance and vendor certification;<hr><ltbullet>establishes enforcement provisions for noncompliance;<hr><ltbullet>requires audits of certain local education agencies;<hr><ltbullet>establishes implementation timelines; and<hr><ltbullet>makes conforming changes.

title: Data Sharing Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to social media data portability and interoperability.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allows users to select portions of their social media data to transfer; <hr><ltbullet>requires social media platforms to share user data in real time when users move to other platforms;<hr><ltbullet>requires consent from users before their comments or interactions can be included when others transfer data;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies when users must give permission for their data to be shared; and<hr><ltbullet>protects social media companies from penalties for temporary technical problems if they make good faith efforts to fix them.

title: Legislator Leave Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to legislators who are public employees.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides paid leave to a state employee or teacher for the purpose of serving as a state legislator;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the use and administration of legislator leave;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a legislator may not receive salary or accrue service credit or receive retirement related contributions for time during which the legislator uses legislator leave;<hr><ltbullet>allows a state employer or local education agency to seek partial reimbursement for the costs related to legislator leave; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Water Leasing Amendments
description: This bill addresses leasing of water.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>makes appropriations to the Great Salt Lake Preservation Program (program) nonlapsing;<hr><ltbullet>addresses diversion or impoundment by an intervening user of leased water;<hr><ltbullet>provides for streamlined leasing of certain water;<hr><ltbullet>directs the Great Salt Lake commissioner to facilitate leasing of water for the Great Salt Lake;<hr><ltbullet>creates the program;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Great Salt Lake Preservation Board (board);<hr><ltbullet>provides for rulemaking by the board;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the leasing process;<hr><ltbullet>addresses applications related to a lease of water;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the board to take action if a person violates a lease;<hr><ltbullet>requires reporting by the board and the state engineer;<hr><ltbullet>enacts a sunset date; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: Human Trafficking Hotline Amendments
description: This bill directs the attorney general to seek a three-digit dialing code for the National Human Trafficking Hotline.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>no later than December 31, 2026, requires the attorney general, in coordination with the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), to petition the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to initiate a rulemaking regarding the designation or use of a three-digit dialing code to access the National Human Trafficking Hotline (hotline);<hr><ltbullet>if the FCC approves a three-digit dialing code for the hotline:<hr><ltbullet1>requires DHHS to coordinate with a federal agency and nonprofit entity to support implementation of three-digit access to the hotline; and<hr><ltbullet1>authorizes the attorney general to coordinate with telecommunications providers and to conduct public education and outreach regarding the availability of the dialing code; and<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the state is not authorized to control numbering resources or require call routing, except as permitted under federal law.

title: Surplus Interconnection Service Amendments
description: This bill makes changes to the Energy Resource Procurement Act.

title: First Responder Health Modifications
description: This bill addresses health coverage and resources for first responders.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>changes the amount of revenue transferred to the Utah State Retirement Office from the insurance premiums tax and used to pay for certain firefighter retirement programs;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Firefighter Cancer Benefit Trust Fund (trust fund);<hr><ltbullet>creates a board of trustees;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the duties of the board of trustees; <hr><ltbullet>provides funding for the cancer screening program;<hr><ltbullet>provides funding for the trust fund;<hr><ltbullet>amends eligibility requirements for the Volunteer Emergency Medical Service Personnel Insurance Program;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Public Safety (department) to annually submit a report on first responder agencies' compliance with requirements to provide mental health resources to first responders and first responders' spouses to the:<hr><ltbullet1>Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee; and<hr><ltbullet1>State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice's public safety portal;<hr><ltbullet>amends eligibility for receiving mental health resources for separated first responders and separated first responders' spouses;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Mental Health Resources for First Responders Restricted Account to provide funding for the department to provide certain mental health resources to eligible small first responder agencies; and<hr><ltbullet>provides a sunset date for grants to first responder agencies.

description: This bill enacts provisions related to patient interfacility transportation.

title: Hit and Run and DUI Offense Amendments
description: This bill increases the penalty for leaving the scene of an accident and modifies deadlines for an administrative driver license hearing following an individual's arrest for driving under the influence.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>increases penalties for convictions of leaving the scene of an accident with property damage or injury if the operator has been previously convicted of:<hr><ltbullet1>the same offense; or<hr><ltbullet1>driving under the influence;<hr><ltbullet>creates a mitigation against an enhanced offense for an individual who obtains a negative chemical test;<hr><ltbullet>allows the Driver License Division to request a peace officer's presence for a driver license suspension hearing;<hr><ltbullet>adds that a Driver License Division hearing for a driving under the influence arrest cannot be dismissed solely due to a peace officer's failure to appear; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Judicial Nomination Amendments
description: This bill addresses judicial selection.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>contingent on passage of a proposed constitutional amendment:<hr><ltbullet1>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet1>authorizes the governor to request a list of nominees from a judicial nominating commission when the governor is filling a judicial vacancy;<hr><ltbullet1>removes the authority of the chief justice of the Supreme Court to fill a judicial vacancy if the governor fails to fill the vacancy;<hr><ltbullet1>authorizes the governor to appoint any qualified candidate even if the candidate is not nominated by the judicial nominating commission;<hr><ltbullet1>addresses the time period during which a judicial nominating commission may accept an application from an individual seeking nomination to fill a judicial vacancy;<hr><ltbullet1>removes the time constraint on the governor to make a judicial appointment; and<hr><ltbullet1>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Local Government Fees Amendments
description: This bill modifies and enacts provisions related to municipal and county fees.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a city from imposing a fee on the general public for broadband or public safety service, with exceptions;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a town from imposing a fee on the general public for public safety services, with exceptions;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a municipality or a county to impose a transportation utility fee; <hr><ltbullet>establishes the process and requirements for a municipality or county to impose or increase a transportation utility fee;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the process and requirements for a municipality or county to use the revenue generated by a transportation utility fee;<hr><ltbullet>requires a municipality or county that establishes a transportation utility fee to:<hr><ltbullet1>establish an appeal process; and<hr><ltbullet1>conduct an annual review of the fee;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an ordinance imposing a transportation utility fee is subject to local referenda; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Tax Increment Financing Modifications
description: This bill modifies the process by which a public entity may utilize tax increment financing.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>beginning July 1, 2026, requires a public entity seeking to utilize tax increment to first:<hr><ltbullet1>conduct an application authorization meeting; and<hr><ltbullet1>submit an application to the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity (office); <hr><ltbullet>authorizes the office to review an application and:<hr><ltbullet1>approve the application; or<hr><ltbullet1>if the information in the application is unclear, vague, or demonstrably inaccurate, deny the application;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a public entity that receives an approved application to begin the process to trigger and utilize tax increment;<hr><ltbullet>requires a public entity that receives more revenue from tax increment than anticipated to utilize the revenue to defease bonds or otherwise accelerate repayment of debt incurred by the public entity; and<hr><ltbullet>requires the office to ensure certain information from an application is made publicly available.

title: Special Districts Amendments
description: This bill addresses withdrawal of a county or a municipality from a special district under certain circumstances.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>provides a process for a county of the first class to initiate withdrawal from a first responder district;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the process to conduct a feasibility study on withdrawal from a first responder district;<hr><ltbullet>creates a process for a county of the first class or a municipality located in a county of the first class to initiate withdrawal from a garbage disposal district;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a garbage disposal district from incurring debt, issuing bonds, or otherwise incurring a financial obligation for a period of time after the county or municipality initiates the process to withdraw from the garbage disposal district;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a county or municipality and a garbage disposal district to enter into an agreement to withdraw;<hr><ltbullet>describes the requirements for a county or municipality to complete withdrawal from a garbage disposal district absent an agreement, including:<hr><ltbullet1>conducting a feasibility study;<hr><ltbullet1>conducting a public hearing on the proposed withdrawal;<hr><ltbullet1>providing notice of a public hearing on the proposed withdrawal; and<hr><ltbullet1>adopting a resolution to withdraw;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the process to file with the lieutenant governor certain documents;<hr><ltbullet>describes the process to determine the effective date of a withdrawal; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Wildlife Crossing Amendments
description: This bill creates an account and provides funding for wildlife connectivity and livestock protection projects.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates the Wildlife Crossing Account in the Transportation Investment Fund of 2005 for projects that improve wildlife safety and connectivity and livestock safety;<hr><ltbullet>creates an earmark for sales and use tax revenue to be deposited into the account;<hr><ltbullet>defines allowed uses of money in the account;<hr><ltbullet>directs the Department of Transportation, in consultation with the Division of Wildlife Resources and stakeholders, to recommend projects to the Transportation Commission for prioritization;<hr><ltbullet>creates the option for applicants for a vehicle registration or hunting and other licenses to make a voluntary contribution to support wildlife connectivity; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Egg Amendments
description: This bill addresses eggs.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines and modifies terms;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies fee and rulemaking authority for the Department of Agriculture and Food (department) regarding the distribution, sale, and inspection of shell eggs;<hr><ltbullet>establishes that a person may not:<hr><ltbullet1>distribute shell eggs unless the person obtains a license from the department; or<hr><ltbullet1>sell shell eggs from a small producer outside of the state;<hr><ltbullet>requires a large egg producer to register with the department as a food establishment;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the requirements for small and large egg producers; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: State Policy on Judea and Samaria
description: This bill establishes a state policy of referring to certain land controlled by Israel as Judea and Samaria.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>makes it state policy to refer to the land, restored to Israel from Jordan during the 1967 Six-Day War, by the land's historical names of Judea and Samaria; and<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a state agency or official government material from referring to the land described in the preceding paragraph as "West Bank."

title: Environmental Permitting Amendments
description: This bill creates a program for the expedited review of environmental permit applications.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Department of Environmental Quality (department) and Division of Oil, Gas, and Mining (division) to make rules to:<hr><ltbullet1>identify a permit administered by the department or division as a permit eligible for expedited review;<hr><ltbullet1>establish requirements for the expedited review process;<hr><ltbullet1>certify a qualified reviewer;<hr><ltbullet1>authorize a qualified reviewer to complete an expedited review of an eligible permit; and<hr><ltbullet1>establish the maximum number of a days for a qualified reviewer to complete an expedited review;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department and division to conduct a technical review and make a final administrative decision for a permit application upon completion of an expedited review; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.
