title: Artificial Intelligence Amendments
description: This bill enacts the Companion Chatbot Safety Act to regulate operators of companion chatbots and protect consumers.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; <hr><ltbullet>requires operators of companion chatbots to comply with the Utah Consumer Privacy Act; <hr><ltbullet>establishes disclosure and data protection requirements for operators; <hr><ltbullet>establishes additional safety requirements for operators serving minor users; <hr><ltbullet>authorizes rulemaking for age assurance standards; <hr><ltbullet>requires annual reporting by operators to the Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy; <hr><ltbullet>grants enforcement authority to the Division of Consumer Protection; <hr><ltbullet>provides for administrative fines and civil penalties; <hr><ltbullet>establishes a safe harbor provision for operators; <hr><ltbullet>requires the Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy to study and report on companion chatbot safety standards; and <hr><ltbullet>provides a severability clause.

title: Water Planning Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to the planning of future water supply.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines and modifies terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires counties, municipalities, and special districts to adopt a written plan, beginning on January 1, 2028, for determining the reasonable future water requirement of the public before imposing a water exaction;<hr><ltbullet>requires the state engineer to make rules to establish standards for the written plan;<hr><ltbullet>provides a coordination clause with S.B. 284, Local Land Use Modifications, to address a requirement for counties and municipalities to complete a written plan; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Property Transaction Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to property transactions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires, when ownership of certain real property is transferred, the seller or the closing agent make available information about the property, including sales price, to a county assessor;<hr><ltbullet>excludes sales price information shared with the State Tax Commission or the county assessors from the definition of a "private record" for purposes of the Government Records Access and Management Act;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes disclosure of sales price information under certain circumstances; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Amendments to Procedure to Fill A Legislative Vacancy
description: This bill modifies provisions relating to filling a vacancy in the Legislature.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires all vacancies in the Legislature to remain vacant until filled by a special election;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a procedure for calling a special election to fill a vacancy in the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet>describes the dates, which coincide with the dates of other elections, on which a special primary election or a special general election may be held to fill a vacancy in the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet>provides a method for calling a special primary election or a special general election to fill a vacancy in the Legislature on a date other than a date that coincides with the dates of other elections; and<hr><ltbullet>provides for a temporary appointment to fill a vacancy in the Legislature that occurs, or will exist, during a general session of the Legislature, until the vacancy is filled by a special election described in this bill.

title: State Land Access Road Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to the abandonment and closure of a class D road and public access.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends requirements for off-highway vehicle equipment while operating in certain areas;<hr><ltbullet>provides a process necessary for a county and the state to abandon a class D road;<hr><ltbullet>requires public meetings and notice before abandonment of a class D road;<hr><ltbullet>ensures that existing easements and access rights for public utilities and water infrastructure are not impacted by the abandonment of a class D road;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to the closure of a class D road due to lack of public use to include roads across property owned by a public entity or an institution of higher education;<hr><ltbullet>amends a criminal provision related to discharging a firearm near a class D road; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: County Government Land Purchasing
description: This bill deals with a county's acquisition of real property located in another county.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that a county may not acquire real property that is located in another county through exchange, purchase, or lease unless:<hr><ltbullet1>the county where the real property is located provides express permission; and<hr><ltbullet1>the county's acquisition is a joint acquisition with another political subdivision as part of an interlocal agreement;<hr><ltbullet>provides that real property owned by a county that is located outside the geographical boundaries of the county is not exempt from taxation under Title 59, Chapter 2, Property Tax Act, unless exceptions apply; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Conflict of Interest Disclosure Amendments
description: This bill addresses candidate and officeholder disclosures.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>adds the following to the list of conflict of interest disclosures for elected and appointed officeholders and certain other public officials:<hr><ltbullet1>certain unresolved federal or state tax liens; and<hr><ltbullet1>felony and misdemeanor criminal convictions, subject to certain exceptions;<hr><ltbullet>amends the definition of "applicant" for purposes of restrictions on criminal history inquiries by public employers to exclude a person who is required to file a conflict of interest disclosure; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Tobacco Amendments
description: This bill enacts provisions relating to sales of cigars and pipe tobacco.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>authorizes telephone, mail, internet, and other remote retail sales of a cigar or pipe tobacco;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the licensing, bonding, and taxation of cigar and pipe tobacco transactions between a remote seller and a consumer in the state;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a criminal penalty for failing to comply with the licensing, bonding, and tax collection requirements;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes; and<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to align license terms and fees with other tobacco licenses as provided in S.B. 210, Nicotine Amendments.

title: Utah Schools for the Deaf and Blind Amendments
description: This bill addresses the mission, governance, and operation of the Utah Schools for the Deaf and the Blind.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends the mission and role of the Utah Schools for the Deaf and the Blind (USDB);<hr><ltbullet>addresses the educational and financial relationship between USDB and a student's local education agency (LEA) of record;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the appointment of the USDB superintendent;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding the role of the State Board of Education (state board) in relation to USDB;<hr><ltbullet>enacts requirements regarding USDB capital facilities;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions regarding the role of USDB's advisory council;<hr><ltbullet>requires USDB to count students receiving services from USDB;<hr><ltbullet>requires the state board to ensure and report on certain data;<hr><ltbullet>requires state involvement in an eligibility determination for USDB to replace a student's LEA of record as the student's designated LEA;<hr><ltbullet>requires certain consideration of shared or colocated facilities with certain school districts; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Utah Taxpayer Oversight of Government Spending Amendments
description: This bill establishes taxpayer oversight of government spending.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes taxpayer oversight of government spending as required by a proposed amendment to the Utah Constitution, including:<hr><ltbullet1>requiring voters to approve an increase in state or local government revenue through most taxes or government debt;<hr><ltbullet1>limiting the amount of revenue a government entity may spend in a fiscal year unless voters approve increased spending; <hr><ltbullet1>eliminating automatic increases to taxes; and<hr><ltbullet1>requiring a refund of excess revenue to taxpayers;<hr><ltbullet>repeals provisions requiring residential property to be assessed using any method other than the sales comparison approach;<hr><ltbullet>modifies elections provisions to accommodate voting requirements;<hr><ltbullet>exempts business personal property that is not subject to a uniform fee from property tax; <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes; and<hr><ltbullet>makes these changes contingent upon passage of a proposed constitutional amendment.

title: Data Privacy Amendments
description: This bill amends the Government Data Privacy Act and the Government Records Access and Management Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>restructures the Utah Privacy Commission (commission) to include representatives from state agencies, cities, counties, and public education;<hr><ltbullet>transfers support of the commission from the state auditor's office to the Utah Office of Data Privacy (office);<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the commission to establish participation requirements for commission members;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the office to provide recommendations and guidance;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the office to partner with state institutions of higher education for research and support functions;<hr><ltbullet>requires the office and the commission to jointly study the use of passive data collection technology by governmental entities and report findings and recommendations to the Government Operations Interim Committee;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the data privacy ombudsman as a component of the Office of Data Privacy;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a data privacy complaint process;<hr><ltbullet>removes duplicative provisions from the Government Records Access and Management Act;<hr><ltbullet>expands amendment and correction procedures to cover information beyond personal data; <hr><ltbullet>removes the state privacy auditor, and places the state privacy auditor's responsibility with the state auditor's office and makes conforming changes; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Agricultural Amendments
description: This bill addresses funding for agricultural land.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that the conservation commission (commission) may award loans and grants from the Agriculture Resource Development Fund to small farmers:<hr><ltbullet1>to obtain an active farm no larger than 20 acres or expand an active farm up to 20 total acres;<hr><ltbullet1>for the purpose of a down payment; and<hr><ltbullet1>to purchase equipment or cover an operational cost related to developing or maintaining agricultural land;<hr><ltbullet>grants rulemaking authority to the commission related to the small farm assistance program;<hr><ltbullet>appropriates funding for the small farm assistance program;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Agriculture and Food to report to a legislative committee on the status of the small farm assistance program; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Firearm Storage for Concealed Permit Holders on Publicly Supported Entities
description: This bill addresses requirements regarding handgun storage on certain property open to the public owned by entities that receive public funds.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires a private entity that receives public funds, in certain circumstances, to provide for the storage of handguns of individuals with concealed carry permits on property open to the public;<hr><ltbullet>allows a private entity receiving public funds to use the online verification system already established by the Bureau of Criminal Identification for private sales of firearms to validate concealed carry permits; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Unspent Funding Amendments

title: Preterm Birth Amendments
description: This bill addresses preterm birth policies.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires facilities that provide birthing services to:<hr><ltbullet1>develop and publish policies regarding preterm birth;<hr><ltbullet1>inform parents about the facility's capability to provide lifesaving care for a premature infant; and<hr><ltbullet1>report to the Department of Health and Human Services regarding preterm births;<hr><ltbullet>requires a provider to consult with a neonatologist in certain circumstances relating to risk of preterm delivery;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the denial of lifesaving care to an infant based solely on the gestational age of the infant;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Health and Human Services to produce an annual report regarding preterm birth in the state;<hr><ltbullet>requires prenatal health care providers to discuss certain things with a pregnant patient before approximately 20 weeks gestation;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the rights of a patient during preterm birth; and<hr><ltbullet>defines terms.

title: Sexual Offense Evidence and Reporting Procedures Amendments
description: This bill amends evidence and reporting procedures that occur after a sexual offense is committed.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends injury reporting requirements for a health care provider for certain sexual offenses;<hr><ltbullet>allows certain victims of a sexual offense the option of:<hr><ltbullet1>receiving medical treatment, without any report of the sexual offense to law enforcement;<hr><ltbullet1>with or without medical treatment, providing either a full report or a limited report of the sexual offense to law enforcement;<hr><ltbullet1>allowing evidence collection for the sexual offense, including a sexual assault medical forensic examination that collects a sexual assault kit; and<hr><ltbullet1>designating the sexual assault kit as either an unrestricted kit with full disclosure and processing or as a restricted kit that can either be stored without testing or subjected to limited testing;<hr><ltbullet>requires limited victim information to be shared with law enforcement with a restricted kit;<hr><ltbullet>requires that payment of costs for medical treatment and evidence collection for a victim of a sexual offense be the same regardless of whether the victim opts to make a full or limited report to law enforcement or if the victim opts only for medical treatment without reporting the sexual offense to law enforcement;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Bureau of Forensic Services to conduct testing of certain restricted kits;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Public Safety's statewide sexual assault kit tracking system to provide limited access to a victim who has submitted a restricted kit for forensic testing to track the kit's processing status;<hr><ltbullet>establishes procedures for contacting a victim through a victim advocate to request the victim's consent to certain disclosures if a law enforcement agency determines that:<hr><ltbullet1>there may be a serial sexual offender in a particular area; and <hr><ltbullet1>evidence in the victim's restricted kit may provide relevant evidence in the investigation;<hr><ltbullet>revises and reorganizes statutory procedures and requirements that occur after certain sexual offenses are committed;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions to provide for a reparations award for a victim of a sexual assault under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>amends the definition of "sexual offense" for certain sexual offense procedures and victim rights provisions;<hr><ltbullet>inserts the former definition of "sexual offense" into statutes that had relied on the definition of "sexual offense" that this bill amends; title: Candidate Nomination Procedures Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to nominating candidates for elective office and placing candidates on a ballot.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>repeals provisions relating to a qualified political party;<hr><ltbullet>establishes two types of registered political parties:<hr><ltbullet1>a primary nominating party that nominates candidates through signature-gathering only, participates in the regular primary election, and has the name of the primary nominating party listed on the regular general election ballot in association with the party's candidates; and<hr><ltbullet1>a convention nominating party that nominates candidates using a method that does not involve the signature-gathering process described in the preceding paragraph or participation in the regular primary election, and whose candidates are listed on the regular general election ballot without an indication of the convention nominating party that nominated the candidates;<hr><ltbullet>requires a registered political party to choose whether to be a primary nominating party or a convention nominating party;<hr><ltbullet>modifies signature-gathering thresholds; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Tax Increment Financing Revisions
description: This bill deals with the publication of information about tax increment revenue.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires the boards of the Utah Inland Port Authority, the Point of the Mountain State Land Authority, the Utah Fairpark Area Investment and Restoration District, the Military Installation Development Authority, and the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity, on behalf of the convention center reinvestment zones, to publish information related to tax increment revenue on a publicly accessible website; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Colorado River Authority Amendments
description: This bill addresses the Colorado River Authority of Utah.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>moves the Colorado River Authority of Utah (authority) from the governor's office to the Department of Natural Resources, including providing a transition;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the definition provision;<hr><ltbullet>amends the membership provision of the authority including modifying the appointment process;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the operation of the authority;<hr><ltbullet>expands the powers and duties of the authority;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the appointment of the river commissioner;<hr><ltbullet>repeals provision prohibiting the river commissioner from receiving compensation;<hr><ltbullet>amends provision on hiring of the authority's executive director; <hr><ltbullet>repeals the Colorado River Authority Restricted Account; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: Uniform Commercial Code Modifications
description: This bill enacts provisions within Title 70A, Uniform Commercial Code.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends the scope of Title 70A, Chapter 2, Uniform Commercial Code - Sales, and Title 70A, Chapter 2a, Uniform Commercial Code - Leases;<hr><ltbullet>replaces certain references to "writing" with "record" in Title 70A, Uniform Commercial Code;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to a funds transfer;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to hybrid transactions;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions relating to the control of a controllable electronic record;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the discharge of an account debtor's obligation on a controllable account or controllable payment intangible;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the governing law for a controllable electronic record;<hr><ltbullet>provides where a branch of a bank is considered to be located for a choice of law provision;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to control of an electronic document of title;<hr><ltbullet>provides what does not qualify as a financial asset;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to a purchaser's control of a security entitlement;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to the control of a deposit account;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to the control of an electronic copy of a record evidencing chattel paper;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which a secured party has control of a controllable electronic record;<hr><ltbullet>provides a limitation on when a security interest does not attach;<hr><ltbullet>amends the duties of a secured party with control of collateral;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions governing perfection and priority of security interests in chattel paper, controllable accounts, controllable electronic records, and controllable payment intangibles;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to perfection by control;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions governing perfection by possession and control of chattel paper;<hr><ltbullet>amends the contents of a notification of disposition of collateral;<hr><ltbullet>enacts transitional provisions for the Uniform Commercial Code Amendments (2022); and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Development Planning and Coordination Amendments
description: This bill addresses economic development planning and programs within the Governor's Office of Economic Development.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>renames the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity to the Governor's Office of Economic Development;<hr><ltbullet>exempts the Governor's Office of Economic Development from procurement requirements related to the correctional industries division;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the duties of the executive director of the Governor's Office of Economic Development (executive director);<hr><ltbullet>establishes the Economic Development Council (council);<hr><ltbullet>describes the membership of the council;<hr><ltbullet>describes the duties of the council;<hr><ltbullet>establishes reporting requirements for the council;<hr><ltbullet>requires reports to the Economic Development and Workforce Services Interim Committee;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Insanity Defense Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions relating to the criminal defense of not guilty by reason of insanity.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies the circumstances under which a defendant may plead not guilty to a first degree or capital felony by reason of insanity;<hr><ltbullet>places the burden of proof on a defendant asserting a defense of not guilty by reason of insanity to a first degree or capital felony charge;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions relating to supervision, assessment, and release of a defendant committed to the Department of Health and Human Services after being found not guilty of a criminal offense by reason of insanity;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a judge presiding over the prosecution of an individual asserting the defense of not guilty by reason of insanity may exercise discretion in ordering the Department of Health and Human Services to conduct a mental examination of the defendant under certain circumstances; <hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Election Code Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions relating to elections.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>modifies voter registration forms and other forms to allow a voter to request, for future elections, whether the voter will receive a ballot by mail and whether the voter desires to return a ballot by mail;<hr><ltbullet>requires a voter to make a request described in the preceding paragraph at least every eight years;<hr><ltbullet>provides that, beginning in 2029, a voter:<hr><ltbullet1>will not receive a ballot by mail unless the voter makes a timely request to receive a ballot by mail; and<hr><ltbullet1>subject to certain exceptions, will not be permitted to return a ballot by mail unless the voter makes a timely request to return a ballot by mail;  <hr><ltbullet>provides that a voter may return a ballot to a ballot drop box only when the ballot drop box is attended by at least two poll workers;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements regarding the required number of drop boxes and the days and hours during which voters may return ballots to drop boxes;<hr><ltbullet>requires a voter who returns a ballot to a ballot drop box to first provide identification to a poll worker at the ballot drop box;<hr><ltbullet>describes the requirements for verification of identity at a ballot drop box;<hr><ltbullet>describes the requirements for returning a ballot by mail;<hr><ltbullet>describes requirements relating to voting a ballot;<hr><ltbullet>describes the requirements for returning a ballot to a polling place or voting at a polling place;<hr><ltbullet>extends emergency ballot provisions to an individual with a disability who is restricted in the individual's ability to travel from the individual's residence;<hr><ltbullet>modifies forms, voting requirements, and other provisions to conform with the provisions of this bill;<hr><ltbullet>creates a process for an individual to receive a voter registration form and voter registration information when purchasing a hunting or fishing license;<hr><ltbullet>describes the type of personal identifying information that must be redacted from certain political disclosure reports and provides civil and criminal penalties for publicly disclosing the information;<hr><ltbullet>modifies a provision relating to the frequency of an elections audit performed by the Office of the Legislative Auditor General; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill addresses medical records.

title: Transportation Modifications
description: This bill amends license plate provisions, repeals the clean vehicle program, amends distribution frequency for class B and class C road funding, and amends provisions related to local corridor preservation fund administration.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to local jurisdiction over real property as pertaining to commuter rail property;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the clean vehicle program;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms related to license plates;<hr><ltbullet>changes the process for the design and issuance of standard license plates;<hr><ltbullet>amends the process for redesign of standard license plate options;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to the visibility and readability of license plates, including replacement of faded license plates;<hr><ltbullet>changes the process for creation of a new special group license plate and eligibility of the sponsor;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Motor Vehicle Division to establish certain service fees related to license plate administration;<hr><ltbullet>provides a process to transfer control and revenue related to special group license plates;<hr><ltbullet>amends the design and approval process for special group license plates;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to the design review board, including duties and membership;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to the State Tax Commission's contract with a license plate designer;<hr><ltbullet>requires driver license and identification card designs to be approved by the design review board;<hr><ltbullet>amends certain duties of the Department of Transportation;<hr><ltbullet>amends rates related to the road usage charge program;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions related to privileged information pertaining to rail road safety responsibilities and coordination;<hr><ltbullet>provides flexibility in distribution frequency of class B and class C road funding; <hr><ltbullet>directs local corridor preservation funds to go directly to the relevant local government instead of passing through the Transportation Fund;<hr><ltbullet>modifies certain uses for local corridor preservation funds; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

description: This bill amends provisions related to social studies instructional materials and art standards.

title: Water Optimization Reporting Amendments
description: This bill creates a study related to agricultural water optimization.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Water Resources, in coordination with the Division of Water Rights, to study water diversions classified as an agricultural diversion to determine:<hr><ltbullet1>the number, type, and volume of diversions currently classified as an agricultural diversion; and<hr><ltbullet1>the volume of water diverted from an agricultural diversion for non-agricultural use;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Water Resources to report the results of the study to the Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Interim Committee before November 30, 2026; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: State Highway Designation Amendments
description: This bill creates a process and standards for the special designation of state highways.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides standards and a process for the proposal of a special designation of a highway;<hr><ltbullet>provides limitations on multiple designations for the same individual, or multiple designations on the same highway;<hr><ltbullet>allows special designations by the Legislature to apply only to state highways;<hr><ltbullet>limits designations to proposals to honor an individual who has been deceased for at least five years;<hr><ltbullet>creates a committee for review of the special designation proposals;<hr><ltbullet>limits special designations to one per year; and<hr><ltbullet>provides standards for the highway signage for a special designation.

title: Transportation, Infrastructure, and Housing Amendments
description: This bill modifies transportation, infrastructure, and housing provisions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates the State Housing Infrastructure Partnership Fund (fund) and provides for the use of fund money;<hr><ltbullet>creates the State Housing Infrastructure Partnership Board (infrastructure loan board) and describes the infrastructure loan board's membership and duties;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity to provide staff support to the infrastructure loan board;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the infrastructure loan board to make loans from the fund to qualifying political subdivisions to finance system improvements that will facilitate the construction of housing;<hr><ltbullet>establishes terms and requirements for infrastructure loans awarded by the infrastructure loan board;<hr><ltbullet>directs the state treasurer to complete a study that analyzes the economic effect of the infrastructure loan program;<hr><ltbullet>exempts conduct arising from the provision of affordable housing, if the housing benefits are provided to all qualified residents, from certain ethics requirements for public officers;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the membership of the Affordable Housing Infrastructure Grant Board (grant board) for the provision of affordable housing infrastructure grants;<hr><ltbullet>limits to owner-occupied the affordable housing for which public entities in certain counties may qualify for an affordable housing infrastructure grant;<hr><ltbullet>allows the grant board, in relation to awarding affordable housing infrastructure grants, to:<hr><ltbullet1>determine whether an owner-occupied dwelling qualifies as an affordable housing unit; and<hr><ltbullet1>waive certain preliminary cost estimate requirements;<hr><ltbullet>increases the maximum amount of bonds the Utah Department of Transportation (department) may authorize for affordable housing infrastructure grants;<hr><ltbullet>allows the department to use certain local option sales tax revenue to pay for affordable housing infrastructure grants, subject to repayment from bond proceeds;<hr><ltbullet>diverts a certain portion of revenue from the County of the First Class Highway Projects Fund for revitalization of a convention center;<hr><ltbullet>establishes expenditure requirements for revenue in the County of the First Class Highway Projects Fund;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements in relation to a public transit hub project for the Cottonwood Canyons;<hr><ltbullet>reduces the amount of revenue the department may allocate from the Transportation Investment Fund to pay for a certain roadway project;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the Convention Center Reserves Restricted Account (account);<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Finance to transfer a certain amount of revenue from the Transportation Investment Fund to the account;<hr><ltbullet>limits the use of money deposited into the account for revitalization of a convention center;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for the department to coordinate and assist on certain projects, subject to availability of funding;<hr><ltbullet>allows state agencies to sell surplus real property at pre-entitlement appraised value to certain qualifying entities and defer payment for the purchase of such property;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the sale or disposal of real property by the department and other state agencies; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Capital Felony Case Amendments
description: This bill amends statutes related to capital felony cases.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines and modifies terms related to capital felony cases;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the statutory provisions regarding a sentencing proceeding in a capital felony case;<hr><ltbullet>requires the sentencing court to advise a defendant in a capital felony case of the right to a direct appeal and of the statutory provisions for postconviction relief;<hr><ltbullet>requires the sentencing court to appoint appellate counsel for a defendant who is sentenced to death;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the automatic review process by the Utah Supreme Court in a capital felony case in which the defendant is sentenced to death;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the priority of capital felony cases;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the extension of a report on a defendant's competency to stand trial;<hr><ltbullet>allows for the appointment of a psychologist to determine if a defendant is intellectually disabled when a prosecutor intends to seek a sentence of death;<hr><ltbullet>modifies statutory provisions regarding the pretrial process for determining whether an individual is intellectually disabled and not subject to a sentence of death;<hr><ltbullet> allows for an appeal of an order determining whether a defendant is intellectually disabled and not subject to a sentence of death;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies statutes regarding the execution of a sentence of death;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the requirements for a stay or suspension of a sentence of death and for an order of execution;<hr><ltbullet>modifies statutory provisions regarding a notification of pregnancy or incompetency of an inmate who is sentenced to death;<hr><ltbullet>addresses a petition for an inquiry on whether a defendant is competent to be executed, including the requirements for a successive petition;<hr><ltbullet>amends the examination process for a petition to determine whether an inmate is competent to be executed; <hr><ltbullet>addresses the procedures when there is a finding of competency or incompetency for an inmate sentenced to death;<hr><ltbullet>amends the subject matter jurisdiction of the Utah Supreme Court and the district court with regard to a capital felony case;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Utah Supreme Court, after a direct appeal, appoint defense counsel to represent an individual sentenced to death on a petition for postconviction relief;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Utah Supreme Court to maintain a list of qualified defense counsel for purposes of appointing defense counsel for an individual sentenced to death on a petition for postconviction relief;<hr><ltbullet>increases the amount of attorney fees and litigation expenses that a court may authorize for a petition for postconviction relief in a death penalty case;<hr><ltbullet>repeals a statute pertaining to capital cases; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: School Attendance Modifications
description: This bill creates citizenship grade standards, attendance-based grading, and a test-out option for core classes.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>permits and establishes requirements for standardizing citizenship grades; <hr><ltbullet>allows parents to opt out of citizenship grading;<hr><ltbullet>allows attendance-based grading; <hr><ltbullet>repeals individualized attendance plans for attendance-based grading; <hr><ltbullet>creates a test-out option for core classes; <hr><ltbullet>establishes a citizenship grade scholarship program in higher education funded through voluntary tax return contributions; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Vehicle Tax and Fee Amendments
description: This bill reclassifies certain taxes and fees and reorganizes vehicle tax and fee provisions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>reclassifies certain taxes and fees related to vehicles and vehicle registration, designating service fees, regulatory fees, and vehicle taxes;<hr><ltbullet>reorganizes code related to the imposition of vehicle taxes and fees;<hr><ltbullet>reorganizes the distribution of revenue related to vehicle taxes and fees;<hr><ltbullet>creates a new restricted account for deposits from vehicle regulatory fees and funding for the Motor Vehicle Division;<hr><ltbullet>removes the option for a six-month registration;<hr><ltbullet>removes the annual adjustment of certain vehicle taxes and fees due to inflation; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: State Coordination of Regional and Local Economic Development Projects Amendments
description: This bill addresses local and regional economic development projects and related provisions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a political subdivision from providing an incentive to a large load data center, with exceptions;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the State Reinvestment Restricted Account (account);<hr><ltbullet>describes the potential uses for money in the account;<hr><ltbullet>directs the Utah Inland Port Authority to deposit certain revenues into the account;<hr><ltbullet>modifies certain requirements for a public infrastructure district;<hr><ltbullet>provides a process for the dissolution of a public infrastructure district;<hr><ltbullet>requires the disclosure of the expected annual cost of a public infrastructure district's certified tax rate, as shown on the last equalized assessment rolls, in the conveyance of residential real property, if applicable;<hr><ltbullet>creates the optional County Energy Excise Tax;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Tax Commission to deposit revenue, in certain circumstances, into the account;<hr><ltbullet>provides that certain records related to economic development projects, including nondisclosure agreements, may be classified as protected records;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the process for a person providing a record to a governmental entity to make a claim of confidentiality regarding the record;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions governing the sharing of a protected record;<hr><ltbullet>requires the risk manager to make rules to establish the limit of liability for damages from the intentional disclosure of a protected record;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a housing and transit reinvestment zone, first home investment zone, convention center reinvestment zone, or home ownership promotion zone may not be created after January 1, 2028;<hr><ltbullet>provides retrospective operation for certain provisions governing a housing and transit reinvestment zone, first home investment zone, and convention center reinvestment zone to May 4, 2022;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Political Subdivisions Interim Committee to create a working group and describes the membership of the working group;<hr><ltbullet>creates a process for a county or city to propose a regionally significant development zone (zone) and for a committee to approve the creation of a zone;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a zone to capture and utilize certain forms of tax increment;<hr><ltbullet>describes how a zone will be managed, including how a community reinvestment agency (agency) will manage zone funds, prepare zone budgets, conduct zone audits, and make biennial reports;<hr><ltbullet>describes the circumstances in which an agency or a county treasurer shall transfer a percentage of zone revenue into the account;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the prohibition on local government offering a financial incentive for an energy development project outside an electrical energy development zone; <hr><ltbullet>coordinates this bill with H.B. 475, Development Planning and Coordination Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: State Facilities Modifications
description: This bill addresses state facilities.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes the Higher Education Appropriations Subcommittee as the subcommittee to hear and prioritize requests for state funding of capital facility projects within the Utah System of Higher Education;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for the proposal of a technical college or degree-granting institution for a capital facility project funding request;<hr><ltbullet>requires compliance with the dedicated and non-dedicated project approval process for higher education capital facility projects;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the process for requesting capital development appropriations by distinguishing between architectural programming and design-and-construction phases;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes an agency to request funding for architectural programming without requiring the submission of a feasibility study;<hr><ltbullet>requires an agency to complete architectural programming before requesting an appropriation for the design and construction of a capital development project; <hr><ltbullet>increases, from $100,000 to $1,500,000, the maximum project cost for which a state entity may directly supervise the design and construction of a state facility and establishes higher supervisory thresholds for certain institutions within the Utah System of Higher Education;<hr><ltbullet>requires a state entity that elects to directly supervise the design and construction of a state facility project to enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Division of Facilities Construction and Management (division) that addresses compliance with division standards;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a state entity described above from accessing the division's statewide contingency reserve or project reserve for the state facility project;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the director of the division to assume control of a project described above when division inspection or review determines that the work is deficient or noncompliant with division design, construction, or code inspection standards;<hr><ltbullet>aligns revocation authority for delegated projects by allowing the director of the division to revoke delegation to address inspection-based deficiencies; <hr><ltbullet>requires that design criteria exceeding the state construction code to be appropriate for the facility's intended use and cost-effective over the facility's expected useful life;<hr><ltbullet>adds required components to a capital development feasibility study by requiring inclusion of a space utilization plan and capital budget estimate approved by the division;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Legislature to transfer any excess amount from the statewide contingency reserve to the General Fund or the Income Tax Fund;<hr><ltbullet>if the excess amount described above is attributable to a higher education or technical college capital project, requires the Legislature to transfer the excess amount to the applicable capital project fund;<hr><ltbullet>requires the division to submit an annual request for appropriation to the Legislature for each year covered by the five-year building plan;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the director of the division to approve certain design modifications for capital development projects of institutions of higher education and to allocate resulting construction cost savings between the institution and the state;<hr><ltbullet>exempts construction contracts administered by the division from statutory performance and payment bond requirements;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the division to require a performance or payment bond when necessary to protect the division from financial loss or performance risk; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill creates a study related to wetlands.

title: Municipal Incorporation Modifications
description: This bill modifies the process to incorporate as a preliminary municipality.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the lieutenant governor's office to charge and collect a fee;<hr><ltbullet>modifies uses of the Municipal Incorporation Expendable Special Revenue Fund;<hr><ltbullet>requires an applicant to engage in good faith coordination with a county for 18 months before the applicant may file a feasibility request as part of an application to incorporate an area as a preliminary municipality, with an exception;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the process for a person to apply to incorporate an area as a preliminary municipality;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a sponsor and a county to submit data, information, and analysis to the feasibility consultant evaluating a proposed preliminary municipality;<hr><ltbullet>requires the feasibility consultant to rely on data, information, and analysis that is objective, reliable, and grounded in area-specific information from the preceding 10 years, including information from nearby areas;<hr><ltbullet>extends the period of time in which a feasibility study shall be completed;<hr><ltbullet>requires the lieutenant governor to hold public information sessions following a feasibility study;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the requirements to file a petition for incorporation of a preliminary municipality, including:<hr><ltbullet1>modifying the requirements for a bond, cash deposit, or letter of credit;<hr><ltbullet1>requiring a property owner to include an executed improvement warranty; and<hr><ltbullet1>requiring a certification that the preliminary municipality will be developed in accordance with the description in the certified feasibility request; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Procurement Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions of Title 63G, Chapter 6a, Utah Procurement Code.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines the term "resident supplier";<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the rulemaking authority for a procurement unit to make rules governing small purchases that encourage procurements from resident suppliers over non-resident suppliers;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the process to create an approved vendor list;<hr><ltbullet>requires the rulemaking authority to create a procedure to ensure vendors on an approved vendor list that are resident suppliers have increased opportunity to compete for a contract for a procurement item in comparison to non-resident suppliers on the approved vendor list;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a procurement unit shall give a preference to bidders that certify on the bid that the bidder qualifies as a resident supplier; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill modifies provisions involving land surveyors.

title: Attorney General Funding Amendments
description: This bill addresses funding for the Office of the Attorney General.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet> exempts the Office of the Attorney General (office) from the provisions governing internal service funds with respect to charges for legal services the office provides to an agency;<hr><ltbullet>provides that when the office charges an agency for legal services, the office shall calculate the charge based on the actual time spent on the legal services;<hr><ltbullet>requires the office and each agency to annually agree on a retainer amount to be included in the governor's proposed budget that represents the total anticipated cost of the agency's legal services for the upcoming fiscal year;<hr><ltbullet>after the Legislature appropriates each agency's retainer, directs the office and each agency to execute a service-level agreement that includes the agency's expected legal services needs, the rates at which the office will charge for the legal services, and specified information about the money used to pay for the legal services;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the Legal Services Retainer Fund into which each agency will transfer the agency's retainer;<hr><ltbullet>allows the office to use money in the Legal Services Retainer Fund to pay for the legal services that the office charges to each agency during the fiscal year;<hr><ltbullet>requires an agency to use the agency's existing budget to pay for any legal services charges that exceed the agency's balance in the Legal Services Retainer Fund; <hr><ltbullet>creates the Legal Services and Litigation Program to pay costs of defending the state in civil litigation that meets specified criteria;<hr><ltbullet>provides that appropriations made to the Legal Services and Litigation Program are nonlapsing; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Utah Energy Council Amendments
description: This bill creates the Utah Energy Infrastructure Service District and modifies provisions relating to the Utah Energy Council.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; <hr><ltbullet>expands the Utah Energy Council (council) membership from five to seven members; <hr><ltbullet>establishes a co-chair structure for council leadership; <hr><ltbullet>designates the council as a state energy financing institution;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Utah Energy Infrastructure Service District (district) as a political subdivision of the state; <hr><ltbullet>provides that council members serve concurrently as the board of trustees of the district; <hr><ltbullet>authorizes the district to acquire, own, and operate energy infrastructure facilities within a designated service area; <hr><ltbullet>authorizes the district to issue revenue bonds payable solely from district revenues and not subject to the state constitutional debt limitation;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Finance Review Commission to review and approve district revenue bonds before issuance;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Energy Infrastructure Enterprise Fund; <hr><ltbullet>authorizes the district to enter into operating contracts with private operators for district-owned facilities; <hr><ltbullet>exempts district property from taxation and subjects operators to the privilege tax; <hr><ltbullet>provides for dissolution of the district by the board or by an act of the Legislature; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill establishes the Graduate Student Supplemental Revolving Loan Fund to provide supplemental financial aid to certain graduate students.

title: Landlord Communication Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to unlawful detainer.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that if a renter believes a residential rental unit has a deficient condition, the renter shall inform the owner;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a renter may take commercially reasonable steps to correct a deficient condition in a residential rental unit;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to an owner's duty to return to the renter a security deposit and prepaid rent;<hr><ltbullet>provides that if an owner takes substantial action to correct a deficient condition before receiving a notice of deficient condition, the owner satisfies the owner's duties to correct the deficient condition;<hr><ltbullet>extends the corrective period for a standard of habitability;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to the notice of a dangerous condition or notice of a deficient condition;<hr><ltbullet>provides that if an owner believes that a renter's residential rental unit is not habitable an owner may terminate a rental agreement;<hr><ltbullet>provides the notice requirements for an owner that terminates a rental agreement after determining that a residential rental unit is not habitable;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a renter is guilty of unlawful detainer if a renter remains on the premises of a residential rental unit after an owner terminates a rental agreement;<hr><ltbullet>provides that if an owner terminates a rental agreement after determining that a residential rental unit is not habitable does not waive the owner's other claims;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends the circumstances under which a tenant is guilty of unlawful detainer;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a tenant is guilty of unlawful detainer if an animal under control of the tenant engages in certain acts;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a tenant is guilty of unlawful detainer if the tenant violates a provision of the lease agreement that the lease agreement designates as an incurable violation; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: School Curriculum Amendments
description: This bill modifies requirements for social studies education in elementary and secondary schools.

title: Unclaimed Property Modifications
description: This bill modifies the Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes standards for the unclaimed property administrator's (administrator's) custody of digital assets presumed abandoned, including requirements for:<hr><ltbullet1>the presumption of abandonment for digital assets;<hr><ltbullet1>the delivery of abandoned digital assets to the administrator's custody;<hr><ltbullet1>the sale or liquidation of abandoned digital assets by the holder at the direction of the administrator;<hr><ltbullet1>the maintenance of abandoned digital assets by the holder if delivery is not possible; and<hr><ltbullet1>the sale or liquidation of abandoned digital assets by the administrator; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Public Education Economic Stabilization Restricted Account Amendments
description: This bill requires the appropriation of a certain amount of funds in the Public Education Economic Stabilization Restricted Account to a new trust fund for public education.

description: This bill requires a school district to report open enrollment data to the State Board of Education (state board) and requires the state board to publish that data.

description: This bill provides for the election of a secretary of state in the 2028 regular general election and transfers most of the duties,currently assigned by statute to the lieutenant governor to the secretary of state.

title: State Permitting Council
description: This bill creates a permitting coordinator within the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; <hr><ltbullet>creates a permitting coordinator within the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity (office), appointed by the executive director of the office;<hr><ltbullet>establishes duties for the permitting coordinator, including serving as a central point of contact for projects or activities requiring one or more state permits, providing permitting information and guidance, and facilitating coordination among state, federal, and tribal entities;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the permitting coordinator to work with governmental entities to identify administrative and legislative changes that may improve the efficiency, transparency, and predictability of state permitting;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the permitting coordinator does not have the authority to issue, approve, deny, or modify a permit;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the permitting coordinator to share information with state, federal, tribal, and local governmental entities on permitting matters;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the permitting coordinator's activities and sharing of information with other governmental entities does not obligate the state or a permitting agency to approve a permit or enter into a binding agreement; and<hr><ltbullet>requires the office to include, in the office's annual report, a summary of the permitting coordinator's assistance and coordination activities and any recommendations for administrative or legislative changes to improve state permitting.

title: Student Health and Wellbeing Amendments
description: This bill creates the School-based Behavioral Health Pilot Program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a report upon request;<hr><ltbullet>creates the School-based Behavioral Health Pilot Program (program) to award program funds to an implementation partner to:<hr><ltbullet1>implement a multi-tiered system of mental health support; and<hr><ltbullet1>enhance mental health in schools;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Health and Human Services to:<hr><ltbullet1>solicit proposals to participate in the program;<hr><ltbullet1> coordinate the implementation of the program with another, similar grant program;<hr><ltbullet1>enter into a contract or memorandum of understanding with certain entities to administer the program; and<hr><ltbullet1>distribute program funds;<hr><ltbullet>requires a local education agency (LEA) or regional education service agency (RESA) participating in the program to:<hr><ltbullet1>contract with an implementation partner;<hr><ltbullet1>comply with certain requirements; and<hr><ltbullet1>submit an application to the Department of Health and Human Services;<hr><ltbullet>requires an implementation partner to:<hr><ltbullet1>contract with and provide certain support to a participating LEA or RESA;<hr><ltbullet1>use program funds for certain eligible initiatives; and<hr><ltbullet1>support the implementation of the program;<hr><ltbullet>creates a repeal date for the program; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Firearm Immunity Amendments
description: This bill addresses immunity for certain firearm discharges.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>grants governmental immunity for an injury or damage resulting from a firearm discharge by an individual when firearm possession is allowed on government-owned, leased, or controlled property in accordance with law, policy, or practice;<hr><ltbullet>creates an exception to the immunity described above if the governmental entity or the governmental entity's officers or employees affirmatively encourage or aid a firearm discharge for an unlawful purpose;<hr><ltbullet>expands the class of tenants who are immune from liability for injury or harm resulting from a firearm discharge by an individual on the tenant's property by amending the definition of "property occupant" to:<hr><ltbullet1>remove the requirement that the property be privately owned; and<hr><ltbullet1>include legal entities, rather than only an individual, who has the right to occupy property under an agreement; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Disposition of Public Property Modifications
description: This bill deals with the disposition of certain publicly owned property.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms and modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>provides a process for a local governmental entity to dispose of public property;<hr><ltbullet>requires a local governmental entity to determine if public property constitutes a significant parcel;<hr><ltbullet>requires the governing body of a local governmental entity to approve the disposal of a significant parcel in a public meeting;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a local governmental entity shall comply with statutory provisions specific to the type of local governmental entity in addition to the provisions of Title 11, Chapter 1, Part 2, Disposal of Public Property, when disposing of public property, subject to certain exemptions;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a school district to sell surplus property in accordance with Title 11, Chapter 1, Part 2, Disposal of Public Property, if no eligible entity purchases the surplus property within a certain time period; <hr><ltbullet>repeals a criminal penalty; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Criminal Conduct on Public Lands Amendments
description: This bill concerns criminal conduct on public lands.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Public Lands Restoration and Protection Fund (fund) to be administered by the State Historic Preservation Office;<hr><ltbullet>amends the criminal offense of defacing by graffiti on public lands, including to add conduct involving natural and archaeological features;<hr><ltbullet>amends penalty provisions for certain criminal violations of the offense of antiquities alteration, removal, injury, or destruction;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a court may order criminal restitution to be deposited into the fund for a violation of:<hr><ltbullet1>defacing by graffiti, damage, or destruction on public lands; or<hr><ltbullet1>antiquities alteration, removal, injury, or destruction, if the violation is on state lands; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Public Safety Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions related to public safety.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies the venue for a criminal action;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the definition of cohabitant for the battered person mitigation statute;<hr><ltbullet>defines and modifies terms related to domestic violence, including expanding the definition of a domestic violence offense;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the right to bail for a domestic violence offense;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies a term regarding a predominant aggressor when a law enforcement officer is responding to multiple incidents of domestic violence;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the requirements for responding to an allegation of a domestic violence offense;<hr><ltbullet>amends the appearance requirements for a domestic violence offense;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies and amends definitions for protective order statutes, including the definition of cohabitant;<hr><ltbullet>amends the requirements for a workplace violence protective order;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a jail release agreement may not prohibit an individual arrested or cited for the commission of domestic violence in the presence of a child from communicating with a minor child in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a parent from waiving the conditions of a jail release agreement when the minor child is the alleged victim and the parent was arrested or cited for the qualifying offense;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to modify a definition if this bill and H.B. 221, Coercion Amendments, both pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to modify a definition if this bill and H.B. 90, Sexual Offenses Amendments, both pass and become law.

description: This bill addresses public access to court records and proceedings and judicial financial disclosures.

title: Budgetary Modifications
description: This bill modifies provisions related to public funds.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>changes the name of:<hr><ltbullet1>the Agriculture Conservation Easement Account; and<hr><ltbullet1>the LeRay McAllister Working Farm and Ranch Fund;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the following accounts and funds, including related references:<hr><ltbullet1>the Navajo Water Rights Negotiation Account;<hr><ltbullet1>the Conversion to Alternative Fuel Grant Program Fund, including the Conversion to Alternative Fuel Grant Program;<hr><ltbullet1>the Wildlife Resources Conservation Easement Account;<hr><ltbullet1>the Wild Game Meat Donation Fund; and<hr><ltbullet1>the Colorado River Authority Restricted Account;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the permissible uses of funds in the Department of Public Safety Restricted Account;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that an agency that administers a state grant on another agency's behalf shall comply with the applicable grant requirements;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the state auditor may audit grant funds in accordance with the state auditor's authority;<hr><ltbullet>for a direct award grant, prohibits an administering agency from using grant funds to administer the grant, unless otherwise provided in the grant appropriation's intent language;<hr><ltbullet>modifies certain reporting requirements for a competitive grant;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a member of the Board of Examiners is disqualified from reviewing a line item overexpenditure report if the line item is part of the member's office's budget;<hr><ltbullet>allows an agency to expend up to 100% of the dedicated credits revenue that the agency receives in excess of the amount appropriated, if the dedicated credits are appropriated to a specified type of fund;<hr><ltbullet>amends the administration of the Industrial Assistance Account (account) by:<hr><ltbullet1>replacing the annual transfer to the account with an annual set aside; and<hr><ltbullet1>directing the GOEO board to make recommendations to the administrator regarding applications for loans, grants, or other financial assistance from the account;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the state auditor's authority related to:<hr><ltbullet1>expenses and personnel; and<hr><ltbullet1>performing audits of funds and accounts to determine compliance with the law;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Energy Development Infrastructure Fund to make loans to public entities to finance infrastructure development that supports nuclear power generation and transmission in the state;<hr><ltbullet>changes the Electrical Energy Development Investment Fund from an expendable special revenue fund to a special revenue fund and makes appropriations from the fund nonlapsing;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the permissible uses of the Electrical Energy Development Investment Fund;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes; and<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause that makes technical changes if this bill and H.B. 473, Colorado River Authority Amendments, both pass and become law.

title: Public Lands Duty of Care Amendments
description: This bill addresses the jurisdictional management of public lands.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>asserts the state's jurisdictional interest in land controlled by the federal government under a proprietary interest;<hr><ltbullet>directs the Public Lands Policy Coordinating Office (office) to promote the state's jurisdictional interests on landscape-scale public lands; <hr><ltbullet>requires the office to:<hr><ltbullet1>identify and map landscape-scale lands in the state;<hr><ltbullet1>establish map layers for certain criteria on landscape-scale lands;<hr><ltbullet1> map a landscape public nuisance area on landscape-scale lands containing forested areas; and<hr><ltbullet1>report annually on the map to the Federalism Commission;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Forestry, Fire, and State Lands to assist the office in identifying a landscape public nuisance area for landscape-scale lands containing forested areas; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Transnational Repression Amendments
description: This bill addresses transnational repression by foreign governments and foreign terrorist organizations against individuals in this state.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms, including transnational repression;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Utah Board of Higher Education to direct the state's institutions of higher education to provide information on transnational repression to international students and how to report transnational repression to law enforcement;   <hr><ltbullet>creates a criminal penalty enhancement for any crime if the crime is committed by an individual at the direction of a foreign government or an agent of a foreign terrorist organization in order to cause a victim to undertake, or refrain from undertaking, certain conduct; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Primary Election Amendments
description: This bill addresses primary elections.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that a municipality may hold a primary election if the number of candidates for a municipal office exceeds twice but does not exceed three times the number of individuals needed to fill that office;<hr><ltbullet>requires a municipality to hold a primary election if the number of candidates for a municipal office exceeds three times the number of individuals needed to fill that office;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the circumstances under which a special district may hold a primary election; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Behavioral Health Amendments
description: This bill addresses provisions related to behavioral health.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>changes the entity that administers and reports on the Governor's Suicide Prevention Fund from the governor to the Office of Substance Use and Mental Health (office);<hr><ltbullet>creates a community-based peer support specialist grant program;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to individuals eligible for admission to the Utah State Hospital;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Health and Human Services (department) to maintain a database of involuntary commitments;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the office appoints the statewide suicide prevention coordinator;<hr><ltbullet>amends the duties of the Behavioral Health Commission (commission), including to add certain duties that were previously assigned to the Utah Substance Use and Mental Health Advisory Committee;<hr><ltbullet>changes the name of the Utah Substance Use and Mental Health Advisory Committee to the Utah Behavioral Health Policy Review Committee and amends the committee's duties and other related provisions;<hr><ltbullet>requires the commission's Legislative Policy Committee to form a working group to investigate and make recommendations to the Legislature regarding a statewide central authority for coordinating behavioral health initiatives;<hr><ltbullet>creates a family outreach specialist within the department to:<hr><ltbullet1>engage with the family of an individual who has recently died by suicide or overdose; and <hr><ltbullet1>assist the medical examiner with suicide intervention,  and postvention;<hr><ltbullet>makes changes to responsibilities related to the Underage Drinking Prevention Media and Education Campaign Restricted Account;<hr><ltbullet>amends the duties and membership of the Behavioral Health Crisis Response Committee;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill modifies provisions related to government debt collection.

title: Revisor's Technical Corrections to Utah Code
description: This bill makes technical corrections to the Utah Code.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies parts of the Utah Code to make technical corrections, including:<hr><ltbullet1>eliminating or correcting references involving repealed provisions;<hr><ltbullet1>eliminating redundant or obsolete language;<hr><ltbullet1>making minor wording changes;<hr><ltbullet1>updating cross-references; and<hr><ltbullet1>correcting numbering and other errors;<hr><ltbullet>amends the Sunset Act and the Repeal Dates by Title Act to repeal sunset and repeal dates that have passed and taken effect; and<hr><ltbullet>adds a coordination clause to subordinate changes in this bill that are in conflict with other legislation that passes during the 2026 General Session.

title: Elections Amendments
description: This bill requires the posting of certain information relating to a candidate for public office.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires an election officer to post the following information relating to a candidate for public office:<hr><ltbullet1>the name and campaign contact information of the candidate;<hr><ltbullet1>the office that the candidate is seeking; and<hr><ltbullet1>the political party affiliation of the candidate, regardless of whether the candidate is a candidate for partisan or nonpartisan office; and<hr><ltbullet>exempts a judge who is a candidate in a retention election from the provisions of this bill.

title: Ambulance Amendments
description: This bill enacts provisions relating to ambulance membership organizations.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that accident and health insurance does not include an ambulance membership contract;<hr><ltbullet>enacts Title 31A, Chapter 6c, Ambulance Membership Organizations;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an ambulance membership organization is exempt from certain chapters of Title 31A, Insurance;<hr><ltbullet>provides the powers and duties of the commissioner of the Insurance Department (commissioner) in relation to Title 31A, Chapter 6c, Ambulance Membership Organizations;<hr><ltbullet>provides the licensing requirements for an ambulance membership organization;<hr><ltbullet>provides the license renewal process for an ambulance membership organization;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an ambulance membership organization shall submit an annual report to the commissioner;<hr><ltbullet>provides requirements for an ambulance membership organization to maintain reserve funds and a surety bond;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an ambulance membership organization may charge a fee to a member of the ambulance membership organization;<hr><ltbullet>provides an ambulance membership organization's required disclosures to the ambulance membership organization's members;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for an ambulance membership contract;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an ambulance membership organization from selling, offering for sale, or providing an ambulance membership contract to an individual enrolled in Medicaid;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for an individual who purchases an ambulance membership contract and who subsequently enrolls in Medicaid;<hr><ltbullet>enacts marketing requirements and required disclosures for an ambulance membership organization;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the commissioner to revoke or suspend an ambulance membership organization's license;<hr><ltbullet>provides for penalties related to a violation of Title 31A, Chapter 6c, Ambulance Membership Organizations; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Use of Motorized Vehicles by Minors Amendments
description: This bill  addresses the use of mini-motorcycles and motorcycles.

title: Homeowners Insurance Amendments
description: This bill creates an independent state agency to provide real property insurance coverage when such coverage is not available from insurers.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet> enacts the Access to Insurance Plan Act;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Access to Insurance Plan Association as an independent state agency; <hr><ltbullet>requires each admitted insurer that writes property insurance in the state to participate in the association as a condition of transacting business;<hr><ltbullet>requires the association to establish and operate a residual market property insurance plan (fair plan);<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the fair plan to provide residential and commercial property insurance when coverage is not available in the admitted market;<hr><ltbullet>establishes governance of the association by a board of directors that the governor appoints;<hr><ltbullet>requires the board to adopt and submit a plan of operation to the insurance commissioner for approval;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for rates, underwriting standards, coverage limits, and policy forms under the fair plan; <hr><ltbullet>requires an applicant to demonstrate that at least three admitted insurers declined coverage before obtaining coverage through the fair plan;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the association to assess member insurers to fund startup costs and ongoing financial obligations;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes member insurers to recover certain assessments through policyholder surcharges;<hr><ltbullet>grants the insurance commissioner oversight, enforcement authority, and rulemaking authority; and<hr><ltbullet>provides for judicial review of final administrative actions.

title: Radon Amendments
description: This bill creates a new section in the Utah Construction Trades Licensing Act governing radon mitigation.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires a person that installs, repairs, maintains, cleans, or replaces a radon mitigation system to complete training and certification;<hr><ltbullet>requires an individual who sells radon mitigation or vents a radon mitigation system to complete training and certification;<hr><ltbullet>requires an employer to ensure that an employee performing radon mitigation work obtains required training and certification before performing that work; and<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the division to exempt an individual from certification requirements if the individual works under direct one-to-one supervision of a certified professional.

title: Health Care Transparency Amendments
description: This bill addresses transparency in the Medicaid program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Integrated Healthcare (division) to maintain a dashboard of certain Medicaid data;<hr><ltbullet>requires the division to publish certain data and reports on the division's website;<hr><ltbullet>requires certain participants in the Medicaid program to:<hr><ltbullet1> identify, report on, and repay improper payments; and<hr><ltbullet1>develop corrective action plans to address improper payments;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Health and Human Services (department) to publish reports of improper payments and corrective action plans on the department's website;<hr><ltbullet>provides rulemaking authority, including for sanctions for violations of the provisions of this bill;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Outdoor Recreational Infrastructure Grant Program Amendments
