title: Immigrant Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions concerning immigrants and immigration.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a Utah depository institution from accepting certain forms of identification;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Financial Institutions to make rules to ensure compliance with and enforcement of the identification prohibition for a Utah depository institution;<hr><ltbullet>for a licensee under the Money Transmitter Act:<hr><ltbullet1>prohibits a licensee from initiating an international money transmission unless the licensee has verified that the sender is not an unauthorized alien;<hr><ltbullet1>requires certain record keeping; and<hr><ltbullet1>imposes penalties for a violation;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Financial Institutions to conduct random quarterly audits of licensees under the Money Transmitter Act to ensure compliance;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a person from hiring or employing an unauthorized alien, and provides penalties for a violation, including fines and business license suspension or revocation;<hr><ltbullet>creates a right of action against a person who hired, employed, or recruited an unauthorized alien and the actions of the unauthorized alien caused an injury or death;<hr><ltbullet>upon request from a federal immigration agency, requires a sheriff, or sheriff's designee who operates a county jail, to provide:<hr><ltbullet1>a list of all prisoners who are held at the county jail; and <hr><ltbullet1>information regarding each prisoner's immigration status;<hr><ltbullet>exempts an adult unauthorized alien from the definition of "employee" for purposes of the Workers' Compensation Act;<hr><ltbullet>requires an employer who knowingly hires or employs an unauthorized alien to be personally liable for all medical and treatment costs resulting from an injury sustained by the unauthorized alien during the unauthorized alien's employment, and imposes fines and other penalties;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Industrial Accidents to investigate and enforce violations involving an unauthorized alien injured during employment;<hr><ltbullet>requires an employer to verify an employee's employment eligibility through the federal status verification system before submitting a claim for workers' compensation for the employee, and if the employer fails to do so, the employer is:<hr><ltbullet1>ineligible to receive indemnity or medical coverage from the employer's workers' compensation insurance provider for the employee's injuries; and<hr><ltbullet1>personally liable for all costs, expenses, and benefits that would have been covered;<hr><ltbullet>for purposes of the Uniform Commercial Driver License Act, requires the Driver License Division to:<hr><ltbullet1>require that all licensing procedures, testing, and instruction be in English; and<hr><ltbullet1>prohibit the use of an interpreter or other alternative language accommodations;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the risk manager from adjusting, settling, or paying a claim relating to an adult unauthorized alien; <hr><ltbullet>requires an agency or political subdivision to verify the lawful presence of an adult who applies for:<hr><ltbullet1>a license or certification issued under Title 13, Commerce and Trade, Title 31A, Insurance Code, Title 58, Occupations and Professions, or Title 61, Securities Division - Real Estate Division; or<hr><ltbullet1>assistance as a first-time home buyer under the First-Time Homebuyer Assistance Program;<hr><ltbullet>restricts the definition of "first-time homebuyer" to an individual who is lawfully present in the United States for purposes of the First-Time Homebuyer Assistance Program;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a state or local governmental agency may not limit the authority of certain agencies from assisting the federal government in certain aspects of federal immigration enforcement, including:<hr><ltbullet1>complying with an immigration detainer;<hr><ltbullet1>providing inmate and prisoner immigration status, release dates, and other information;<hr><ltbullet1>providing access to inmates and prisoners for an interview;<hr><ltbullet1>executing a judicial warrant; or<hr><ltbullet1>participating in a federal immigration operation with a federal immigration authority;<hr><ltbullet>requires a state or local governmental agency to use the agency's best efforts to support the enforcement of federal immigration law;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a state or local governmental agency from restricting a law enforcement officer from executing, or assisting with the execution of, a lawful judicial warrant;<hr><ltbullet>prevents, with certain exceptions, a state or local governmental agency from prohibiting a law enforcement agency from taking certain actions with regard to information concerning an individual's immigration status, including:<hr><ltbullet1>sending, receiving, and exchanging the information;<hr><ltbullet1>recording and maintaining the information;<hr><ltbullet1>using the information to comply with an immigration detainer;<hr><ltbullet1>using the information to confirm a detained individual's identity; or<hr><ltbullet1>providing certain prisoner information;<hr><ltbullet>if a state or local governmental agency violates certain immigration-related requirements, provides that:<hr><ltbullet1>the attorney general may investigate and file suit to seek declaratory or injunctive relief; <hr><ltbullet1>for an officer subject to impeachment, the violation may result in impeachment; and<hr><ltbullet1>for an officer subject to removal from office by judicial proceeding, the violation may result in removal from office; <hr><ltbullet>requires a law enforcement agency and magistrate or court to follow certain procedures regarding an immigration detainer;<hr><ltbullet>provides that if a state or local governmental agency adopts an ordinance, regulation, rule, or other policy of refusing to comply with, or directing officials, employees, or others to refuse to comply with, an immigration detainer:<hr><ltbullet1>the attorney general shall initiate an action to enforce compliance; and <hr><ltbullet1>a court, upon making certain findings, shall enjoin the application of the ordinance, rule, or other policy, and assess a civil fine;<hr><ltbullet>creates a new felony criminal offense for the unlawful employment of multiple unauthorized aliens; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Behavioral Health, Mental Health, and Social Services Amendments
description: This bill addresses social services interventions, including for behavioral health, mental health, and homelessness.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>changes the entity that administers and reports on the Governor's Suicide Prevention Fund from the governor to the Office of Substance Use and Mental Health (office);<hr><ltbullet>requires the Office of Licensing within the Department of Health and Human Services (department) to make rules related to a behavioral health receiving center's communication with prosecutors and law enforcement regarding a justice involved individual's participation in the behavioral health receiving center's treatment program;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department to provide a list of mental health and substance use disorder screening tools used in jails; <hr><ltbullet>requires the department to create a standard form for justice involved individuals to consent to disclosure of a mental health disorder or substance use disorder to certain persons, including health care providers, first responders, courts, local health authorities, county pretrial and parole services, and the Division of Adult Probation and Parole;<hr><ltbullet>permits first responders to provide an electronic list of local mental health services to certain individuals under certain circumstances; <hr><ltbullet>creates a community-based peer support specialist program;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to involuntary commitment and court ordered assisted outpatient treatment for mental illness;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department to maintain a database of involuntary commitments;<hr><ltbullet>amends the duties of the Behavioral Health Commission (commission), including adding certain duties that were previously assigned to the Utah Substance Use and Mental Health Advisory Committee;<hr><ltbullet>changes the name of the Utah Substance Use and Mental Health Advisory Committee to the Utah Behavioral Health Policy Review Committee and amends the committee's duties and other related provisions;<hr><ltbullet>requires the commission's Legislative Policy Committee to form a working group to investigate and make recommendations to the Legislature regarding a statewide central authority for coordinating behavioral health initiatives;<hr><ltbullet>creates a family outreach specialist within the department to:<hr><ltbullet1>engage with the family of an individual who has recently died by suicide or overdose; and<hr><ltbullet1> assist the medical examiner with suicide intervention, prevention, and postvention;<hr><ltbullet>permits a service provider to expand a congregate shelter's bed capacity limit under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>changes provisions related to participating local government tax revenue distributions for homeless shelters;<hr><ltbullet>makes changes to responsibilities related to the Underage Drinking Prevention Media and Education Campaign Restricted Account;<hr><ltbullet>amends the duties and membership of the Behavioral Health Crisis Response Committee;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill addresses statutory timelines in child welfare cases.

title: Guardianship and Conservatorship Resources Amendments
description: This bill addresses guardianship and conservatorship resources.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires local mental health authorities, the state protection and advocacy agency, and certain offices and divisions within the Department of Health and Human Services to provide information and referrals to resources related to guardianship and conservatorship to individuals that contact those entities;<hr><ltbullet>permits the Office of Public Guardian to provide training and assistance related to guardianship and conservatorship;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to an advance mental health care directive to include an individual's preferences regarding a person to serve as guardian for the individual;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Medicaid Funding Modifications
description: This bill addresses funding for Medicaid services.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>directs that interest earned on money in the Medicaid ACA Fund shall be deposited into:<hr><ltbullet1>the Division of Services for People with Disabilities Restricted Account; and<hr><ltbullet1>Medicaid Growth Reduction and Budget Stabilization Account, except in certain circumstances; <hr><ltbullet>directs money deposited into the Division of Services for People with Disabilities Restricted Account from the Medicaid ACA Fund to be used to provide services to eligible individuals who would otherwise remain on the Division of Services for People with Disabilities' waitlist for services; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Initiative and Referenda Signature Amendments
description: This bill creates a process to cure an initiative or referendum petition signature that is declared invalid.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes a process to cure a signature on an initiative or referendum petition that is declared invalid by a county clerk because the signature does not match the signature on file in the statewide voter registration database;<hr><ltbullet>requires a county clerk to notify an individual described above when the county clerk determines that the individual's signature does not match the signature on file;<hr><ltbullet>allows the individual to cure the invalid signature by delivering to the county clerk a signed affidavit attesting to the validity of the signature;<hr><ltbullet>establishes deadlines related to the processes described above; and<hr><ltbullet>provides that a county clerk may not count the individual's signature as valid unless the affidavit is timely received.

title: State Employee Leave Amendments
description: This bill modifies retirement benefits for state employees.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes the Unused Sick Leave Retirement Option Program III (Program III) for state employees;<hr><ltbullet>provides that, under Program III, a state employee employed on or after January 4, 2014, receives a payment equal to 50% of the value of the employee's unused sick leave hours, calculated at the employee's rate of pay at the time of retirement;<hr><ltbullet>allows a state employee with unused Program I or Program II sick leave hours to make a one-time, irrevocable election to convert those hours to Program III sick leave hours eligible for the 50% payment described above; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Child Therapy Amendments
description: This bill addresses continuity of mental health treatment and services for children in, and leaving, the custody of the Division of Child and Family Services.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires certain insurers to offer a single case agreement to allow certain children leaving the custody of the Division of Child and Family Services (division) to receive mental health treatment and services from the mental health therapist providing those services while the child was in the custody of the division;<hr><ltbullet>requires the division to, under certain circumstances:<hr><ltbullet1>determine whether a child entering the custody of the division has a mental health therapist, and facilitate continuity of care for the child with that mental health therapist; and<hr><ltbullet1>coordinate with a child's parent or guardian or the Department of Health and Human Services when a child leaves the custody of the division to facilitate continuity of care for the child with the therapist that provided mental health treatment and services while the child was in the custody of the department;<hr><ltbullet>provides rulemaking authority; and<hr><ltbullet>defines terms.

title: Nuisance Amendments
description: This bill addresses private and public nuisances.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>renumbers and repeals statutes in Title 47, Nuisances;<hr><ltbullet>modifies definitions for public nuisance crimes;<hr><ltbullet>repeals and renumbers statutes related to a civil action for a public nuisance;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers statutory provisions in Title 78B, Chapter 6, Part 11, Nuisance, to Title 78B, Chapter 6a, Civil Actions for Nuisances;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms related to public and private nuisances;<hr><ltbullet>abrogates the common law right of action for a public or private nuisance;<hr><ltbullet>provides an exception for the attorney general with regard to the abrogation of the common law civil right of action for a public or private nuisance;<hr><ltbullet>creates a reporting requirement for the Judiciary Interim Committee regarding the exception for the attorney general to the abrogation of the common law civil right of action for a public or private nuisance;<hr><ltbullet> creates rights of action for a public nuisance;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies and amends the right of action for a private nuisance;<hr><ltbullet>addresses defenses for private and public nuisance actions; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Municipal Incorporation Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to the incorporation of a preliminary municipality.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that:<hr><ltbullet1>a person may not apply to incorporate an area as a preliminary municipality after February 1, 2026; and<hr><ltbullet1>a person who applies to incorporate an area as a preliminary municipality by filing a feasibility request on or before February 1, 2026, may proceed in accordance with Title 10, Chapter 2a, Part 5, Incorporation of a Preliminary Municipality, after February 1, 2026;<hr><ltbullet>requires:<hr><ltbullet1>a proposed preliminary municipality to agree that initial landowners will fully compensate the county for damages to county property or infrastructure before the preliminary municipality can transition into a town;<hr><ltbullet1>a preliminary municipality to comply with terms, conditions, or restrictions that were established in a development agreement between the initial landowners and the county before the feasibility request was filed; and<hr><ltbullet1>that a petition to transition a preliminary municipality into a town shall certify that damages to county property or infrastructure have been paid in full; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Homelessness Amendments
description: This bill addresses provisions regarding homeless services.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies and defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends exceptions for conveyance, lease, or disposal of certain property owned by the Division of Facilities Construction and Management with the consent of the governing body of the municipality in which the property is located;<hr><ltbullet>provides funds received from a lease may be used for the operations and maintenance of the leased space;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Mitigation Fund Task Force; <hr><ltbullet>amends the name of the Shelter Cities Advisory Board to the Shelter Cities Coordinating Council;<hr><ltbullet>amends the name of the Shelter Counties Advisory Board to the Shelter Counties Coordinating Council;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding code blue alerts;<hr><ltbullet>permits the office to issue future services payments to a homeless service provider under certain conditions; <hr><ltbullet>creates the Homeless Services Restricted Account (account) to assist counties regarding provisions of homelessness;<hr><ltbullet>allows the office to disburse funds from the account to certain counties for certain purposes;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Tax Commission to transfer certain funds from the Cigarette Tax Restricted Account to the account;<hr><ltbullet>gives the office rulemaking authority under certain conditions for certain purposes; <hr><ltbullet>permits a service provider to expand the shelter's bed capacity limit under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes; and<hr><ltbullet>provides a special effective date.

title: Alcohol Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to alcohol.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Point of the Mountain State Land Authority is a local authority under Title 32B, Alcoholic Beverage Control Act;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a driver license issued by a foreign country or a driver license card is a valid proof of age;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions relating to the local consent of a local authority when the commission issues a license;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to a designated conveyance area;<hr><ltbullet>lowers the number of rooms for a facility to qualify as a hotel;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a restaurant licensee is only required to verify proof of age if the individual appears to be 35 years old or younger;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions requiring that a person verify whether an individual is an interdicted person;<hr><ltbullet>repeals requirements related to the scanning device a licensee shall use when verifying proof of age;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions to allow the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Services (department) to round up or round down the price of liquor when a customer pays with cash;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the department coordinate with law enforcement before beginning a disciplinary action;<hr><ltbullet>places the internal audit division of the department under the control of the director of the department;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Alcoholic Beverage Services Commission (commission) may propose internal audit policies and recommend changes to the division's internal audit plan;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to the commission's authority to deny a license;<hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement that a liquor storage area be locked at all times;<hr><ltbullet>provides the conditions under which a patron may transport an alcoholic beverage from a bar establishment to a restaurant establishment;<hr><ltbullet>amends the percentage requirement of alcohol to food that a licensee shall maintain;<hr><ltbullet>describes the language that the department shall require in each off-premise beer retailer display;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the department make a report to the Legislative Management Committee regarding the language the department requires that an off-premise beer retailer display;<hr><ltbullet>increases the number of reception center licenses that the commission may issue;<hr><ltbullet>removes the notice requirements relating to issuing an event permit;<hr><ltbullet>amends the definition of "beer"; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Uterine Fibroid Amendments
description: This bill addresses uterine fibroid research and education.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Health and Human Services (department) to coordinate research and education related to uterine fibroids;<hr><ltbullet>permits the department to coordinate with medical research organizations to carry out the department's research and education coordination efforts, including data sharing;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department to report to the Health and Human Services Interim Committee; <hr><ltbullet>provides a repeal date for research and education efforts, and related reporting requirements; <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes; and<hr><ltbullet>defines terms.

title: Social Services Funding Amendments
description: This bill addresses social services funding.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that interest earned on money in the Medicaid ACA Fund shall be deposited into the General Fund;<hr><ltbullet>requires immunosuppressive drugs to be added to the Medicaid preferred drug list;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Health and Human Services (department) to:<hr><ltbullet1> transition the state's Children's Health Insurance Program from a separate program, to providing benefits under the state's Medicaid program; and<hr><ltbullet1>after the transition, to the extent possible, provide dental services to individuals covered by the Children's Health Insurance Program through the University of Utah School of Dentistry;<hr><ltbullet>requires certain funds to be distributed from the Electronic Cigarette Substance and Nicotine Product Proceeds Restricted Account for substance use treatment and prevention services; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Local School Board Election Amendments
description: This bill moves the election of a local school board member to coincide with the municipal election dates in an odd-numbered year.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>moves a primary election for a local school board office to the date of a municipal primary election;<hr><ltbullet>moves a general election for a local school board office to the date of a municipal general election;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the declaration of candidacy period for a local school board office;<hr><ltbullet>extends the term of office of certain local school board members to effectuate the transition from elections held in even-numbered years to elections held in odd-numbered years; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: Surveillance and Investigatory Technology Amendments
description: This bill concerns the use of surveillance and investigatory technology.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes limitations on the ability of a law enforcement agency to use a surveillance or investigatory technology;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the exclusion of information obtained in violation of law in certain circumstances; <hr><ltbullet>creates a private right of action against a law enforcement agency for the law enforcement agency's prohibited use of a surveillance or investigatory technology, and waives governmental immunity for the private right of action;<hr><ltbullet>requires a law enforcement agency to annually report information concerning the law enforcement agency's use of certain technology to the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice (commission);<hr><ltbullet>requires the commission to annually collect and report information received from law enforcement agencies regarding the use of certain technology to the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee; <hr><ltbullet>creates a sunset review for the law enforcement agency technology data reporting requirements; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: House Concurrent Resolution on State Management of Federal Public Lands
description: This resolution urges the federal government and state entities to identify public lands for the state to manage for outdoor recreation.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>highlights the need to develop and maintain state parks, monuments, and campgrounds to provide the people of Utah with outdoor recreational opportunities;<hr><ltbullet>suggests land that the Division of State Parks (division) may consider for a potential state park, state monument, or state campground; <hr><ltbullet>encourages the division to work with federal agencies to acquire, lease, or manage properties considered suitable for use as a state park, monument, or campground;<hr><ltbullet>urges Congress to establish a framework for state operation of federal public lands, under a joint management agreement, to improve public land management and reduce federal expenditures;<hr><ltbullet>requests that the division petition the Bureau of Land Management to transfer land to the state for the creation of the Little Sahara State Park;<hr><ltbullet>requests that the division negotiate with the United States Forest Service to transfer the Antelope Flat Campground to the state for the creation of the Flaming Gorge State Park; and<hr><ltbullet>requests that the division update the Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Interim Committee on the division's study regarding new state parks and state campgrounds.

description: This concurrent resolution celebrates the upcoming 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence.

title: Concurrent Resolution Supporting the Transfer of Federally Managed Lands
description: This resolution is related to the disposition of federally managed lands for affordable housing.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>acknowledges that Utah's growth has intensified housing affordability challenges;<hr><ltbullet>recognizes that affordable housing is critical to workforce stability and community retention; <hr><ltbullet>notes that unreserved lands managed by the federal government are located near existing communities and infrastructure;<hr><ltbullet>recognizes that limited and targeted disposition of unreserved lands may support moderate income housing needs;<hr><ltbullet>affirms that any land disposition should preserve the public interest and responsible land stewardship;<hr><ltbullet>urges Congress to allow limited use of unreserved lands near existing communities and infrastructure for moderate income housing; and<hr><ltbullet>encourages Congress to support land transfers or exchanges in line with responsible stewardship.

title: Joint Rules Resolution - Amendments to Joint Rules
description: This resolution modifies joint rules.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>defines "minority leader" and "minority party";<hr><ltbullet>modifies the definition of "increase legislative workload";<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the secretary of the Senate's and the chief clerk of the House's record keeping duties;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the publication of the Senate and House draft journals;<hr><ltbullet>addresses rules and procedures that apply to an extraordinary session;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel to request a bill on behalf of a legislator if the bill is necessary to implement a constitutional joint resolution; <hr><ltbullet>allows a legislator to co-sponsor legislation that originates in the opposite chamber of which the legislator is a member;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies provisions related to committee notes;<hr><ltbullet>defines "sunset bill" and requires:<hr><ltbullet1>the Senate to table a House sunset bill on third reading; and<hr><ltbullet1>the House to refer a Senate sunset bill to the House Rules Committee; <hr><ltbullet>modifies the process related to legislation that increases legislative workload; <hr><ltbullet>modifies a Legislative Expenses Oversight Committee's meeting requirements; <hr><ltbullet>limits the number of committee bill files that an authorized legislative committee may open; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Resolution Regarding Prison Security and Successful Inmate Reentry
description: This joint resolution encourages Congress to support policies or programs that assist with successful inmate reentry and enhance security within correctional facilities.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>calls upon Congress to vote in favor of the 2025 Second Chance Reauthorization Act and restore eliminated funding of the Act;<hr><ltbullet>encourages Congress to support policies and programs that provide inmates with affordable health care prior to reentry;<hr><ltbullet>urges Congress to vote in favor of the 2025 Cell Phone Jamming Reform Act;<hr><ltbullet>requests that Congress criminalize the flying of drones over correctional facilities; and<hr><ltbullet>asks Congress to allow law enforcement and correctional agencies to implement a pilot program to mitigate drones that fly over critical infrastructure.

title: Proposal to Amend Utah Constitution - Judicial Nominations
description: This joint resolution of the Utah Legislature proposes to amend the Utah Constitution to modify the judicial nominating process.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>authorize the Governor to request a list of nominees from a judicial nominating commission when the Governor is filling a judicial vacancy;<hr><ltbullet>authorize the Governor to appoint any qualified candidate even if the candidate is not nominated by the nominating commission; <hr><ltbullet>remove the time constraint on the Governor to make an appointment; and<hr><ltbullet>remove the authority of the chief justice of the Supreme Court to fill a judicial vacancy if the Governor fails to fill the vacancy.

title: Proposal to Amend Utah Constitution - Judicial Retention
description: This joint resolution of the Utah Legislature proposes to amend the Utah Constitution to modify provisions related to retention of judges.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>authorize the Legislature to initiate a special retention process that allows the voters to vote on whether a judge shall remain in office when a judge engages in certain conduct; and<hr><ltbullet>provide that a judge who is subject to a special retention election is still subject to a regular retention election but that the special retention election may replace the regular retention election if the elections occur in the same year.

title: Joint Rules Resolution - Requests for Appropriation
description: This resolution modifies rules related to requests for appropriation.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>directs the Executive Appropriations Committee to set aside a specified portion of available revenue to fund district requests for appropriation;<hr><ltbullet>allows each legislator a set amount of the available funding to fund, through a district request for appropriation, a project or program within the legislator's district;<hr><ltbullet>provides requirements for a district request for appropriation;<hr><ltbullet>directs the assigned joint appropriations subcommittee to review each district request for appropriation for compliance with the applicable requirements; and<hr><ltbullet>requires the Executive Appropriations Committee to include in a final appropriations bill each district request for appropriation approved by a joint appropriations subcommittee.

title: Proposal to Amend Utah Constitution - Utah Taxpayer Oversight of Government Spending
description: This joint resolution of the Utah Legislature proposes to amend the Utah Constitution to create taxpayer oversight of government spending.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>require residential real property to be assessed using the sales comparison approach;<hr><ltbullet>authorize the Legislature to exempt business personal property from property tax; and<hr><ltbullet>establish taxpayer rights that include:<hr><ltbullet1>requiring voters to approve an increase in tax revenue or most types of government debt;<hr><ltbullet1>limiting the amount of revenue a taxing entity may spend in a fiscal year without voter approval; and<hr><ltbullet1>requiring a refund of excess revenue to taxpayers.

title: House Rules Resolution - Lobbyist Ethics Amendments
description: This resolution modifies House rules related to lobbyist ethics.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a volunteer lobbyist from certain House spaces under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a lobbyist, volunteer lobbyist, or government official from:<hr><ltbullet1>participating in the prioritization of legislation for floor action or referral to a standing committee; and<hr><ltbullet1>using a representative's, elected or appointed state official's, state employee's, or legislative employee's identification badge; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: House Rules Modifications
description: This rules resolution modifies House Rules.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>defines "sponsor's supporting information";<hr><ltbullet>allows a chief sponsor of legislation to provide the sponsor's supporting information, subject to certain requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires a legislative sponsor to sit at the presenter's table while a standing committee considers the legislative sponsor's legislation, with exceptions;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the process by which a standing committee chair allows a response to motions;<hr><ltbullet>amends the definition of "nonbinding resolution";<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that reinstating a word or words does not count toward the word limit under a verbal amendment;<hr><ltbullet>allows legislation assigned to the consent calendar to be reassigned to the third reading calendar, under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the prohibited references on the floor; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Public Education Budget Amendments
description: This bill supplements or reduces appropriations otherwise provided for the support and operation of public education for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2025, and ending June 30, 2026, and appropriates funds for the support and operation of public education for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026, and ending June 30, 2027.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the Digital Teaching and Learning Grant Program and an associated reporting requirement;<hr><ltbullet>creates reporting requirements regarding:<hr><ltbullet1>the state superintendent transferring money appropriated to the Minimum School Program; and<hr><ltbullet1>student personnel and data standards for the Utah Schools for the Deaf and the Blind;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Board of Education (state board) to establish certain student and personnel data standards for the Utah Schools for the Deaf and the Blind;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions related to:<hr><ltbullet1>weighted pupil units for college and career counseling;<hr><ltbullet1>the calculation of educator salary adjustments;<hr><ltbullet1>the state board's distribution of public education mental health screening funds; and<hr><ltbullet1>a scholarship student's use of funds under the Utah Private Course Choice Empowerment Program;<hr><ltbullet>creates a repeal date for:<hr><ltbullet1>the Personalized, Competency-based Learning Grants Program; and<hr><ltbullet1>small school student access to online courses;<hr><ltbullet>allows the state superintendent to transfer certain money related to state board line items;<hr><ltbullet>provides appropriations for the use and support of school districts, charter schools, and state education agencies;<hr><ltbullet>creates a new College and Career Counseling program by transferring funding and weighted pupil units from the Career & Technical Education - Add-on program;<hr><ltbullet>increases weighted pupil units for the Students At-Risk WPU Add-on program;<hr><ltbullet>provides appropriations for other purposes as described;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes; and<hr><ltbullet>provides intent language.

title: Statutorily Required Reports and Presentations Amendments
description: This bill addresses reports and presentations made to legislative interim committees.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTLAW", "name": "Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>removes, due to expired statutory deadlines, requirements for a report or presentation to the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee;<hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement for an annual presentation given to the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee from the Sentencing Commission regarding the master offense list and collateral consequence guide;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Sentencing Commission to publish the master offense list and collateral consequence guide on the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice's website each year;<hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement for an annual report submitted to the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee from:<hr><ltbullet1>the Office of the Attorney General regarding a joint strike force to combat criminal activity that may have a negative impact on the state's economy;<hr><ltbullet1>the Board of Pardons and Parole regarding certain metrics related to recidivism, offender time under the board's jurisdiction, prison releases, parole revocations, alignment with the sentencing guidelines in decisions, and reasons for any departures from the sentencing guidelines in decisions;<hr><ltbullet1>the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice regarding prosecutorial data collection;<hr><ltbullet1>the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice regarding the Pretrial Release Programs Special Revenue Fund;<hr><ltbullet1>the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice regarding bail and court appearance data;<hr><ltbullet1>the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice regarding progress made on the goals of the Justice Reinvestment Initiative;<hr><ltbullet1>the Bureau of Criminal Identification regarding fees from the Concealed Weapons Account; and<hr><ltbullet1>the Department of Corrections regarding supervision models used in state correctional facilities;<hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement for a report submitted to the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee and the Political Subdivisions Interim Committee from the Division of Emergency Management regarding the emergency alert system throughout the state;<hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement for a report submitted to the Judiciary Interim Committee, the Health and Human Services Interim Committee, the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee, and related appropriations subcommittees from the Department of Corrections regarding certain information about Department of Corrections programs;<hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement for an annual report submitted to the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee, Utah Substance Use and Mental Health Advisory Committee, and an advocacy agency designated by the governor from the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice regarding certain statistics gathered from county jails;<hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement for an annual report submitted to the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee and the Utah Substance Use and Mental Health Advisory Committee from the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice regarding certain statistics gathered from the Department of Corrections; <hr><ltbullet>enacts a sunset provision on a report from the Department of Corrections regarding in-custody deaths;<hr><ltbullet>enacts sunset provisions requiring an interim committee to review the following subsections and sections that establish a report to an interim committee:<hr><ltbullet1>Subsection , regarding a report submitted by the Department of Health and Human Services to the Health and Human Services Interim Committee and the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee on certain statistics related to inmate health; <hr><ltbullet1>Section 53-28-403, regarding an annual report on crime in student housing;<hr><ltbullet1>Subsection 64-13-6(3)(b), regarding a report submitted by the Department of Corrections to the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee on inmate programs;<hr><ltbullet1>Subsection 78A-2-109.5(6), regarding an annual report by the multi-agency strike force to combat violent and other major felony crimes associated with illegal immigration and human trafficking; and<hr><ltbullet1>Subsections  and (6), regarding an annual report by the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice on offenses committed by minors; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Technical Changes
description: This bill addresses obsolete programs and makes other technical changes to statutes within the purview of natural resources, agriculture, and environment or related legislative committees.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTNAE", "name": "Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>repeals language related to outdated authorizations to borrow or lend money from the Agricultural Water Optimization Account;<hr><ltbullet>repeals sections codifying the titles of a title, chapter, or part;<hr><ltbullet>requires certain annual reports to legislative committees be submitted by no later than October 1;<hr><ltbullet>repeals outdated reviews, reports, or studies;<hr><ltbullet>repeals outdated transitional language related to membership of boards;<hr><ltbullet>repeals outdated language regarding fees;<hr><ltbullet>corrects typographical errors;<hr><ltbullet>makes conforming amendments to sunset provisions;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies language regarding the federal Recreation and Public Purposes Act;<hr><ltbullet>repeals outdated deadlines for required management plans for water conveyance facilities;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the procedure for the Great Salt Lake commissioner's submission of a strategic plan;<hr><ltbullet>repeals obsolete provisions related to mercury switch removal;<hr><ltbullet>repeals outdated provisions related to presenting rules for carbon capture and geological storage;<hr><ltbullet>repeals completed study of transportation, heating, and electricity-generating fuel storage reserves;<hr><ltbullet>repeals outdated provisions related to regulatory certainty;<hr><ltbullet>repeals outdated requirement to participate in a survey;<hr><ltbullet>repeals outdated emergency water resources chapter; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: Geothermal Amendments
description: This bill addresses geothermal resources or fluids.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTNAE", "name": "Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>addresses the reservation of a geothermal resource on state and institutional trust land;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the purposes of the geothermal chapter;<hr><ltbullet>addresses definitions;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions related to ownership of geothermal resources or fluids;<hr><ltbullet>amends powers of the Division of Water Rights related to confidentiality of information;<hr><ltbullet>addresses bonding requirements; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: Assault or Threat of Violence Amendments
description: This bill addresses the offense of assault or threat of violence against a peace officer or military service member.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTLAW", "name": "Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>separates into two statutes the offenses of assault or threat of violence against a peace officer and assault or threat of violence against a military service member in uniform;<hr><ltbullet>amends the offense of assault or threat of violence against a peace officer to include:<hr><ltbullet1>assaults or threats of violence against off-duty peace officers if the actor committed the offense because of the peace officer's status as a peace officer; and<hr><ltbullet1>assaults or threats of violence against family members of a peace officer if the actor committed the offense because of the peace officer's status as a peace officer;<hr><ltbullet>amends the offense of assault or threat of violence against a military service member in uniform by:<hr><ltbullet1>renaming the offense to assault or threat of violence against a military service member;<hr><ltbullet1>including assaults or threats of violence against off-duty military service members and military service members not in uniform during the assault or threat of violence if the actor committed the offense because of the military service member's status as a military service member; and<hr><ltbullet1>including assaults or threats of violence against family members of a military service member if the actor committed the offense because of the military service member's status as a peace officer; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Human Trafficking, Exploitation, and Smuggling Amendments
description: This bill concerns human labor trafficking, human trafficking for sexual exploitation, and human smuggling.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTLAW", "name": "Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>removes the applicability of statutory defenses to offenses concerning human trafficking or human smuggling;<hr><ltbullet>repeals a freestanding definition section and incorporates the repealed section's definitions into the human smuggling offenses in which the terms are referenced;<hr><ltbullet>amends the following offenses concerning human trafficking, including revising the name and elements of the offense, and, for some offenses, requiring specific conduct for a violation:<hr><ltbullet1>human trafficking for labor;<hr><ltbullet1>human trafficking for sexual exploitation;<hr><ltbullet1>human trafficking of a child (for labor and for sexual exploitation); and<hr><ltbullet1>human trafficking of a vulnerable adult (for labor and for sexual exploitation);<hr><ltbullet>divides the offense of aggravated human trafficking for labor or sexual exploitation into two separate offenses;<hr><ltbullet>revises the offense of benefiting from human trafficking or human smuggling:<hr><ltbullet1>to no longer be a separate criminal offense by removing penalty provisions; and<hr><ltbullet1>to add human trafficking offenses concerning vulnerable adults to the list of offenses included in the statute;<hr><ltbullet>creates the following new offenses:<hr><ltbullet1>patronizing a victim of human labor trafficking;<hr><ltbullet1>patronizing a child victim of human labor trafficking; and<hr><ltbullet1>patronizing a vulnerable adult victim of human labor trafficking; <hr><ltbullet>amends the offenses of human smuggling and aggravated human smuggling to incorporate definitions from the repealed freestanding definitions section; <hr><ltbullet>changes cross references in other statutes referencing human trafficking offenses to include citations to additional trafficking and patronizing offenses; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Office of Professional Licensure Review Amendments
description: This bill modifies the scope of practice requirements for health professions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a physical therapist may prescribe durable medical equipment;<hr><ltbullet>expands the medical imaging a physical therapist may order;<hr><ltbullet>allows a physical therapist assistant to perform limited joint mobilization;<hr><ltbullet>provides a certified registered nurse anesthetist prescriptive authority immediately before and after a procedure;<hr><ltbullet>extends the amount of time a student may work as a registered nurse apprentice;<hr><ltbullet>requires a minimum level of registered nursing experience before licensure as an advanced practice registered nurse;<hr><ltbullet>permits an advanced practice registered nurse and a physician assistant to perform minor surgical procedures;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the authority of an advanced practice registered nurse and a physician assistant to perform minor surgical procedures on July 1, 2028;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies collaboration requirements between an athletic trainer and a physician;<hr><ltbullet>allows an occupational therapist to prescribe durable medical equipment and adaptive devices;<hr><ltbullet>gives the division rulemaking authority for occupational therapists;<hr><ltbullet>directs the division to create and issue a respiratory care apprentice license;<hr><ltbullet>reduces the number of hours required for a physician assistant to work without a collaborative agreement;<hr><ltbullet>allows an acupuncturist to delegate a low-risk task to an unlicensed aide under specified conditions;<hr><ltbullet>changes the training requirements for an acupuncturist performing injection therapy;<hr><ltbullet>gives the division rulemaking authority to determine additional substances an acupuncturist may inject;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the titles an acupuncturist may use;<hr><ltbullet>aligns dry needling for occupational therapists and physical therapists; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Child Abuse Homicide Corrections
description: This bill revises the offense of child abuse homicide.
comm_note: [{"id": "INTLAW", "name": "Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Interim Committee"}]
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>corrects the erroneous inclusion of the offense of child torture in the child abuse homicide statute, based on the child torture offense already having been included in the offense of murder;<hr><ltbullet>provides an immediate effective date; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Public Education Revisions
description: This bill amends provisions and programs regarding the operation of the public education system.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms, including "general control and supervision" of the public education system;<hr><ltbullet>corrects references regarding the State Superintendent's Annual Report;<hr><ltbullet>allows the State Board of Education (state board) to authorize the state superintendent of public instruction to appoint and supervise the superintendent of the Utah Schools for the Deaf and the Blind (USDB);<hr><ltbullet>renames the Catalyst Center Grant Program to the Applied Educational Experience Grant Program and amends associated provisions regarding eligibility for and use of program funds;<hr><ltbullet>amends the allowable use of funds in the Grow Your Own Educator Pipeline Program for paraprofessionals;<hr><ltbullet>aligns terminology regarding juvenile justice reintegration to apply to all local education agencies rather than only school districts;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions to allow the USDB to coordinate with the state security chief rather than the county security chief of the county for each USDB campus;<hr><ltbullet>allows the state board to reduce suicide prevention grant amounts in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause with H.B. 1, Public Education Base Budget Amendments, to adjust language regarding the Applied Educational Experience Grant Program; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Consumer Protection Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions relating to consumer protection.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers Title 13, Chapter 2, Division of Consumer Protection;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers Title 13, Chapter 21, Credit Services Organizations Act;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers Title 13, Chapter 22, Charitable Solicitations Act;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers and renames Title 13, Chapter 23, Health Spa Services Protection Act;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers Title 13, Chapter 26, Telephone Fraud Prevention Act;<hr><ltbullet>adds Title 13, Chapter 77, Generative Artificial Intelligence - Consumer Disclosures and Enforcement, to the list of chapters the Division of Consumer Protection (division) enforces;<hr><ltbullet>amends the division's investigatory authority to investigate conduct related to statutes that the division administers and enforces;<hr><ltbullet>amends filing requirements a person makes with the division; <hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to an entity's surety bond and certificate of deposit;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which the division may recover costs from a surety bond or a certificate of deposit;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a person correct information contained in a filing the person makes with the division if the information becomes incorrect or incomplete;<hr><ltbullet>provides that certain persons may not represent that the division or the state endorses or approves the person;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the issuance of certain documents does not constitute an approval or endorsement by the division or the state;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which the division may deny, suspend, or revoke certain documents;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a person that registers with the division maintain a registered agent in this state;<hr><ltbullet>provides requirements for the information a person shall maintain for a registered agent in this state;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to the division's enforcement powers and penalties the division may impose;<hr><ltbullet>provides the actions a court may take when the division brings an enforcement action;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which a court may order disgorgement of money;<hr><ltbullet>amends charitable solicitation financial report requirements;<hr><ltbullet>changes references in Title 13, Chapter 23, Health Spa Service Protection Act from "health spa" to "fitness center";<hr><ltbullet>provides registration and renewal requirements for certain entities and individuals;<hr><ltbullet>provides the length of a term for certain registrations;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to criminal background checks for an entity applying for registration with the division;<hr><ltbullet> provides that a seller or a seller's solicitor provide a consumer certain disclosures;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which the attorney general shall give legal advice to and act as counsel for the division;<hr><ltbullet>updates terminology to refer to the division;<hr><ltbullet>removes redundant provisions from provisions the division enforces;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to an annual report a person is required to file with the division;<hr><ltbullet>removes references to the attorney general's enforcement powers in relation to the division; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Investment Zones Amendments
description: This bill enacts, renumbers, amends, and repeals certain provisions of certain investment zones within the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>enacts, renumbers, and amends provisions of a convention center reinvestment zone and convention center reinvestment zone in a capital city;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers and amends provisions of:<hr><ltbullet1>a station area plan;<hr><ltbullet1>a housing and transit reinvestment zone; and<hr><ltbullet1>home ownership promotion zones in a municipality and county;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers provisions of:<hr><ltbullet1>a first home investment zone;<hr><ltbullet1>a capital city revitalization zone; and<hr><ltbullet1>a transportation reinvestment zone;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions of a home ownership promotion zone in a municipality or county to include a certain area within a boundary of a school;<hr><ltbullet>repeals an outdated section of code; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Business Entity Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to business entities.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>lists the areas of code the Division of Corporations and Commercial Code (division) administers;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the division shall offer to sell or license a copy of each document filed with the division under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>enacts Title 16, Chapter 1a, Provisions Applicable to All Business Entities;<hr><ltbullet>establishes standardized entity filing requirements for all business entities;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the division may provide forms for an entity filing;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a standard for the effective date and time of an entity filing;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which a person may withdraw an entity filing before effectiveness;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the standards for correcting an entity filing;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the division has a duty to file an entity filing that complies with certain standards;<hr><ltbullet>establishes signing requirements for an entity filing;<hr><ltbullet>provides for liability for a person that provides inaccurate information in a filed record;<hr><ltbullet>provides the manner by which the division may deliver a record to a person;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for an entity's annual report to the division;<hr><ltbullet>establishes standards for permissible names for an entity;<hr><ltbullet>provides the name requirements for specific entities;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the process by which a person may reserve an entity name;<hr><ltbullet>provides the process by which a foreign filing entity may register a name;<hr><ltbullet>provides which business entities are required to maintain a registered agent in this state;<hr><ltbullet>provides the process for designating a registered agent;<hr><ltbullet>provides the process for the listing of a commercial registered agent;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the process for the termination of the listing of a commercial registered agent;<hr><ltbullet>provides the process by which a represented entity may change the represented entity's registered agent;<hr><ltbullet>provides the process by which a noncommercial registered agent may change the noncommercial registered agent's name or address;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the process by which a commercial registered agent may change the commercial registered agent's name, address, type of entity, or jurisdiction of formation;<hr><ltbullet>provides the process by which a registered agent may resign as a registered agent;<hr><ltbullet>provides how a person may make service of process, notice, or demand on an entity;<hr><ltbullet>describes the duties of a registered agent;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a foreign entity shall register with the division to do business in this state;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for filing and amending a foreign registration statement;<hr><ltbullet>provides that certain activities of a foreign entity do not constitute doing business in this state;<hr><ltbullet>provides the process by which a foreign entity may adopt an alternate name that complies with the name requirements of this state;<hr><ltbullet>provides the process by which a registered foreign entity may withdraw the registered foreign entity's registration with the division;<hr><ltbullet>provides for a transfer of a registered foreign entity's registration under certain conditions;<hr><ltbullet>provides the conditions and manner under which the division may terminate a registered foreign entity's registration;<hr><ltbullet>provides the grounds under which the division may administratively dissolve a domestic filing entity;<hr><ltbullet>provides the procedure and effect of an administrative dissolution of a domestic filing entity;<hr><ltbullet>provides the conditions under which and process by which a domestic filing entity may be reinstated after administrative dissolution;<hr><ltbullet>provides the process by which an entity may take part in a merger;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for a plan of merger;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements to approve a plan of merger;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the process for amending or abandoning a plan of merger;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a merging entity sign a statement of merger;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the effect of a merger;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an interest holder in an entity that undergoes a merger, conversion, or domestication has appraisal rights;<hr><ltbullet>provides the process by which an entity may take part in an interest exchange;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for a plan of interest exchange;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements to approve a plan of interest exchange;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the process for amending or abandoning a plan of interest exchange;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an acquired entity sign a statement of interest exchange;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the effect of an interest exchange;<hr><ltbullet>provides the process by which an entity may take part in a conversion;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for a plan of conversion;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements to approve a plan of conversion;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the process for amending or abandoning a plan of conversion;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a converting entity sign a statement of conversion;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the effect of a conversion;<hr><ltbullet>provides the process by which an entity may take part in a domestication;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for a plan of domestication;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements to approve a plan of domestication;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the process for amending or abandoning a plan of domestication;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a merging entity sign a statement of domestication;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the effect of a domestication;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers Title 48, Chapter 1d, Utah Uniform Partnership Act, to Title 16, Chapter 18, Utah Uniform Partnership Act;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers Title 48, Chapter 2e, Utah Uniform Limited Partnership Act, to Title 16, Chapter 19, Utah Uniform Limited Partnership Act;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers Title 48, Chapter 3a, Utah Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, to Title 16, Chapter 20, Utah Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act;<hr><ltbullet>changes references in code from "assumed name" to "D.B.A.";<hr><ltbullet>provides what the name of a D.B.A. may contain;<hr><ltbullet>provides the standards for registering as a D.B.A.;<hr><ltbullet>provides the process for amending a D.B.A. certificate;<hr><ltbullet>provides the manner by which a D.B.A. may transfer ownership;<hr><ltbullet>provides the expiration, renewal, and cancellation of a registration process for a D.B.A.;<hr><ltbullet>provides penalties for a person that transacts business as a D.B.A. without complying with Title 42, Chapter 2, Conducting Business as a D.B.A.;<hr><ltbullet>repeals provisions in existing code that the enactment of Title 16, Chapter 1a, Provisions Applicable to All Business Entities, makes redundant; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Kratom Adjustments
description: This bill amends provisions related to kratom.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a kratom processor and kratom retailer to register with the Department of Agriculture and Food;<hr><ltbullet>only allows a retail tobacco specialty business to sell kratom;<hr><ltbullet>bans the sale of certain kratom products;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to penalties and fees;<hr><ltbullet>amends the age for who can purchase a kratom product;<hr><ltbullet>schedules 7-hydroxymitragynine, including synthetics, if the 7-hydroxymitragynine concentration exceeds a certain percentage as a schedule I controlled substance; and<hr><ltbullet>schedules Mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, including synthetics; and<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause with H.B. 387, Kratom Modifications, directing the Legislature to not enroll H.B. 387.

title: Natural Organic Reduction Amendments
description: This bill addresses natural organic reduction.

title: Carson Smith Opportunity Scholarship Program Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions of certain scholarship programs.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>eliminates income based eligibility requirements for the scholarship; <hr><ltbullet>removes scholarship eligibility for a sibling; <hr><ltbullet>aligns the scholarship requirements with the Utah Fits All Scholarship Program;<hr><ltbullet>allows the scholarship granting organization to approve qualified providers and private schools;<hr><ltbullet>requires the scholarship granting organization to ensure physical education and extracurricular caps are followed;<hr><ltbullet>amends the definition of scholarship expense to be the same across multiple scholarship programs;<hr><ltbullet>establishes primary residency verification to be eligible for a scholarship;<hr><ltbullet>creates a deadline for an eligible student to accept the scholarship that the scholarship granting organization determines;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies entities that are not eligible to be a qualified provider under the scholarship program; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Alimony Amendments
description: This bill addresses alimony.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires a court to consider the tax consequences of alimony on each party when determining or modifying alimony;<hr><ltbullet>addresses when a court shall consider the length of two marriages between the same individuals as the length of one marriage for purposes of determining alimony;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the modification of alimony after a court enters a divorce decree; and<hr><ltbullet>addresses the effect of cohabitation on alimony.

title: Government Records Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to the Government Records Access and Management Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a summary of government records requirements to be developed and provided to employees of a governmental entity;<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions relating to fees charged in relation to a record request;<hr><ltbullet>modifies requirements for responding to a record request, including:<hr><ltbullet1>deadlines;<hr><ltbullet1>a request for an expedited response; <hr><ltbullet1>appeals; and<hr><ltbullet1>other requirements;<hr><ltbullet>adds certain federal employees to the definition of an "at-risk government employee";<hr><ltbullet>modifies provisions relating to certain protected records;<hr><ltbullet>requires a governmental entity to conduct an annual review of records retention requirements and compliance with those requirements;<hr><ltbullet>amends requirements for an ordinance or policy adopted by a political subdivision in relation to public records;<hr><ltbullet>makes it a crime to destroy a record with the intent to avoid disclosure in response to a pending record request; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Minimum Basic Tax Rate Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to the minimum basic tax that school districts impose.

description: This bill addresses obscene animal abuse material.

title: Online Age Verification Amendments
description: This bill enacts provisions related to online providers of content harmful to minors.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides legislative findings;<hr><ltbullet>imposes an excise tax on certain entities that provide content harmful to minors; <hr><ltbullet>provides for administration and collection of the excise tax by the State Tax Commission based on referrals from the Division of Consumer Protection; <hr><ltbullet>creates the Minor Mental Health Restricted Account within the General Fund; <hr><ltbullet>directs tax revenues to the Department of Health and Human Services and the Division of Consumer Protection to be used for mental health programs and enforcement of age verification requirements; <hr><ltbullet>provides for liability for publishers and distributors of material harmful to minors who fail to perform age verification; <hr><ltbullet>grants the Division of Consumer Protection authority to investigate and enforce age verification requirements; <hr><ltbullet>provides administrative fines and civil penalties for violations of age verification requirements; <hr><ltbullet>creates the Minor Online Safety Restricted Account (account) within the General Fund and provides for deposits from tax revenue and from fines and civil penalties; <hr><ltbullet>directs money in the account to the Division of Consumer Protection to be used for enforcement of age verification requirements and online safety for minors;<hr><ltbullet>provides rulemaking authority to the Division of Consumer Protection to establish standards for substantial portion determinations and age verification methods;<hr><ltbullet>provides safe harbor for approved age verification methods; <hr><ltbullet>provides a severability clause; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Motor Vehicle Civil Action Amendments
description: This bill amends the Insurance Code to establish requirements relating to policy-limit demands and disclosures in third-party liability claims related to motor vehicle liability.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for the content of policy-limit demand letters from a claimant to a liability insurance carrier;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for correspondence from a claimant or a claimant's legal counsel to an unrepresented insured;<hr><ltbullet>requires a liability insurance carrier to provide written disclosure to the insured regarding defense and indemnification;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the effect of a disclosure and the consequences of noncompliance; and<hr><ltbullet>preserves existing rights and remedies.

title: Residential Rental Payment Reporting Amendments
description: This bill enacts provisions relating to residential rental reporting requirements.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an owner may provide a renter an offer of rent reporting at the time the owner and renter enter into a rental agreement;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an owner charge a fee for rent reporting that may not exceed the actual cost of the rent reporting;<hr><ltbullet>provides the consequences for a renter failing to pay the fee for rent reporting;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a renter may enroll and unenroll in rent reporting at any time during the duration of the rental agreement;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a renter from reenrolling in rent reporting for at least six months if the renter fails to pay the fee for rent reporting or the renter unenrolls in rent reporting; and<hr><ltbullet>provides that the provisions this bill enacts apply only to an entity that owns one or more residential rental units or an individual that owns 16 or more residential rental units.

title: Property Tax Relief Amendments
description: This bill modifies property tax relief provisions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes counties to provide certain property tax relief to qualifying individuals through a country relief program;<hr><ltbullet>establishes notice and public hearing requirements before a county may approve a county relief program by ordinance;<hr><ltbullet>requires a county to impose a separate county relief levy for the relief the county provides through a county relief program;<hr><ltbullet>changes the qualifications, scope, duration, and interest rate applicable to the nondiscretionary deferral program;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Multicounty Appraisal Trust to make loans to counties to pay the costs of granting nondiscretionary deferrals;<hr><ltbullet>repeals certain property tax relief programs;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to incorporate changes to Section 59-2-1602 in S.B. 206, Tax Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Dyslexia Testing Amendments
description: This bill addresses dyslexia assessment and diagnosis.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires a school district or charter school to take certain actions, including individualized intervention, if a dyslexia assessment administered by a licensed individual practicing within the scope of practice for the individual's license, indicates that a student lacks reading competency, demonstrates characteristics of dyslexia, or is lagging in acquiring a reading skill;<hr><ltbullet>provides certain protections to educational professionals;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to the scope of practice for mental health therapists and psychologists to:<hr><ltbullet1> align with an approved diagnostic and statistical manual for mental disorders; and<hr><ltbullet1>clarify that the scope of practice includes the evaluation and treatment of disorders as defined in the approved diagnostic and statistical manual for mental disorders, including dyslexia;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Naloxone Amendments
description: This bill extends protections for prescribing, dispensing, furnishing, and administering an expired opiate antagonist.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>for administering an opiate antagonist:<hr><ltbullet1>extends immunity from liability for administering an opiate antagonist in good faith to include the administration of an expired opiate antagonist; and<hr><ltbullet1>clarifies that immunity includes immunity from a civil action and criminal prosecution; <hr><ltbullet>provides that a person licensed under Utah law to dispense an opiate antagonist may dispense an expired opiate antagonist;<hr><ltbullet>requires a health care provider who dispenses an opiate antagonist to an individual or overdose outreach provider to provide education on the safety, efficacy, and risks of administering an expired opiate antagonist;<hr><ltbullet>provides that it is not unlawful or unprofessional conduct for a person who is licensed to prescribe or dispense an opiate antagonist to prescribe or dispense an expired opiate antagonist;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an overdose outreach provider may furnish an expired opiate antagonist;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes; and<hr><ltbullet>defines terms.

title: Occupational Licenses for Veterans and Service Members
description: This bill addresses provisions related to veterans and service members obtaining an occupational license.

title: Motor Vehicle Registration Services Amendments
description: This bill amends vehicle registration fees to provide funding for Motor Vehicle Division services in counties of the third through sixth class.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides funding for counties that provide Motor Vehicle Division services on behalf of the division;<hr><ltbullet>modifies vehicle registration fees;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Vehicle Registration Services Restricted Account;<hr><ltbullet>increases the required contribution for the historical black license plate from $25 to $50;<hr><ltbullet>allocates special group license plate revenue from the historical black license plate; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Public Speaking Amendments
description: This bill establishes risk assessment and security requirements for public events at an institution of higher education (institutions).
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires institutions to conduct content-neutral risk assessments for public events with outside speakers;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a multi-level threat classification system;<hr><ltbullet>assigns coordination responsibilities to the Department of Public Safety;<hr><ltbullet>mandates security measures corresponding to assigned threat levels;<hr><ltbullet>requires insurance coverage and authorizes security fees based on threat levels;<hr><ltbullet>establishes an event application, approval, and appeal process;<hr><ltbullet>permits event modification or cancellation based on emerging threats;<hr><ltbullet>protects certain assessment records under state law while maintaining public access to key information;<hr><ltbullet>requires reporting and oversight by the Board of Higher Education and the Legislature under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>mandates training and designates institutional coordinators; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Tax Revenue Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to tax revenue.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>limits the amount of reserve funds maintained by cities and counties;<hr><ltbullet>reduces the amount of the residential property tax exemption for rental properties, with certain exceptions;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the applicability of the residential exemption for owners of multiple primary residences in the state; <hr><ltbullet>requires counties to provide information to the Multicounty Appraisal Trust regarding business entities that receive the residential exemption;<hr><ltbullet>excludes certain property valuation increases from the calculation of locally assessed new growth;<hr><ltbullet>excludes increases to the value of tangible personal property from the calculation of project area new growth;<hr><ltbullet>subtracts from a city's certified tax rate calculation any amount of reserve funds maintained by the city in excess of the maximum amount authorized, beginning in fiscal year 2032; <hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to incorporate changes to the Multicounty Appraisal Trust in S.B. 206, Tax Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.
