title: Substance Use Rehabilitation Amendments
description: This bill authorizes the Department of Health and Human Services to establish a recovery ready workplace certification program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Department of Health and Human Services (department) to establish, in consultation with the Department of Workforce Services, a certification program for employers to be certified as a recovery ready workplace (program); <hr><ltbullet>if the department establishes the program, requires the department to establish an application process and criteria;<hr><ltbullet>provides that funds may be appropriated by the Legislature from the Electronic Cigarette Substance and Nicotine Product Proceeds Restricted Account for the program;<hr><ltbullet>grants the department rulemaking authority; <hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Emergency Reporting Offense Amendments
description: This bill modifies the offense of emergency reporting abuse.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies the offense of emergency reporting abuse to include conduct in which an actor contacts a 911 emergency response service when the actor knows, or reasonably should know, that no actual or perceived emergency, crime, or other circumstance jeopardizing public safety exists; <hr><ltbullet>moves a definition to the statute in which the definition is referenced; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Federalism Revisions
description: This bill modifies provisions related to federalism.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the registration and use of certain federalism related trademarks;<hr><ltbullet>extends requirements for publishing and reporting federal guidance letters to certain education entities;<hr><ltbullet>changes the statewide website on which state agencies are required to publish federal guidance letters;<hr><ltbullet>requires a state agency that receives a federal guidance letter to submit an electronic report to the Federalism Commission containing information and recommendations regarding the impacts and scope of the federal guidance letter;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a state agency to publish federal guidance letters received prior to the date on which the requirements for publishing and reporting federal guidance letters first took effect;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Federalism Commission to report annually to the Legislative Management Committee regarding federal guidance letters reported by state agencies; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Specialized Product Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to specialized products.

description: This bill addresses use of force.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends when criminal intent may be transferred;<hr><ltbullet>amends the defense of justification when using force in defense of person or property to remove the actor's ability to claim the defense if the actor recklessly, or with criminal negligence, causes an injury to, or the death of, a bystander while using force that would otherwise be justified against another individual;<hr><ltbullet>amends the pretrial justification hearing procedures to allow a defendant who is charged with recklessly, or with criminal negligence, causing an injury to, or the death of, a bystander while using force that the defendant claims was justified against another individual to seek a pretrial justification hearing; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Veterinary Post-employment Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to veterinarians.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a veterinarian non-compete agreement that a veterinarian and a person enter into on or after May 6, 2026, is void;<hr><ltbullet>provides that if a veterinarian has a 5% ownership interest in a person's business, the veterinarian and the person may enter into a non-compete agreement;<hr><ltbullet>makes void a provision requiring that a dispute arising from a veterinarian non-compete agreement be resolved outside of this state;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a nondisclosure clause or a nonsolicitation agreement that a person and a veterinarian enter into on or after May 6, 2026, is void; <hr><ltbullet>amends provisions providing for an award of damages and attorney fees for a nonsolicitation agreement or a nondisclosure clause;<hr><ltbullet>provides a coordination clause between this bill and H.B. 270, Healthcare Worker Post-employment Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Mental Health Services in Higher Education
description: This bill creates the Peer-to-Peer Coaching and Mental Health Counseling Grant.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Peer-to-Peer Coaching and Mental Health Counseling Grant;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Utah Board of Higher Education to:<hr><ltbullet1>administer the grant;<hr><ltbullet1>distribute funds; and<hr><ltbullet1>create rules;<hr><ltbullet>requires an institution to:<hr><ltbullet1>establish and implement a peer coaching program; or<hr><ltbullet1>use the funds for other mental health services for students;<hr><ltbullet>requires an institution to approve certain training; and<hr><ltbullet>exempts a peer coach from liability for an act or failure to act under this section.

title: Medical Cannabis Program Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to the medical cannabis program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends when the Cannabis Production Establishment and Pharmacy Licensing Advisory Board must meet to review an ownership change application;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to labeling of cannabis products;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to cannabis remediation;<hr><ltbullet>repeals language related to electronic payments;<hr><ltbullet>amends how medical cannabis cardholders may transport medical cannabis;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions related to the safe storage of medical cannabis for medical cannabis deliveries;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to when a recommending provider employee may access information;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to the processes of obtaining certain medical cannabis cards;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to when a medical cannabis pharmacy agent may access the electronic verification system;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to acceptable forms of identification;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to the revocation of certain medical cannabis agent cards;<hr><ltbullet>allows a medical cannabis guardian card to be issued to the legal guardian of an adult who is incapacitated;<hr><ltbullet>creates a voucher program for patients to obtain medical cannabis or a medical cannabis device; <hr><ltbullet>extends the repeal of the medical cannabis governance structure working group; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: HOA Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to homeowners' associations.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which a homeowners' association may convey a portion of the common areas;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the Office of the Homeowners' Association Ombudsman (office) make public each advisory opinion the office issues;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the office provide a list of statutes and frequently asked questions that impact persons under the jurisdiction of a homeowners' association;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the office publish educational materials on the office's website;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the office direct individuals making a phone call to the office to resources the office creates;<hr><ltbullet>provides that an action by an attorney employed by the office does not create an attorney-client relationship;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the filing fee a person pays for an advisory opinion from the office is nonrefundable;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a homeowners' association may not require a person to engage in binding arbitration before obtaining an advisory opinion from the office;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for the contents of a request for an advisory opinion from the office;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to a civil penalty associated with an action that arises from the same set of facts as an advisory opinion the office issues;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to what type of vehicle a rule may restrict from parking on a driveway;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a homeowners' association's declaration may not contain certain provisions;<hr><ltbullet>amends the circumstances under which a lot owner may continue renting a lot in a homeowners' association without a fee;<hr><ltbullet>renames an association transfer fee to an administrative setup fee;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the requirement that the parties to an advisory opinion split the cost of the advisory opinion;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the conditions under which Title 57, Chapter 8, Condominium Ownership Act, or Title 57, Chapter 8a, Community Association Act, applies;<hr><ltbullet>requires that an association of unit owners prepare and adopt an annual budget for the association;<hr><ltbullet>removes the requirement that a board member and president of an association provide a physical address to the Department of Commerce for registration;<hr><ltbullet>provides that certain documents are considered property of an association;<hr><ltbullet>provides that if a person maintains a document considered property of an association, the person shall provide the document to the association upon request;<hr><ltbullet>provides the duties of a declarant during the period of administrative control;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which the period of administrative control may be extended for a large master planned development; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Privacy and Cybersecurity Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to the Utah Cyber Center.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>adds the Department of Environmental Quality an as entity that the Utah Cyber Center will collaborate with when performing legislative duties; <hr><ltbullet>modifies the deadline for developing a statewide strategic cybersecurity plan;<hr><ltbullet>expands the Utah Cyber Center's duties to include local education agencies;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the composition of the Cybersecurity Commission to include a representative from the Utah Education and Telehealth Network; <hr><ltbullet>creates the Utah Cyber Center Restricted Account (account) and makes appropriations from the account nonlapsing; <hr><ltbullet>repeals a section related to government cybersecurity; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Child Welfare Modifications
description: This bill addresses protective custody warrants and child safety warrants relating to child welfare.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding the issuance of warrants by a juvenile court;<hr><ltbullet>distinguishes between a protective custody warrant and a child safety warrant;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a juvenile court to issue a child safety warrant related to the health, safety, or welfare of a child;<hr><ltbullet>states that a peace officer or child welfare caseworker who is executing a protective custody warrant or a child safety warrant may request assistance in executing the warrant;<hr><ltbullet>specifies that a child safety warrant does not give a peace officer or child welfare caseworker authority to take a child into protective custody;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill addresses offenses related to theft.

title: School Swimming and Lifeguarding Programs
description: This bill enacts provisions in public education related to water safety.

title: River Restoration Amendments
description: This bill addresses provisions related to Jordan River improvement projects.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies how the Division of Forestry, Fire, and State Lands (division) expends money related to a Jordan River improvement project, including:<hr><ltbullet1>allowing the division to expend money for an activity along the entire length of the Jordan River; and<hr><ltbullet1>requiring the division to consult with the Jordan River Commission before expending money for an improvement project;<hr><ltbullet>creates a matching grant program for counties and municipalities to fund improvement projects that increase access to a recreational activity on the Jordan River;<hr><ltbullet>appropriates funding for the matching grant program; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Nuclear Reprocessing Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions relating to energy development.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Office of Energy Development (office) to coordinate with public and private entities regarding nuclear fuel recycling facility development in the state;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the office to serve as a liaison between private entities and local communities regarding nuclear fuel recycling facility development;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Utah Energy Council (council) to provide strategic guidance and conduct preliminary assessments for nuclear fuel recycling facility development;<hr><ltbullet>requires the office to report on nuclear fuel recycling coordination activities as part of the office's existing annual report;<hr><ltbullet>requires the council to report on nuclear fuel recycling recommendations as part of the council's existing annual report; <hr><ltbullet> authorizes the office to pursue development of a Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campus (campus); <hr><ltbullet>requires the office to analyze state laws and rules for barriers to hosting a campus and report findings; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Enforcement Activities Amendments
description: This bill creates requirements for certain enforcement activities.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits certain state or local law enforcement officers from assisting with a federal immigration enforcement operation in a sensitive location or house of worship;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits, with certain exceptions, an employee of a law enforcement agency from using a facial covering;<hr><ltbullet>provides:<hr><ltbullet1>a criminal penalty for an illegal use of a facial covering;<hr><ltbullet1>a waiver of immunity and allowance for damages against an employee of a law enforcement agency who violates the facial mask prohibition and commits a specified offense; and<hr><ltbullet1>an exemption from the criminal penalty if the employing law enforcement agency has established and publicly posted a facial covering policy;<hr><ltbullet>requires a law enforcement agency to establish and publicly post a facial covering policy and includes requirements for a law enforcement facial covering policy;<hr><ltbullet>requires, with certain exceptions, a governmental entity operating a sensitive location to not allow into certain non-public areas an individual who is seeking access to conduct an immigration enforcement operation;<hr><ltbullet>contains severability clauses; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Notary Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions of the Notaries Public Reform Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>modifies requirements for providing satisfactory evidence of identity;<hr><ltbullet>for a notary who, on or after May 6, 2026, receives a notary commission, or receives a new notary commission:<hr><ltbullet1>implements a requirement for the notary to keep a journal; and<hr><ltbullet1>modifies requirements for the content of a journal;<hr><ltbullet>modifies requirements relating to the retention of a journal or an electronic recording of a remote notarization;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a journal or an electronic recording of a remote notarization are not records under the Government Records Access and Management Act;<hr><ltbullet>describes the circumstances under which a journal may be inspected;<hr><ltbullet>makes it a crime to, without legal authority, use, forge, or take certain other actions in relation to a notarization, a journal, an official seal, or other items relating to notarization;<hr><ltbullet>describes the action that a notary is required to take upon discovery of:<hr><ltbullet1>a crime described in this bill; or<hr><ltbullet1>the loss, damage, or destruction of a journal or related items; <hr><ltbullet>exempts attorneys, law firms, and title agencies from certain requirements relating to a journal; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Election Adjustments

title: Child Welfare Amendments
description: This bill makes changes related to the Division of Child and Family Services and child welfare processes.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allows the Division of Child and Family Services (DCFS) to share information with the Division of Professional Licensing for certain purposes;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the definition of "relative";<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the timeline for certain rights for foster parents;<hr><ltbullet>requires DCFS to notify all parties when DCFS files a court report or child and family plan;<hr><ltbullet>requires placement objections to be filed and resolved within a certain time; <hr><ltbullet>addresses shelter removal findings; and<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that a postadoption contact agreement is not limited to children who are in the custody of DCFS.

title: Utah Exemptions Act Amendments

title: Lobbying Amendments
description: This bill amends and enacts provisions relating to lobbying.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>modifies and clarifies the definitions of lobbyist, lobbying, and a principal;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the limits for certain expenditures;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits consideration, a reward, or an incentive for lobbying that is contingent on certain government action and provides criminal and civil penalties for violation of the prohibition;<hr><ltbullet>replaces the offense of employing or soliciting a person to lobby for contingent compensation with the offense described in the preceding paragraph;<hr><ltbullet>creates an exception to the definition of "expenditure" in relation to certain sporting events, performances, or exhibitions of a state institution of higher education or a private, nonprofit institution of higher education;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to lobbying by a former state official; and<hr><ltbullet> makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Office of Inspector General of Medicaid Services Amendments
description: This bill addresses oversight of the Office of Inspector General of Medicaid Services.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes the Office of Inspector General of Medicaid Services (office) as an office within the Department of Government Operations (department);<hr><ltbullet>removes the office as an independent entity subject to Title 63H, Independent State Entities;<hr><ltbullet>amends the office's audit and other responsibilities;<hr><ltbullet>requires the office to submit a budget for the office to the department;<hr><ltbullet>requires the executive director of the department (executive director) to:<hr><ltbullet1>establish performance metrics for the office;<hr><ltbullet1>establish a process for employees and members of the public to report concerns to the executive director;<hr><ltbullet1>report the concerns to an advisory board; and<hr><ltbullet1>report to the advisory board on the office's performance based on performance metrics; <hr><ltbullet> requires the inspector general of Medicaid services (inspector general) to:<hr><ltbullet1>submit an annual report to the Social Services Appropriations Subcommittee; <hr><ltbullet1>collaborate with the Office of the Legislative Auditor General; and<hr><ltbullet1>present certain information at meetings of the Social Services Appropriations Subcommittee and the Health and Human Services Interim Committee;<hr><ltbullet>requires the executive director to create an advisory board to:<hr><ltbullet1>promote coordination of Medicaid program integrity activities; <hr><ltbullet1>make recommendations regarding audit prioritization to the office and the department;<hr><ltbullet1>review employee concerns reported to the executive director; <hr><ltbullet1>make recommendations regarding improving the office's performance to the inspector general, the executive director, and the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet1>review the office's annual risk assessment and the office's annual audit plan;<hr><ltbullet1>review limitations that impede the office's ability to appropriately conduct audits; and<hr><ltbullet1>review agencies' implementation of the office's audit recommendations; <hr><ltbullet>provides a sunset date for the advisory board and related provisions;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: General Oversight Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to legislative general oversight, including administrative rulemaking.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>renames the Rules Review and General Oversight Committee to the General Oversight Committee (committee);<hr><ltbullet>amends the membership of the committee;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to what actions the committee may take regarding hearings, bill files, and administrative rules;<hr><ltbullet>amends when the committee may close meetings;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to the process and procedures for making administrative rules;<hr><ltbullet>amends the responsibilities of the Office of Administrative Rules;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the governor's authority to revive rules that the Legislature has voted to not reauthorize; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Licensing Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions relating to licensing.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>repeals Title 53, Chapter 9, Private Investigator Regulation Act;<hr><ltbullet>repeals Title 53, Chapter 11, Bail Bond Recovery Act;<hr><ltbullet>enacts Title 58, Chapter 92, Private Investigation Licensing Act, and Title 58, Chapter 93, Bail Bond Licensing Act;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Division of Professional Licensing (division) administers Title 58, Chapter 92, Private Investigation Licensing Act, and Title 58, Chapter 93, Bail Bond Licensing Act;<hr><ltbullet>adds members to the Security Services Licensing Board;<hr><ltbullet>provides license classifications and qualifications for licensure for a private investigator agent, a private investigator apprentice, and a private investigator registrant;<hr><ltbullet>provides the requirements for a private investigation agency;<hr><ltbullet>provides general qualifications for licensure under Title 58, Chapter 92, Private Investigation Licensing Act;<hr><ltbullet>provides the licensing requirements for a private investigator apprentice, a private investigator registrant, and a private investigator agent;<hr><ltbullet>enacts requirements related to evidence of licensure under Title 58, Chapter 92, Private Investigation Licensing Act, and Title 58, Chapter 93, Bail Bond Licensing Act;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the division may establish operating standards for Title 58, Chapter 92, Private Investigation Licensing Act;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the division may establish grounds for the denial of a license and disciplinary proceedings;<hr><ltbullet>provides requirements for a private investigator agent establishing a private investigation agency;<hr><ltbullet>provides what constitutes unlawful conduct and unprofessional conduct under Title 58, Chapter 92, Private Investigation Licensing Act, and Title 58, Chapter 93, Bail Bond Licensing Act;<hr><ltbullet>provides for penalties under Title 58, Chapter 92, Private Investigation Licensing Act, and Title 58, Chapter 93, Bail Bond Licensing Act;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the division may use money collected under Title 58, Chapter 93, Bail Bond Licensing Act, for certain purposes;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the division may appoint certain individuals to the Security Services Licensing Board;<hr><ltbullet>provides license classifications and qualifications for licensure for a bail bond agency, a bail enforcement agent, a bail recovery agent, and a bail recovery apprentice;<hr><ltbullet>provides general qualifications for licensure under Title 58, Chapter 93, Bail Bond Licensing Act;<hr><ltbullet>provides experience requirements for a bail bond agent and a bail recovery agent;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the division to adopt rules to exempt an applicant from certain training requirements this bill enacts;<hr><ltbullet>provides requirements for a bail bond enforcement agent or bail bond recovery agent to maintain identification cards;<hr><ltbullet>provides badge and clothing requirements for a licensee under Title 58, Chapter 93, Bail Bond Licensing Act;<hr><ltbullet>provides requirements for a bail enforcement agent, bail recovery agent, or bail recovery apprentice when interacting with law enforcement or engaging in a search or apprehension;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the provisions this bill enacts supersede a contrary legislation, code, or ordinance enacted by a political subdivision of this state;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to a private investigator agent, a private investigator registrant, or a private investigator apprentice serving process; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Healthcare Providers Scope of Practice Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to the Office of Professional Licensure Review.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the Office of Professional Licensure Review (office) conduct a scope of practice review (review);<hr><ltbullet>provides how a requestor may request a review;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the office make a determination as to whether the office will conduct a review;<hr><ltbullet>requires that, when conducting a review, the office convene a group to consult on the review;<hr><ltbullet>provides which individuals the office shall include in a group to consult on the review;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the office determine whether to provide a recommendation that a regulated healthcare occupation incorporate an innovation into the regulated healthcare occupation's practice;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the office create a report that details the office's recommendation following a review;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the office provide the report to the Business and Labor Interim Committee;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the office create a final report after incorporating any changes from the Business and Labor Interim Committee;<hr><ltbullet>provides the criteria the office shall consider when conducting a review; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Public and Higher Education Collaboration
description: This bill establishes a process for sharing grades 7through12 student data between public education and higher education.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes a data sharing process between state and higher education boards for grades 7 through 12 student data;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes disclosure to support college readiness programs and higher education access;<hr><ltbullet>requires compliance with federal privacy laws and state student data protections;<hr><ltbullet>mandates parent notification of opt-out rights for data sharing;<hr><ltbullet>requires training of higher education employees who will have data access; <hr><ltbullet>delegates rulemaking authority to the Board of Higher Education; and<hr><ltbullet>makes conforming changes.

title: Election Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to elections.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>modifies and recodifies provisions relating to:<hr><ltbullet1>the information in a voter registration record that is available to a person based on the capacity in which the person requests the information; and<hr><ltbullet1>the requirements to obtain additional privacy protection for a voter registration record;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a voter's voter registration record that, before April 6, 2026, was classified as private without requiring a reason for the classification will be reclassified as a public voter registration record, unless the voter takes certain action to obtain additional protection for the voter's voter registration record;<hr><ltbullet>requires an election officer to notify a voter whose voter registration is subject to reclassification as described in the preceding paragraph in order to give the voter an opportunity to apply for additional protection for the voter's voter registration record;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the voter registration form to reflect the changes made in this bill and to give a voter the option of authorizing disclosure of the voter's telephone number or email address to the political party with which the voter affiliates;<hr><ltbullet>requires the lieutenant governor to post information relating to the number of at-risk voters in the state and in individual state House of Representatives districts;<hr><ltbullet>establishes additional requirements to ensure the removal of deceased individuals from voter registration records;<hr><ltbullet>modifies penalties that may be imposed in relation to the unlawful disclosure of a voter registration record;<hr><ltbullet>places restrictions on the use and disclosure of information from the voter registration list;<hr><ltbullet>provides criminal penalties for unlawfully obtaining, using, or disclosing information from the voter registration list; <hr><ltbullet>provides that if a voter, whose voter registration record is classified as private due to the voter's status as an at-risk voter, signs a petition, the voter's voter identification and the date the voter signed the petition may be publicly disclosed to the same extent, and in the same manner, as the voter identification number and signature date of a voter signing the petition who does not have a private voter registration record;<hr><ltbullet>requires a petition to contain a warning regarding the provision described in the preceding paragraph;<hr><ltbullet>changes the person responsible for preparing the ballot title and analysis for a proposed constitutional amendment submitted to the voters;<hr><ltbullet>provides a coordination clause to merge provisions of this bill with H.B. 209, Voting Amendments, and H.B. 361, Elections Provisions Amendments; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: New Motorboat Distributor Act
description: This bill enacts the New Motorboat Distributor Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>grants the executive director of the Department of Commerce authority to administer and enforce the chapter and conduct adjudicative proceedings, issue cease-and-desist orders, and impose administrative fines of up to $1,000 per day for violations;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits certain coercive, unfair, or inequitable business practices by motorboat distributors;<hr><ltbullet>establishes standards governing the sale, transfer, and succession of motorboat dealerships;<hr><ltbullet>restricts termination, nonrenewal, relocation, or establishment of a motorboat dealership without good cause, notice, and opportunity for administrative review;<hr><ltbullet>establishes evidentiary standards for determining good cause;<hr><ltbullet>requires a distributor to provide written warranty, recall, and service policies and to reimburse a dealership;<hr><ltbullet>requires a distributor to compensate a dealership for incidental labor, administrative tasks, and on-water testing related to warranty and recall repairs;<hr><ltbullet>requires a distributor, upon termination or discontinuance, to repurchase certain inventory, parts, tools, equipment, signs, and related property;<hr><ltbullet>provides a private right of action for a violation of the chapter;<hr><ltbullet>governs changes in distribution plans;<hr><ltbullet>recognizes and limits sub-distributee agreements; and<hr><ltbullet>repeals the Motorboat Agreements Act.

title: Evaluations in Guardianship Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to guardianship.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that a person's rights under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 are not altered or abridged by Utah code provisions related to the rights of a person alleged to be incapacitated;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to the qualifications of a health care provider appointed by a court to assess an individual alleged to be incapacitated, and standards for the tools the health care professional uses for the assessment;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the court appointed health care professional's report must be filed with the court;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that a court appointed visitor's report must be filed with the court;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the court appointed health care provider may interview the person seeking to be appointed a guardian, but may not base the health care provider's assessment solely or predominately on that individual's opinion; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: School Construction Amendments
description: This bill transfers oversight of public school construction from the State Board of Education to the Division of Facilities Construction and Management (division).
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes permitting and inspection authority for the division regarding public school construction projects;<hr><ltbullet>repeals and reenacts sections related to state board coordination with the division;<hr><ltbullet>establishes educational facility planning requirements for a local education agency (LEA), including notification requirements;<hr><ltbullet>establishes public school construction oversight under the division;<hr><ltbullet>establishes division authority to adopt comprehensive construction rules covering square footage, safety, costs, and building standards;<hr><ltbullet>requires consultation with the state security chief on mandatory safety and security standards;<hr><ltbullet>creates architect and design professional cost oversight with benchmarks and review requirements;<hr><ltbullet>establishes plan review and approval authority for the division before construction can begin;<hr><ltbullet>sets mandatory technical compliance requirements including fire safety, accessibility, and energy codes;<hr><ltbullet>creates an online document management system for construction documentation and compliance tracking;<hr><ltbullet>establishes inspection verification and monitoring procedures with qualified inspector requirements;<hr><ltbullet>implements standardized cost reporting systems with detailed requirements and cost database development;<hr><ltbullet>requires an LEA to obtain division approval that projects fit within established cost matrices before construction;<hr><ltbullet>requires training and technical assistance programs including resource manuals and annual training conferences;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the division to delegate oversight authority to qualified school districts with demonstrated internal capacity; <hr><ltbullet>authorizes the division to establish a fee schedule to recover costs of oversight activities;<hr><ltbullet>designates a school construction liaison for coordination between the state board and division;<hr><ltbullet>allows division-managed construction services for a school district with fee structures and reimbursement requirements;<hr><ltbullet>creates enforcement and penalty provisions including administrative penalties up to $25,000 and mandatory compliance audits;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a qualified contractor and vendor registry for public school construction projects;<hr><ltbullet>requires an LEA to submit historical project information and documentation to the division upon request;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the division to establish a fee schedule to recover costs of oversight activities;<hr><ltbullet>provides the division with construction permitting authority;<hr><ltbullet>sets an implementation timeline requiring full compliance by January 1, 2027; and<hr><ltbullet>makes conforming changes.

title: Economic Mobility Initiative
description: This bill establishes a partnership to support community-based partnerships focused on educational and economic outcomes.

description: This bill modifies provisions related to reintegration and enrollment of students with disciplinary issues.

title: School Attendance Amendments
description: This bill modifies graduation requirements and provides services for high school students experiencing homelessness or involved in the child welfare system.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires local education agencies to offer diplomas based on the state baseline graduation standard;<hr><ltbullet>limits local graduation requirements for eligible students;<hr><ltbullet>requires acceptance of partial credits from various sources;<hr><ltbullet>exempts students from additional requirements when transferring schools;<hr><ltbullet>mandates academic support and personal graduation plans;<hr><ltbullet>restricts disciplinary removals for eligible students;<hr><ltbullet>establishes data collection and reporting requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires staff training and school point of contact designation; and<hr><ltbullet>creates rulemaking authority for implementation.

description: This bill ensures students meeting graduation requirements can participate in graduation ceremonies.

description: This bill modifies the Money Transmitter Act to regulate virtual currency kiosk operations.

title: Exercise of Religious Beliefs and Conscience Amendments
description: This bill addresses the right of a person to refuse to participate in certain activities relating to a health care service that violates the person's religious beliefs or conscience.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a health care provider has a right of religious belief or conscience that permits the health care provider to refuse to provide or participate in a health care service that violates the health care provider's religious beliefs or conscience;<hr><ltbullet>protects a person who exercises the person's right of religious belief or conscience from being held civilly, criminally, or administratively liable for exercising the right;<hr><ltbullet>requires a health care provider who refuses, under the right of religious belief or conscience, to participate in a health care service, to provide advance notice to the health care institution where the service is provided;<hr><ltbullet> prohibits discrimination or adverse action against a person in retaliation for the person exercising the person's right of religious belief or conscience;<hr><ltbullet>provides for certain government entities to investigate and take administrative action against a person regulated by the government entity who violates the provisions of this bill relating to the exercise of the right of religious belief or conscience;<hr><ltbullet>permits legal action, under certain circumstances, against a person who violates the provisions of this bill relating to the exercise of the right of religious belief or conscience; <hr><ltbullet>permits a health care provider, on the grounds of religious belief or conscience, to refuse to perform or participate in the disposal of remains from the termination of a pregnancy; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Wage Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions relating to wages.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires that an employer include information relating to wages and other compensation in a job listing;<hr><ltbullet>increases the minimum wage in the state to $20 per hour;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Labor Commission (commission) may not establish a minimum wage that is lower than $20 per hour;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the commission adjust the minimum wage for inflation at least once per year; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: School Discipline Amendments
description: This bill establishes minimum safety standards for seclusion rooms in schools.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes minimum physical standards for seclusion rooms including room size, ceiling height, construction materials, and structural integrity requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires proper lighting with fixtures located outside the room and controls that prevent student access;<hr><ltbullet>mandates adequate ventilation, heating, and cooling systems comparable to other school rooms;<hr><ltbullet>sets safety requirements including prohibition of dangerous objects, unbreakable windows, and specific door and locking mechanism standards;<hr><ltbullet>requires audio and video recording equipment that records all activities during seclusion;<hr><ltbullet>ensures compliance with federal and state student privacy laws;<hr><ltbullet>ensures compliance with state and local fire and building codes;<hr><ltbullet>applies standards to both existing seclusion rooms and any new school construction that includes seclusion rooms;<hr><ltbullet>gives the State Board of Education authority to adopt additional rules for safety standards, compliance verification, and  program administration;<hr><ltbullet>integrates the new standards into existing policy, documentation, and enforcement requirements; and<hr><ltbullet>makes conforming changes.

description: This bill addresses the admission of attorneys to county jail facilities.

title: Surveillance Camera Amendments
description: This bill concerns a law enforcement officer's ability to tamper with a surveillance camera on private property.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a law enforcement officer, or an individual acting on behalf of a law enforcement officer, from tampering with, changing the viewing direction of, or disabling a person's surveillance camera on the person's private property; and<hr><ltbullet>creates exceptions to the prohibition.

title: Justice System Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to the justice system.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that a city attorney may employ a deputy attorney to perform the duties of public prosecutor or civil counsel;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a city attorney may deputize, for a limited time or limited purpose, an attorney licensed to practice law in the state and in good standing with the Utah State Bar;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a court may enter a judgment of conviction for a lower degree of offense than established by statute if a defendant, within one year after sentencing, provides substantial assistance in the criminal investigation, arrest, or prosecution of another individual; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Renter Credit Reporting Amendments
description: This bill enacts provisions relating to renter credit reporting.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a housing authority shall provide a renter an offer of rent reporting at the time the housing authority and renter enter into a rental agreement;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a housing authority shall provide an offer of rent reporting at least once annually;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a housing authority may charge a fee for rent reporting that may not exceed the actual cost of the rent reporting;<hr><ltbullet>provides the consequences for a renter failing to pay the fee for rent reporting;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a renter may enroll and unenroll in rent reporting at any time during the duration of the rental agreement;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a renter from reenrolling in rent reporting for at least six months if the renter fails to pay the fee for rent reporting or the renter unenrolls in rent reporting; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Trailer Registration Amendments
description: This bill amends vehicle registration notification requirements and provides an option for a lifetime registration period for certain vehicles.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides an option for a registration period for a trailer for the lifetime of the person's ownership of the vehicle;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the calculation and deposit of registration and various other fees and taxes due at the time of registration to account for a lifetime vehicle registration period;<hr><ltbullet>imposes a penalty for fraudulently declaring a trailer as a commercial trailer; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Tow Yard Amendments
description: This bill codifies existing rules regarding state impound lot standards and creates a mandatory waiting period for a person removed from a towing rotation to rejoin a towing rotation in a first or second class county.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for an impound lot;<hr><ltbullet>allows the Motor Vehicle Division to review an impound lot's qualifications;<hr><ltbullet>creates procedures for retrieval of items from an impounded vehicle;<hr><ltbullet>creates a waiting period for a person removed from a towing rotation from being added to a towing rotation in a first or second class county with a new tow truck motor carrier; <hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause providing that substantive changes to Section 41-1a-1101 in this bill supersede the changes to that section in S.B. 120, Towing Modifications; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Legislative Activities Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to legislative activities.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the Legislative Management Committee (LMC) oversees workplace harassment and discrimination policy governance and updates references to that policy;<hr><ltbullet>modifies LMC's quorum and meeting requirements;<hr><ltbullet>provides that LMC shall oversee and develop policies governing branch-wide internal administrative matters for the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet>eliminates certain administrative duties of the presiding officer and the majority and minority leader of each chamber of the Legislature and the chairs of LMC;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the LMC Subcommittee on Oversight;<hr><ltbullet>provides that LMC policy governs the general counsel's representation of a legislative client before a court or administrative agency or tribunal;<hr><ltbullet>reorganizes and amends the legislative general counsel's responsibility to correct technical errors in legislation and the Utah Code;<hr><ltbullet>eliminates the Legislature's responsibility to print, store, and distribute the Utah Code Annotated;<hr><ltbullet>repeals a provision governing legislators who attend meetings of the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet>updates the definition of a legislative procurement unit to include the House of Representatives, the Senate, or a state office of the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet>repeals certain quinquennial reporting requirements applicable to legislative boards and the Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the president of the Senate and the speaker of the House of Representatives are vice chairs of the State Capitol Preservation Board (board);<hr><ltbullet>directs the board to make rules related to specified activities on capitol hill;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the board's authority to make rules to govern, administer, and regulate capitol hill does not restrict LMC's authority to adopt policies that govern the legislative area;<hr><ltbullet>provides that, if there is a conflict between a board rule and an LMC policy governing the legislative area, the LMC policy prevails;<hr><ltbullet>directs the executive director of the board to notify and consult with the president of the Senate and the speaker of the House of Representatives when a person appeals an administrative denial of a requested activity in the legislative area;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a bill summary by a staff member of the Senate or the House of Representatives, or by a staff office for the Legislature, is not evidence of legislative intent; and<hr><ltbullet>make technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill addresses state legal holidays and holy days.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>makes Good Friday a legal holiday in Utah;<hr><ltbullet>requires a school district, a charter school, and an institution of higher education to prioritize, to the extent possible, scheduling school breaks to coincide with state holy days;<hr><ltbullet>requires a government entity to place a high priority on approving an employee's request to take personal leave on a state holy day; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Election Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions relating to elections.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>beginning on January 1, 2027, prohibits a county clerk's or election officer's name from:<hr><ltbullet1>inclusion in the official endorsement for a ballot;<hr><ltbullet1>inclusion on a return envelope for a ballot; or<hr><ltbullet1>inclusion on a ballot, except to the extent that the county clerk or election officer is listed as a candidate on the ballot;<hr><ltbullet>enacts a temporary provision regarding the computation of time;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits certain action by a county clerk;<hr><ltbullet>requires the lieutenant governor to create a written conflict of interest avoidance plan;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the crime of electronic communications abuse of elections or elected office;<hr><ltbullet>subject to certain exceptions, provides that, when poll workers verify a voter's identity in relation to a ballot returned by mail, the poll workers are required to verify the signature on the affidavit in addition to the last four digits of an identification number;<hr><ltbullet>requires an incumbent county clerk who is running for reelection to contract with another county clerk to provide certain services in relation to verifying candidate signatures for the race;<hr><ltbullet>permits the use of campaign funds for certain goods or services relating to security; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Workforce Development
description: This bill establishes a statewide youth apprenticeship governance council and authorizes participation in the federal Workforce Pell Grant program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>modifies definitions;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the governor to delegate approval authority for eligible workforce programs to the Utah Board of Higher Education;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Department of Workforce Services to provide wage record data to the Utah Board of Higher Education;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the Utah Board of Higher Education to enter into interstate agreements;<hr><ltbullet>provides governmental immunity;<hr><ltbullet>classifies certain student data as protected records;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the Statewide Youth Apprenticeship Governance Council to coordinate youth apprenticeship programs across state agencies and education providers; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill amends provisions related to wrongful liens.

title: Transportation Funding and Governance Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to the governance of a large public transit district and financial reporting of public transit districts.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires public transit districts to provide an annual financial report to the Transportation and Infrastructure Appropriations Subcommittee;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the structure of the large public transit district board of trustees and changes the body to a transit commission;<hr><ltbullet>provides for selection process, appointment, and duties of the transit commission of a large public transit district;<hr><ltbullet>defines duties and reallocates certain responsibilities between the executive director and transit commission of a large public transit district;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the transition of the governance structure of a large public transit district;<hr><ltbullet>changes the appointment process for the executive director of a large public transit district to be appointed by the governor;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the requirement of a large public transit district to have a local advisory council; <hr><ltbullet>requires the State Tax Commission, beginning in fiscal year 2028, to annually deposit a certain amount of new growth derived from state sales and use taxes into the Transit Transportation Investment Fund; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Water Project Management Amendments
description: This bill creates an office within the Division of Water Resources for managing state water projects.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Office of Water Management (office) within the Division of Water Resources (division);<hr><ltbullet>establishes the duties of the office;<hr><ltbullet>provides for a water manager to administer the office;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the role of the water manager;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Water Resources Board to create a process for a political subdivision, special district, or state agency to nominate a water project for management by the office;<hr><ltbullet>requires the office to:<hr><ltbullet1>adopt a capital asset management plan; and <hr><ltbullet1>report to two legislative committees on the capital asset management plan no later than July 1, 2030, and every five years thereafter; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Tax Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions relating to tax.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates the Statewide Tax Administration and Technology Solutions program, which includes the following services: <hr><ltbullet1>maintenance and enhancement of the statewide property tax system, including statewide web portals;<hr><ltbullet1>provision of property valuation services;<hr><ltbullet1>valuation of personal property of telecommunications service providers;<hr><ltbullet1>participation in a study on the rate of a recovery fee for rentals of heavy equipment; and<hr><ltbullet1>collation of information from county auditors on project areas and from entities that seek to receive and receive tax increment financing;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the program manager;<hr><ltbullet>transfers responsibilities from the Multicounty Appraisal Trust (MCAT) to the program manager;<hr><ltbullet>transfers existing MCAT personal property and unexpended revenue to the program manager; <hr><ltbullet>imposes accounting and reporting obligations on the program manager; <hr><ltbullet>grants rulemaking authority to the State Tax Commission to establish the requirements for the statewide property tax system and for a county to comply with a factoring order;<hr><ltbullet>provides the conditions for a county to opt out of use of the statewide property tax system; <hr><ltbullet>beginning July 1, 2026, requires an entity intending to use tax increment to first:<hr><ltbullet1>conduct a public meeting; and<hr><ltbullet1>submit information to the program manager and notice to the taxing entities providing tax increment and the entities distributing tax increment;<hr><ltbullet>requires most types of entities that receive more revenue from tax increment than anticipated to use the revenue to pay off debt;<hr><ltbullet>requires an entity that receives tax increment to report annually to the program manager;<hr><ltbullet>excludes certain property valuation increases from the calculation of locally assessed new growth;<hr><ltbullet>excludes increases to the value of tangible personal property from the calculation of project area new growth;<hr><ltbullet>modifies definitions relating to public service districts to reflect the transition of land within the public service districts from unincorporated county to incorporated cities or towns since the public service districts formed; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Protection from Unfair Treatment Based on Religion or Other Irrelevant Characteristics
description: This bill prohibits, in relation to certain matters, unfair treatment based on a person's religion or other irrelevant characteristics.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits unfair treatment, by creditors or credit reporting agencies, based on a person's religion or other irrelevant characteristics;<hr><ltbullet>provides for administrative and legal enforcement of the provisions described in the preceding paragraph;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits unfair treatment by an insurer based on a person's religion or other irrelevant characteristics;<hr><ltbullet>provides for enforcement of the provisions described in the preceding paragraph;<hr><ltbullet>requires a local education agency to establish a policy granting an excused absence from school for a student to observe a religious holiday or attend religious instruction;<hr><ltbullet>requires a state institution of higher education to reasonably accommodate an individual's religious beliefs, faith, or conscience in relation to:<hr><ltbullet1>the state institution's admission process;<hr><ltbullet1>a student's attendance in class;<hr><ltbullet1>the scheduling of an examination or academic requirement; or<hr><ltbullet1>participation in a specific academic requirement; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill amends provisions related to vehicle emissions inspections to enhance the ability to investigate whether an individual has avoided a required emissions inspection.

title: Nicotine Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to products that contain nicotine.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>repeals provisions related to local health department inspections of electronic cigarette retailers;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to fees to be collected by the State Tax Commission for the sale of tobacco products, nicotine products, and electronic cigarette products;<hr><ltbullet>directs that certain fee money be used to dispose of confiscated electronic cigarette products and additional enforcement;<hr><ltbullet> amends provisions related to fines and license suspensions for selling products not listed on the electronic cigarette product registry; and<hr><ltbullet>amends criminal penalties related to the sale of a product containing nicotine.

title: Free Exercise of Religion Revisions
description: This bill amends provisions relating to an action brought for a violation of the free exercise of religion.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends the Governmental Immunity Act of Utah to clarify that the government waives immunity in relation to a cause of action described in Title 63G, Chapter 33, Free Exercise of Religion; and<hr><ltbullet>amends Title 63G, Chapter 33, Free Exercise of Religion, to clarify that a cause of action described in that chapter makes multiple types of relief available to a person that brings the action, including:<hr><ltbullet1>damages;<hr><ltbullet1>declaratory relief;<hr><ltbullet1>injunctive relief; and<hr><ltbullet1>all other types of legal relief.

description: This bill modifies the private cause of action for the payment of wages.

title: Local Food Amendments
description: This bill addresses provisions related to locally-produced foods.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines and modifies terms;<hr><ltbullet>removes a signage requirement for a direct-to-sale farmers market;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies when a producer or producer's designated representative may sell a homemade food product at a direct-to-sale location; <hr><ltbullet>provides that a producer retains ownership of a homemade food product distributed, sold, delivered, held, stored, or offered for sale by a designated representative unless otherwise agreed upon by the producer and designated representative; <hr><ltbullet>exempts from state sales tax food and food ingredients or prepared food sold by a home cook, including a homemade food product sold at a direct-to-sale farmers market or direct-to-sale location; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Constable Modifications
description: This bill regulates the practice of a constable.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the process by which a city or county may contract with a constable;<hr><ltbullet>beginning January 1, 2027, requires that an individual contracted by a municipality or county to act as a constable hold a constable license;<hr><ltbullet>enacts the Constables Licensing Act;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Constables Licensing Board (board);<hr><ltbullet>describes the membership, duties, and powers of the board;<hr><ltbullet>describes the duties of the Division of Professional Licensing in regard to individuals who apply for or receive licensure (licensees);<hr><ltbullet>provides an exemption from licensure for certain licensees performing certain services;<hr><ltbullet>describes unlawful and unprofessional conduct by a licensee or an unlicensed individual performing like a licensee;<hr><ltbullet>provides a disciplinary process;<hr><ltbullet>provides for state preemption of local regulation of constables; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Highway Signage Amendments
description: This bill amends certain restrictions on highway signage that is required to be relocated or remodeled because of the widening, construction, or reconstruction of a highway.

title: Public Corporation Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to the Utah Inland Port Authority and the State Fair Park Authority.

title: Fatal Motor Vehicle Accident Amendments
description: This bill addresses requirements for a chemical test of an individual involved in a motor vehicle accident.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires a peace officer to direct an individual to submit to a chemical test if the peace officer has reasonable suspicion that the individual was operating a vehicle in violation of certain alcohol or drug related offenses;<hr><ltbullet>requires a peace officer investigating a fatal motor vehicle accident to review the facts of the accident with a senior officer before declining to seek a warrant for a chemical test; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Punitive Damages Amendments
description: This bill enacts provisions relating to punitive damages.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>provides that an insurer may not rely on the existence, likelihood, possibility, or exposure to punitive damages when taking actions under Title 31A, Insurance Code;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances in which a court may award punitive damages against an employer, managing agent, or principal for the conduct of the employer's, managing agent's, or principal's employee or agent;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the provisions this bill enacts apply only to a claim arising after the effective date of the bill; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: State Employee Benefits Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to state employee benefits.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>beginning on a specified date, establishes a paid time off program under which the following employees receive paid time off in lieu of annual leave and sick leave:<hr><ltbullet1>new agency employees; and <hr><ltbullet1>current agency employees who elect to participate; <hr><ltbullet>for each current agency employee who elects to participate in the program, directs the Division of Finance to convert the employee's accrued annual leave hours to paid time off hours at a one-to-one ratio;<hr><ltbullet>grants the Division of Human Resources authority to make rules governing the accrual and use of paid time off;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the 401(k) match available to a qualifying employee who participates in the paid time off program by changing the match rate and increasing the maximum employer contribution; <hr><ltbullet>requires each agency to establish and administer a leave bank program; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Regulatory Impacts on Families
description: This bill requires state agencies, counties, municipalities, and local school boards to consider the impact of certain governmental actions on families.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires a state agency engaged in rulemaking to consider the impact a proposed rule may have on family health, stability, and formation;<hr><ltbullet>requires a state agency that reasonably expects a proposed rule to have a measurable negative impact on family health, stability, or formation to consider reasonable alternatives to reduce the impact;<hr><ltbullet>requires a county or municipal legislative body, before passing an ordinance, to consider the impact the proposed ordinance may have on family health, stability, and formation;<hr><ltbullet>specifies that a county or municipal legislative body's failure to comply with the requirement described above does not invalidate an ordinance enacted by the legislative body or create a cause of action;<hr><ltbullet>creates an exception to the family impact considerations described above for a county or municipal ordinance enacted in response to an emergency;<hr><ltbullet>requires a local school board, before adopting a policy or taking other formal action, to consider the impact the proposed rule or action may have on family health, stability, and formation; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Judicial Performance Evaluation Amendments
description: This bill makes changes related to the Judicial Performance Evaluation Commission.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends definitions;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers and reorganizes statutory provisions in Title 78A, Chapter 12, Judicial Performance Evaluation Commission;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the requirements for a meeting of the Judicial Performance Evaluation Commission (Commission);<hr><ltbullet>requires the Commission to perform a study regarding reversal on appeal and provide a report to the Judiciary Interim Committee on the study;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Commission to allow a judge to appear and speak at a commission meeting in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the requirements for the judicial performance survey, including the contents of the survey;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the certification standards for judicial performance, including the certification standards for a justice of the Utah Supreme Court and a judge of the Utah Court of Appeals; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Property Tax Exemption Process Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to the property tax exemption process.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes deadlines for:<hr><ltbullet1>a property owner to file an application with the county board of equalization for a property tax exemption; and<hr><ltbullet1>the county board of equalization to render a written decision on an application for a property tax exemption;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the county board of equalization to request additional information from an applicant for a property tax exemption, in addition to or in lieu of holding a hearing on the application;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the county board of equalization to revoke a property tax exemption if property no longer qualifies for an exemption;<hr><ltbullet>requires the county board of equalization to include notice of a property owner's appeal rights in a written decision regarding a property tax exemption; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Driver License Division and Motor Vehicle Division Consolidation Amendments
description: This bill requires the Department of Public Safety and the State Tax Commission to conduct a joint study regarding the feasibility of consolidating certain motor vehicle-related divisions under a single umbrella agency.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Public Safety and the State Tax Commission to jointly study the feasibility of combining the Motor Vehicle Division, the Motor Vehicle Enforcement Division, and the Driver License Division under a single umbrella agency;  <hr><ltbullet>requires the study to evaluate potential cost savings, efficiency gains, and improvements to customer experience;  <hr><ltbullet>requires a written report of findings and recommendations to the Transportation Interim Committee; and<hr><ltbullet>provides a repeal date.

title: Property Tax Adjustments
description: This bill modifies property tax provisions.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires residential property owners to apply to the county to receive a residential exemption if the property was ineligible for the residential exemption in the prior year, an ownership interest in the property changes, or the county has reason to believe the property no longer qualifies for the residential exemption;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies burden of proof requirements in appeals involving property assessed by the State Tax Commission;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the content and publication of the advertisement required for taxing entities to impose a judgment levy;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the requirements for taxing entities to impose judgment levies and increase property taxes through truth in taxation;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the time frame in which the State Tax Commission is required to certify a taxing entity's compliance with truth in taxation requirements; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: State Homeless Campus Amendments
description: This bill enacts provisions relating to a state homeless services campus.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines and amends terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires the coordinator for the Office of Homeless Services (coordinator), in cooperation with the Utah Homeless Services Board (board), to create a comprehensive plan for homeless services campus (campus) residents and the surrounding community within a certain time frame after announcing or recommending the location of a campus that addresses:<hr><ltbullet1>safety;<hr><ltbullet1>transportation;<hr><ltbullet1>use of the homeless services campus as an emergency shelter; <hr><ltbullet1>the types of treatment and support services offered to residents;<hr><ltbullet1>treatment and support service provider and staff requirements; and<hr><ltbullet1>other certain services;<hr><ltbullet>requires the coordinator, in cooperation with the board, to coordinate with certain public safety entities to receive incident reports created in response to certain services provided to the campus and the campus's residents, employees, or volunteers;<hr><ltbullet>requires the homeless services ombudsman (ombudsman) to conduct an investigation of the campus under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>allows the ombudsman to make recommendations and assist the coordinator in creating a remediation plan if a campus is found in violation of law;<hr><ltbullet>provides a certain time for the campus to cure a violation;<hr><ltbullet>allows the ombudsman to recommend that the campus cease operations under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Legislature may withhold campus funding in certain circumstances; <hr><ltbullet>gives the ombudsman rulemaking authority to implement and carry out a campus investigation; <hr><ltbullet>creates reporting requirements; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Higher Education Institutional Governance
description: This bill addresses roles and responsibilities of a higher education institution's board of trustees and president.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>consolidates and reorganizes general duties of boards of trustees for institutions of higher education;<hr><ltbullet>establishes certain aspects of the relationship between an institution's board of trustees and the institution's president, including:<hr><ltbullet1>organizational governance;<hr><ltbullet1>roles and responsibilities in the budgeting process;<hr><ltbullet1>faculty and personnel issues; and<hr><ltbullet1>presidential performance evaluation;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the authority of the board of trustees over internal audits of an institution;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions regarding a president's authority in relation to administrative roles, cabinet members, and the institution's general counsel;<hr><ltbullet>enacts provisions regarding the duties of an institution's legal counsel, including requiring the Board of Higher Education to make rules regarding the scope of the role of an institution's legal counsel;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits the president of an institution from retaining outside legal counsel for litigation;<hr><ltbullet>amends the membership of a technical college board of trustees with a service region containing a certain number of school districts;<hr><ltbullet>requires reporting of certain institutional compensation information;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding agencies hiring and paying for outside legal counsel rather than the attorney general; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Early Literacy
description: This bill establishes a framework of literacy interventions in kindergarten through grade 3 within the public education system.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a third-grade level reading goal for 2030;<hr><ltbullet>requires a local education agency (LEA) to, based on the student's performance on a benchmark reading assessment, provide a student with an individualized reading plan that identifies specific reading interventions to remediate a reading deficiency, including considering retention in lower grades and requiring retention in grade 3 except in cases of certain good cause exemptions;<hr><ltbullet>requires regional education service agencies and certain school districts to provide formal professional learning and information training in the science of reading;<hr><ltbullet>dedicates a certain amount of funding to provide literacy training and paraprofessionals who support literacy;<hr><ltbullet>requires certain school performance monitoring;<hr><ltbullet>excludes the practice of "three-cueing" from an LEA's reading curriculum;<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Board of Education (state board) to distribute funding to regional education service agencies and certain school districts for literacy coaching and training;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Utah Board of Higher Education to partner with the state board in certain duties regarding teacher preparation programs;<hr><ltbullet>requires the use of a certain portion of a school's allocation under the Teacher and Student Success Program on literacy interventions if the school's third grade students score below the statewide benchmark goal;<hr><ltbullet>includes science of reading and literacy as components of an elementary educator evaluation;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Center for the School of the Future at Utah State University, in collaboration with the Utah Board of Higher Education, to develop a plan to improve science of reading knowledge and ability in teacher graduates from a state institution of higher education; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Transportation Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to transportation, including road usage charge, towing dispatch, and local option sales tax use.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>allows a political subdivision to prohibit a mobile business from operating on a street or sidewalk that is temporarily closed for certain events;<hr><ltbullet>requires commercial electric vehicles with a gross weight of 6,001 pounds or more to pay a road usage charge with a higher road usage charge cap;<hr><ltbullet>exempts buses operating on the bus's planned route to temporarily cross lane lines to stop at a bus stop;<hr><ltbullet>exempts the Department of Transportation from certain requirements related to receiving a conveyance of real property;<hr><ltbullet>provides a sales tax exemption for construction materials purchased by the Department of Transportation for certain public transit capital development projects;<hr><ltbullet>amends certain allowed uses of local option sales taxes for transportation;<hr><ltbullet>increases bonding authorization related to commuter rail expansion;<hr><ltbullet>defines the Utah trail network;<hr><ltbullet>delegates certain authority to the executive director of the Department of Transportation during a natural disaster;<hr><ltbullet>requires local governments that receive funds from the County of the First Class Highway Projects Fund to report on the expenditure of funds and the progress of projects;<hr><ltbullet>allows the Transportation Commission to prioritize the use of Transit Transportation Investment Fund revenue for corridor preservation purposes and provides parameters for the use of the revenue;<hr><ltbullet>allows certain rail road transportation funds to be used to repair tracks and rail infrastructure located on state lands;<hr><ltbullet>allows the Department of Transportation to waive sovereign immunity for public transit projects;<hr><ltbullet>amends the definition of "state transportation purposes";<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to the ability to charge towing dispatch service fees and pass through a reasonable towing dispatch service fee;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the study required by the Department of Transportation and Salt Lake City regarding highway reduction strategies;<hr><ltbullet>codifies certain requirements based on the findings and results of the study on highway reduction strategies; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.
