title: Cardiac Emergency Response Plans in Schools
description: This bill establishes requirements for cardiac emergency response plans in schools.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires each school to develop a cardiac emergency response plan;<hr><ltbullet>requires plans to include evidence-based core elements for emergency cardiovascular care;<hr><ltbullet>requires appropriate placement and maintenance of automated external defibrillators (AED);<hr><ltbullet>requires training of appropriate school staff in first aid, CPR, and AED use;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a grant program to aid in implementing cardiac emergency response plans; and<hr><ltbullet>requires the State Board of Education to make rules.

title: Child Care Expansion Act
description: This bill enacts the Employer-Based, State-Assisted Child Care Capacity Expansion Program to expand available high quality child care in the state.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>describes the purpose of the Employer-Based, State-Assisted Child Care Capacity Expansion Program (program);<hr><ltbullet>requires coordination between the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity and certain other state agencies to implement certain provisions of the program;<hr><ltbullet>permits the Division of Facilities and Construction Management (DFCM) to enter into leases with certain employers for an expanded child care facility;<hr><ltbullet>provides for provisions for certain employers who lease a facility from DFCM to enter into a contract with a certain child care provider for child care;<hr><ltbullet>requires DFCM to be responsible for operations and maintenance of an expanded child care facility; <hr><ltbullet>provides for rulemaking authority under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>provides for limitations on state liability regarding operations of a child care opportunity facility; <hr><ltbullet>creates the Child Care Capacity Expansion Restricted Account to receive certain funds and lease payments, which funds shall be nonlapsing and used: <hr><ltbullet1>for certain purposes to implement the provisions of the program; and<hr><ltbullet1>by DFCM for payment of operations and maintenance costs associated with the program;<hr><ltbullet>requires an annual report; and <hr><ltbullet>provides intent language that provides for capital improvement funds appropriated for fiscal year 2027 shall be used by DFCM to retrofit warehouse space in an existing State Tax Commission building into a childcare facility for purposes of the Employer-Based, State-Assisted Child Care Capacity Expansion Program.

title: Public Employee Negotiation Amendments
description: This bill addresses collective bargaining for public employees.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the Labor Relations Board (board);<hr><ltbullet>describes the composition and duties of the board;<hr><ltbullet>describes the entities the board may employ;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the board's rulemaking authority;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the board to subpoena witnesses and administer oaths;<hr><ltbullet>establishes who may serve as counsel for public employers and the board;<hr><ltbullet>creates protections for public employees regarding self-organization;<hr><ltbullet>allows a public employer to deduct an employee's dues for a collective bargaining unit from an employee's pay;<hr><ltbullet>requires that labor organizations represent employees without discrimination;<hr><ltbullet>requires that the board investigate a petition on a representation question under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>establishes criteria and the function of a representation election at the direction of the board;<hr><ltbullet>establishes who may represent a public employer in collective bargaining;<hr><ltbullet>establishes management rights of a public employer;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a duty to bargain collectively for both the public employer and an exclusive representative;<hr><ltbullet>describes what a collective bargaining agreement shall contain;<hr><ltbullet>permits and describes the mediation of disputes relating to collective bargaining;<hr><ltbullet>describes how to initiate fact finding relating to a dispute regarding collective bargaining;<hr><ltbullet>establishes fact finding proceedings in a dispute related to collective bargaining;<hr><ltbullet>allows arbitration for a dispute resulting from collective bargaining;<hr><ltbullet>requires the board to establish an education course for fact finders and arbitrators;<hr><ltbullet>describes an unfair labor practice of a public employer;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the process by which an unfair labor practice is investigated and resolved;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a hearing process for an unfair labor practice complaint hearing;<hr><ltbullet>describes the process of the court enforcement and review of a board order;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits police officers from engaging in strikes;<hr><ltbullet>establishes criteria for mediation of a dispute under certain circumstances; and<hr><ltbullet>establishes the criteria for arbitration under certain circumstances.

title: Library Materials Amendments
description: This bill enacts provisions related to requirements in a public school library.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires a local education agency (LEA) to adopt a policy that governs practices related to:<hr><ltbullet1>library development;<hr><ltbullet1>collection of library instructional material; and<hr><ltbullet1>reconsideration of library instructional material;<hr><ltbullet>allows an individual to submit a request for reconsideration of certain material;<hr><ltbullet>requires a digital resource provider to provide certain services related to library instructional material;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an LEA from:<hr><ltbullet1>retaliating against educational professionals in certain situations; and<hr><ltbullet1>tracking certain student data; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Extracted Natural Resources Amendments
description: This bill addresses natural resources within the state.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>facilitates faster permitting by the Department of Environmental Quality and the Division of Oil, Gas, and Mining;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the tax credit for mining exploration;<hr><ltbullet>creates the State Reinvestment Restricted Account and diverts various streams of income related to severance taxes into the State Reinvestment Restricted Account;<hr><ltbullet>addresses property tax differentials based on critical minerals zones;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the state critical minerals objectives and policy, including providing for annual reviews;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Critical Minerals Council (council), including establishing the council's operations, powers, and duties;<hr><ltbullet>makes money appropriated to the council nonlapsing;<hr><ltbullet>addresses areas of coordination by certain council members;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a process to designate critical minerals zones, including providing for property tax differential revenue;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the creation of a clearinghouse of data to be known as the "Critical Minerals Atlas";<hr><ltbullet>addresses the creation of the Minerals for Industrial, National, and Economic Security Center;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Critical Minerals Development Account;<hr><ltbullet>coordinates with H.B. 373, Higher Education Innovation, to address inclusion of critical minerals projects in the eligible research areas for research grants; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming amendments.

title: Identity Protection Modifications
description: This bill amends provisions related to libel and slander to address artificial intelligence and digitally manipulated content.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that defamation law applies to content created through artificial intelligence or other technological means;<hr><ltbullet>requires notice to a publisher before filing a defamation action based on digitally created content;<hr><ltbullet>limits recovery to actual damages if the publisher removes the content within 10 days after receiving notice; <hr><ltbullet>establishes an exclusive right to consent to the use of an individual's personal identity; <hr><ltbullet>expands the definition of abuse of personal identity to include unauthorized distribution and trafficking in identity-replication tools; <hr><ltbullet>provides exemptions for certain uses of personal identity; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Domestic Relations Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to domestic relations.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends definitions for, and the use of, "parent" and "natural parent" throughout the Utah Code to reflect the definition of a parent-child relationship under Title 81, Chapter 5, Uniform Parentage Act;<hr><ltbullet>creates definitions related to the definition of "parent";<hr><ltbullet>requires the Office of Recovery Services to review the requirements for calculating a minimal child support award for a child support order and to report to the Judiciary Interim Committee regarding the review;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies language regarding the parent-child relationship for purposes of intestate succession;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the district court of each judicial district assign any case or proceeding involving the same child or family to a single judge;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the requirements for a marriage license with regard to parties that are not physically present in the state in the same location as the officiant;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a man is not presumed to be the father of a child in certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the authority of a court to deny a motion for genetic testing, or disregard genetic test results, in a parentage proceeding;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms related to child support;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the inclusion of Social Security Disability Insurance in the calculation of the gross income of a parent for purposes of child support;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the requirements for child care expenses in a child support order, including the requirements for a minimal child care award;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the base child support award is automatically adjusted for the remaining children in the child support order when parental rights to a child are terminated for the parent who is obligated to pay child support;<hr><ltbullet>creates a table for the purposes of establishing a minimal child care award for certain child support orders entered or modified on or after January 1, 2027;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the list of offenses requiring notification when a parent is residing with an individual, or providing an individual with access to the parent's minor child, who has been convicted of an offense;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a court may not require a parent in a custody and parent-time proceeding to disclose the parent's address if the parent relocated due to domestic violence or family violence by the other parent;<hr><ltbullet>addresses the establishment and modification of a parent-time schedule;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the list of offenses related to when a court may order supervised parent-time;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies, for purposes of modifying custody due to a substantial and material change, the list of offenses for when a parent is residing with an individual, or providing an individual with access to the parent's minor child, and the parent knows that the individual has been convicted of an offense;<hr><ltbullet>addresses a change of custody or parent-time for a minor child who turns five years old;<hr><ltbullet>addresses make-up parent-time when a parent has been denied parent-time due to an investigation by the Division of Child and Family Services;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the parent-time requirements upon the relocation of a parent;<hr><ltbullet>addresses telephone contact and virtual parent-time for a noncustodial parent when a parent relocates;<hr><ltbullet>requires the time periods for extended parent-time by a parent for summer break or off-track time to be consecutive;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the parent-time schedules to address consistency issues;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the parent-time schedules for Mother's Day and Father's Day;<hr><ltbullet>removes Columbus Day and Veterans Day as holidays in the parent-time schedules;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the list of offenses regarding when a court cannot grant custody to an individual who is convicted, pleads guilty, or pleads no contest to an offense;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming corrections;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to modify a term if this bill and H.B. 30, Human Trafficking, Exploitation, and Smuggling Amendments, both pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to address a substantive conflict with the parent-time schedule for Juneteenth National Freedom Day if this bill and H.B. 309, Juneteenth Observance Amendments, both pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet>includes a coordination clause to address make-up parent-time requirements in H.B. 304, Protective Order Amendments.

title: Infant at Work Amendments
description: This bill makes permanent the Infant at Work Program and expands the program to other executive branch agencies.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>makes permanent the Infant at Work Program (program) available for Department of Health and Human Services (department) employees and removes obsolete pilot-related references;<hr><ltbullet>repeals the June 30, 2026 sunset date for the program;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes an executive branch agency to opt-in to the program by submitting written notice from the agency head to the Division of Human Resource Management (division);<hr><ltbullet>makes an agency's participation in the program subject to division approval;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the division to withdraw or revoke an agency's approval if the agency's participation is detrimental to the program's administration or the agency's work environment;<hr><ltbullet>requires an agency that participates in the program to:<hr><ltbullet1>adopt a written participation policy; and<hr><ltbullet1>determine whether an employee of the agency may participate in the program based on workplace considerations;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the division to adopt rules to administer the program;<hr><ltbullet>adds a July 1, 2029 repeal date, subject to review by a legislative interim committee; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Evidence Declaration Amendments
description: This bill requires a signed statement regarding evidence collected in a criminal case for a felony offense.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires certain individuals to sign a statement that evidence of a felony offense was obtained or provided in compliance with state and federal law;<hr><ltbullet>requires a prosecuting attorney to sign a statement regarding evidentiary disclosures in a criminal case for a felony offense; and<hr><ltbullet>makes it a crime to fail to comply with the requirements of a signed statement.

title: Dangerous Weapons at Institutions of Higher Education
description: This bill addresses dangerous weapons at institutions of higher education.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>authorizes an institution of higher education to make rules and regulations regarding the carrying or possession of firearms at the institution of higher education;<hr><ltbullet>expands the offense of carrying a dangerous weapon at an institution of higher education to include carrying, possessing, or storing a dangerous weapon in a dormitory located on higher education grounds; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Pharmacy Practice Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to the practice of pharmacy.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends the definition of a collaborative pharmacy practice agreement to conform to other provisions of code regarding a pharmacist's role under a collaborative pharmacy practice agreement;<hr><ltbullet>adds vaccines and epinephrine to the list of prescription drugs that a pharmacist may prescribe; <hr><ltbullet>permits online sales of pseudoephedrine under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Professional Licensing, in collaboration with the Board of Pharmacy, to approve and implement an electronic tracking system to monitor the sale of pseudoephedrine under certain circumstances; <hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Uniform Community Property Disposition at Death Act Amendments
description: This bill enacts the Uniform Community Property Disposition at Death Act.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>specifies which personal and real property is treated as community property at death based on the domicile of the spouses and the law of the jurisdiction where the property was acquired;<hr><ltbullet>excludes property that spouses partition, reclassify, or waive by agreement;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for how community-property spouses may partition, reclassify, or waive rights to community property;<hr><ltbullet>creates a presumption that property acquired while domiciled in a community-property jurisdiction is community property unless rebutted by a preponderance of the evidence;<hr><ltbullet>provides that one-half of community property belongs to the surviving community-property spouse and one-half belongs to the decedent and is subject to disposition at death;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that a decedent's share of community property is not subject to the elective-share right of the surviving community-property spouse;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a court to apply equitable principles and consider the law of other jurisdictions when resolving community-property claims at death;<hr><ltbullet>establishes time limits and procedures for claims brought by a surviving community-property spouse, an heir, a devisee, and a nonprobate transferee;<hr><ltbullet>protects third parties who transact in good faith and for value with a community-property spouse or estate representative;<hr><ltbullet>directs the court to construe the chapter to promote uniformity with other states that enact the uniform act;<hr><ltbullet>includes saving, transitional, and severability provisions; and<hr><ltbullet>repeals the existing Utah Code provisions governing community-property disposition at death and replaces the provisions with the new uniform chapter.

title: County Governance Revisions
description: This bill modifies the power and duties of a county manager.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>vests the executive powers of a county in the county council in a council-manager form of government;<hr><ltbullet>limits the powers, functions, and duties a county council may delegate to a county manager;<hr><ltbullet>limits the terms of an employment contract with a county manager;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an unelected county employee from exercising the powers, functions, and duties of an elected county executive or county officer; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Software in Education Amendments
description: This bill requires the State Board of Education (state board) to study best practices regarding the use of software in public schools.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>requires the state board to:<hr><ltbullet1>conduct a study regarding the use of software and digital services in public schools;<hr><ltbullet1>review best practices related to the educational effectiveness, design, and data practices of software that students use;<hr><ltbullet1>publish guidance describing best practices for the responsible use of software in a public school; and<hr><ltbullet1>upon request, report the findings of the study to the Education Interim Committee; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the Office of Interscholastic Activities (office) within the State Board of Education (state board) to govern interscholastic activities and provides the office's duties;<hr><ltbullet>allows the office to contract with a private association to carry out certain functions regarding operation of interscholastic activities;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding the scope of authority of an activities association;<hr><ltbullet>establishes an advisory council and provides the council's duties;<hr><ltbullet>requires reporting to the state board and the Education Interim Committee; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: License Plate Amendments
description: This bill amends provisions related to license plate design, special group and standard license plates, and procedures for creating and changing license plate designs.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms related to license plates;<hr><ltbullet>changes the process for the design and issuance of standard license plates;<hr><ltbullet>creates a rotating process for issuance of standard license plate options;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to the visibility and readability of license plates, including replacement of faded license plates;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to required contributions for special group license plates, including allocation of funds generated;<hr><ltbullet>changes the process for creation of a new special group license plate and eligibility of the sponsor;<hr><ltbullet>amends the design and approval process for special group license plates;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to the design review board, including duties and membership;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to the State Tax Commission's contract with a license plate designer;<hr><ltbullet>requires driver license and identification card designs to be approved by the design review board; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: State-Endorsed Digital Identity Program Amendments
description: This bill creates the State-Endorsed Digital Identity Program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a digital identity bill of rights; <hr><ltbullet>creates the State-Endorsed Digital Identity Program within the Department of Government Operations;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for state-endorsed digital identities; <hr><ltbullet>adds a state-endorsed digital identity as an acceptable form of proof of age;<hr><ltbullet>establishes application and eligibility requirements for obtaining a state-endorsed digital identity; <hr><ltbullet>establishes identity proofing standards; <hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for governmental entities, health care providers, digital wallet providers, verifiers, and relying parties; <hr><ltbullet>creates a duty of loyalty related to processing identity attributes;<hr><ltbullet>provides for complaint and enforcement procedures;<hr><ltbullet>provides for a one-time audit by the Office of the Legislative Auditor General;<hr><ltbullet>provides for coordination with state agencies on use cases for the state-endorsed digital identity program;<hr><ltbullet>provides for severability;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the repeal of the electronic license certificate or identification card upon sunset review; and <hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Veteran Organization Amendments
description: This bill addresses veteran organizations that are exempt from federal income taxation (tax exempt veteran organizations).
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>extends benefits to tax exempt veteran organizations that are otherwise available for other tax exempt entities, including eligibility to:<hr><ltbullet1>claim a sales and use tax exemption for sales derived from the organization's charitable activities;<hr><ltbullet1> receive excess contributions from individuals and entities that are subject to campaign contribution limits;<hr><ltbullet1>obtain donations from state agencies and assist state agencies in administering relief programs; and<hr><ltbullet1>acquire conservation easements;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that for purposes of statutory construction, the terms "charitable," "nonprofit," and "not-for-profit," in relation to an entity, include both tax exempt veteran organizations and other tax exempt entities unless otherwise excluded in statute; and<hr><ltbullet> makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Utah Homes Investment Program Amendments
description: This bill modifies provisions related to the Utah Homes Investment Program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>expands the projects for which a qualified depository may offer loan financing to a developer or city under the Utah Homes Investment Program (program) to include:<hr><ltbullet1>multi-family housing development projects that meet specified criteria;<hr><ltbullet1>affordable rental projects;<hr><ltbullet1>acquisition of housing development projects that meet specified criteria; and<hr><ltbullet1>city-operated programs that provide low-interest loans to income-eligible homeowners to make improvements;<hr><ltbullet>allows a municipality with an eligible shelter to obtain financing through the program;<hr><ltbullet>following the end of the program, directs the state treasurer to complete a study that analyzes the economic effect of the program;<hr><ltbullet>allows the state treasurer to contract with a third party to complete the study;<hr><ltbullet>removes the limitation on the rate at which a qualified depository may offer loan financing to a developer or city; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Development Authority Modifications
description: This bill deals with the Point of the Mountain State Land Authority.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a municipality to coordinate with a state agency, independent entity, or regional economic development authority with exclusive control over the management, development, and disposition of a parcel of state-owned land in order to ensure future alignment with municipal general plans and land use regulations;<hr><ltbullet>requires a public infrastructure district created by a development authority to have a majority of the public infrastructure district's board members appointed by the governing body of the development authority, subject to exceptions;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a public infrastructure district created by a development authority that issues a bond may not issue additional or subsequent bonds but may refinance bonds one time;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Point of the Mountain State Land Authority (authority) may coordinate with Draper when the authority intends to dispose of a parcel of point of the mountain state land to a private party;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the distribution percentages of privilege tax to the authority for certain parcels of point of the mountain state land;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the percentage of property tax augmentation that shall be distributed to the authority for certain transferred parcels;<hr><ltbullet>reduces the percentage of state sales and tax revenue the State Tax Commission is directed to distribute to the authority;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a borrower to request and the Division of Finance to consider an amendment to a loan agreement to extend or forgive a loan made from certain infrastructure revolving loan funds;<hr><ltbullet>repeals a sunset date and creates a sunset date; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Local Land and Water Modifications
description: This bill modifies provisions related to local land use and water
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends requirements for a modified feasibility request related to a proposed municipal incorporation;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies standards for county and municipal land use regulations and requirements;<hr><ltbullet>modified requirements for an ordinance establishing a planning commission;<hr><ltbullet>modifies planning commission powers and duties;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the process for reviewing and approving a new or unlisted business use;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements for regulating structure height;<hr><ltbullet>requires a county or municipal legislative body to make a decision on proposed land use regulation if the planning commission fails to make a timely recommendation;<hr><ltbullet>requires counties, municipalities, and special districts to adopt a written plan, beginning on January 1, 2028, for determining the reasonable future water requirement of the public before imposing a water exaction (written plan);<hr><ltbullet>requires the state engineer to make rules to establish standards for the written plan; <hr><ltbullet>addresses exaction for water and a land use authority's review of a land use application;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the requirement to place certain infrastructure completion assurances in an interest-bearing account;<hr><ltbullet>establishes requirements relating to development agreements;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the burden of proving that a land use authority's decision was arbitrary, capricious, or illegal;<hr><ltbullet>addresses requirements relating to an appeal or variance hearing;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a legislative body from acting as an appeal authority;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the standard of review of a land use authority's decision to deny or approve a land use application;<hr><ltbullet>modifies appeal requirements; <hr><ltbullet>requires a specified municipality to allow a detached accessory dwelling unit as a permitted use in certain zones;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies notice requirements for a proposed county land use ordinance that is ministerial in nature;<hr><ltbullet>modifies a county's authority to deny an applicant a building permit or certificate of occupancy if the applicant has not completed an infrastructure improvement; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Targeted Advertising Tax
description: This bill imposes a tax on targeted advertising in the state.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>imposes an annual tax on entities that deliver targeted advertising in Utah and meet certain revenue thresholds, based on the entity's gross receipts from targeted advertising in the state;<hr><ltbullet>requires entities subject to the tax to annually remit a return to the State Tax Commission that includes information related to the tax;<hr><ltbullet>provides for administration and collection of the tax by the State Tax Commission;<hr><ltbullet>provides rulemaking authority to the State Tax Commission for administration of the tax;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the Targeted Advertising Restricted Account (restricted account) for the deposit of tax revenue;<hr><ltbullet>provides for the use of money deposited into the restricted account; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Medicaid Provider Amendments
description: This bill addresses provisions related to Medicaid providers.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires the Department of Health and Human Services (department) to:<hr><ltbullet1>establish quality measures for evaluating certain Medicaid providers' performance; <hr><ltbullet1>evaluate certain Medicaid providers on performance as measured by the quality measures; and<hr><ltbullet1>annually report to the Social Services Appropriations Subcommittee on the performance based on the quality measures of the Medicaid providers determined by the Legislature;<hr><ltbullet>requires the department to implement a closed loop referral system for referrals for the delivery of health-related social needs care to Medicaid-eligible individuals;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Services for People with Disabilities (division) to notify a provider of amendments to the provider's contract with the division;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

description: This bill amends a student's eligibility for state-supported transportation.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends a student's eligibility for state-supported transportation;<hr><ltbullet>requires a school district that receives certain transportation funds to provide transportation to certain students;<hr><ltbullet>allows a parent to petition a school district;<hr><ltbullet>allows the state board to designate certain transportation funds for a specific purpose; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Autonomous Systems Amendments
description: This bill amends and enacts provisions related to product liability for automated driving systems.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>amends and enacts definitions related to automated driving systems and product liability;<hr><ltbullet>imposes a statutory limit on awards of noneconomic loss in product liability cases related to automated driving systems;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions related to product defects and liability related to automated driving systems and reasonably alternative technologies available at the time of manufacture;<hr><ltbullet>creates an affirmative defense against product liability if certain state-of-the-art technology standards are met;<hr><ltbullet>limits liability of certain automated driving system manufacturers and developers to certain types of claims; <hr><ltbullet>requires a sunset review of provisions related to liability of automated driving systems and vehicles; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Consumer Pricing Data Amendments
description: This bill enacts provisions related to consumer pricing.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>enacts Title 13, Chapter 82, Consumer Pricing Act;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the Division of Consumer Protection (division) shall administer and enforce Title 13, Chapter 82, Consumer Pricing Act;<hr><ltbullet>subject to certain exceptions, provides that a supplier may not use a consumer's data to set the price of a good or a service;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a supplier may use a consumer's data to operate a loyalty program or offer discounts to the customer;<hr><ltbullet>provides that if a supplier uses an automatic pricing system, the supplier shall retain the data the automatic pricing system uses to set prices for at least three years;<hr><ltbullet>provides the enforcement mechanisms the division may use; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Intellectual Diversity in Education and Government
description: This bill amends and enacts provisions regarding intellectual diversity within the public and higher education systems and state government.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding prohibited discriminatory practices, submissions, and training within the public and higher education systems and state government, including reporting requirements;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions regarding curricular and noncurricular clubs within the public education system, including ensuring objective and uniform treatment of noncurricular clubs;<hr><ltbullet>provides that existing prohibitions on a discriminatory practice does not restrict a presentation or instruction by a guest lecturer in an academic course or a speaker who speaks at an institution of higher education by invitation;<hr><ltbullet>requires each institution of higher education to:<hr><ltbullet1>organize certain events on public policy issues, including debates and representation of differing perspectives; and<hr><ltbullet1>provide public accessibility and transparency through event calendars; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Student Consent Amendments
description: This bill enacts provisions related to a student's educational data and informed consent.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>enacts certain rights regarding student data;<hr><ltbullet>requires an education entity and institution of higher education to:<hr><ltbullet1>disclose student data under certain circumstances;<hr><ltbullet1>offer a secure, digital mechanism for obtaining informed consent; and<hr><ltbullet1>follow certain procedures when obtaining a student's informed consent;<hr><ltbullet>allows an education entity and an institution of higher education to impose certain limitations;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits an education entity and an institution of higher education from:<hr><ltbullet1>restricting a student's ability to grant informed consent;<hr><ltbullet1>requiring a student to waive certain rights; or<hr><ltbullet1>imposing certain limitations on a student's informed consent;<hr><ltbullet>requires a parent to provide informed consent on behalf of the parent's minor student;<hr><ltbullet>creates a private right of action; and<hr><ltbullet>allows the State Board of Education and the Utah Board of Higher Education to issue best practices for informed consent.

title: Programmable Money Amendments
description: This bill modifies the Uniform Commercial Code.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>excludes programmable money from the standard definition of money;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits a person from requiring the use of programmable money for a transaction unless the person also offers a free, non-digital alternative;<hr><ltbullet>outlaws an issuer denying a transaction based on discriminatory criteria, including a person's political opinions, religious beliefs, medical history, or lawful ownership of a firearm;<hr><ltbullet>prevents an issuer from using environmental, social, or governance standards and diversity programming compliance as a basis for failing or restricting a transaction;<hr><ltbullet>requires an issuer to provide a detailed written statement of the specific reason for a denied transaction or terminated service within 30 days of an affected party's request;<hr><ltbullet>grants an aggrieved party the right to seek punitive damages or the revocation of an issuer's business authorization; and<hr><ltbullet>does not prohibit the purchase or sale of cryptocurrency or other assets by public or private parties.

title: Single Payer Health Insurance Amendments
description: This bill establishes a state operated health financing program.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>establishes a state operated health financing program;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Utah Health Services Commission;<hr><ltbullet>establishes duties for the Utah Health Services Commission;<hr><ltbullet>moves health workforce councils and offices from the Department of Health and Human Services to the Utah Health Services Commission;<hr><ltbullet>directs the Department of Health and Human Services to begin transitioning the operation and management of the Medicaid program to the state operated health financing program;<hr><ltbullet>transitions the Public Employees' Benefit and Insurance Program into a state operated health financing program that is open to the public;<hr><ltbullet>allows all state residents to enroll in the state operated health financing program;<hr><ltbullet>prohibits billing by health care facilities;<hr><ltbullet>requires the state operated health financing program to begin billing on behalf of health care facilities;<hr><ltbullet>requires all government entities to transition government employees to the state operated health financing program;<hr><ltbullet>repeals certain unnecessary or obsolete programs; and<hr><ltbullet>creates a tax to fund the state operated health financing program.

title: Protective Order Amendments
description: This bill addresses protective orders.

title: Single-family Home Rental Modifications
description: This bill addresses rentals of single-family homes.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms, including "single-family home";<hr><ltbullet>establishes a registration requirement for owners, including property managers, of single-family homes used for rental;<hr><ltbullet>imposes a penalty for failure to register;<hr><ltbullet>requires notice of the registration requirement to be included with the 2026 property valuation notice;<hr><ltbullet>subjects an owner of 25 or more single-family homes used for rental to an excise tax per home;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Division of Real Estate to provide owners who register with information about the excise tax and to share information about registered property with the county assessors for purposes of verifying eligibility for the primary residential exemption;<hr><ltbullet>creates a competitive grant program for a municipality to obtain funding to transition single-family homes to owner-occupied homes;<hr><ltbullet>schedules the repeal of the registration requirement, the excise tax, and the grant program but requires legislative review before repeal; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Public Employee Attorney Fee Recovery Amendments
description: This bill amends a provision of law relating to the recovery of reasonable attorney fees and court costs incurred by an officer or employee of a public entity, under certain circumstances, to defend against criminal charges brought against the officer or employee in relation to the officer's or employee's public employment.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>clarifies and restates an existing provision of law entitling an officer or employee of a public entity to recover reasonable attorney fees and courts costs, under certain circumstances, for defending against criminal charges arising out of the officer's or employee's service or employment;<hr><ltbullet>modifies an exception under current law that prohibits the recovery of attorney fees and court costs described in the preceding paragraph if the charges are quashed or dismissed upon application or motion of the prosecuting attorney, by limiting the exception to circumstances where the quashing or dismissal occurs more than 45 days after the day on which the charges are bound over for trial as a result of a preliminary hearing;<hr><ltbullet>makes the modification described in the preceding paragraph only in relation to charges brought by filing an information; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical changes.

title: Opioid Terminology Amendments
description: This bill addresses terminology related to opioids.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>makes the following changes throughout the code and makes related, conforming changes:<hr><ltbullet1> changes the defined term "opiate" to "opioid-like substance";<hr><ltbullet1>changes the defined term "opiate antagonist" to "opioid antagonist"; and<hr><ltbullet1>changes the defined term "opiate-related drug overdose event" to "opioid-related drug overdose event";<hr><ltbullet>changes the term "opiate" to "substance" in the description of certain controlled substances;<hr><ltbullet>includes coordination clauses to coordinate changes in this bill and H.B. 301, Drug Recodification, S.B. 87 Naloxone Amendments, and S.B. 98 Substance Use Rehabilitation Amendments;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Health Insurance Preauthorization Amendments
description: This bill amends requirements for health insurance preauthorization.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires an insurer to post certain information regarding preauthorizations and preauthorization requirements on the insurer's website;<hr><ltbullet>requires an insurer to disclose whether the insurer uses artificial intelligence in the process of reviewing a request for authorization;<hr><ltbullet>defines a maximum time in which an insurer is required to make an authorization or adverse preauthorization determination;<hr><ltbullet>provides minimum periods that an authorization must be valid for health care services to treat chronic or long-term care conditions;<hr><ltbullet>amends requirements for reporting to the Insurance Department related to preauthorization statistics, including information related to prescription drugs;<hr><ltbullet>requires an individual reviewing an adverse preauthorization determination to use independent medical judgment and not rely solely on recommendations from any other source;<hr><ltbullet>requires an insurer to provide certain information in a notice regarding an adverse preauthorization determination;<hr><ltbullet>defines terms; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Municipal Election Amendments
description: This bill establishes annual year-end campaign finance reporting for municipal candidates until campaign account dissolution.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>requires a municipal office candidate to file a year-end campaign finance summary report (year-end report) with the municipal clerk no later than January 10 of the year after the municipal general election is held;<hr><ltbullet>establishes the required contents of a year-end report, including totals of contributions and expenditures;<hr><ltbullet>requires a municipal office candidate to continue filing a year-end report each January 10 until the candidate files a statement of campaign account dissolution and final summary report showing a zero account balance;<hr><ltbullet>specifies how a municipal office candidate may spend down a campaign account;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes the municipal clerk or recorder to impose a $250 fine against a candidate who fails to file a year-end report;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes a municipality to adopt an ordinance imposing more stringent year-end reporting requirements; and<hr><ltbullet>makes conforming changes.

title: Educational Technology Regulatory Sandbox
description: This bill creates an educational technology regulatory sandbox within the public education system.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates the Educational Technology Regulatory Sandbox; <hr><ltbullet>establishes minimum standards for artificial intelligence use in public education; <hr><ltbullet>coordinates with the Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy;<hr><ltbullet>assigns pilot administration to the Office of Regulatory Relief; <hr><ltbullet>establishes an Education Technology Advisory Council; <hr><ltbullet>limits the State Board of Education's role in pilot application approval;<hr><ltbullet>provides for state board safety and privacy enforcement; <hr><ltbullet>requires vendor safety testing through red teaming; <hr><ltbullet>requires evidence-based evaluation; <hr><ltbullet>requires state board review and legislative authorization before statewide adoption; <hr><ltbullet>establishes evidence-based criteria for state board recommendations; <hr><ltbullet>provides coordination with innovative education programs;<hr><ltbullet>integrates crisis response with SafeUT infrastructure; <hr><ltbullet>establishes parental transparency and opt-out rights; <hr><ltbullet>maintains educator authority over grading and instructional decisions; <hr><ltbullet>maintains academic integrity and authentic student work standards; <hr><ltbullet>establishes student rights to transparency and human review; <hr><ltbullet>integrates enforcement of Title 53E, Chapter 9, Part 3, Student Data Protection; <hr><ltbullet>creates safe harbor for de-identified data; <hr><ltbullet>establishes vendor accountability and transparency requirements; <hr><ltbullet>provides liability protection for good-faith compliance; <hr><ltbullet>prohibits artificial intelligence systems from simulating romantic or personal relationships with students; <hr><ltbullet>requires annual safety reviews for multi-year pilots; <hr><ltbullet>establishes educational principles to guide artificial intelligence deployment;<hr><ltbullet>establishes legislative findings regarding education technology regulation; <hr><ltbullet>requires historical source integrity for AI-supported instruction in history, civics, and social studies;<hr><ltbullet>requires independent evaluation and legislative reporting upon request; <hr><ltbullet>provides technical assistance for Utah-based education technology companies; <hr><ltbullet>grants rulemaking authority to the state board; and<hr><ltbullet>provides a five-year sunset.

title: Criminal and Juvenile Justice Recodification
description: This bill recodifies and amends provisions related to criminal and juvenile justice.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>creates Title 75E, Criminal and Juvenile Justice Administration;<hr><ltbullet>creates the Department of Criminal Justice within Title 75E, Criminal and Juvenile Justice Administration;<hr><ltbullet>recodifies to Title 75E, Criminal and Juvenile Justice Administration:<hr><ltbullet1>Title 63M, Chapter 7, Criminal Justice and Substance Abuse;<hr><ltbullet1>Title 77, Chapter 38, Part 6, Safe at Home Program;<hr><ltbullet1>Title 78B, Chapter 22, Part 4, Utah Indigent Defense Commission;<hr><ltbullet1>Title 78B, Chapter 22, Part 4a, Office of Indigent Defense Services;<hr><ltbullet1>Title 78B, Chapter 22, Part 7, Indigent Aggravated Murder Defense Fund;<hr><ltbullet1>Title 78B, Chapter 22, Part 8, Child Welfare Parental Representation Program;<hr><ltbullet1>Title 78B, Chapter 22, Part 9, Indigent Appellate Defense Division; and<hr><ltbullet1>Title 78B, Chapter 22, Part 11, Youth Defense Fund;<hr><ltbullet>changes the name of:<hr><ltbullet1>Title 76, Utah Criminal Code, to Title 76, Criminal Offenses; and<hr><ltbullet1>Title 77, Utah Code of Criminal Procedure, to Title 77, Criminal Procedure; <hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes roles and responsibilities of the Department of Criminal Justice and the commissioner of the Department of Criminal Justice;<hr><ltbullet>reassigns certain responsibilities of the Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice to the Department of Criminal Justice;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies roles, responsibilities, and administration of certain entities within the Department of Criminal Justice;<hr><ltbullet>removes obsolete programs, responsibilities, and reporting requirements of certain entities within the Department of Criminal Justice;<hr><ltbullet>revises the names of certain entities within the Department of Criminal Justice;<hr><ltbullet>provides that the governor may direct the Department of Criminal Justice to assist with extradition;<hr><ltbullet>updates terminology;<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes; and<hr><ltbullet>includes coordination clauses to substantively and technically coordinate changes between this bill and:<hr><ltbullet1>H.B. 122, Pregnant and Postpartum Inmate Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>H.B. 220, Public Safety Data Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>H.B. 271, Multi-Agency Joint Strike Force Modifications, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>H.B. 230, Offender Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>H.B. 114, Adult-oriented Performance and Material Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>S.B. 13, Statutorily Required Reports and Presentations Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>H.B. 34, Victim Rights Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>H.B. 48, Criminal and Juvenile Justice Changes, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>H.B. 188, Juvenile Justice Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>H.B. 274, Sentencing Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>H.B. 345, Victim Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>S.B. 233, Judicial Performance Evaluation Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>S.B. 313, Recidivism Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>S.B. 86, Firearm Safe Harbor Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>H.B. 90, Sexual Offenses Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>H.B. 137, Violent Crime Clearance Rate Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>S.B. 145, Lobbying Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>S.B. 67, Law Enforcement Quota Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>H.B. 72, Criminal Use of Cryptocurrency Amendments, if both bills pass and become law;<hr><ltbullet1>H.B. 338, First Responder Health Amendments, if both bills pass and become law; and<hr><ltbullet1>S.B. 35, Amendments to Interdisciplinary Parental Representation Pilot Program.

title: Outcome-based Investment Grant Pilot Framework
description: This bill establishes the Outcome-based Investment Grant Pilot Framework to provide a process for administering certain grant funding for projects using measurable outcomes.
highlighted_provisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>establishes a pilot framework for a grant administering agency to award grant funding for projects using measurable outcomes;<hr><ltbullet>requires the Office of the Legislative Auditor General to establish evaluation standards and requirements;<hr><ltbullet>requires grant applicants to submit a pre-analysis plan identifying expected outcomes and metrics;<hr><ltbullet>requires the use of independent evaluators to measure project outcomes;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes review of evaluation findings by the Office of the Legislative Auditor General;<hr><ltbullet>requires certain reporting from the administering agency to a relevant appropriations subcommittee;<hr><ltbullet>includes appropriations for use under the Outcome-based Investment Grant Pilot Framework; and<hr><ltbullet>establishes a sunset date for the pilot framework.

title: Concurrent Resolution on State Innovation for Transition from Government Benefits to Self-reliance
description: This resolution urges the federal government to give more flexibility and autonomy to states to allow for greater innovation and experimentation to help families who receive government benefits more successfully transition off of welfare programs and into work-based self-reliance.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>articulates the strength of Utah's economy and nation-leading upward mobility;<hr><ltbullet>establishes Utah's track record as an innovative leader already showcasing the successes and advantages of state-driven approaches to work and welfare;<hr><ltbullet>identifies evidence of families in Utah who still struggle to fully realize the American Dream due to perceived or actual disincentives in the social safety net in the form of the "benefits cliff" and "benefits plateau"; and<hr><ltbullet>urges the federal government to increase flexibility and autonomy to allow states the ability to innovate through experiments and pilots to better transition families off of federally funded safety net programs and into work-based self-reliance.

title: Concurrent Resolution Regarding Critical Minerals Development and Funding
description: This resolution addresses Utah's critical minerals industry.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>highlights the urgency to develop domestic supplies of critical minerals;<hr><ltbullet>describes Utah's position as a top mining jurisdiction;<hr><ltbullet>outlines the role of the proposed Minerals for Industrial, National, and Economic Security Center (MINES Center) in establishing Utah as a critical minerals hub;<hr><ltbullet>expresses support for the creation of the MINES Center;<hr><ltbullet>encourages the federal government to distribute federal money for critical minerals development through block grants; and<hr><ltbullet>calls on the state's congressional delegation to support the state's efforts to create a MINES Center and to achieve a designation and funding for a critical minerals national lab in the state.

title: Concurrent Resolution Emphasizing Utah's Commitment to Advanced Air Mobility
description: This resolution recognizes Utah's role in aerospace innovation and affirms the state's commitment to developing and implementing Advanced Air Mobility technologies.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>recognizes Utah's history as a global leader in aerospace innovation and research;<hr><ltbullet>describes the potential of Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) technologies;<hr><ltbullet>recognizes Utah's ideal political, economic, and geographic environments for the testing and implementation of AAM technologies;<hr><ltbullet>outlines Utah's long-term goal to establish an operational AAM system and vertiport network before the 2034 Winter Olympic Games; and<hr><ltbullet>expresses the intent of the Senate to collaborate with federal agency partners, including the Federal Aviation Administration and the United States Department of Transportation.

title: Joint Resolution Regarding Utah's Protection and Advocacy Agency
description: This resolution urges the Governor to review Utah's designation of the Disability Law Center as the state's Protection and Advocacy agency to ensure that all individuals with disabilities, regardless of type or functional capacity, receive equitable advocacy and representation.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>recognizes the federal framework establishing Protection and Advocacy (P&A) systems to protect the rights of individuals with disabilities;<hr><ltbullet>encourages the Governor to initiate a formal review of the current P&A designation and consider redesignation, if warranted;<hr><ltbullet>outlines steps for a transparent redesignation process consistent with federal requirements, including public notice, comment, and hearings; and<hr><ltbullet>urges that any review or redesignation process ensure inclusive representation and advocacy for all individuals with disabilities across the state.

title: Joint Resolution to Initiate a Law School at Utah Valley University
description: This resolution directs Utah Valley University to conduct a feasibility study for establishing a law school.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>recognizes the need for increased access to legal education in the state;<hr><ltbullet>acknowledges Utah Valley University's mission to serve working professionals;<hr><ltbullet>directs Utah Valley University to study the feasibility of establishing a law school at the Thanksgiving Point campus;<hr><ltbullet>requires evaluation of facility needs, faculty requirements, accreditation pathways, and market viability;<hr><ltbullet>directs Utah Valley University to design programming focused on evening and weekend instruction for working professionals; and<hr><ltbullet>requires a report to the Legislature on findings and recommendations.

title: Joint Resolution Honoring Irish and Irish-American Contributions to the Founding of the United States
description: This resolution honors Irish and Irish-American contributions to the founding of the United States.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>commemorates the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States by recognizing the contributions of Irish and Irish-American individuals to the American Revolutionary War effort and the signing of the Declaration of Independence;<hr><ltbullet>highlights specific Irish and Irish-American figures involved in the founding of the United States, including signers of the Declaration of Independence, military leaders, and early advocates of American independence;<hr><ltbullet>acknowledges the influence of American independence on political thought and reform movements beyond the United States, including in Ireland, and recognizes ongoing opportunities for state-level cultural and economic engagement with Ireland;<hr><ltbullet>expresses support for expanding Utah-Ireland relations and encourages joint engagement efforts, including a cooperative committee and Ireland's consideration of appointing an Honorary Consul General in Utah; and <hr><ltbullet>directs that a certified copy of the resolution be sent to specified officials and organizations in Ireland and the United States.

title: Joint Rules Resolution - Legislative Ethics Amendments
description: This joint rules resolution amends Joint Rules, Title 6, Legislative Ethics and Adjudication of Ethics Complaints.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>removes term limits for a member of the Independent Legislative Ethics Commission (commission);<hr><ltbullet>modifies the circumstances under which the commission may dismiss a complaint;<hr><ltbullet>authorizes, under certain circumstances, the chair of the commission or the chair of the House or Senate Ethics Committee (committee) to designate a member of the commission or committee to preside;<hr><ltbullet> clarifies provisions related to the commission's and a committee's subpoena powers;<hr><ltbullet>requires an affidavit from the complainants, respondent, and each witness involved in a complaint;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies commission staff's role in reviewing a complaint; <hr><ltbullet>clarifies provisions related to the privacy of an ethics complaint; <hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the commission's recommendation is a private record; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Proposal to Amend Utah Constitution - Legislative Duties
description: This joint resolution of the Utah Legislature proposes to amend the Utah Constitution to modify provisions related to the annual general session.

title: Senate Rules Resolution - Amendments to Senate Rules
description: This resolution modifies Senate rules.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>defines "minority leader" and "minority party";<hr><ltbullet>addresses rules and procedures that apply to an extraordinary session;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the dates on which the Senate convenes;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies the rules that apply to a guest who accompanies a senator on the Senate floor;<hr><ltbullet>corrects a wording error related to substitute legislation;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies procedures related to a Senate executive office confirmation committee;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies when the presiding officer may speak to a point of order;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the procedure for legislation on the consent calendar;<hr><ltbullet>modifies the rules that do not apply during a committee of the whole; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.

title: Resolution Encouraging the Integration of Agriculture into Residential Development
description: This resolution promotes the integration of agricultural features into the fabric of traditional residential neighborhoods.
highlighted_provisions: This resolution:<hr><ltbullet>recognizes the importance of agriculture to Utah's past, present, and future;<hr><ltbullet>encourages municipalities, counties, developers, and builders to be flexible and creative in local planning to allow the integration of agriculture, including working farms, community gardens, orchards, edible landscapes, educational spaces, and other food-producing elements, into the fabric of traditional residential neighborhoods; and<hr><ltbullet>expresses the Senate's support for incorporating agricultural principles into residential development wherever feasible.
